# SuuUI review, 2026-11-15

A review of the whole addon for bugs, performance, architecture and gaps,
written so that another agent can fix from it.

**Reviewed code: `origin/main` at `36f5f407` (Release 0.17.0, API 0.46.0).**
**Status brought up to date at `b9348dff` (2026-11-16)**, after a first
update at `d74864f8` (2026-11-15). The `- where:` of every finding still
open or partly fixed is for `b9348dff`; a finding fixed or withdrawn on
2026-11-16 keeps its `- where:` at `d74864f8`; every other `file:line` in
this document (the quotes in "what", findings fixed or withdrawn earlier,
the sections' notes) is for `36f5f407`. If your checkout is older or newer,
re-locate by the quoted code, not by the line number. The findings the
branch `high-perf` changed (2026-11-16, see the status below) keep their
`- where:` at `b9348dff` too. On 2026-11-19 the probe answers recorded
since (2026-11-15 to 19) were added, read against the code at `3dcdc41e`
(see "Probe answers of 2026-11-19" below); the hand-over of the probe
session is `Docs/plans/open-probes.md`.

## Status on 2026-11-16, at `b9348dff`

The first update (2026-11-15, at `d74864f8`) covered six commits: module
lifecycle ownership (`4950cdcd`), shared services and the modules moved onto
them (`db302207`: Core/Comm, UI/Dismiss, UI/VirtualList, owned timers, CVars
and anchors), loose ends (`68ae02ee`), feature modules importing only the
public API (`a5082e2d`), the split of the largest files (`bcd11307`, no
behaviour change) and a group finder fix (`d74864f8`).

Since then: the bug fixes for gold, items and loot rolls (`740e3d27`:
auction bids, Mail's Collect all and every mail action, loot rolls of the
same item, notification cards, the group finder ad, NPC dialogue), the
probes (`26b69c95`, `3257ac13`) and their answers from the game, cheaper
owned hooks and timers and a perf check that can fail (`d8fa5ced`), and two
fixes that were not review findings (`27f94cc1`, and the tests running with
the dev build's script monitor, `b9348dff`). 25 findings moved: 16 to
fixed, 6 to partly fixed, 3 withdrawn on the game's answer. BAG-11, UIW-7
and GRP-9 are open now instead of unverified, UIW-19 the other way round,
and 14 more have a probe answer or a note added with the same status.
Each of them was checked by reading the code at `b9348dff`; no tests were
run.

Then, on 2026-11-16, the branch `high-perf` (not merged yet) fixed eight
more: UIP-2 (the game's windows SuuUI restyles keep their text styles when
they redraw), X-2.1 and UIW-5 (the encounter timeline is laid out once per
change and moves only what moves, and its module refreshes once per frame),
HUD-UF-4 (unit frames draw health at most once a frame, only the parts that
changed), HUD-UF-6, HUD-UF-7, UF-1 and X-3.1 (one roster pass per burst in
the raid and party modules, on the next frame, drawing only frames that show
someone new; shared listeners instead of per-frame ones). UIP-1 is partly
fixed with UIP-2, and UF-9's note is brought up to date (still partly).
They were checked by reading the code at the branch's head, by its unit
tests and by the perf scenarios, which now measure a player's build (no
runtime checks, no dev monitor: `tests/perf/README.md`). Instructions a
frame before and after the three fixes: the raid boss fight 2,452 to
2,064, the roster scenario 44,288 to 8,608, 144,822 to 17,929 and 100,610
to 13,296 (forming, out of combat, in a fight), the timeline scenario 2,657
to 1,155 while abilities ride toward now. One probe is owed: whether
`UnitGUID("raidN")` is secret in combat on Forever (UF-1). The high
findings left open are HUD-UF-1, HUD-UF-2 and CHAT-2.
Each finding's `- status:` says one of: `fixed in <commit> (…)`, `partly
fixed (…)` (what is done and what remains), `open`, `open (unverified: …)`
(what would settle it), or `withdrawn (…)`. A finding a probe answered has a
`- probe (<date>, …):` line.

### Found after the review

Problems found since the review that have no finding ID:

- **The chat send path (open, by decision).** A taint scan taken right
  after a slash command was typed, out of combat, already listed
  `ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX`, `LAST_ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX`, `ChatFrame1EditBox.text`
  and `ChatFrame1EditBox.autoCompleteParams` as addon-written, and on
  2026-11-15 a `SendChatMessage` was blocked in combat after a whisper
  started by a click in SuuUI's chat. The seed is SuuUI opening the chat
  line from its own code: click-to-whisper, the Whisper buttons, a link
  inserted while the chat line is closed; the command palette and the
  recall of typed lines are further suspects. The owner decided not to fix
  it now: the chat will be redone as a reskin of the game's own chat
  frames. X-6.1, X-6.3 and CHAT-12 point here. On 2026-11-19 the probe
  (WHISPER-taint) saw a whisper SuuUI started out of combat (a name clicked
  in SuuUI's chat) mark `ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX`, `LAST_ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX`
  and the edit box's `text` as SuuUI's, and a line sent in the following
  fight was **not** blocked; `ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX` read as the game's own
  again at that send. One observation: the block of 2026-11-15 needs more
  than a whisper started out of combat, most likely the name clicked in a
  fight (not probed).
- **Fixed in `27f94cc1`:** the bags, the bank, the loot window and every
  panel whose height follows its body opened without a size in dev builds
  only: `Panel:PlaceBody` compared `GetScript("OnSizeChanged")` with its
  own function, and a dev build wraps every script. `b9348dff` runs the
  tests with the same script monitor, so such a comparison fails there too.
- **Fixed in `d74864f8`:** the group finder's search on opening was
  refused by the game when the window was opened by its key binding, and
  reported as an error; now the list refreshes on the first click in the
  window instead. The probe (LFG-opens, 2026-11-15 to 18) then saw 5
  openings by the key binding, and SuuUI's search on opening was refused in
  none of them; the fallback stays harmless, the comment above
  `SearchOnOpen` should say so.

## How to use this document

- Part 1 (this part) is the overview: what was reviewed, how far to trust
  it, the 30 high findings, the themes that run through several areas, a
  suggested order of work, and what must be probed in game first.
- Part 2 is an index of all 429 findings (ID, severity, kind, confidence,
  status at `b9348dff`, title).
- Part 3 holds the findings in full, one section per area. Each finding is
  self-contained: where, what the code does (with quoted lines), why it
  matters, and how to fix it, with the test file to extend. Search for the
  ID (`BAG-1:`) to jump to one.
- Each area section ends with "Fixed since the first pass" and "Withdrawn"
  lists (see "Method"), and with cross-cutting observations.
- `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/` holds the reviewers' scan scripts (the
  import scan behind API-1, the and/or truncation scan, the forward-local and
  global-write scans, the data measuring scripts). Their paths were rewritten
  to run from the repository root and they were not re-run after that; treat
  them as a starting point.

Rules for whoever fixes from this:

1. **Do not act on a finding marked `needs in-game probe` before probing**
   (`/suu probe <topic>`, CLAUDE.md "Probes first"). The finding says what
   to probe. `likely` findings rest on client behaviour that the code or its
   comments record but nobody re-checked; read the evidence before changing.
2. A change comes with its test (CLAUDE.md "Tests"). Most findings name the
   test file.
3. Several findings are the same root cause seen from different areas. The
   "Themes" section groups them; fix the root once, not each copy.
4. Severity is the reviewers' judgement: **high** = wrong behaviour or a
   noticeable cost in common play, or anything touching gold, items or
   quitting; **medium** = edge cases, moderate cost, structural debt;
   **low** = minor. No finding was rated critical.

## Scope

In scope: `src/Core`, `src/EditMode`, `src/SettingsUI`, `src/UI`,
`src/Units` (about 160,000 lines on 0.17.0), `tests/`, `tools/` and the
shape of the generated `src/Data`, `Examples/`, `Docs/API.md`,
`Docs/PluginGuide.md`, `wowlua.json` and CI.

Out of scope, by the owner's choice: `src/Diagnostics`. The `foreverlfg`
package was read only where SuuUI calls it; its chat parser's handling of
crafted lines is **not reviewed**.

## Method, and how far to trust it

The review ran in two passes, each with one reviewer agent per area (15
areas) and a lead who merged the results.

1. **First pass** on the local checkout, commit `4c6ea485` (0.6.0-beta.1).
   Every file of each area was read in full. The test suite was run once
   there: 3,618 passed, 0 failed, 185 files, 181 s; coverage 98.9 % lines,
   77.1 % branches, 97.7 % functions, 73.3 % conditions.
2. The checkout turned out to be 246 commits behind `origin/main`. A
   **second pass** re-checked every first-pass finding on 0.17.0 (still
   present, changed, fixed, withdrawn) by a different reviewer, and reviewed
   the code added since: new files in full, changed files by diff plus the
   surrounding code.

What that means for trust:

- **Nothing was run on 0.17.0.** No build, check or test: the installed
  compiler (0.13.7) is older than 0.17.0 requires (^0.13.15). Test and
  coverage numbers above are for the old commit. Nothing was checked in the
  game at any point.
- **Unchanged code in 0.17.0 was read once** (first pass), then re-read only
  at the places findings cite. Code added since 0.6.0 was read once (second
  pass). Each area section starts with a "Coverage" list of what was and was
  not read; a few long unchanged stretches and some widgets behind a module
  are listed there as not re-read.
- **Performance findings are from reading, not measuring.** Counts such as
  "1,600 calls per roster event" or "15,000 lookups per vote line" are
  derived from the code. `tests/perf` (see TEST-12) is the instrument to
  confirm them before and after a fix. Memory figures for `src/Data` were
  measured in Lua 5.4 outside the game.
- **The lead checked these findings against the code personally** (the rest
  were checked by two reviewers, not by the lead): BAG-1, BAG-2, BAG-32
  (header and call sites), CD-1, GRP-21, GRP-3, GRP-1, CHAT-23, X-11.b5,
  UF-2, UIP-3, UIP-4 (as far as the file's apply/reapply code), SET-1 and
  SET-3 (code shape), UIW-1 (the `userInput` gate), CORE-2 and CORE-3, and
  TEST-1 on the old commit.
- Reviewer agents can be wrong. One first-pass finding was withdrawn in the
  second pass because the first reviewer misread the stdlib, and several
  were corrected in detail. Treat each finding as a well-evidenced claim to
  confirm while fixing, not as a verdict.
- On 2026-11-15 the status of every finding was brought up to date by
  reading the code at `d74864f8` (one agent per group of areas, merged by a
  lead), without running tests or the game. On 2026-11-16 one agent brought
  it up to `b9348dff`: the findings the later commits touch, their
  neighbours and the probes' answers from the game (`/suu probe all`,
  2026-11-15, build 70888), read in the code at `b9348dff`, again without
  running tests; see "Status on 2026-11-16".

## State of the code in one page

What is in good order (so nobody re-checks it):

- `wowlua check` is clean in strict mode; there is no `:: any` cast in
  scope, and every guarded unit or aura read is narrowed before use.
- No `local a, b = cond and f()` truncation anywhere (scan script kept, see
  the cross-cutting section).
- No module parses the combat log; meters, death recap and swing timer use
  the client's own APIs.
- Of the secure-API call sites read (188 found, 99 read, plus all of
  MouseBindings and the secure buttons in Bags and Spellbook), none lacks a
  combat guard. Plain `Show`/`Hide`/`SetPoint` on secure frames elsewhere
  were not swept exhaustively.
- Window bodies in `src/UI` take data in and report through callbacks; that
  split with their owning modules is consistent.
- Money-critical automation is conservative: NpcDialogue automates nothing;
  AutoQuests never picks between rewards or selects gossip and makes gold
  and item turn-ins opt-in; bind-on-pickup roll confirmations come only from
  the player's click; the reworked auction Buy out goes through the game's
  own page and popup.
- Quest data is indexed per map, trainer data built for the player's class
  only, the big data tables are built lazily, CooldownManager's migrations
  are idempotent.
- Docs and exports agree for API 0.20 to 0.46 apart from three undocumented
  names; build profiles follow "Builds per site".

## The 30 high findings

Grouped by what they put at risk. "Conf." is the reviewers' confidence:
C = confirmed from code, L = likely, P = needs an in-game probe first.
"Status" is at `b9348dff` (see "Status on 2026-11-16"), "(high-perf)" a
fix on that branch (2026-11-16, not merged yet); "probe agrees" means the
game's answer (2026-11-15, build 70888) confirms the fix's design.

**Gold, items, quitting the game**

| ID | Conf. | Status | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| BAG-1 | C | fixed (740e3d27) | Auction Bid acts on a row index that goes stale when the list is re-read, and places the typed amount with no check or confirmation; an amount at or above the buyout buys outright. |
| BAG-32 | L | partly (740e3d27) | Bid, Bid again and the Bids tab's Buy out call `PlaceBid` directly, which the file's own header says Forever blocks; a blocked call is reported and stored as a placed bid. |
| BAG-2 | C | fixed (740e3d27) | Mail's Collect all retries a refused take every 0.25 s until the mailbox closes and never reaches later mails. |
| CD-1 | C | fixed (db302207) | The secure `/quit` cover over the shared confirm dialog's OK button is not hidden when "Exit the game?" closes in combat; a later question's OK can quit the game. |
| CHAT-23 | C | fixed (740e3d27) | Two open loot rolls for the same item are confused: your vote locks the wrong row, and a decided roll removes one still open (Blizzard's roll frames are off screen, so that roll is lost). |

**Other players can act on your client**

| ID | Conf. | Status | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| GRP-21 | C | fixed (db302207) | Timeline: anyone can start or cancel your pull countdown (with voice) by an addon whisper, also in combat. |
| GRP-22 | C | fixed (db302207) | Marks: shared marks are accepted from anyone, without limit, and saved (up to 200; your own are evicted). |
| CD-2 | C | fixed (db302207) | The same finding from the cooldowns area: addon messages are taken from any channel and sender; covers Marks, Timeline, Convergences, Campsite. |
| UF-2 | C | fixed (db302207) | Readiness broadcasts addon messages constantly (every roster event, every 2 s while cooldowns move), also while its panel is off; every client answers `RDYQ`. |

**Things that cannot be turned off, or come back wrong**

| ID | Conf. | Status | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| X-11.b5 | C | fixed (4950cdcd) | Mouseover bindings cannot be turned off: `OnDisable` calls `Apply()`, which branches on `IsEnabled()`, still true during `OnDisable`. |
| UIP-4 | C | fixed (4950cdcd) | `UI/Visibility` never lets go of a frame: a disabled module's frame is shown again on edit mode, keybind mode or combat, and re-enabling leaves it hidden. |
| UIP-3 | C | fixed (740e3d27) | A reused notification card keeps an old action button visible with its old click handler (sparse pools hidden with `ipairs`). |
| UIP-2 | C | fixed (high-perf) | `reskinText` is not idempotent: a second pass turns titles, numbers and captions into labels. |
| UIW-1 | C | fixed (740e3d27) | Group Finder ad edits are never reported (gated on `userInput`, never true on Forever), so the generated text replaces them within 15 s. |
| MAP-1 | C | fixed (740e3d27) | NpcDialogue can leave the whole UI dimmed until a reload (records UIParent's alpha mid-fade); AutoQuests (MAP-20) makes the timing likelier. |

**Keyboard lost in combat (probed: the keyboard rule holds)**

| ID | Conf. | Status | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| SET-1 | P | fixed (db302207), probe agrees | FilterMenu's panel swallows all keys while open in combat. |
| UIP-5 | P | fixed (db302207), probe agrees | Esc handling is copied with different combat guards; the context menu can hold back every key in combat. |
| CHAT-1 | L | fixed (db302207), probe agrees | The welcome panel swallows all keys if combat starts before a key is pressed. |
| CD-27 | P | fixed (68ae02ee); `OnLeave` fires on hide, a safety net | A unit frame that hides under the mouse leaves its mouseover keys bound to a dead unit. |

| HUD-UF-2 | L | open | Buff indicators with source "mine" rely on the `PLAYER` token, which other players' auras pass. |

| ID | Conf. | Status | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| UF-1 | C | fixed (high-perf) | A raid roster change re-scans and redraws everything at once, uncoalesced. |
| X-3.1 | C | fixed (high-perf) | The same from the sweep: every unit frame has its own roster listener, then the raid module walks all buttons again. |
| HUD-UF-4 | C | fixed (high-perf) | `UpdateHealth` runs in full, with allocations, on every health, heal-prediction and absorb event (three per heal, every frame). |

## Themes: one root cause, several findings

Fix these at the root. IDs in one line describe the same problem or the same
missing piece.

**T1. Acting later on an index taken earlier.** A row, inbox, merchant or
roster index is stored, the list changes, and the action lands on something
else. BAG-1 (auction bid), BAG-3 (COD confirmation), BAG-4 (merchant queue),
X-4.2 (merchant and raid moves), UIW-8 (raid page drag), CHAR-2 and CHAR-29
(toy and summon cards in combat), CD-28 (rank upgrade slot numbers). Fix
pattern: store the identity (auction ID, mail's sender+subject+money, item
ID, GUID, spell ID), re-resolve it at the moment of acting, and refuse when
it no longer matches.

*Status at `b9348dff`:* BAG-1 and BAG-3 are fixed (`740e3d27`: the auction
by its ID, a mail by its content, each found again and compared at the
moment of acting; Mail's Delete, Return, Take and row clicks the same way).
BAG-4 and X-4.2 are partly fixed as before (Merchant still sends the
remaining steps after a refused buy; the raid planner still moves by raid
indices). UIW-8, CHAR-2, CHAR-29 and CD-28 are open; their files did not
change since `d74864f8`.

**T2. Loops without a progress check.** BAG-2 (Collect all), MAP-5 (Train
all: fixed 0.35 s pacing, buys beyond what was confirmed), BAG-15 (any red
error text stops a sort), BAG-17 (scan cooldown). Fix pattern: advance on
the game's answer event, stop on the first refusal or when nothing changed.

*Status at `b9348dff`:* BAG-2 is fixed (`740e3d27`: Collect all asks for one
thing, moves on by the game's answer and skips a refusal) and BAG-17 earlier
(`68ae02ee`). MAP-5 and BAG-15 are open (Trainer and the sort did not
change).

**T3. Addon messages are trusted.** Six receivers on the prefix `SuuUI`,
none reads the channel: GRP-26 (the table and the proposed shared receiver),
GRP-21, GRP-22, GRP-3, GRP-23, GRP-24, GRP-25, CD-2, CD-9, and on the
sending side UF-2, X-3.2, GRP-8, MAP-21 (quest announcements unthrottled to
raid chat). Tests: TEST-10. Fix once: one receiver in Core
(`M:OnAddonMessage` / `M:SendAddonMessage`) that checks the allowed channel
set per verb (which is the membership check, since the server delivers
PARTY/RAID/GUILD only from members), an optional leader/assistant rank,
per-sender rate limits, a reply floor for question verbs, and field
validators. Wire formats must stay as they are (older clients).

*Status at `b9348dff` (unchanged since `d74864f8`):* largely done. Core/Comm (`db302207`) is the shared
receiver; GRP-26, GRP-21, GRP-22, GRP-3, GRP-23, GRP-24, GRP-25, CD-2, UF-2,
X-3.2 and TEST-10 are fixed. Left: GRP-8 (group finder notes without an
overall limit) and MAP-21 (quest announcements unthrottled) are open; CD-9
is partly fixed (one receiver now; Marks and Convergences still each keep
their own minimap pin code).

**T4. The module lifecycle has holes.**
- `IsEnabled()` is false during the whole of `OnEnable` and true during the
  whole of `OnDisable` (`Core/Modules.wowlua`, `enable`/`disable`). Code
  that branches on it inside either callback does the opposite of what it
  means: X-11.b5 (mouse bindings), X-11.b6 (loot rolls at a reload),
  X-11.a8, X-11.b7. Decide the semantics once (for example a "turning off"
  state, or pass the target state to the callbacks) and sweep.
- A module cannot own a timer, hook, published anchor or visibility
  registration, so `releaseAll` cannot take them away: CORE-8, X-4.1 (add
  `M:After`/`M:Every`), CORE-2 (queued out-of-combat work survives disable),
  UIP-4, X-5.1 (stacking hook), X-11.a1, X-4.3 to X-4.6, CD-3 and X-11.b3
  (Timeline shows after being turned off), CD-30, CD-31, SET-18.
- CVars and other game state a module changes are not given back, or the
  old value is kept in a profile setting and lost on a profile switch:
  X-11.a2, X-11.b2, X-11.b1, X-11.a4, UF-5, UF-6, GRP-7, CD-4, CD-5, UF-3,
  CD-11, X-11.a3, MAP-8. Fix once: a Core helper that remembers the player's
  value per character (not per profile) and restores it on release.
- Registration order: API-4 (plugin enabled before its `OnEnable` exists,
  the style the PluginGuide teaches), CORE-11 (`replaces` after login),
  API-2 (a replaced service is not restored), CORE-3 (combat queue order).
- None of this is tested: TEST-2, TEST-3.

*Status at `b9348dff` (as at `d74864f8`; `d8fa5ced` made owned hooks and
timers about as cheap as plain ones):* largely done. `IsEnabled` is true inside `OnEnable`
and false inside `OnDisable` (`4950cdcd`), which fixes X-11.b5, X-11.b6,
X-11.a8 and X-11.b7. Owned timers, hooks, anchors and visibility
(`4950cdcd`, `db302207`) fix CORE-2, UIP-4, X-5.1, X-11.a1, X-4.3, X-4.6,
CD-3, X-11.b3, CD-30 and CD-31; `M:SetCVar` fixes X-11.a2, X-11.b2, X-11.b1,
X-11.a4, UF-3, UF-6, GRP-7, CD-4 and CD-11; API-4 and CORE-3 are fixed;
MAP-8 is withdrawn. Left: CORE-8 and X-4.1 partly (work built ahead, themes,
aura filter lists and suppressed frames have no owner; 36 plain `after`
calls remain), UF-5, CD-5 and X-11.a3 partly, SET-18, CORE-11 and API-2
open; TEST-2 and TEST-3 partly (`cycle()` exists and 22 module tests use
it).

**T5. Keyboard propagation in combat.** SET-1, UIP-5, CHAT-1 (and
duplicated click-outside/Esc code, SET-12). One probe settles what
`SetPropagateKeyboardInput` does in lockdown on Forever; then one shared
helper replaces the five copies.

*Status at `b9348dff`:* SET-1, UIP-5 and CHAT-1 are fixed by UI/Dismiss
(`db302207`, the last copies in `68ae02ee`), and the probe settles the
question: in combat lockdown `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` is refused on an
addon's own frame and `EnableKeyboard` is allowed, so letting go before the
lockdown and calling nothing during it, as UI/Dismiss does, is the design
that works. SET-12 is partly fixed (edit mode keeps its own click
handling).

**T6. Aura filters on Forever.** Other players' auras pass `X` and `!X`
alike, and tokens such as `PLAYER` and `RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE` do not
select on them. 0.17.0 records this in comments and fixed the inline icons,
but not: HUD-UF-1, HUD-UF-2, HUD-CD-5, UF-7, UF-24, UF-25, CORE-24, CHAT-10.

*Status at `b9348dff`:* not started. HUD-UF-1, HUD-UF-2, UF-7, UF-24,
CORE-24 and CHAT-10 are open; HUD-CD-5 and UF-25 are open (unverified):
`/suu probe all` has not answered them yet.

*Since, on 2026-11-19 (probe answers):* UF-25 is confirmed: a crowd
control aura on a party member passes `CROWD_CONTROL|DISPELLABLE` and
`CROWD_CONTROL|!DISPELLABLE` alike (and `HARMFUL|DISPELLABLE` although it
has no dispel type). HUD-CD-5's mob half goes the other way: on a mob,
other players' debuffs passed `HARMFUL|!PLAYER` and not `HARMFUL|PLAYER`,
so there the split holds (your own were not sampled); player targets, the
finding's case, cannot be probed on the owner's PvE ruleset. The rule
above stands for other players' auras on players; on mobs `PLAYER` and
`!PLAYER` split by caster as `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` recorded on
2026-10-12.

**T7. Whole-thing redraws on frequent events.** Roster: UF-1, X-3.1,
HUD-UF-7, HUD-UF-6, UF-9, UF-23, CD-29. Auras and health: HUD-UF-4, X-3.3,
HUD-CD-3, HUD-DM-4. Per frame: X-2.1, UIW-5, X-2.2, X-2.6, MAP-3, MAP-9,
UF-4. Per line or keystroke: CHAT-2, CHAT-3, X-3.5, CHAR-6, SET-2, SET-6.
Bags and tooltips: BAG-8, BAG-9, BAG-12, BAG-13. Settings pages and themes:
SET-4, UIP-1, UIP-12, UIP-23. Common fixes: coalesce to one pass per frame
per event kind, early-out on unchanged values, register unit events instead
of all-units events, do not run while hidden. Lists are not virtualised
anywhere (UIW-6, BAG-20); one pooled list widget would serve all windows.

*Status at `b9348dff`:* CHAT-3 and X-3.5 are fixed (`740e3d27`: a vote line
redraws only its roll's row, once a frame at most, and the group is read

*Since, on 2026-11-16 (branch `high-perf`):* UF-1, X-3.1, HUD-UF-6 and

## For wowlua itself

Seen while reviewing; not SuuUI bugs:

- On the old commit a file-level `local GLYPHS` was used inside class
  methods above its declaration; the compiled Lua read a global there and
  strict `check` did not flag it (the game's global string of the same name
  hid the error). 0.17.0 no longer has the case and a scan found no other,
  but the checker gap remains, in exactly this form: when the local's name
  is also a declared game global, a use above its declaration passes strict
  check and reads the global (a name that is not a declared global is
  rejected with E1001). Reproduced on wowlua 0.13.7 and filed as
  https://github.com/DomenikIrrgang/wowlua/issues/249.
- The stdlib has no notion of an owner for timers (`after`, `every`); every
  SuuUI module guards by hand (X-4.1).
- `wowlua publish` on a tag runs the tests but not `--coverage`, so the
  minimums in `wowlua.json` are enforced by nothing automatic (TEST-9).
- The garbage collector is still stopped in every test as a 0.9.1 workaround
  (TEST-19); whether 0.13.15 still needs it was not checked.

# Part 2: index of all findings

Status is at `b9348dff` (2026-11-16): fixed, partly (fixed), open, or withdrawn; open includes the findings marked "open (unverified)" in Part 3. Confidence is the review's, except where a probe settled it (UIW-7, GRP-9, and on 2026-11-19 UF-25, CHAR-27, X-6.3: confirmed; HUD-4: confirmed from code for what is left). BAG-11 was marked confirmed on 2026-11-16 and is back to `probe` (the answer did not confirm it). The probe answers of 2026-11-19 are in the statuses. Before that update this column said whether a finding was still present, changed or new against the first pass; Part 3's area notes keep that history.

# Part 3: findings in full

## Area: Core


All file:line references are for the 0.17.0 export (NEW), repo-relative.

### Coverage

Re-checked on NEW: all 21 first-pass findings (CORE-1 to CORE-21).

Read in full in NEW: `Ahead`, `AuraFilters`, `Data`, `Settings` (all 1,599 lines), `Themes` (all 711),
`Roles`, `Vision`, `Combat`, `Blizzard`, `Anchors`, `Services`, `Root`, `RolePresets`, `Pixel`, `TaintScan`,
`Fault` (95-361), `Events` (20-236), `Modules` (395-420 and 530-934).

Read as a diff against `4c6ea485`, with the surrounding NEW code where it mattered: `API` (whole diff),
`Modules` (whole diff: 18 lines), `Events`, `Fonts`, `Init`, `Messages.d`, `Motion`, `ServiceKeys`.
`Fault`, `Extend`, `Combat`, `Services`, `Perf`, `Serialize`, `DB`, `Util` have no diff between the two
commits; the lines each finding quotes were read again in NEW.

Skimmed for shape and load cost only: `ThemesBuiltin` (14 themes), `ThemesRaids` (21 themes). Not read:
`Tokens.wowlua` (generated; only its glyph and texture name lists were looked at).

Checked outside the area to settle claims: the wowlua stdlib `events.wowlua` and `combat.wowlua`
(`~/repositories/wowlua/crates/wowlua-stdlib/std`), callers in `src/Units`, `src/UI/Auras.wowlua`,
`src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua`, `Sections.wowlua`, `Registry.wowlua`.

Not done: nothing was built or run. `Extend.wowlua` lines 1-213 and 312-370, 392-445, 468-570 and `Modules`
1-394, 421-529 were not re-read (no diff, or a diff of a few lines read as a diff). `Docs/API.md` was only
searched, not compared name by name with `API.wowlua`.

### Summary

Core grew by about 4,000 lines; the three new pieces (work built ahead, lazy data tables, aura filter lists)
are small and careful, and two first-pass problems are gone or nearly gone: the role lookup is cached, and
colour vision puts the glows back. The event bus no longer walks every listener to remove one.

What remains is mostly what was there before, untouched: the combat queue (stale job after a newer one,
jobs of a disabled module), the blocked-action handler (a full taint scan per event, with a scan list that
has since doubled), profile changes in combat, unchecked imported values, and the module teardown that
covers only Core's own registries. `Fault`, `Extend`, `Combat`, `Services`, `Perf` and `Serialize` have not
changed at all.

The newest code, layouts per screen size (the last feature before the release), brings three new
findings: a layout is stored for every screen size and scale the client ever reports, a setting that
becomes a layout setting later loses its stored value, and manual layout copies are not deferred in combat.
One new bug in the aura filters: an allow list marked "not for" your class hides every aura instead of
not counting.

### Findings

#### CORE-6: Switching, copying, importing or resetting a profile (and copying a layout) in combat notifies every watcher at once
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (depends on each module's watchers; in game: `/suu profile use X` in combat, then `/suu errors`)
- where: src/Core/Settings.wowlua:723-744 (`useProfile`), 808-830 (`copyProfile`), 1011-1018
  (`importProfile`), 500-515 (`reset`), 1211-1228 (`copyLayout`); callers without a combat check:
  src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:691, src/SettingsUI/Sections.wowlua:552, 651, 677, 722,
  src/Core/API.wowlua:1284
- known: no
- what: these call `notify` synchronously for every changed key (positions, sizes, visibility of every
  module). The automatic paths defer themselves: the role switch with `combat.run("roleProfile", …)`, the
  screen-size switch with `combat.run("root:layout", …)`, and `rolePresets.apply` refuses
  (`if InCombatLockdown() then return false, "After the fight." end`). The manual paths have no guard:
  the profile select in the settings window (`profiles.use(name or "")`), import, "Reset everything",
  `/suu profile use`, `/suu reset all`, "Copy" from another profile, and the new "Copy" from another
  layout (`settings.copyLayout`). A settings row's `combat = true` only adds a note to its description
  (src/SettingsUI/Registry.wowlua:35-36); nothing blocks a control in combat.
- why it matters: a profile or layout change in combat runs dozens of module watchers that move or resize
  secure frames. Any watcher that does not defer itself produces blocked actions; the profile is then half
  applied on screen until the next layout.
- fix: one rule in Core: `useProfile`, `copyProfile`, `importProfile`, `copyLayout` and a whole-namespace
  or whole-profile `reset` return `false, "After the fight."` while in lockdown (inject a
  `combat.CombatState` into `SettingsStore`, as `ModuleRegistry` takes one), or queue them with
  `combat.run`. Tests in `tests/unit/Core/Settings.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-22: A layout is stored for every screen size and scale the client ever reports, in every profile used
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code); how fast it grows for a windowed player needs an in-game look at `SuuUIDB.profiles[*].__layouts` after resizing the window
- where: src/Core/Settings.wowlua:275-300 (`layoutAt` with `create`), 1153-1167 (`useLayout`), 1281 (`bind`),
  734 (`useProfile`), 819 (`copyProfile`); src/Core/Root.wowlua:86-106
- known: no
- what: the layout key is the screen's pixels over the scale, `("%dx%d"):format(math.floor(w / s + 0.5),
  math.floor(h / s + 0.5))`. Every `DISPLAY_SIZE_CHANGED` and every `SUUUI_ROOT_SCALED` calls
  `settings.useLayout(layoutSize())`, and `useLayout` always runs `self:layoutAt(p, size, true)`, which
  stores a full copy of the closest layout under the new key (`made = copy(near)` … `all[size] = made`),
  whether or not the player ever changes anything at that size. `bind`, `useProfile` and `copyProfile`
  create one the same way. Nothing removes a layout except "Forget" in the settings, by hand. Two more
  sources: `ui.scale` is per profile, so `useProfile` first creates a layout in the target for the *old*
  profile's size (line 716, before the scale watcher runs) and then another for its own; and each layout
  carries a `__seeded` table naming every registered namespace.
- why it matters: a player in windowed mode who drags the window's edge, or tries several values of the
  scale slider (0.5 to 2 in steps of 0.05, two sliders' worth of sizes), collects one copy of every
  position and group layout setting per size, in every profile, saved for good, copied again by every
  "new profile" and exported with every profile string. The layout list in Settings › Profiles fills with
  sizes nobody chose.
- fix: do not materialise a layout on read. In `storedIn`, when the profile has layouts but none for the
  size in use, read from `closest(all, size)` (as `valueAtSize` already does at line 1141) and fall back to
  the profile's own values; create the layout only in `write` and `setProfileValues`. Drop the `create`
  calls in `bind`, `useProfile`, `copyProfile` and `useLayout`. Optionally, in `bind`, remove layouts equal
  to their closest neighbour. Tests in `tests/unit/Core/Settings.test.wowlua`: `useLayout` through five
  sizes without a write leaves `__layouts` unchanged; a write at the fifth creates exactly one.

#### CORE-23: A setting that becomes a layout setting in a later version loses its stored value at every size already seen
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Settings.wowlua:249-271 (`seed`), 304-312 (`storedIn`), 204-217 (`register`'s `layout`)
- known: no
- what: a layout takes the profile's values of a namespace once: `seed` marks `done[namespace] = true` and
  returns early from then on. Which keys are layout settings is decided now (`isLayout`: a position by
  shape, or a key in the module's `layout` list). `storedIn` reads a layout setting only from the layout
  when one exists (`return stored(l, namespace, key)`), never from the profile's own values. So when a
  module adds a key to its `layout` list in a later release (today only `party` and `raid` name any:
  src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:809, src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1168), every existing layout already has
  that namespace marked as seeded, does not hold the key, and the setting reads as its default. The
  player's value is still in the profile's own values but nothing reads it. The same happens to an
  existing table setting whose default gains a `point` field.
- why it matters: layouts shipped in the last commit before 0.17.0, so the first release that moves a
  setting such as a frame's width into `layout` resets it for every player at the sizes they have used,
  with no migration hook to prevent it (migrations see stored values per namespace, not the seeding).
- fix: record seeding per key (`__seeded[namespace][key] = true`), and in `seed` copy every layout key not
  yet marked; or, simpler, in `storedIn` fall back to the profile's own value when the layout does not hold
  the key and the key is not marked as seeded. Test in `tests/unit/Core/Settings.test.wowlua`: bind with a
  layout made while `width` was not a layout key, register with `layout = { "width" }`, expect the stored
  width.

#### CORE-2: Work queued with `M:RunOutOfCombat` survives the module being turned off
- status: fixed in 4950cdcd (releaseAll cancels the module's waiting `m:<id>:` combat work, and a cancelled job never runs)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Modules.wowlua:409-411 (`RunOutOfCombat`), 616-624 (`releaseAll`);
  src/Core/Combat.wowlua:47-68
- known: no
- what: `RunOutOfCombat` queues under `"m:" .. self.id .. ":" .. tostring(key)`. `releaseAll` clears
  events, watchers, commands, settings sections, movers, extend entries and services; `CombatQueue` has no
  way to drop jobs, so the module's waiting ones stay.
- why it matters: in combat the player turns a module off (the `"module:<id>"` job is queued), then one of
  the module's still-live event handlers queues `m:<id>:layout`. When combat ends the queue runs in order:
  the module is disabled and released, then its layout job runs on a disabled module and shows or moves
  frames that `OnDisable` just hid. The same happens after `fail()`.
- fix: add `CombatQueue:cancel(prefix)` that replaces the waiting job's `fn` with a no-op for every string
  key starting with the prefix (keep the entry so `pending` stays balanced), and call it from `releaseAll`
  with `"m:<id>:"` (pass the module, read its id). Tests: `tests/unit/Core/Combat.test.wowlua` (a cancelled
  job doesn't run, `pendingCount` stays right) and `Modules.test.wowlua` (disable in combat, then a
  `RunOutOfCombat`, end combat: fn not called).

#### CORE-3: The combat queue can run an older job after a newer one for the same key
- status: fixed in 4950cdcd (a run for a key that still waits replaces the waiting job's function instead of running at once, so only the latest runs, once)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); how often it bites in play: likely rare
- where: src/Core/Combat.wowlua:47-68; wowlua `combat.wowlua` `flush` (on `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`, one entry at
  a time, `InCombatLockdown()` already false)
- known: no
- what: `run` checks only `inCombat()`. Out of combat it calls `fn` at once and leaves `self.waiting[key]`
  alone. During the flush at the end of combat, a `run(key, new)` made by an earlier job (or by any
  `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` listener that runs before the stdlib's flush) runs `new` immediately; the
  deferred closure for `key` then runs the older `latest.fn` afterwards.
- why it matters: the queue's contract is "the latest function runs". Example: the `"module:<id>"` job
  enables a module whose `OnEnable` calls `RunOutOfCombat("layout", …)` while an older `m:<id>:layout` job
  still waits further back; the old closure, captured before the change, runs last and wins. A harmless
  instance exists today: the `"root:scale"` job emits `SUUUI_ROOT_SCALED`, whose listener calls
  `combat.run("root:layout", …)` while an older `"root:layout"` waits (src/Core/Root.wowlua:60-103); it
  only repeats a no-op there.
- fix: in `run`, when not in combat and `self.waiting[key]` exists, replace that job's `fn` with a no-op
  before calling `fn`. Test in `tests/unit/Core/Combat.test.wowlua`: queue A1 and B1 in combat; on combat
  end A1 calls `run("B", B2)`; expect B2 once and B1 never.

#### CORE-5: Every blocked-action event runs a full taint scan and `debugstack` before deduplicating
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Fault.wowlua:380-415 (`blocked`), src/Core/TaintScan.wowlua:172-237 (`scan`), 19-128
  (`GLOBALS`), 131-167 (`FRAMES`)
- known: no
- what: for `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED`/`FORBIDDEN` blamed on SuuUI, `blocked` takes `debugstack(2)` and runs
  `taintScan.scan()`, and only then calls `log:report`, which drops a repeat. The scan checks 108 globals,
  every `UISpecialFrames` entry, every string field of 31 Blizzard frames and tables, the guild control's
  dropdowns, the open menu manager, the world map's scroll container and every pin pool, and up to 16 bag
  slot buttons with their parents: one `pcall(issecurevariable, …)` per field, and the label string is
  built for every field before the check (`check(label .. "." .. k, t, k)`), secure or not. For blocks
  blamed on another addon it takes `debugstack(2)` and `date()` and does `table.remove(saved, 1)` per event.
- why it matters: a blocked call usually repeats (a protected `Show`/`SetPoint` retried from an event or
  `OnUpdate` in combat). Each repeat costs several thousand calls and string allocations, in combat,
  exactly when something is already going wrong.
- fix: build the report key first (`"Taint\0" .. what .. ": " .. tostring(func)`) and skip stack and scan
  when the log already has it (add `FaultLog:has(source, message)`); record the other-addon case once per
  `addon .. func` per session; in `scan`, pass the label's parts to `check` and concatenate only when
  `not secure`. Test in `tests/unit/Core/Fault.test.wowlua`: two identical blocked events call
  `taintScan.scan` once.

#### CORE-7: An imported profile is checked by top-level type only
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the damage depends on each module's tolerance
- where: src/Core/Settings.wowlua:951-1008 (`sanitize`), 329-336 (`valueOf`), 524-552 (`screen`), 1251-1285
  (`bind`); src/Core/Serialize.wowlua:27-72 (legacy reader, `tonumber` at 40 and 48), 170-183 (`decode`)
- known: no
- what: `sanitize` keeps a value when `type(v) == type(defs[key])`, for the profile and for each of its
  layouts (any number of them, any key matching `^%d+x%d+$`). `screen` then applies only the registered
  vetoes. So an import can carry numbers out of any range (the legacy `n…;` reader uses `tonumber`, which
  also accepts hex, and `inf`/`nan` on some platforms), strings that name no known option, and table
  settings of any inner shape (`position = { x = "a" }`). Namespaces SuuUI does not know are kept verbatim,
  copied by every later `createProfile`. `decode` does not look at the version in `!SUU:<n>!`, so a string
  from a future format is read as today's. `bind` trusts hand-edited saved data: a non-table
  `profiles[name]` for the current character raises in `layoutAt` at load (`p[LAYOUTS] = …`).
- why it matters: profile strings are meant to be shared between players. A bad or hostile one cannot run
  code, but it can make modules error in `OnEnable` or in layout (module marked errored, or frames off
  screen), and the player's only way back is another profile.
- fix: (1) give `settings.register` an optional per-key validator (min/max for numbers, allowed values for
  strings, a shape function for tables) applied in `valueOf`, `set` and `sanitize`; modules already know
  these limits for their sliders and selects. (2) In `sanitize`, drop non-finite numbers (`v ~= v`,
  `math.huge`) at any depth, cap unknown namespaces and the number of layouts. (3) In `decode`, refuse a
  version above `VERSION`. (4) In `bind`, replace a non-table profile with `{}`. Tests in
  `tests/unit/Core/Settings.test.wowlua` and `Serialize.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-8: `releaseAll` covers only Core's own registries; timers, hooks, anchors, work built ahead, themes, aura filter lists and suppressed frames are each module's own job
- status: partly fixed (timers, secure hooks, anchors, visibility, queued combat work and CVars now go with the module in releaseAll; work built ahead, plugin themes and aura filter lists, and suppressed Blizzard frames still have no owner or undo)
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Ahead.wowlua:75-84 (no owner, no cancel); src/Core/AuraFilters.wowlua:200-261 (no owner, no
  unregister); src/Core/Blizzard.wowlua:101-146 (`restore` never restores); src/Core/API.wowlua:241-250
  (`RegisterTheme`, `RegisterAuraFilter`), 294 (`BuildAhead`), 546 (`SuppressBlizzard`)
- known: partly (Blizzard.wowlua:18: "Only a reload brings a suppressed frame back")
- what: the module contract says everything a module registers goes when it turns off. That holds for the
  seven registries in `releaseAll` (events, watchers, commands, settings sections, movers, extend,
  services). It does not hold for: `wowlua:timer` handles and `wowlua:hooks` hooks (the stdlib has no owner
  for either, so modules cancel by hand or gate on `IsEnabled`); `SuuUI.PublishAnchor` (21 calls in
  `src/Units`; `fail()` runs `OnDisable` only for an `OnEnable` failure, so a module that errors later
  leaves its frame published); `ahead.schedule` jobs (each of the seven callers gates its step on
  `self:IsEnabled()` by hand); a plugin's theme and aura filter list (kept, and still attached to frames,
  after the plugin's module is off); and `SuuUI.SuppressBlizzard` (24 calls; cannot be undone). Example of
  the last: src/Units/Durability.wowlua:777 suppresses `DurabilityFrame` in a module that is not
  `reloadToToggle`, so turning it off leaves neither figure until a reload.
- why it matters: every module re-implements teardown, which is where "listener registered twice on
  re-enable" and "timer outlives a disabled module" bugs come from.
- fix: add owner-scoped helpers on `Module`, released in `releaseAll`: `M:After(sec, fn)` / `M:Every(sec, fn)`
  (handles kept per module, cancelled on release), `M:HookGame(target, method, fn)` (wrapper gated on a
  per-module `live` flag), `M:PublishAnchor(name, frame)` (unpublished on release), `M:BuildAhead(key, step)`
  (`ahead.cancel(key)` on release; add `cancel` to Ahead). Give `auraFilters.register` and
  `themes.register` an owner and an `unregister(owner)`. For suppression, warn in dev builds when a module
  that is not `reloadToToggle` calls `SuppressBlizzard`. Document each in `Docs/API.md` under the next API
  version.

#### CORE-9: TRANSITION state: all built-in modules are classes; the loose view remains in `GetModule`, Diagnostics and two tests
- status: fixed in a5082e2d (ModuleOf and LooseDef are gone; GetModule returns AnyModule?, and other modules are read through Setting and IsEnabled)
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Modules.wowlua:536-609 (`ModuleOf`, `LooseDef`), 807-812 (`register`);
  src/Core/API.wowlua:134-137 (`GetModule`); src/Diagnostics/Diagnostics.wowlua:10;
  tests/unit/Core/Modules.test.wowlua:31-33, tests/unit/Units/MicroBags.test.wowlua:20-39
- known: no (the TRANSITION comments are the only record)
- what: 61 files in `src/Units` call `SuuUI.AddModule(X.new())`; none calls `RegisterModule`.
  `RegisterModule` is used only by `src/Diagnostics/Diagnostics.wowlua` and by plugins (`Examples/*`), for
  which `PluginModule` is the permanent path. What still depends on `ModuleOf`: the return type of
  `registry:register`, and `API.GetModule`, which hands any caller another module typed loosely
  (`[string]: unknown`). 27 call sites use it (23 in `src/Units`, 7 of them in `Windows.wowlua`; 4 in
  `src/Diagnostics`): most read a setting or `:IsEnabled()`; a few call the other module's own methods, and
  `Docs/API.md:679-680` documents `GetModule("marks"):Marks()` and `GetModule("convergences"):Spots()` as
  API. `ModuleOf` is a hand-kept mirror of `Module` (the 0.32 change to `Migrate` had to be made in both
  places).
- why it matters: the loose view is how modules reach into each other untyped; a renamed setting or method
  in one module fails silently in another.
- fix, in order: (1) `register` takes `PluginDef` and returns `PluginModule`; (2) `API.GetModule` returns
  `AnyModule?` (it has `Setting`, `IsEnabled`, `state`); change `:Get(...)` on other modules to
  `:Setting(...)`; (3) move cross-module method calls to service keys (`MARKS` and `CONVERGENCES` exist)
  and keep the documented `GetModule("marks")` methods working through the class's public methods;
  (4) convert Diagnostics to a class; (5) delete `ModuleOf`/`LooseDef` and update the two tests.

#### CORE-10: A repeating error pays `debugstack` and string work on every call, and evicted errors are announced again
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Fault.wowlua:138-141 (handler), 146-166 (`report`), 169-175 (`finish`)
- known: no
- what: the xpcall handler always runs `self.lastStack = debugstack(2)`; `report` then builds
  `tostring(message):match(...)` and the key string before finding the existing entry and only counting.
  Nothing ever stops calling a listener that fails every time. The list keeps `maxKept` entries; an evicted
  entry's key is removed (`self.byKey[old.source .. "\0" .. old.message] = nil`), so the same error is
  announced in chat and saved again later. Messages that embed varying data (a table address, a unit name,
  a number) are each distinct and each print a chat line.
- why it matters: one listener that errors on `UNIT_AURA` or in a per-frame callback produces a full stack
  string per call for the rest of the session, and a message with varying text floods the chat.
- fix: keep the current source in the log during `call` so the handler can look in `byKey` first and take
  `debugstack` only for a new key; keep announced keys in a set that eviction does not clear; cap chat
  announcements per source per minute (the list still records them). Optionally stop calling a listener
  after N consecutive failures. Tests in `tests/unit/Core/Fault.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-11: A plugin that `replaces` a module and loads after login runs beside it; a replaced module never comes back
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Modules.wowlua:878-886 (`replacer`), 888-935 (`start`), 954-987 (`add`), 852-875 (`sync`)
- known: no
- what: replacement is decided inside `start(m)` of the module being replaced, by looking for a
  registered, enabled replacer at that moment. A replacer registered after `startAll` goes through `add` →
  `start(replacer)`, which never looks at the module it replaces, so both are enabled and both provide the
  same services (see CORE-14). In the other direction, once `replacedBy` is set, `sync` returns early for
  the original for the whole session (`if m.state == ModuleState.Incompatible or m.replacedBy then return
  end`): if the replacer fails in `OnEnable` or is turned off, the feature is gone until a reload, and
  `describe` still says "replaced by X" with no reload hint.
- why it matters: plugin authors following `Docs/PluginGuide.md` get two unit-frame sets, or none.
- fix: in `add`, when `self.started` and `m.replaces` names a started module, either refuse with a chat
  line ("X replaces Y: reload to switch") or disable Y first when Y is not `reloadToToggle`. In `fail` and
  `disable` of a replacer, set `pendingReload` on the replaced module (or, when it is not `reloadToToggle`,
  clear `replacedBy` and `sync` it). Tests in `tests/unit/Core/Modules.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-24: An allow list that is "not for" your class hides every aura instead of not counting
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code, against the rule stated in the file's header)
- where: src/Core/AuraFilters.wowlua:335-353 (`filterFor`), 280-299 (`collect`), 364-388 (`groupSpells`);
  src/UI/Auras.wowlua:564, 572-577
- known: no
- what: the header says "An entry or a whole list can be 'not for' classes: for a player of such a class
  it doesn't count". In `filterFor`, an attached allow list makes the allow set exist before the class is
  looked at:
  `if l.kind == "allow" then into = allow or {}; allow = into … end; collect(id, who, into, {})`,
  and `collect` returns at once for an excluded class (`if not l or seen[id] or excludes(l.notFor, class)
  then return end`). The result is an empty allow set, not `nil`. `groupSpells` then returns an empty
  include list (`return sorted(out), nil`, or `out = {}` for a group with its own list), and the aura
  engine shows nothing for an empty include list. The settings let the player set "Not for" on a whole
  list of either kind (src/Units/AuraFilters.wowlua:872, 1179), and plugins can register one.
- why it matters: a player who attaches an allow list marked "not for Priest" to the party frames' buffs
  sees no buffs at all there on a priest, where the rule says the list should be ignored and everything
  shown. The same for an attached allow list whose only content is another list not for the class.
- fix: in `filterFor`, skip a list excluded for the class before choosing `into`
  (`if l and not excludes(l.notFor, who) then …`). Decide and document whether an allow list that is
  merely empty hides everything (it does today). Test in `tests/unit/Core/AuraFilters.test.wowlua`: an
  allow list with `notFor = { "MAGE" }` attached, `filterFor(kind, set, "MAGE")` returns `nil` for allow.

#### CORE-1: The talent tree is still read on every role lookup while no points are spent
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Roles.wowlua:117-127 (`points`), 129-141 (`spec`), 143-156 (`current`)
- known: no
- what: `points()` now returns the cached tree points until a talent event clears them. Two things are
  left. The cache is kept only when `total > 0` ("Nothing spent yet … is read again each time"), so a
  character with no talent points (low level, or just reset) in a group without an assigned role still
  walks every node in `treePoints()` on each `current()`/`spec()` call, which modules make per threat
  update and target change. And a cache hit allocates a new three-entry table per call
  (`return { k.pts[1], k.pts[2], k.pts[3] }, k.total`), although `current()` only needs the best tree.
- why it matters: small; a per-event allocation on the nameplate threat path, and the full walk for
  unspecced characters in a party.
- fix: cache the zero result too (`known = { pts = …, total = 0 }`) and rely on the nine talent events to
  clear it; keep the best tree in the cache and have `current()` read that instead of calling `spec()`.
  `tests/unit/Core/Roles.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-12: A theme with a malformed colour or font entry aborts `themes.apply` half way and drops colour vision
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Themes.wowlua:468-558 (`register` checks token and style names only), 619-737 (`apply`),
  642-654, 667-681
- known: no
- what: `apply` calls `reset()` first, then for each colour `token[1], token[2], token[3] = c[1], c[2], c[3]`
  and `hex(c[1], c[2], c[3])`. `register` validates textures, glyphs, spacing, sizes, radii and the dress
  in detail, but for `colors` only the token names and for `fonts` only the style names; a `colors`
  function's result is not validated at all. A colour entry that is not a table of three numbers, or a
  font entry with a non-number `size`, raises inside `apply` (or in `fonts.refresh`) after `reset()` undid
  colour vision, before `vision.apply`, `draw.reskin`, `draw.repaint` and `SUUUI_THEME_CHANGED`.
- why it matters: one bad plugin theme leaves a colour-blind player without their preset and the UI half
  recoloured; at login the error is caught by `fault.call("Themes", …)`, so it looks like a quiet failure.
- fix: validate colour and font values in `register` (static tables) and per entry in `apply` (skip an
  entry that is not three numbers in 0..1), and run the tail (`vision.apply` onwards) even when the theme
  part fails. `tests/unit/Core/Themes.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-13: Core/Events still mirrors what wowlua:events does itself
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed against the wowlua working tree (`crates/wowlua-stdlib/std/events.wowlua`)
- where: src/Core/Events.wowlua:84-92 (`guarded`), 136-153 (`onUnit`), 155-194 (`off`, `offAll`);
  Docs/wowlua-port-notes.md S1
- known: partly (S1 records the layering, not that it became redundant)
- what: (1) `byOwner` duplicates the stdlib's own owner bookkeeping; `wl.offAll(owner[, name])` exists and
  does what `off` and `offAll` do. (2) `guarded` re-checks `sub.active`, which the stdlib's dispatch
  already checks per handler; the comment about dispatching from a snapshot no longer applies. (3)
  `onUnit` splits the list into pairs and registers each pair separately, but `wl.onUnit` takes any number
  of units and skips duplicates; SuuUI's pairing does not, so `{ "a", "b", "a" }` delivers `a`'s events
  twice. (4) every dispatch nests two `xpcall`s (the stdlib's and `fault.call`).
- why it matters: a small per-event overhead on every listener, and bookkeeping to keep in step with the
  stdlib for no benefit beyond the name-first argument and Fault attribution.
- fix: keep `guarded` only for name-first and Fault; implement `off` as `wl.offAll(owner, name)` and
  `offAll` as `wl.offAll(owner)` through the `Dispatcher` interface with a per-owner counter for `count`;
  pass the whole unit list to `wl.onUnit`. `tests/unit/Core/Events.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-14: Services keep one provider per name; a second provider that leaves takes the service with it
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Services.wowlua:33-38, 57-64
- known: no
- what: `provide` overwrites `self.providers[name]`. `unregister(owner)` removes the entry when the owner
  is the current provider. If A provides "bags", then B provides "bags", then B turns off, the service is
  nil although A is still enabled. `unregister` also emits `SUUUI_SERVICE_CHANGED` while iterating
  `providers` with `pairs`; a listener that calls `provide` for a new name during that adds a key
  mid-traversal.
- why it matters: reachable through CORE-11 (a replacer beside the original) or a plugin that offers a
  built-in service additionally.
- fix: keep a list of providers per name (the last one wins, the previous one returns when it leaves);
  collect the names first in `unregister`, then emit. `tests/unit/Core/Services.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-15: Extend's wrappers allocate per call and lose return values
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Extend.wowlua:237-281 (`wrap`), 222-235 (`base`), 296-308 (`flush`), 378-388 (`each`),
  449-460 (`unregister`)
- known: no
- what: (a) an override wrapper does `local res = { reporter:call(source, instead, this, inner, ...) }` and
  `unpack(res, 2)` on every call: a table per call, and `unpack` stops at the first nil, so an override
  returning `nil, x` loses `x`. (b) the post-hook wrapper returns only four values
  (`local a, b2, c, d = inner(this, ...)`). (c) `ownerName(postOwners[i])` is computed per call. (d) `base`
  caches `{ fn = raw or obj[method] }` even when that is nil, and `wrap` returns silently for a
  non-function, so a hook on a method added later, or on a misspelt name, is ignored for that instance
  for good. (e) `each` runs `fn` on every instance in `made`, including ones still in `queue`; `flush`
  then runs every extender on those again, so an extender registered in the same frame as a queued
  instance runs twice on it. (f) `unregister` runs `undo` for every instance in `made`, including queued
  ones `fn` never saw.
- why it matters: plugins only, but `M:Override` on a unit frame's update method puts a table allocation
  on one of the hottest paths in the addon.
- fix: use a vararg helper (`local function pass(ok, ...) if ok then return ... end end` with a fallback)
  instead of packing; return `inner`'s results through a vararg helper; precompute owner names when
  wrapping; warn when a hooked method is missing on every instance of the kind; in `each`, skip objects
  still in `queue` (or record per extender which objects it ran on, which also fixes f).
  `tests/unit/Core/Extend.test.wowlua`.

#### CORE-16: Core imports upward into UI, SettingsUI and EditMode, and RolePresets hard-codes module settings
- status: partly fixed in a5082e2d (Themes, Init and Modules no longer import UI, SettingsUI or EditMode values: those layers hand their parts over as they load; RolePresets still hard-codes 32 module settings, `setProfileValues` still skips unknown keys silently, and `closestSize` still repeats `closest`)
- severity: low
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/RolePresets.wowlua:34-138, 146-157 (`closestSize`); src/Core/Settings.wowlua:858
  (`setProfileValues`), 124-141 (`closest`)
- known: no
- what: the stated layering is Core → UI → Units, but four Core files import values from the layers above
  (legal only because the uses are inside functions). `RolePresets` lists 32 `namespace.key` pairs of
  seven feature modules (`unitframes`, `castbars`, `cooldowns`, `swingtimer`, `threat`, `party`, `raid`),
  their healer values and their per-size overrides; `setProfileValues` skips a key that no longer exists
  without a word (`defs and defs[key] ~= nil`), so a renamed setting silently drops out of the preset.
  `M:AddToRolePreset` exists for exactly this and no built-in module uses it. `RolePresets.closestSize`
  (146-157) repeats `Settings.closest` (124-141).
- why it matters: the cycle risk grows with every import (a use at load time in a cycle is an error), and
  the preset cannot be checked against the modules it configures.
- fix: have `/UI/Draw` and `/UI/Dress` register their theme steps with Themes at load (or listen for a
  `SUUUI_THEME_APPLYING` message), register the settings window toggle with Init, pass the settings
  registry's and edit mode's release functions into `ModuleRegistry` like the other collaborators; move
  each module's preset values into that module with `self:AddToRolePreset(...)` (extend it with a per-size
  form), and make `setProfileValues` report unknown keys.

- status: open

  with a `__seeded` table naming every namespace), and possibly `charRoles[key]`, `lastRoles[key]` and
  `charData[key][namespace]`. Only `forgetCharData(namespace, key)` removes anything, per module. A
  deleted or renamed character's entries stay for good, and the profile list grows by one per character.

#### CORE-18: Watcher notification and `M:Setting` copy table values each time
- status: open

#### CORE-19: `/suu perf` keeps timing and a once-a-second memory update until stopped by hand
- status: open
- severity: low

- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Perf.wowlua:36-42, 220-270; src/Core/Fault.wowlua:208-217
- known: no
- what: after `/suu perf`, every `fault.call` makes two `debugprofilestop` and two `collectgarbage("count")`

#### CORE-20: `suppress` with `keepParent` never hides a protected frame when called in combat
- status: open

#### CORE-21: `SuuUI.UI` and `SuuUI.Raw.UI` are two hand-kept lists of the same components
- status: open

#### CORE-25: Work built ahead and the lazy data tables are Core internals that feature modules import directly
- status: partly fixed in a5082e2d (BuildAhead and the lazy data handles are exported as SuuUI.BuildAhead and SuuUI.Data, and modules import only the public API; two built-in whole-table reads remain unguarded)
- severity: low
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/AutoQuests.wowlua:57-62 (`dataLevel`: `SuuUI.QuestStarts()`),
  src/Units/FlightMap/Taxi.wowlua:95 (`SuuUI.FlightPaths()`)
- known: no
- what: the rule is that modules in `src/Units` use only the public API. `ahead.schedule` and the
  `LazyData` objects (`Ready`, `Prepare`, `Then`, `Until`) are not exported in `src/Core/API.wowlua` and
  not in `Docs/API.md`, so nine built-in modules import them from Core. The public API offers only the
  whole table: `API.QuestStarts()` and the five others call `:Get()`, which builds whatever is missing in
  one frame (QuestStarts was measured at 3 MB). The built-in modules guard their calls with
  `lazyData.x:Ready()`; a plugin has no way to ask, and some built-in calls are unguarded
  (src/Units/AutoQuests.wowlua:54, src/Units/FlightMap.wowlua:219).
- why it matters: a plugin (or an unguarded built-in path) that reads quest or map data pays the whole
  build in one frame, the hitch the lazy loading was made to remove; and the layering rule now has nine
  exceptions.
- fix: export them: `SuuUI.BuildAhead(key, step)` (or `M:BuildAhead`, see CORE-8) and `SuuUI.Data` with
  `Ready(name)`, `Prepare(name, fn, key)`, `Then(name, fn, key)`; switch the nine modules to those;
  document under the next API version.

#### CORE-26: All 35 built-in themes are built in full at load, whichever one is chosen
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: likely (the tables are confirmed from code; the memory figure is an estimate, measure with `/suu perf`)
- where: src/Core/ThemesRaids.wowlua:45-52 (`glyphs`), 57-84 (`textures`), 1157-1179 (`registerRaids`);
  src/Core/ThemesBuiltin.wowlua:531-538 (`jungleGlyphs`); src/Core/Themes.wowlua:468-558 (`register`)
- known: no
- what: `ThemesBuiltin` registers 14 themes and `ThemesRaids` 21 as the files load. Each raid theme (and
  both Stranglethorn themes) builds a glyph table with one path string per glyph token
  (`out[name] = dir .. "Glyphs\\" .. name .. ".tga"`, 95 names), a texture table of about 20 paths and a
  dress, and `register` validates every entry. That is roughly 2,200 distinct path strings and 70 tables
  kept for the session (an estimated 250-350 KB), for a player who never leaves the default theme.
- why it matters: small beside the 8 MB the lazy data work removed, but it is the same kind of cost at
  every login, and it grows with each theme added.
- fix: let a theme give `glyphs`, `textures` and `dress` as functions worked out in `apply` (as `colors`
  already can be), or register the raid themes as `{ id, name, description, build = fn }` and build one
  when it is applied or previewed.

#### CORE-27: A lazy data step that errors leaves its waiters untold, and Ahead builds a string every frame
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Core/Data.wowlua:70-81 (`Step`), 183-212 (driver); src/Core/Ahead.wowlua:41-59, 92-101
- known: no
- what: `Step` advances and drops the step before running it (`self.nextStep = i + 1; self.steps[i] = nil;
  step(self.value)`). When a step raises under the frame driver, the table is taken off `preparing`
  (`if not ok or not more then table.remove(preparing, 1)`) and `Done` is called only `if ok`, so whoever
  waited through `Prepare`/`Then` is never called, `waitingKeys` keeps their keys, and the remaining steps
  run only if someone calls `Prepare` or `Get` again; the failed step's rows are missing for the session
  while `Ready()` later says true. Separately, `stepOnce` in Ahead builds `"Ahead: " .. job.key` on every
  frame a job runs (Data avoids exactly this with its `sources` cache).
- why it matters: the steps are generated code, so an error is unlikely, but when it happens a window
  that waits for the data (the world map, the professions list) stays empty without a second error.
- fix: in the driver, on `not ok` keep the table in `preparing` so the later steps run and `Done` still
  fires (the Fault log has the error); keep the source string in the Ahead job (`job.source`) when it is
  scheduled. `tests/unit/Core/Data.test.wowlua`, `Ahead.test.wowlua`.

### Fixed since the first pass

- CORE-4 (switching colour vision back to Normal, or changing theme, left the previous glow colours):
  `vision.apply` now runs `syncGlows()` for every mode, Normal included (src/Core/Vision.wowlua:77-94;
  commit e41b8868).

### Withdrawn

- None.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Teardown by hand.** Anything not in `releaseAll` (timers, hooks, anchors, frame scripts, CVars,
  suppressed frames, queued combat work, work built ahead, themes, aura filter lists) is each module's
  responsibility. Sweep `src/Units` for `after(`/`every(`/`hook(`/`ahead.schedule(` whose handle is not
  cancelled or gated in `OnDisable`.
- **Layout settings read through one more step.** Every `get`/`peek` now goes through `isLayout` and
  `layoutAt` (src/Core/Settings.wowlua:301-309). It is a few table lookups, but it is on every settings
  read, including `M:Peek` in event handlers; worth one look in a perf run.
- **A profile's own values and its layouts are two copies of the same settings.** A write goes to both
  (`write`, 442-452); a read comes only from the layout. Anything that edits a profile outside the store's
  `set` (migrations, role presets for a profile not in use, imports) has to treat both, and
  `setProfileValues` without a size writes only the copy that is not read once a layout exists.
- **Whole-table reads of lazy data.** `SuuUI.QuestStarts()` and its siblings build everything on the
  first call; callers outside `WorldMap`, `Professions` and `Collections` should be checked for a
  `Ready()` guard or a `Prepare`.
- **API getters that compute per call:** `SuuUI.Instances(kind)` (collects and sorts), `SuuUI.Commands()`,
  `SuuUI.ListModules()`, `SuuUI.AuraFilters()` (deep copy of every list), `SuuUI.AuraFilterSpells` (walks
  the lists and sorts): fine at configuration time, not in handlers.
- **Reads of another module's settings through `GetModule`** with a typed fallback hide renamed keys
  (27 call sites; CORE-9).
- **Combat rules are per call site, not per layer.** Role switching and the screen-size switch defer, role
  presets refuse, manual profile and layout changes do neither (CORE-6).
- **Docs drift.** `Docs/wowlua-port-notes.md` S1 describes a stdlib that dispatched from a snapshot; the
  current stdlib does not, so the reasons given there for SuuUI's own event layer are out of date.

## Area: EditMode and the settings window


### Coverage
