Diffs `4c6ea485..36f5f407` read in full for every file of the area that changed: `src/EditMode/EditMode.wowlua`, `src/EditMode/LayoutCheck.wowlua`, `src/SettingsUI/Sections.wowlua`, `src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua`, `src/UI/Controls.wowlua`, `src/UI/FilterMenu.wowlua`, `src/UI/Inputs.wowlua`, `src/UI/KeybindMode.wowlua`, `src/UI/Select.wowlua`, `src/UI/SettingRow.wowlua`, `src/UI/SettingsMatrix.wowlua`. Unchanged since the first pass: `src/SettingsUI/GameMenu.wowlua`, `src/SettingsUI/Registry.wowlua`, `src/UI/Pickers.wowlua`.

NEW files read beyond the diffs: `src/UI/FilterMenu.wowlua` 84-686 (all code), `src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua` 150-550 and 786-1333, `src/SettingsUI/Sections.wowlua` 205-354, 395-484, 517-952, `src/EditMode/LayoutCheck.wowlua` 34-196, and in `src/EditMode/EditMode.wowlua`, `src/UI/SettingRow.wowlua`, `src/UI/Select.wowlua`, `src/UI/Inputs.wowlua`, `src/UI/KeybindMode.wowlua` the ranges each finding cites.

Read to check claims: `src/UI/Draw.wowlua` (layout/onLayout/relayout, glyph, skin, relayoutPixels), `src/Core/Themes.wowlua` (when `draw.relayout` runs), `src/Core/Root.wowlua`, `src/Core/Settings.wowlua` (layouts per screen size, getTable), `src/Core/Modules.wowlua`, `src/Core/API.wowlua` (imports), `src/SettingsUI/Registry.wowlua` (forOwner, register).

Not done: the unchanged parts of the larger files were not read a second time start to end (the first pass read them in full; the diff shows they did not change). Nothing was run.

### Summary

Between 0.6.0-beta.1 and 0.17.0 this area changed little in behaviour: most of the diff is theme support (spacing and sizes read when laid out through `draw.layout`, glyphs and textures by token), a "range" group and a group action button in `FilterMenu`, three account-wide colour rows and a "Screen sizes" group in the settings, a preview that scales down to fit, and `LayoutCheck` reading each screen size's own layout.

None of the 17 first-pass findings was fixed; all are still in the code, three in a changed form. The theme work adds one new cause for the page leak (a theme with other spacing drops every built page) and makes a previously hypothetical listener leak real (SET-18).

Biggest problems on 0.17.0, unchanged: `FilterMenu`'s panel can hold the keyboard in combat (SET-1, needs a probe); the settings window refreshes every row of every built page on any setting change (SET-2) and overwrites text being typed (SET-3); pages are dropped and built again instead of reused (SET-4); `FilterMenu`'s panel is on `UIParent` at another scale (SET-5); the first search keystroke builds every page (SET-6); Core imports EditMode and SettingsUI (SET-7).

### Findings

#### SET-1: FilterMenu's panel swallows all keyboard input while open in combat
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe (the code path is certain; the probe is whether, on Forever, a frame with `EnableKeyboard(true)` consumes keys when `SetPropagateKeyboardInput(true)` was not called, and whether `SetPropagateKeyboardInput`/`EnableKeyboard` are blocked in combat)
- status: fixed in db302207 (the panel goes through UI/Dismiss: keys pass on at rest, the keyboard is taken only out of combat and let go on PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED; the probe confirms the design: in combat lockdown `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` is refused and `EnableKeyboard` allowed)
- probe (2026-11-15, build 70888): `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` is refused in combat lockdown on an addon's own frame, `EnableKeyboard` is allowed (tried on a hidden frame of the probe's own in the first fight). So the finding was real: a handler that waits for the fight to call `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` cannot, and UI/Dismiss's design (let go before the lockdown, call nothing during it) is the one that works. The fix no longer waits on the game for this point.
- where: src/UI/FilterMenu.wowlua:633-645 (Build), 649-664 (Open), 666-681 (Close)
- known: no
- what: the panel enables the keyboard and decides propagation per key, but returns before deciding when in combat:
  ```
  p:EnableKeyboard(true)
  p:SetScript("OnKeyDown", function(panel, key: string)
      if InCombatLockdown() then
          return
      end
      if key == "ESCAPE" then
          panel:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(false)
          menu:Close()
      else
          panel:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(true)
      end
  end)
  ```
  The propagate flag keeps whatever it was last set to. It is `false` on a freshly built panel (a frame's default; and the panel is built again after every theme change and every `SetGroups`) and after every close by Esc. `Open()` and `Close()` do not touch the flag.
- why it matters: open a filter menu (world map "Map filters", professions, the auction house) during combat for the first time since it was built, or after having closed it with Esc: the panel is shown with the keyboard enabled and propagation off, the handler returns early, so every key (abilities, movement, Esc) is consumed until the player clicks outside. That is lost input in a fight.
- fix: do not hold the keyboard in combat. In `Open()` call `p:EnableKeyboard(not InCombatLockdown())`; on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` call `EnableKeyboard(false)` on the open menu's panel (one `events.onGame` next to the theme listener at line 209, using `openMenu`), or close it. Call `p:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(true)` once in `Build()` (out of combat) and again in `Close()` when not in lockdown, so a stale `false` is never left. Probe first with `/suu probe` what Forever allows in combat for the two calls. Test: tests/unit/UI/FilterMenu.test.wowlua (open in combat after an Esc close: the panel does not have the keyboard).

#### SET-2: Every setting change refreshes and re-lays-out every row of every built page
- severity: medium (high once a search has built all pages)
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the frame cost itself needs measuring in game
- status: open
- where: src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:1038-1062 (refreshNow/refreshAll), 382-400 (BoundRow.Refresh), 489-503
  (SettingsPage.Refresh), 1208-1214; src/UI/SettingRow.wowlua:155-164 (Relayout), 232-250 (SetModified,
  SetDisabled)
- known: no
- what: `SUUUI_SETTING_CHANGED` (any namespace, any key, including runtime writes by modules) → `refreshAll` → next frame `refreshNow`:
  ```
  for _, page in pairs(pages) do
      page:Refresh()
  end
  ```
  for every page ever built, shown or not. Per row, `BoundRow.Refresh` calls `get()` (a `settings.get` copy), re-runs `options` functions and `SetOptions`, re-runs `description` and `disabled` functions, then `self:SetDisabled(...)` and `self:SetModified(...)`. `SettingRow.SetDisabled` ends in `self:SetModified(self.modified)`, and `SetModified` always calls `Relayout()`, which runs `Arrange()` (several `ClearAllPoints`/`SetPoint`, `GetStringHeight`, `SetHeight`) and, once per row per frame, queues another `Arrange` through `after(0)` with a new closure. So one refresh is two `Arrange` now, one more next frame and one timer per row, changed or not.
- why it matters: the sources hold roughly 300 static rows plus generated ones (about 40 module switches). `search()` builds every page on the first keystroke (Window.wowlua:1022-1026) and they stay built. From then on, dragging a live slider (one write per step, so a full refresh per frame), or any module writing a setting while the window is open, re-reads every setting and re-anchors over a thousand regions per frame.
- fix: (1) in `refreshNow`, refresh only pages whose frame is shown and mark the others dirty per page (a `dirty` field on `SettingsPage`); refresh a dirty page in `applyView` when it becomes visible. (2) Pass the changed namespace and key through (`refreshAll(namespace, key)` from the message's arguments) and, for rows bound to a plain `namespace` + `key` without `get`/`disabled`/function `options`/function `description`, skip rows of other keys; keep the full refresh for the others. (3) In `SettingRow.SetModified` and `SetDisabled`, return early when the state and the reason text did not change, so an unchanged row does no layout and queues no timer. Tests: tests/unit/SettingsUI/Window.test.wowlua (a hidden page is not refreshed until shown), tests/unit/UI/SettingRow.test.wowlua (no relayout when nothing changed).

#### SET-3: A refresh overwrites what the player is typing in a text field or stepper
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:240-253 (text), 224-239 (stepper), 382-387; src/UI/Inputs.wowlua:799-804
  (TextField.SetValue), 675-678 (Stepper.SetValue), 103-106 (showText)
- known: no
- what: `BoundRow.Refresh` always does `self.ctl.show(get())`; for a text row that is `f:SetValue(...)` → `showText(self.edit, self.value)` → `e:SetText(value); e:SetCursorPosition(0)`, with no check for focus. `Stepper.SetValue` does the same. `redrawOnShow` (Inputs.wowlua:108-117) and edit mode's `showPosition` (EditMode.wowlua:314-319) both guard on `HasFocus()`, and FilterMenu's new range boxes are only set "where they read otherwise" (FilterMenu.wowlua:413-424); these two are not guarded.
- why it matters: a text or stepper row writes on Enter or focus lost. While the player types, any `SUUUI_SETTING_CHANGED` (a module's runtime write, a role-based profile switch, a layout switch after a resolution change) triggers the window's refresh one frame later and replaces the half-typed text with the saved value, cursor at 0.
- fix: in `TextField.SetValue` and `Stepper.SetValue`, when `self.edit:HasFocus()` and the new value equals `self.value`, do nothing; or in `BoundRow.Refresh` skip `ctl.show` for a control whose edit box has focus (give `Control` an optional `busy(): boolean`). Tests: tests/unit/UI/Inputs.test.wowlua and tests/unit/SettingsUI/Window.test.wowlua (focus a text row, change another setting, advance a frame: the typed text stays).

#### SET-4: Pages are dropped and built again, never reused: on a section re-registered and now on a theme with other spacing
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:1245-1271 (`SUUUI_SETTINGS_SECTIONS_CHANGED`), 1272-1296
  (`draw.onLayout`), 432-462 (SettingsPage constructor), 480-487 (Clear);
  src/SettingsUI/Registry.wowlua:132-168; src/UI/Draw.wowlua:884-907, 926-946
- known: no
- what: two handlers drop pages with
  ```
  f.pagesStack:Remove(page.frame)
  page.frame:Hide()
  pages[id] = nil
  ```
  (a) the sections handler, when `page.section ~= registry.get(id)`: `registry.register` always makes a new `Section` table, so a module turned off and on always gets a new page. Each register and each unregister emits its own message, so one module toggle runs the handler twice (`buildNav`, sorted `registry.list()` calls, and with a search active `getPage` for every section, here without the `fault.call` that `search()` uses). (b) new: the `draw.onLayout(f, …)` handler drops every page when a theme's spacing or sizes change (`Themes.wowlua:707-709`: `draw.relayout()` when the geometry differs), and builds the open one again (all of them while a search is active). `SettingsPage.Clear()` (the Modules page, on every `SUUUI_MODULE_REGISTERED`) leaves its groups behind the same way. Frames cannot be freed, so each dropped page stays in memory with its rows, controls and select popovers. They also stay in Draw's `layouts` table (weak keys, but each closure holds its frame, so the entries are never collected): every later `draw.relayout()` sorts and runs the dead pages' layout functions too, and Draw's repaint keeps painting their textures.
- why it matters: the window is where modules are toggled and where a theme is picked; a role-based profile switch that toggles several modules does it in bulk. After one search every page is built (SET-6), so each toggle leaks a page and each switch between two themes of different spacing leaks all of them (about 350 rows) and makes every following theme change slower.
- fix: (1) sections: store the `SectionDef` on the `Section` (`s.def = def` in `registry.register`) and in the handler keep the page when `page.section.def == new.def` (modules pass the same literal on each enable): rebind `page.section` to the new Section instead of dropping; coalesce the handler to once per frame (`after(0)` with a flag) so an unregister/register pair is handled once; wrap its `getPage` calls in `fault.call` as `search()` does. (2) theme: do not drop pages; the rows already keep their own layout (`draw.layout` in `SettingRow`, `TextField`, `Select`), the stacks take token gaps (`gap = "space-7"`), so what is missing is only the page width (`contentW()`/`wideW()`) and each row's `Relayout()`: add `SettingsPage:Resize()` that sets the width on the frame, title, groups and rows and calls their `Relayout()`, and call it from the `onLayout` handler. Test: tests/unit/SettingsUI/Window.test.wowlua (toggle a module twice, and apply a theme with other spacing: `pages[id].frame` is the same object; the number of children of `content.child` does not grow).

#### SET-5: FilterMenu's panel is parented to UIParent, so it is drawn at UIParent's scale, not SuuUI's
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (confirm with a screenshot at a UI scale where the two differ)
- status: fixed in db302207 (the filter panel is made under SuuUI's root, at its scale)
- where: src/UI/FilterMenu.wowlua:436 (`FilterPanel.new(nil, UIParent)`), 658 (anchored to the field); compare src/UI/Select.wowlua:712 (`panel(root, …)`), src/UI/Pickers.wowlua:151, src/Core/Root.wowlua:20-22 (`root:SetIgnoreParentScale(true)`), 58-66 (scale = pixel-perfect × `ui.scale`)
- known: no
- what: SuuUI's root ignores its parent's scale and runs at pixel-perfect scale times `ui.scale`. Select's list and the anchor popover are children of `root`. The filter panel is a child of `UIParent`, so its 292 px width, 24 px chips, 72 px range boxes, text and paddings are in UIParent units.
- why it matters: on a 1440p screen the root's scale is about 0.53 while UIParent's is usually 0.64 to 1, so the panel is 1.2 to 1.9 times larger than its own field and every other SuuUI control, and it ignores Appearance › Scale. The world map, professions and auction house windows show it.
- fix: create the panel under `root` (`import root from "/Core/Root"`, as Select does), keep strata `FULLSCREEN_DIALOG` and the level above the catcher. Test: tests/unit/UI/FilterMenu.test.wowlua (`panel:GetEffectiveScale() == menu:GetEffectiveScale()`).

#### SET-6: The first search keystroke builds every section's page in one frame
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: likely (the work is certain; the length of the hitch needs measuring)
- status: open
- where: src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:1018-1031 (`search`); 508-529 (Filter)
- known: no
- what: `search()` calls `getPage(section)` for every listed section that has no page yet, synchronously inside the search box's `OnTextChanged`. A page creates a frame per row plus label, description, lock, reset button, rule and the control. The same loop runs in the two handlers at 1260-1264 and 1287-1291 while a search is active.
- why it matters: the first letter typed into "Search settings" creates on the order of 350 rows (several thousand regions) before the letter appears: a visible freeze on a slower machine. It also feeds SET-2 and SET-4.
- fix: search the definitions, not the frames. `Filter` only needs `section.label`, `group.title/description` and `row.label/description`, all in the registry's data (`section.groups` and `registry.merged(id)`); only sections with `build` (Modules) need a page to be searched. Add a `matches(section, q)` over the definitions and build a page only for sections with a hit. Test: tests/unit/SettingsUI/Window.test.wowlua (a search with one hit builds one page).

#### SET-7: Layer inversions around edit mode, the settings registry and keybind mode
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed in a5082e2d (Modules and Init no longer import the layers above, keybind mode closes the others through Core/Modes, and movers declare apartFrom/anchorOnly with Root's scale and size rules exported for the layout check; Core/API still imports EditMode and SettingsUI, and edit mode and the settings window still do not close keybind mode)
- where: src/Core/API.wowlua:28-30; src/Core/Modes.wowlua:1-21 (only keybind mode uses it to close the
  others); src/EditMode/EditMode.wowlua:1095-1118 (`enter`)
- known: no
- what: (a) Core (`Modules`, `API`) imports `/SettingsUI/Registry`, `/SettingsUI/Window` and `/EditMode/EditMode`, which import `UI`, which imports Core: the order Core → UI → Units does not hold, and it loads only because the uses are inside functions. (b) `UI/KeybindMode` imports `/EditMode/EditMode` and `/SettingsUI/Window` to close them on enter, while `editMode.enter()` closes neither keybind mode nor the settings window: the exclusion between the three modes is one-sided and lives in the lowest of the three files. (c) `LayoutCheck` hardcodes other modules' setting ids (`APART`: `party.position`/`raid.position`, `flightmap.timerPosition`/`timeline.position`; `ANCHOR_ONLY`: `tooltips.position`, `bags.position`, `bags.bankPosition`, `loot.position`), so a renamed key or a plugin's mover silently falls out of the rules, and it re-implements Root's automatic scale rule (`rootSize`, lines 62-69, against `autoScale` in src/Core/Root.wowlua:43-49) and Root's size name (`("%dx%d"):format(W + 0.5, H + 0.5)` at line 127 against `layoutSize()` in Root.wowlua:83-87).
- why it matters: `releaseAll`'s list in Core grows with every UI-level registry; a mode added later must know to import the other two; the layout check reports false overlaps for any new pair of frames that never show together, and reads the wrong layout if Root's size naming ever changes.
- fix: (a) give Core an owner-release hook list (`modules.onRelease(fn)`); `EditMode` and `SettingsUI/Registry` register their `unregister` there, and `Module:RegisterMover/RegisterSettings` are attached from those files (or through `/Core/Extend`/`Services`). (b) one "exclusive mode" helper in Core (`modes.enter(name, exitFn)` exits the others), used by edit mode, keybind mode and the settings window; move `KeybindMode` out of `UI/` next to `EditMode`. (c) add `MoverOptions.anchorOnly` and `MoverOptions.apartFrom` so modules declare these themselves, carry them in `MoverInfo`, and export `autoScaleFor(height)` and `layoutSizeFor(w, h, scale)` from `/Core/Root` for `LayoutCheck`. Document new options in Docs/API.md.

#### SET-8: Dragging a mover re-syncs every other mover's outline on every frame
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/EditMode/EditMode.wowlua:466-492 (StartDrag's OnUpdate), 334-369 (sync), 153-164 (positionOf),
  273-278 (settingsSection); src/SettingsUI/Registry.wowlua:192-203 (forOwner walks `list()`)
- known: no
- what: while a drag runs, `OnUpdate` calls `sync(other)` for every shown overlay. `sync` does `positionOf` (a `settings.getTable` copy plus a new Position table), `("%d × %d"):format`, `m.label .. …`, two `SetValue`, `paintFill`, `SetColor`, and for the selected one `showPosition` and `settingsSection` → `registry.forOwner` → `registry.list()` (builds and sorts all sections).
- why it matters: with about 40 movers that is 40 copies, 40 formatted strings and 80 tables per frame for the length of the drag, only to follow the few frames that move with the dragged one (bars attached to the dock).
- fix: in the drag's `OnUpdate`, only reposition outlines: a `follow(m)` that reads `rect(m.frame)` and sets the overlay's point and size when the rectangle changed (keep the last l, b, w, h on the overlay); leave tag, colour, hidden state and toolbar to `sync` at drag stop. Cache `settingsSection(m)` per mover until `SUUUI_SETTINGS_SECTIONS_CHANGED`. Test: tests/unit/EditMode/EditMode.test.wowlua (outlines of attached frames still follow a drag).

#### SET-9: The edit panel's Snap switch and Grid size slider do not follow the settings
- severity: low
- category: bug

- status: open
- where: src/EditMode/EditMode.wowlua:657-677 (built once from the values at that time), 744-753 (Place),

- known: no

#### SET-10: The drawn grid and the snap grid disagree for edge-anchored frames
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code, by arithmetic)
- status: open
- where: src/EditMode/EditMode.wowlua:243-249 (snap), 495-512 (StopDrag), 578-584 (drawGrid), 210-225
  (anchorFor)
- known: no
- what: grid lines run out from the centre (`for x = W / 2 % g, W, g do`), but a drop snaps the offset from the frame's anchor (`save(mv, point, snap(x), snap(y))`), which for a LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM anchor is a distance from that screen edge. The two coincide only when `W / 2` (and `H / 2`) is a multiple of the grid size.
- why it matters: on a 2560 × 1440 root with grid 12, 24 or 28 (1280 % 24 = 8, 720 % 28 = 20), or on 3440 wide with grid 16 or 32 (1720 % 32 = 24), a frame in the left or right third snaps between the lines the player sees. A centre-anchored frame of odd width lands on half pixels because its centre, not its edge, is snapped.
- fix: snap in screen coordinates on the drawn grid, then convert: snap the dropped rectangle's `l` and `b` to `W / 2 + k * g` and `H / 2 + k * g`, call `anchorFor` with the snapped rectangle and store the offsets rounded to integers, not snapped again. Test: tests/unit/EditMode/EditMode.test.wowlua (a drop in the left third at grid 24 on a 2560 root lands on a grid line).

#### SET-11: `cond and v or nil` drops a `false` value in Select.SetValue and FilterMenu.Draw
- severity: low

- known: no

- fix: write both as `if type(v) ~= "table" then … = v else … = nil end`. Tests: tests/unit/UI/Select.test.wowlua, tests/unit/UI/FilterMenu.test.wowlua (value `false` is shown as chosen).

#### SET-14: Slider values carry float noise into the profile
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: likely
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Inputs.wowlua:402-407 (snap), 507-516; compare 658-673 (Stepper.Clamp)
- known: no
- what: the slider's `snap` returns `min + math.floor((v - min) / step + 0.5) * step` unrounded; `Stepper.Clamp` rounds the same expression to four decimals ("no float noise (0.1 steps make 0.30000000000000004)"). Settings stores a value unless it equals the default, and "is default" means nothing stored.
- why it matters: a slider with a fractional step (five rows use one: 0.05 in src/SettingsUI/Sections.wowlua:72 and src/Units/MicroBags.wowlua:119, 0.01 in PartyFrames and RaidFrames) can produce a value one bit off the literal default; dragged back to the default it is then not equal, so it is stored, the row keeps its "changed" diamond and counts in "n changed", and the saved variables carry the noise.
- fix: round in the slider's `snap` as `Stepper.Clamp` does (one shared helper `roundStep(v, min, step)` in Inputs.wowlua). Test: tests/unit/UI/Inputs.test.wowlua (min 0.5, step 0.05, and min 0, step 0.01: every stop equals `tonumber(("%.4f"):format(v))`).

- why it matters: for long lists (spells, sounds, fonts, profiles: hundreds of options) each wheel notch does hundreds of measurements to show ten rows.
- fix: compute the list width in `SetOptions` (and when the theme changes), store it, and let `Refresh` only place rows. Test: tests/unit/UI/Select.test.wowlua (the width is unchanged after scrolling; options changed → new width).

#### SET-16: Smaller gaps in edit mode and the layout check
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/EditMode/EditMode.wowlua:55-57, 153-164, 168-180 (`rel` dead in `place`); 1033-1070 (nudge);
  717-730 (Reset all); 1261-1273 (SUUUI_ROOT_SCALED); src/EditMode/LayoutCheck.wowlua:61-72 (place), 84-110
  (framesOf), 113-125
- known: no
- what:
  - `Position.rel` is documented ("the frame's own point when it differs") and read by `positionOf`, but `place()` always does `m.frame:SetPoint(pos.point, root, pos.point, pos.x, pos.y)` and `LayoutCheck.place` ignores it too: a dead field.
  - Arrow-key nudges save `pos.x + nudge[1] * step` without the screen range that typed values get (`range(point, w, h)` in `showPosition`), so a frame can be nudged off screen.
  - "Reset all" in the panel resets every mover's position on one click, beside "Done"; every other destructive button in this area arms first ("Click again to reset").
  - `SUUUI_ROOT_SCALED` redraws the grid but does not `sync` the outlines; a scale or resolution change while edit mode is open (which now also switches to that size's layout, Root.wowlua:91-103) leaves outlines at the old rectangles for frames whose setting did not change.
  - New: `LayoutCheck.issuesOn` takes each screen size's own position (`settings.valueAtSize`), but `framesOf` decides once, from the layout in use, which frames take part (`not pos.hidden`) and how large they are (`m.frame:GetSize()`). A frame hidden in the layout in use is skipped for every size, one hidden only in another size's layout is checked there, and the party and raid frames (laid out per screen size) are checked at every size with the size they have now.
- fix: drop `rel` from `Position`/`positionOf` (or honour it in `place` and `LayoutCheck.place`); clamp nudges with `range(pos.point, w, h)`; arm "Reset all" like `ResetSection` (Window.wowlua:788-809); in the `SUUUI_ROOT_SCALED` handler (and on `SUUUI_LAYOUT_CHANGED`) `sync` every shown overlay on the next frame while active; in `issuesOn` read `hidden` from the position at that size and say in the report's first line that sizes are those of the layout in use. Tests: tests/unit/EditMode/EditMode.test.wowlua, tests/unit/EditMode/LayoutCheck.test.wowlua.

#### SET-17: Smaller gaps in the settings controls
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:174-182, 388-390 (segmented options); src/UI/FilterMenu.wowlua:200-215,
  359-365 (panel dropped); src/SettingsUI/Sections.wowlua:147-150, 168-171, 194-197, 240-243;
  src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:1150, 1172-1191 (profile string version); 999-1016, 1261-1265, 1288-1292 (page
  build errors)
- known: no
- what:
  - A `segmented` row evaluates `options` once (`options = nothing` in its `Control`), so `options = function` (allowed by `RowDef`, re-read for `select`) is stale for segmented rows, including each option's `disabled`/`reason`.
  - `FilterMenu` sets `m.panel = nil` for every menu on every `SUUUI_THEME_CHANGED` and in `SetGroups`; the old panel (a full frame tree, now with text fields and buttons) is left behind each time. `SUUUI_THEME_CHANGED` fires on every `themes.apply()`, which the settings rows Health colour, NPC reaction colours, Cast bar colour and Colours (colour vision) call on each change, not only when a theme is picked. `Controls.wowlua` avoids the same work for its badges by comparing the text style it was measured in (`badgeStyle()`).

  - `show()` builds the page without `fault.call` (line 1007), as do the two handlers' `getPage` calls; a section whose `build` throws raises from the nav click every time, and each attempt leaves a new half-built page frame under `content.child` (the page is stored only after the constructor returns).
- fix: give Segmented a `SetOptions` (or build the control again when the option list changed) and call it from `BoundRow.Refresh`; in FilterMenu's theme listener drop the panel only when the styles and spacing it was built with changed (a key of `T.type.caption`, `T.type.label`, `T.type.body` and the `S` values used, as `badgeStyle()` does), and for `SetGroups` hide and reuse; check `v` in `doImport` (refuse a newer one with a clear line); build pages through `fault.call` in `show()` and the handlers, and show an error line instead of the page. Tests: tests/unit/SettingsUI/Window.test.wowlua, tests/unit/UI/FilterMenu.test.wowlua (a theme change that keeps the text styles keeps `menu.panel`).

#### SET-18: Custom controls and the Modules page keep their listeners when their page is dropped
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/SettingsUI/Sections.wowlua:431-452 (PickAndAct: three `events.on(…, self)`), 490-504
  (LayoutInUse: two), 947-956 (Modules page); src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:1272-1296
- known: no
- what: these controls subscribe with themselves (or the page) as owner and nothing ever calls `events.offAll` for them:
  ```
  build = function(page: registry.Page)
      buildModules(page)
      events.on(
          "SUUUI_MODULE_REGISTERED",
          function()
              buildModules(page)
          end,
          page
      )
  end,
  ```
  Until 0.17.0 the Profiles and Modules pages were built once per session. Now the `draw.onLayout` handler drops every page when a theme changes spacing or sizes and builds them again, so each such theme change leaves the old Profiles page's five controls (four `PickAndAct`, one `LayoutInUse`: 14 listeners) and the old Modules page's listener registered next to the new ones.
- why it matters: after n theme changes with other spacing, each `SUUUI_PROFILE_CHANGED`, `SUUUI_PROFILES_CHANGED` and `SUUUI_LAYOUT_CHANGED` refreshes n dead sets of selects (`SetOptions`, `SetValue`), and each `SUUUI_MODULE_REGISTERED` runs `buildModules` on n dead pages: `page:Clear()` and about 45 new rows of frames per dead page, never shown. The cost grows for the session; nothing visible breaks.
- fix: give pages a teardown. In `SettingsPage`, keep a list of owners to release (`page:Own(owner)`; the page itself is one) and a `Release()` that calls `events.offAll(owner)` for each; call `page:Release()` wherever a page is dropped (the two handlers in Window.wowlua:1247-1253 and 1276-1280). `buildControl`'s custom branch (Window.wowlua:268-278) can register the built frame as an owner of its page, so `PickAndAct` and `LayoutInUse` need no change. With SET-4's fix (pages kept on a theme change) the leak goes away for this path, but the teardown is still right for a section that is re-registered. Test: tests/unit/SettingsUI/Window.test.wowlua (drop and rebuild the Profiles page, emit `SUUUI_PROFILES_CHANGED`: only one set of controls refreshes; count listeners through the events module's test access).

### Fixed since the first pass

None. No commit between `4c6ea485` and `36f5f407` addresses any of SET-1 to SET-17.

### Withdrawn

None. One detail of SET-2 is corrected above: the `after(0)` in `SettingRow.Relayout` is guarded by `relayoutQueued`, so it is one timer per row per frame, not one per call.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Keyboard frames and combat** (SET-1): `EnableKeyboard(true)` appears in `src/UI/FilterMenu.wowlua:634`, `src/UI/Panel.wowlua:571`, `src/UI/ContextMenu.wowlua:105`, `src/UI/KeybindMode.wowlua:262`, `src/EditMode/EditMode.wowlua:1006`. Edit mode and keybind mode close on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`; the other three should be checked for the same stale-propagation case.
- **Popovers parented to `UIParent` instead of `root`** (SET-5) get the wrong scale. Sweep `CreateFrame(…, UIParent)` and `.new(nil, UIParent)` in `src/UI` and `src/Units` for frames with a size of their own.
- **"Set to nil and build again" for frames** (SET-4, SET-17): pages, FilterMenu panels, `SettingsPage.Clear`. With 0.17.0's themes, anything that rebuilds on `SUUUI_THEME_CHANGED` or in a `draw.onLayout` handler leaks per theme change, and the dead frames stay in Draw's `layouts`, paint and skin tables (weak keys do not help: the kept closures hold their frame). Sweep `draw.onLayout(` and `SUUUI_THEME_CHANGED` listeners that create frames.
- **`SUUUI_THEME_CHANGED` is not only "a theme was picked"**: `themes.apply()` runs for colour vision, health colour, NPC colours and cast colour too. Listeners that measure or rebuild should compare what they depend on (as `Controls.wowlua`'s `badgeStyle()` does) before doing work.
- **Listeners owned by a frame that is later dropped** (SET-18): `events.on(…, self)` inside a widget constructor with no matching `offAll`. Sweep widget classes in `src/UI` and window bodies for `events.on(` with `self` as owner where the widget can be rebuilt.
- **Setters that always re-layout** (SET-2): `SettingRow.SetModified`/`SetDisabled`, `SettingsGroup.Relayout`; the `Relayout()` + `after(0)` pair makes every "refresh all" expensive.
- **`x and v or nil` with boolean values** (SET-11): same family as the `and` truncation pitfall; grep `and v or nil` / `and value or nil` where the value may be `false`.
- **Unrounded step arithmetic** (SET-14): any other place that stores `min + n * step` for fractional steps.
- **Core importing higher layers** (SET-7): `Core/Modules` and `Core/API` import `EditMode`, `SettingsUI` and `UI/*`.
- **Text fields refreshed while focused** (SET-3): any window that calls `TextField:SetValue`/`Stepper:SetValue` from a data refresh has the same risk; FilterMenu's range boxes show the guard to copy.

## Area: UI primitives


All file:line references are for the 0.17.0 export (NEW), repo-relative.

### Coverage

First-pass findings re-checked on NEW: all 22 (UIP-1 to UIP-22).

Read in full in NEW: `src/UI/Draw.wowlua` (1,695 lines), `Dress.wowlua` (386),
`Layout.wowlua` (571), `Panel.wowlua` (1,104), `WindowSkin.wowlua` (985),
`Reskin.wowlua` (1,920), `Notification.wowlua` (1,143).

Read as diff (`git diff 4c6ea485 36f5f407`) plus the surrounding NEW code:
`Alert`, `Bar`, `ContextMenu`, `MapPin`, `Stage`, `TabMarker`, `Tooltip`.

Unchanged between the two commits (not in the diff; the first-pass lines
were re-read in NEW where a finding depends on them): `Text`, `Icon`,
`Visibility`, `LoadingMark`, `Crest`.

Read in part to check claims: `src/Core/Fonts.wowlua`, `Core/Tokens.wowlua`
(text style sizes, `gilt-text`, the `glow` texture token), `Core/Themes.wowlua`
(`apply`), `Core/ThemesBuiltin.wowlua` and `ThemesRaids.wowlua` (which dress
kinds have motes and sway), `Core/Motion.wowlua`, and the callers in
`Units/MicroMenu`, `ObjectiveTracker`, `Notifications`, `Talents`,
`CooldownManager`, `Chat`, `Welcome`, `UI/FilterMenu`, `UI/UnitFrame`.

Not done: nothing was run. Blizzard's Forever UI source was not consulted,
so what depends on ScrollBox, CallbackRegistry or keyboard propagation
behaviour stays `likely` or `needs in-game probe`. The callers of `layout.stack` were not surveyed for
the risk noted under "Cross-cutting observations" (pinned containers).

### Summary

0.17.0 fixed the cheap-to-fix performance items of this area: `Draw.keep`
now returns early for an unchanged paint, `Stack:Arrange` keeps its last
arrangement, `MapPin:SetData` skips unchanged data, borders are held per
frame (so they follow a scale change), and a ScrollBox's re-skin is
coalesced to one pass a frame inside a time budget.

What remains:

- The behavioural bugs of the first pass are all still there, unchanged:
  the non-idempotent text pass in `Reskin` (UIP-2), stale notification
  buttons (UIP-3), `Visibility` without a release (UIP-4), the Esc
  handling copies (UIP-5), the single modal shade (UIP-9).
- The ScrollBox re-skin still restyles every row on every update, and its
  drains can overlap, so the per-frame budget is not a cap while scrolling
  (UIP-1, changed).
- New code: `Dress` creates new animation groups on every dressing and
  never reuses them, and re-dresses on every size change of a frame with
  motes (UIP-23). Two smaller things in the new parts of `Draw` (UIP-24,
  UIP-25).
- `Draw` grew from 550 to 1,695 lines and now holds seven registries
  (paints, skins, repeats, glyphs, patterns, borders, dividers/ornaments);
  with `Reskin` (1,920) it is the second file that needs cutting (UIP-22).

Modules that skin Blizzard windows and tooltips are `reloadToToggle`, so the
missing "unskin" in `skinWindow`, `reskin*` and `skinTooltip` is still not
reported as a bug.

### Findings

#### UIP-2: `reskinText` is not idempotent: a second pass changes the font the first pass chose
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed on 2026-11-16 (branch `high-perf`; UI/Reskin/Pass: each text's style, and the size and font object the game had given it, are remembered on its skin; a later pass sets nothing on a text that still shows its style and colour, and decides anew only when the game put a font of its own on since. Titles keep the header face and their theme colour, numbers the tabular face, captions their size, through repeated passes and a theme change)
- where: src/UI/Reskin/Pass.wowlua:111-149 (`reskinText`); src/Core/Fonts.wowlua:14, 90-91;
  src/Core/Tokens.wowlua:679-684, 127
- known: no
- what: the style is chosen from the text's current font:
  ```
  elseif not long and (size >= 14 or foName:find("Med") or foName:find("Large")) then
      fonts.apply(fs, "header")
      draw.paint(fs, "gilt-text")
  else
      ...
      fonts.apply(fs, foName:find("Number") and "numeric" or (size < 11 and "caption" or (long and "body" or "label")))
      if token then draw.paint(fs, token) elseif r then fs:SetTextColor(r, g, b) end
  ```
  After the first pass the text carries SuuUI's font object, so on the next pass `foName` is `SuuUIFont_header` / `SuuUIFont_numeric` / `SuuUIFont_caption` and `size` is SuuUI's:
  - a big title (first pass: `header`, gilt-text) now has size 13 and no "Med"/"Large" in its font name, so it takes the else branch: `fonts.apply(fs, "label")`; gilt-text matches none of `textColor`'s cases (1284-1304) and `s.token` was never set in the header branches, so `fs:SetTextColor(r, g, b)` sets it raw, which also lets its paint go (no theme follow);
  - a number (first pass: `numeric`) no longer has "Number" in its font name: becomes `label`;
  - small text (first pass: `caption`, size 11) is no longer `< 11`: becomes `label` (12 px).
  Only the colour token is remembered between passes (`s.token`, 1342-1346); the style is not.
- why it matters: passes repeat by design: every ScrollBox update re-skins its rows (UIP-1), `reskin()`/`reskinPart()` are called again on pane shows and refreshes by `Units/Windows` and `Units/CharacterWindow`. So titles lose the display face and their theme-following colour, figures lose the tabular face (columns of numbers stop lining up) and captions grow by a pixel the second time a window or row is drawn, and stay so.
- fix: add `style?: string` to `Skin` (Reskin.wowlua:164-198). In `reskinText`, when `s.style` is set and the text still carries SuuUI's font object (`fo == fonts.get(s.style)`), apply that style again and its remembered token and return; decide anew only when Blizzard put its own font back. Set `s.style` in all three branches and `s.token = "gilt-text"` in both header branches. Test in `tests/unit/UI/Reskin.test.wowlua`: after a second `reskin(f)`, a big title, a number text and a small grey text have the same font object and paint as after the first.

#### UIP-3: A reused notification card keeps old action buttons visible, with their old click handler
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (every pool is hidden with `pairs`, each button losing its click and tooltip; the presence card's Whisper and Invite go through the same layout, which also sets the icon)
- where: src/UI/Notification/Card.wowlua:146-161 (`noteButton`), 441-445 and 789-793 (the hide loops), 796-833
  (the buttons of the new data), 556-578 (presence buttons); src/UI/Notification/Stack.wowlua (cards reused
  from `spare`)
- known: no
- what: buttons are pooled per variant and stored at the action's index: `pool[i]` with `i` the position in `actions` (`noteButton(self, i, a.variant or "quiet")`, line 849). For `actions = { {variant="quiet"}, {variant="primary"} }` the `primary` pool is `{ [2] = button }` with no `[1]`. Both hide loops walk the pools with `for _, b in ipairs(pool) do b:Hide() end`, which stops at the first hole, so that button is never hidden again. Its `OnClick` closure (869-873) still holds the old action.
- why it matters: cards are reused (`table.remove(self.spare)`, and per id). A card that showed Decline (quiet) and Accept (primary) and is later used for data with one action, with hosted Blizzard buttons (`host.buttons`, line 842: no button of its own is laid out), for a presence card, or with another variant at index 2, shows the stale Accept button on top of or beside the new ones (all sit at `RIGHT`, offset 0 for the last action). Clicking it runs the previous notification's action: accepting an invite or a roll choice that is gone. Primary-last is the common layout, so the hole is the common case.
- fix: keep each variant's pool dense: count per variant while laying out (`used[variant] = (used[variant] or 0) + 1; noteButton(self, used[variant], variant)`) in both `SetData` and `SetPresence`, or hide with `pairs(pool)`. Also clear the handler when hiding (`b:SetScript("OnClick", nil)`) so a stale button can never act, and call `btn:SetIcon(nil)` in the presence path (611-621), which the normal path does at 857. Test in `tests/unit/UI/Notification.test.wowlua`: `SetData` with quiet+primary, then with one quiet action, then with `host = { buttons = 1 }`; the primary button must be hidden each time.

#### UIP-4: Visibility never lets go of a frame: a disabled module's frame is shown again, and re-enabling leaves it hidden
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in 4950cdcd (SetVisibility takes the module as owner, and its release lets the frame go: modes, hover and the state driver cleared; every built-in caller passes `self`)
- where: src/UI/Visibility.wowlua:30-33 (strong tables `modes`, `hover`, `also`), 42-67 (`apply`), 69-77 (`setVisibility`), 79-86 (`reapply`); callers `src/Units/MicroMenu.wowlua:466` and `841-850` (`OnDisable`), `src/Units/ObjectiveTracker.wowlua:1178` and `1377-1383`, `src/Units/MicroBags.wowlua:181`, `src/Units/ActionBars.wowlua:792`
- known: no
- what: `setVisibility` records the frame in `modes` for good; nothing removes it. `reapply` (on `SUUUI_EDITMODE_CHANGED` and `SUUUI_KEYBINDMODE_CHANGED`) calls `apply` for every recorded frame, which does `frame:Show()` for any mode but `hidden`. For mode `combat` the state driver `[combat] show; hide` stays registered. And `setVisibility` returns early when the mode is unchanged (`if modes[frame] == mode then return end`).
- why it matters: `MicroMenuModule:OnDisable` (`self.menu:Hide()`) and `ObjectiveTrackerModule:OnDisable` (`parts:Hide()`) only hide their frame. After that: (1) opening or closing edit mode or keybind mode shows the disabled module's frame again; (2) with "In combat" chosen, the next fight shows it again; (3) with "Mouseover", the poll keeps fading it. On re-enable, the module calls `UI.SetVisibility(frame, <same mode>)`, which is a no-op, so the frame stays hidden until the setting is changed or the UI reloads. `CooldownManager` avoids (1)-(3) with `UI.SetVisibility(tracker, "hidden")` in its disable path (`Units/CooldownManager.wowlua:3495`), which shows the pattern is known but not applied everywhere.
- fix: add `releaseVisibility(frame)` to `Visibility.wowlua` (unregister the state driver through `combat.run`, clear `modes`, `hover`, `hoverOn`, `also`, stop a running fade with `motion.alphaTo(frame, 1, 0)`), export it as `SuuUI.UI.ReleaseVisibility` in `src/Core/API.wowlua` next to `SetVisibility` (line 666) and document it in `Docs/API.md`; call it from every `OnDisable` of a module that uses `SetVisibility` (`MicroMenu`, `MicroBags`, `ObjectiveTracker`, `ActionBars`/`UI/ActionBar`, `CooldownManager`). Tests: `tests/unit/UI/Visibility.test.wowlua` (after release, an edit-mode change must not show the frame; `setVisibility` after release applies again).

#### UIP-5: Esc handling is copied with different combat guards; the context menu can hold back every key in combat, a modal calls a combat-refused function per key
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe (what `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` and the default propagation do in combat on Forever; `src/Units/Chat.wowlua:2710-2719` already treats the call as refused in combat and wraps it in `pcall`)
- status: fixed in db302207 (the context menu, filter menu, modals, the welcome and the chat use UI/Dismiss, which never calls the keyboard functions in combat and lets keys pass at rest; the probe confirms the design: in combat lockdown `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` is refused and `EnableKeyboard` allowed)
- probe (2026-11-15, build 70888): `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` is refused in combat lockdown on an addon's own frame, `EnableKeyboard` is allowed (tried on a hidden frame of the probe's own in the first fight). So the finding was real: a handler that waits for the fight to call `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` cannot, and UI/Dismiss's design (let go before the lockdown, call nothing during it) is the one that works. The fix no longer waits on the game for this point.
- where: src/UI/ContextMenu.wowlua:104-119; src/UI/Panel.wowlua:570-579 (`makeModal`); the same block again in `src/UI/FilterMenu.wowlua:634-644`, `src/Units/Welcome.wowlua:615-618`, `src/Units/Chat.wowlua:2710-2719`
- known: no
- what: `MenuFrame` enables the keyboard and its `OnKeyDown` returns at once in combat (`if InCombatLockdown() then return end`), so the propagation flag keeps its last value; it is `false` before the menu's first key out of combat and after every Esc (`self:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(false); close()`). `FilterMenu` has the same shape. `makeModal`'s `OnKeyDown` has no combat guard and calls `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` on every key:
  ```
  modal:SetScript("OnKeyDown", function(self, key)
      if key == "ESCAPE" then self:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(false) self:Hide()
      else self:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(true) end
  end)
  ```
- why it matters: a context or filter menu opened in combat while its flag is `false` takes every key press until it is closed with the mouse: no abilities. A modal open when combat starts (talent dialogs, `confirm`) either raises a blocked-action error per key press or also swallows keys.
- fix: one helper in `src/UI` (for example `escCloses(frame, onEsc)` in `Panel.wowlua`, exported for the modules) used by all five places: `SetPropagateKeyboardInput(true)` when the frame is built or shown out of combat and again on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` (still allowed in that handler), `false` only for Esc out of combat, never called in combat. Consider closing the context and filter menus on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`. Probe first with `/suu probe`: a keyboard-enabled frame in combat (does a key reach the game with the flag unset, with it set true before combat; does the call error in combat). Tests: `tests/unit/UI/ContextMenu.test.wowlua`, `Panel.test.wowlua`.

#### UIP-1: A ScrollBox's rows are all re-skinned on every update; the drains overlap, so the frame budget is not a cap
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the repeated work and the overlap; how often Forever's `ScrollBox:Update` runs while scrolling needs a count in game
- status: partly fixed (2026-11-16, branch `high-perf`, with UIP-2: a pass over unchanged rows sets no font, colour or shadow on their texts. Every row is still walked on every update, `rows()` is still built per pass, the drains still overlap, and a row's status bar is still flattened on each pass)
- where: src/UI/Reskin/Pass.wowlua:359-442 (`reskinScrollBox`: `rows` 374-397, `drain` 398-416, `all`
  417-428), 341-354 (`reskinRow`), 220-318 (`pass`), 111-149 (`reskinText`);
  src/UI/Reskin/Pieces.wowlua:89-168 (`reskinStatusBar`)
- known: no
- what:
  1. Nothing remembers that a row was already done. Each pass calls `reskinRow` for every row; `pass` recurses up to 6 levels and, per frame visited, builds `{ f:GetRegions() }` and `frames.children(f)`, per texture calls `GetAtlas` through `errors.tryMethod`, lowers it and matches it against the 10 `HIDE` patterns, per font string runs `reskinText` (`GetFont`, `GetFontObject`, `GetName`, `GetText`, `GetTextColor`, `fonts.apply`, `draw.paint`). A status bar in a row is flattened and its texts re-anchored on each pass (`reskinStatusBar` guards only the track, 276-302; 303-343 run every time).
  2. `rows()` builds a fresh list per pass through `ForEachFrame` with a closure.
  3. The budget is per drain, not per frame: `all()` is guarded by `queued` only until its `after(0)` fires; a drain that ran out of budget continues with its own `after(0)` chain (1617-1623) over its old list, while the next `Update` starts another drain from row 1:
     ```
     local function all()
         if queued or not box:IsVisible() then return end
         queued = true
         after(0, function() queued = false if box:IsVisible() then drain(rows(), 1) end end)
     end
     ```
     With a list whose full pass takes 4 budgets and an update every frame (scrolling), four drains run per frame: 6 ms a frame instead of 1.5, most of it on rows already restyled this frame or recycled since.
- why it matters: the lists players scroll most (guild roster, reputation, skills, quest log) still pay a full restyle per update, and during a scroll the stated cap does not hold; the garbage (region and child tables per frame visited) is produced every frame of the scroll.
- fix: (a) one drain per box: keep `list`/`index` in the closure; when `all` fires while a drain is running, mark `dirty` and let the running drain start over from a fresh `rows()` when it finishes instead of starting a second one. (b) Remember per row what was skinned: `skins[row].sig` = a cheap signature (the row's element data if `GetElementData` exists, else its first font string's text) and skip a row whose signature is unchanged, so an unchanged row costs one lookup. Better still, skin a row when it is acquired or initialised (`OnAcquiredFrame`/`OnInitializedFrame` of the ScrollBox view: probe which exist on Forever) and drop the `Update` hook. (c) In `reskinStatusBar`, move the font-string block (330-343) inside `if not s.statusBar`. Tests: `tests/unit/UI/Reskin.test.wowlua` (N `Update` calls over several frames with a slow row: never more than one drain alive; an unchanged row is not passed again).

#### UIP-23: Dress makes new animation groups on every dressing and re-dresses on every size change
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Dress.wowlua:107-126 (`stopMotion`, `sway`), 223-240 (`drift`), 128-219 (`placePiece`),
  255-287 (`placeMotes`), 289-328 (`dressOne`), 346-353 (the `OnSizeChanged` script in `register`), 361-369
  (`apply`)
- known: no
- what: the textures are pooled (`w.pieces`, `w.motes`), their animations are not. Each `dressOne` stops the old groups and makes new ones:
  ```
  local function stopMotion(t: Texture)
      local groups = { t:GetAnimationGroups() }
      for _, g in ipairs(groups) do (g :: AnimationGroup):Stop() end
  end
  local function sway(t, point, degrees, seed)
      local g = t:CreateAnimationGroup()
      local r = g:CreateAnimation("Rotation") ...
  ```
  `drift` does the same with three animations per mote. An animation group cannot be removed from its region, so every dressing adds one group per swaying piece and one group with three animations per mote, and `stopMotion` then lists and stops all the earlier ones too (a table per texture per dressing). `dressOne` runs on every theme apply for every registered frame, and, for a kind with motes, from the front frame's `OnSizeChanged`:
  ```
  frontOf(frame, w):SetScript("OnSizeChanged", function()
      local k = current[w.kind]
      if k and k.motes then dressOne(frame, w) end
  end)
  ```
  The front frame is anchored to the dressed frame with `SetAllPoints`, so this fires whenever a titled panel fits itself to its body (`Panel:Fit`), a skinned window changes size with its tab, or a window is laid out. The whole frame is dressed again, not only the motes.
- why it matters: with a dressed theme (Stranglethorn, Pink Cat, the raid themes) every resize of a window leaks about six animation groups (two swaying pieces, four motes) and restarts the motion: the vines jump back to their start angle and the fireflies pop to alpha 0. Over a session the groups per texture grow without bound, and each later dressing walks all of them. A window that changes height while content loads does this several times in a row.
- fix: keep one animation group per texture and reuse it: store `swayOf[t]`/`driftOf[t]` (weak-keyed maps, or fields in two parallel arrays in `Worn`), create on first use, afterwards only `Stop()`, set the new origin, degrees, offsets and durations on the kept animations, and `Play()`. In the `OnSizeChanged` script move only the motes (`SetPoint` from the new width and height) instead of calling `dressOne`; skip it when the size did not change by a pixel. Also: `register` builds the front frame and its script for every registered frame even in SuuUI's own look, although the header says "nothing is made then"; create it in `frontOf` on first use only and set the script there. Tests: `tests/unit/UI/Dress.test.wowlua` (apply the same dress three times and resize: `#{ piece:GetAnimationGroups() }` stays 1).

#### UIP-9: One shade with one owner: closing a dialog opened over a modal removes the dimming of the modal under it
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (UI/Dismiss keeps a stack of open frames: the shade sits under the top modal above the one below it, and goes back to the lower modal when the top one closes)
- where: src/UI/Panel.wowlua:366-395 (`shade`, `attach`), 563-595 (`makeModal`, hooks at 581-591); callers that confirm from inside a modal: `src/Units/Talents.wowlua:417, 473, 595` (modals) with `UI.Confirm` at 1394-2081, `src/Units/CooldownManager.wowlua:684, 711, 1818`
- known: no
- what: `attach` sets `shade.owner = modal` and puts the shade at frame level 1. The modal's `OnHide` hides the shade when `shade.owner == self`:
  ```
  modal:HookScript("OnHide", function(self)
      if shade.owner == self then shade:Hide() shade.owner = nil end
  end)
  ```
  With modal A open and `confirm()` (modal B) shown over it, the owner becomes B; when B hides, the shade hides and `owner` is nil although A is still shown. While B is open the shade is also below A (level 1 against A's 10 or more), so A's controls stay clickable under the question.
- why it matters: after answering the question the first modal stands undimmed, a click outside no longer closes it, and during the question the modal behind it can still be operated.
- fix: keep a stack of open modals in `Panel.wowlua`; place the shade just under the top one (`shade:SetFrameLevel(top:GetFrameLevel() - 1)`, the top raised above the previous), and on hide re-attach to the next one down instead of hiding. Test: extend the modal tests in `tests/unit/UI/Panel.test.wowlua` (two modals: hiding the second leaves the shade shown and owned by the first).

#### UIP-8: Every painted, skinned or glyphed region gets its own `hooksecurefunc` per setter, for its lifetime
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the size of the cost needs measuring
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Draw.wowlua:109-142 (`LETS_GO`, `watch`), 456-517 (`makeRepeat`), 745-770 (`glyph`), 976-998
  (`stylePattern`), 1165-1208 (`Border:SetColor`)
- known: partly, `Docs/port-notes/ui-primitives.md` section 3 ("hooks on hot widget setters": the per-call cost, not the count)
- what: the first paint of a region installs one hook per setter of its kind on that region object: fill 4, vertex 2, text 1, bar 2, gradient 5, fn up to 5. Composite pieces multiply this: a `Border` is 4 textures x 4 = 16 hooks, a `SoftEdge` with a colour table 9 parts x 3 = 27 hooks plus 9 closures, so one titled `Panel` (fill, border, shadow, divider, ornament, texts) carries about 60 hook closures. New in 0.17.0: every glyph texture adds 3 (`SetTexture`, `SetAtlas`, `SetColorTexture`), and under a theme with repeating bar art every bar fill adds about 10 with a closure each. The hooks stay after the paint is let go, and every later call of that setter on that region (SuuUI's own too, in hot paths such as bar colours) runs the hook.
- why it matters: memory that grows with every widget built (thousands of regions in a full UI) and a constant overhead on colour setters in unit frame and aura updates. The file's own comment at 518-522 records the repeat hooks as a measured problem ("about 1,500 in a crowd's profile, each a texture and nine hooks"), solved there by deferral only.
- fix: hook once per widget type instead of once per region: `hooksecurefunc(getmetatable(region).__index, setter, letGo)` the first time a type is painted (a handful of hooks in total; `letGo` is one weak-table write, `letGlyphGo` two). This also runs for Blizzard's regions of that type, so measure both variants with the existing benchmark before choosing. A cheaper alternative with no hooks: let go explicitly in SuuUI's own setters (`Text:SetColor` raw branch, `Border:SetColor` raw branch, `Icon`) and document that a raw colour set by a module needs `draw.unpaint(region)`. Tests: `tests/unit/UI/Draw.test.wowlua` keeps the "letting go per setter" behaviour pinned.

#### UIP-12: Hooks on Blizzard's `SetPoint` and selected textures trigger uncoalesced relayouts
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/WindowSkin/Chrome.wowlua:121-129 (tab `SetPoint` hook), 130-140 (three hooks per selected
  texture), 378-380 (`OnSizeChanged`), 423-472 and 165-183 (`LayoutTabs`, `fitTabs`), 474-494 (`UpdateTabs`),
  496-512 (`PlaceHead`); src/UI/WindowSkin/Row.wowlua:208-215 (window `SetPoint` hook), 97-150 (`layout`)
- known: no
- what: Blizzard re-anchors each tab in turn and shows or hides each tab's selected textures in turn; each call runs a relayout of the whole row:
  ```
  hook(b, "SetPoint", function()
      if chrome.placing then return end
      chrome:LayoutTabs()
      after(0, function() chrome:LayoutTabs() end)
  end)
  ```
  For a 5-tab window one Blizzard tab update is 5 immediate `LayoutTabs`, 5 timers and 5 more `LayoutTabs` a frame later (each with 10 to 15 `measureText` calls and a `SetSize`/`ClearAllPoints`/`SetPoint`/`SetFrameLevel` per tab), plus up to 15 `UpdateTabs`. Every Blizzard `SetPoint` on a row window re-places every open window at once.
- why it matters: a visible hitch when opening or switching tabs in skinned windows, in the path that has to finish before the first frame to avoid flicker.
- fix: keep the immediate `LayoutTabs` (it is there against a one-frame jump) but make the deferred one a single queued call per chrome (`self.layoutQueued`), cache each label's width per chrome (invalidate on `SUUUI_THEME_CHANGED` and when a label changes), and in `LayoutTabs` skip the `SetPoint` of a tab whose point already is the wanted one (compare `b:GetPoint(1)`), which also ends the hook's re-entry early. In `UpdateTabs` keep the last `on/off/hover` per tab and return before `SetColor`/`SetAlpha`/`SetShown` when nothing changed. In the window hook skip `layout()` when the frame's point already is what `layout` would set. Tests: `tests/unit/UI/WindowSkin.test.wowlua`.

#### UIP-10: `WindowFrame` has its own copy of the scroll area, without the clamp and without a scrollbar
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Panel.wowlua:685-701 (window scroll) versus src/UI/Panel/ScrollArea.wowlua:20-176
  (`scrollArea`, with settling and the bar)
- known: no
- what: `WindowFrame` builds a second ScrollFrame by hand (wheel step 40 instead of 48). It has no scrollbar and none of `scrollArea`'s settling: when the content gets shorter the scroll offset is not pulled back. `scrollArea`'s own comment says that case had to be fixed there ("content that got shorter ... pulls the scroll back, so no empty space stays at the bottom"), including the secret scroll range in combat.
- why it matters: in any window whose content changes height (tabs, filters, a list that shrinks) a player scrolled to the bottom sees an empty body until they wheel up; long windows give no hint that they scroll.
- fix: build the window body with `scrollArea(self.body, bar)`, expose its `child` as `window.content` and the area as `window.scroll` (keep the `OnSizeChanged` width sync). Remove the duplicate. Tests: `tests/unit/UI/Panel.test.wowlua`.

#### UIP-11: `NotificationStack.expanded` is set and never cleared

#### UIP-13: Callbacks are registered on Blizzard's registries with the Blizzard frame itself as owner
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- status: open (unverified: the two registries the probe read hold no callback owned by the frame itself, see the probe line; the same registration with the frame as owner runs on every ScrollBox and dropdown the reskin pass skins (`reskinScrollBox`, `reskinDropdown`), and those were not read. Unlikely to matter, and cheap to remove)
- probe (2026-11-15, build 70888): before SuuUI registered, the reputation list had 1 callback for `OnDataRangeChanged` and the Who page's filter dropdown 0 for `OnMenuOpen`, none owned by the frame itself: for these two, SuuUI's registration replaces nothing of Blizzard's.
- where: src/UI/Reskin/Pass.wowlua:432-435 (`errors.tryMethod(box, "RegisterCallback", changed, all, box)`),
  src/UI/Reskin/Menu.wowlua:442-460 (`errors.tryMethod(d, "RegisterCallback", event, fn, d)`)
- known: no
- what: Blizzard's callback registries keep one function per owner per event. Using the ScrollBox or the dropdown itself as the owner replaces any callback Blizzard registered for that event with the same owner, and SuuUI's function then sits in a table Blizzard iterates. The `MenuProxy.OnShow` registration in the same file (853-879) already uses an owner of SuuUI's own, the string `"SuuUI.Reskin"`.
- why it matters: if Blizzard's own code registers with `self` as owner for these events on Forever, its handler is silently replaced (a list that stops reacting to range changes, a dropdown that stops updating on open). The file's comments at 639-644 and 1863-1866 record that hooks on the game's shared menu and popup frames made protected choices fail; these two registrations are the remaining places where SuuUI's functions are stored inside Blizzard's tables.
- fix: use an owner of SuuUI's own for both (a module-level table, or `"SuuUI.Reskin"`). Probe: dump the registry's callback table for the event before registering, on the reputation list and the Who dropdown (`/suu probe`), and run `/suu probe taint` after using a skinned list in combat.

- severity: medium
- category: architecture

- known: no
- what and fix:

The parts share the `painting` flag, `touched` and `restylers`. Cut into `Reskin/Registry`, `Reskin/Pieces`, `Reskin/Menu`, `Reskin/Pass`, `Reskin/Popup`; the menu and popup parts share the undo list and `hideRegion`/`menuText`, which belong in the registry file.
  - `WindowSkin.wowlua` (985 lines): the chrome and its tabs (1-610), the window row and centring (612-833), secure placement (835-983). The row and the placer only need `chrome.frame`, `rise`, `under`, `centered`, `cutW`, `protected`: cut into `WindowSkin`, `WindowRow`, `WindowPlacer`. `add` and `layout` are exported only because they sit in the same file as their caller.
  - `Notification.wowlua` (1,143 lines): the card (1-913), of which `SetPresence` (481-671) is a second layout that repeats the head and action-row code of `SetData` (673-891), and the stack (915-1143). Cut into `Notification` (card, with one shared `layoutHead` and `layoutActions`), `NotificationPresence`, `NotificationStack`. The duplicated action rows already differ (UIP-3's fix has to be made twice; the presence path does not reset a button's icon).
  - `Panel.wowlua` (1,104 lines): close button and key chip, `Panel`, the modal shade and `confirm`, `scrollArea`, `SectionHeader`, `WindowFrame` with its tabs and secure Escape. Cut into `Panel`, `Modal` (shade, `makeModal`, `ConfirmDialog`), `ScrollArea`, `WindowFrame`. `scrollArea` (398-561) sits between `attach` and `makeModal`, splitting the modal code in two.
  - `Tooltip.wowlua` (417 lines): SuuUI's own tooltip, the skin for Blizzard's tooltips (`skinTooltip`), and `spellTooltip` on `GameTooltip`. The last two share nothing with the first and belong in a `GameTooltip` file.
- why it matters: the two largest files are the ones that touch Blizzard's frames and the ones every theme feature now lands in; a change to the menu undo logic means reading the status-bar and popup code as well, and a change to the paint flag means checking six places that set it by hand.

#### UIP-7: `Text:SetValue` does not clear a secret text when given nil, and invalidates its layout on every secret value
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Text.wowlua:62-79; src/UI/Alert.wowlua:69-70
- known: no
- what:
  ```
  function SetValue(v: TextValue?)
      if isSecret(v) then
          self.value = nil
          self:SetText(v)
          self:Changed()
          return
      end
      if v == self.value then return end
  ```
  For a secret value the method sets `self.value = nil`. A later `SetValue(nil)` hits `if v == self.value then return end` (nil == nil) and returns without `SetText`, so the secret text stays on screen. Separately, the secret branch calls `self:Changed()` every time, which invalidates the text's layout even when nothing changed.
- why it matters: (1) a name or number shown from a secret (an enemy's name in a dungeon) is not removed by `SetValue(nil)`; only `SetValue("")` works. (2) a text in a `Stack` that is fed a secret on every `UNIT_HEALTH`/`UNIT_POWER` runs the layout flusher every frame in combat: a list, a `pending` table and a sort closure per flush (UIP-14), and a measure of every child of that stack and of the stacks around it.
- fix: track "shows a secret" separately (`self.secretShown = true` in the secret branch, cleared in the plain branch) and let `SetValue(nil)` and any readable value through when it is set. In the secret branch call `Changed()` only when the text has no `fixedWidth` and was not already showing a secret (a secret text measures as 0 in `Layout.measure`, so its size cannot have changed). Tests: `tests/unit/UI/Text.test.wowlua`.

#### UIP-14: The layout flush allocates on every pass
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Layout.wowlua:384-410 (flush), 509 (`lastResult`), 332-373 (`ApplyNow`)
- known: no
- what:
  ```
  local redo = again
  again = {}
  ...
  for _ = 1, 8 do
      if not next(pending) then return end
      local list: Layout[] = {}
      for l in pairs(pending) do list[#list + 1] = l end
      pending = {}
      table.sort(list, function(a, b) return a.depth > b.depth end)
  ```
- why it matters: small per call, but layouts are invalidated from text changes (UIP-7) and a timer's text, so in combat this is steady garbage: four allocations a frame for as long as one text in a stack changes each frame.
- fix: reuse module-level scratch tables (swap `pending` with a spare and `wipe` it; the same for `again`), hoist the comparator to a module-level function, keep `lastResult` as two number fields (`lastRW`, `lastRH`), and clear `pending[self]` at the top of `ApplyNow`. Tests: `tests/unit/UI/Layout.test.wowlua`.

#### UIP-24: A glow whose `SoftEdge` object is not kept stops following a theme's `glow` file
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Draw.wowlua:336-337 (`edgeToken`, `edgeFile`: weak keys), 1521-1534 (`SoftEdge:Part`), 800-813
  (`reskin` walks `edgeToken`); results discarded at src/UI/Auras.wowlua:397, src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:1021,
  src/Units/ObjectiveTracker.wowlua:408
- known: no
- what: the registry of token-drawn soft edges is weak-keyed on the edge's `parts` array. That array is referenced only by the `SoftEdge` instance; the nine textures do not point back to it and the `bind` closures in `SetColor` capture only the colour table. Where the caller drops the return value, instance and array are collected at the next GC cycle and the entry disappears. `reskin()` then no longer sets a changed `glow` file on those textures. (Borders had the same problem and were given a strong per-frame list, `bordersOf`, in 0.17.0; soft edges were not.)
- why it matters: a theme that replaces the `glow` texture token (possible through `SuuUI.RegisterTheme`; SuuUI's built-in themes keep `Soft.tga`) changes the glows of icons and alerts, which keep their edge, but not the aura highlights, the ward glow on unit frames or the tracker's suggestion glow, depending on when the collector last ran. Their colours still follow, since those are painted per texture.
- fix: hold the instance from something that lives with the frame, as borders do: `edgesOf[frame]` (weak-keyed on the frame, value a list of `SoftEdge`), filled in the constructor; key `edgeToken`/`edgeFile` on the instance or drop them and walk `edgesOf`. Test in `tests/unit/UI/Draw.test.wowlua`: `draw.shadow(f, "glow-arcane")` without keeping it, `collectgarbage()`, change the token's file, `draw.reskin()`, expect the new file on the holder's textures.

#### UIP-25: Three places set the paint flag to false instead of putting it back
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (the code is plain; no caller was found that reaches it inside a repaint today)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Draw.wowlua:1170-1176 (`Border:SetColor`, textured branch), 1328-1335 (`styleDivider`),
  1436-1438 (`styleOrnament`)
- known: no
- what: `painting` tells the `letGo` hooks that the current colour or texture call is SuuUI's own. `keep`, `bind` and `keepSkin` save and restore it (`local was = painting; painting = true; ...; painting = was`, with the comment "a hook may paint while repaint runs: keep its flag"). The three newer places write `painting = true ... painting = false`.
- why it matters: if one of them runs while a repaint or a `bind` function is in progress (a bound function that recolours a textured border, or one that builds a hairline with a divider or an ornament), the flag is false for the rest of that `repaint`: every region drawn after it lets its paint go in its own setter hook (`paints[region] = nil`) and silently stops following the theme. Hard to trace when it happens, because the regions affected depend on table order.
- fix: use the save/restore pattern in all three (or the two helper functions proposed in UIP-22). Test in `tests/unit/UI/Draw.test.wowlua`: `draw.bind(tex, function() texturedBorder:SetColor("gilt") end)` with a theme whose `border` file is not the white square, then `draw.repaint()`; a region painted before must still be kept afterwards.

#### UIP-16: Lines given as 1 or 2 UI units are not physical pixels
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/ContextMenu.wowlua:113-120 (`rule`: `l:SetHeight(1)`); src/UI/WindowSkin/Chrome.wowlua:372-375
  (the tab row's rule); src/UI/Reskin/Pieces.wowlua:60-80 (thumb 2 and 4 wide), src/UI/Reskin/Pass.wowlua:305
  (`headRule`); src/UI/Crest.wowlua:50; src/UI/LoadingMark.wowlua:109; src/UI/Notification/Card.wowlua:448-450
  (drain, height 2); src/UI/Draw.wowlua:1622
- known: no
- what: these lines are sized in UI units while `Draw.hairline` and `Border` use `pixel.size(frame)` (or a fixed pixel unit) and are laid out again on `SUUUI_ROOT_SCALED`. On Blizzard's frames (UIParent scale) and at any root scale other than the pixel-perfect one, a height of 1 is a fraction or a non-integer number of physical pixels. 0.17.0 fixed the same effect for borders in three places (nameplates, tooltips, the skinned window's header: `withPixelUnit`, the `SetScale` hook in `Tooltip.wowlua`, `relayoutPixels`), but `relayoutPixels` only knows borders and hairlines, so the window header's own rule (WindowSkin 393-395) is not covered by the `relayoutPixels(head)` call at 532.

- fix: use `draw.hairline(parent, token)` for the rules (it is registered for the scale message and for `relayoutPixels`), or `pixel.size(frame)` for the others, set again from the same places.

#### UIP-18: A window's key chip is fixed when the window is built
- severity: low

- where: src/UI/WindowSkin/Chrome.wowlua:366-371, 576-585; src/UI/Panel.wowlua:116-120 (`keybind` option)
- known: no
- what: the chip is created only if the binding has a key when the window is skinned (`local key = o.binding and GetBindingKey(o.binding); if key then self.key = keyChip(...)`), and nothing in these files listens to `UPDATE_BINDINGS`. `SetBinding` does nothing when no chip was created. `Panel` takes the key as a fixed string.
- why it matters: after rebinding, the header shows the old key; a window skinned while unbound never shows one.
- fix: always create the chip (hidden when unbound), keep `o.binding` on the chrome, and refresh every chrome on `UPDATE_BINDINGS` (one `events.onGame` in the file, walking `allChromes`). For `Panel`, accept a binding name as an alternative to the key text and refresh the same way.

#### UIP-19: Leftovers and values fixed too early
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/WindowSkin/Chrome.wowlua:266, src/UI/WindowSkin/Row.wowlua:85, 138, 234-240
  (`placeAfterCombat`); Chrome.wowlua:249, 517, 525 (`riseH`/`rise`); Chrome.wowlua:37, 592 (`WINDOW_HEAD_H`);
  Chrome.wowlua:281 (`self.protected`); src/UI/ContextMenu.wowlua:140 (`owner` unused);
  src/UI/Panel.wowlua:100-112, 701-726 (`onClose`); src/UI/WindowSkin/SecurePlacement.wowlua:40-130
- known: no
- what:
  - src/UI/WindowSkin.wowlua:286, 677, 731: `placeAfterCombat` is set and never read (the `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` handler at 827-833 queues a full layout).
  - src/UI/WindowSkin.wowlua:269-270, 537, 545: `riseH` and `rise` always hold the same value.
  - src/UI/WindowSkin.wowlua:58, 985: `WINDOW_HEAD_H` is computed once at load, although `headH()` exists because a theme can change the header's line height and spacing; `src/Units/CharacterWindow.wowlua:888` positions with the stale value, and it is public API (`src/Core/API.wowlua:532`).
  - src/UI/WindowSkin.wowlua:301: `self.protected` is read once at skin time; a window that gains protected children later (SuuUI adds some itself: the `SecureFrameTemplate` marks at 932 and the placer at 889) is then moved in combat.
  - src/UI/ContextMenu.wowlua:163: `owner` is never used; the menu does not close when its owner hides or when combat starts.
  - src/UI/Panel.wowlua:143-149, 989-995, 1004-1012: `onClose` runs only from the close button; Esc (through `UISpecialFrames`, or the secure Escape button's `_onclick`, which calls `Hide()`) hides the window without it. Twelve modules pass `onClose` (`Merchant`, `Macros`, `Inspect`, `AuctionHouse`, `Bags`, `Trainer`, ...).
  - src/UI/WindowSkin.wowlua:901-947: a protected window opened in combat is always placed at the row's first slot (`rowX` is the anchor's left edge), over a window already there; `Track` and `SetTabSize` called in combat are dropped with no retry.
- why it matters: dead state misleads the next change; the others are small wrong results in edge cases.
- fix: remove the dead fields; export `windowHeadHeight()` and keep the constant as deprecated; read `frame:IsProtected()` when needed; close the menu from an `OnHide` hook on its owner and on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`; call `onClose` from the window's `OnHide` when the close button did not already (a flag set by the button); queue `Track`/`SetTabSize` with `combat.run`.

#### UIP-20: Scripts that tick while there is nothing to do
- severity: low

- severity: low

With UIP-8 each also carries its paint hooks, and in 0.17.0 each card and panel also gets a pattern ground, a textured border and, for titled panels, a dress front frame (UIP-23).
