### Fixed since the first pass

- UIP-6 (most borders stop following a scale change): `Border` instances are now held strongly per frame in `bordersOf` (src/UI/Draw.wowlua:1093, 1135-1137), so the weak `borders` set keeps them and `SUUUI_ROOT_SCALED` reaches all of them (1677-1695). Commit 88cd7e71 (#155). The same shape remains for soft edges: UIP-24.
- UIP-15 (setters without an early-out repaint on every call): `keep` returns early for the same kind, token and alpha (src/UI/Draw.wowlua:181-185) and `paintGradient` for the same gradient (229-233), commit 5a4a8cb9 (#111); `MapPin:SetData` skips unchanged data (`dataKey`/`drawnKey`, src/UI/MapPin.wowlua, commit 17d80d4d, #112). So `Bar:SetFill`, `Border:SetColor`, `Notification:SetRemaining` and `WindowChrome:UpdateTabs` now cost a lookup per region. Left over, not worth a finding: `Icon:SetState` (src/UI/Icon.wowlua:57-65) still sets desaturation and vertex colour on every call, `MapPin`'s `dataKey` builds a 13-entry table and a string per call, and a gradient repaint still makes two `CreateColor` objects (Draw.wowlua:171-173).

### Withdrawn

- None. (Parts dropped inside findings that remain: UIP-14's "the tooltip arranges twice per content change", now a kept-result lookup; UIP-19's "presence path does not reset a pooled button's icon", moved into UIP-3's fix.)

### Cross-cutting observations

- **`keep`'s early-out now trusts the let-go hooks completely** (src/UI/Draw.wowlua:181-185). A colour changed by a route that is not in `LETS_GO` leaves the record in place, and painting the same token again then does nothing, where 0.6 would have set it again. Routes not hooked: `SetVertexColor` on a region kept as `fill`; a status bar coloured through `bar:GetStatusBarTexture():SetVertexColor`; a font string whose font object's colour changes; `keepSkin` on a painted bar (it sets the file with `painting = true`, and the comment at 258-260 says a bar's new file may take the bar's own colour, but only `reskin()` marks it `touched`). None was found in use; worth a probe (`SetStatusBarTexture` then `GetStatusBarColor`) and a sweep for mixed raw and painted colour on one region.
- **Layouts whose container size is pinned** (not verified against callers): `Layout:ApplyNow` (src/UI/Layout.wowlua:347-372) compares the container's size with what it wants and, when it differs, sets it, invalidates the outer layout and queues a full re-anchor for the next frame (`again`). A stack left at the default `autoSize = true` on a container whose width or height is fixed by two opposite anchors can never reach the wanted size, so it would re-anchor all its children every frame. A sweep of `UI.Stack`/`layout.stack` callers for containers with two-sided anchors and no `autoSize = "height"`/`"width"`/`false` would settle it; a guard (give up after the size did not change in response to `SetWidth`/`SetHeight`) would make it safe.
- **Sparse pools walked with `ipairs`** (UIP-3): any pool indexed by a caller's position rather than a dense counter has this hole.
- **Passes that decide from the current state of what they restyled** (UIP-2): any restyle that reads font, size or colour to choose what to apply must remember its choice, or it drifts on the second run. The same shape may exist in the skins in `Units/Windows` and `Units/CharacterWindow`.
- **Managed-frame registries without a release** (UIP-4): `Visibility`'s `modes` is the clear case. New in 0.17.0 and of the same kind: `Dress.register` (no way to take a frame out), `Draw.onLayout` (functions only added), `WindowSkin`'s `Row.list`/`allChromes`/`placers`. Acceptable for `reloadToToggle` modules, but `SkinWindow`, `SetVisibility` and the draw functions are public API that plugins reach.
- **Module `OnDisable` that hides a frame directly** while a helper still manages it (Visibility, movers, state drivers): sweep every `OnDisable` for `:Hide()` on a frame passed to `UI.SetVisibility`.
- **Weak registries keyed on a wrapper object the caller may drop** (UIP-24): `edgeToken`/`edgeFile` in `Draw`. The others in these files are keyed on frames, textures or font strings (kept alive by the client) or, for `Layout`'s `tokened`, on a layout that its children's placements hold.
- **Esc/keyboard blocks copied per file** (UIP-5) with three different combat treatments (none, an `InCombatLockdown` return, `pcall`).
- **Animations created per use instead of once per region** (UIP-23): worth a sweep for `CreateAnimationGroup` inside functions that run more than once per region.
- **Frames SuuUI parents to Blizzard windows without `markOwn`**: `Dress`'s front frame (src/UI/Dress.wowlua:95-104) is a child of the skinned Blizzard window and is not marked, unlike the chrome's `head` and `edgeHolder` (WindowSkin.wowlua:342, 350). `Reskin`'s pass walks into it on every `reskin(window)`; its textures have no atlas, so nothing is changed today, but any rule added to `reskinTexture` that matches by layer or file would restyle the dress.
- **Hosted Blizzard buttons and secure overlays on notification cards**: `NotificationStack:SetItems` (src/UI/Notification.wowlua:1055-1138) moves, shows and re-stratas cards with no combat check; if a card holds a protected child (the module's secure click overlays or hosted popup buttons), those calls are blocked in combat. For the Units reviewer to check against `Units/Notifications`.

### Summary

State of the area on 0.17.0: 55 findings remain (3 high, 18 medium, 34 low; 40 still present, 10 changed, 5 new); 2 are fixed in full, none withdrawn in full. No critical finding and no confirmed Lua error.

- Several shared fixes landed between the versions and lowered a group of findings without closing them: `draw.paint`/`paintFill` set nothing for an unchanged colour (`src/UI/Draw.wowlua:181-185`), `events.offAll` looks only at the owner's listeners (`src/Core/Events.wowlua:178-194`), the cast bar's unit events are on one frame per bar, the action buttons' setters skip unchanged state, the cooldown tracker has a usability-only pass, and the stance bar coalesces. HUD-CD-1 dropped from high to low for that reason; HUD-2 and HUD-3 are fixed.
- The three high findings are all in `UnitFrame`: "removable" debuff badges and "mine" buff indicators select by filter tokens that other players' auras always pass (HUD-UF-1, HUD-UF-2; the modules' own comments in 0.17.0 now record that rule, and the inline icons were changed for it, but not the unit frame), and `UpdateHealth` still runs in full for four events, three per heal, and grew (HUD-UF-4).
- Unchanged medium bugs: the cooldown tracker's `inFight` across Stop/Start (HUD-CD-4), shared aura sounds (HUD-CD-6), pool keys that strand engine containers on every settings edit (HUD-CD-2), the meter's spell breakdown indexing a possibly secret table (HUD-DM-1), the totem set lost at a cold login (HUD-DM-2), aura containers that choose their rescan event once (HUD-UF-8), the swing timer's ranged row (HUD-4).
- Still hot: the totem bar redraws uncoalesced on four hot events (HUD-DM-3), the pet bar redoes its secure attribute pass per pet UNIT_AURA (HUD-DM-4), the interrupt's cooldown is read once per nameplate per SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN (HUD-1), roster events fan out per frame (HUD-UF-6, HUD-UF-7).
- New code: `PowerCost`, `HealthFill` and `CombatBadge` gave no findings of their own. The new lazy build of aura buttons moves their construction to the first show, usually in a fight, where the project's own notes say the game's aura buttons refuse addon code (HUD-UF-15, needs a probe), and out of the nameplates' pixel-unit scope (HUD-UF-16). Skipping hidden action buttons in the cooldown pass makes them pop "ready" when their bar shows (HUD-12).
- Structure is as it was: `CooldownTracker` (six concerns in one file, HUD-CD-13) and `ClassBars` (three unrelated bars, HUD-DM-13) are unsplit.

### Findings

#### HUD-UF-1: "Only what you can remove" badges use a filter token that other players' debuffs always pass
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (the token's behaviour on other players is recorded in NEW's module comments; one in-game check of the badge itself is still worth doing)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:951-971 (`buildDispelSet`), 2155-2166 (`SetDispelBadges`); callers
  src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1208, 1500, src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:1232; the rule as the modules now apply
  it: src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:118-133, 155-163, src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:100-108
- known: no (the rule is written down for the inline icons only)
- what: the "removable" set is built as
  `local filter = set == "removable" and { "HARMFUL", "RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE" } or { "HARMFUL" }`
  with `dispelTypes = { kind }` per type, for every frame, whoever it shows. The token is the only thing that separates "removable" from "all". The raid frames' inline icons were changed for exactly this token: their comment reads "the game hides who cast another player's auras, and those then pass both "removable" and "not removable": each showed twice", and their first group now takes `filters = { me = { "HARMFUL", "RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE" }, others = { "HARMFUL" } }`. The badge sets got no such change.
- why it matters: on party and raid frames of other players "removable" shows every typed debuff, the same as "all": a priest sees a Curse border and badge on a raid member and cannot remove it. On the player's own frame it works, so the setting looks right when tested alone. Healers decide whom to dispel from this.
- fix: confirm once in game (a debuff type the class cannot remove on a party member with `debuffBadges = "removable"`). Then stop using the token on frames of others: build the "removable" set with plain `{ "HARMFUL" }` and only the dispel types the player's class can remove (a per-class table of Magic/Curse/Poison/Disease, re-evaluated on `SPELLS_CHANGED` out of combat; `includeDispelTypes` is matched by the engine in combat). One set then serves both modes (leave out the types not in the list) instead of two sets of four containers, which also halves HUD-UF-9. Extend `tests/unit/UI/UnitFrame.test.wowlua` (the dispel set's group specs).

#### HUD-UF-2: Buff indicators with source "mine" rely on the PLAYER token, which other players' auras pass
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (NEW records the token's behaviour for another player's buffs on the target; not yet checked for an engine group with a spell list on a group unit)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:1938 (live container filter), 2049-2062 (the "missing" check), 664
  (`ind.source or "mine"`: the default); the setting: src/Units/BuffIndicators.wowlua:632 ("Yours" /
  "Anyone's"); the recorded behaviour: src/Units/Auras.wowlua:89-92, src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:118-121
- known: no
- what: a live indicator is filtered with
  `local filter = ind.source == "any" and { "HELPFUL" } or { "HELPFUL", "PLAYER" }`,
  and the out-of-combat "missing" check reads
  `local filter = ind.source == "any" and "HELPFUL" or "HELPFUL|PLAYER"` through `C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDataByIndex(u, i, filter)`. "mine" is the default. `src/Units/Auras.wowlua:95-98` says of the target's buffs: "the game hides who cast another player's buffs, and those passed both "yours" and "not yours" (each showed twice; /suu probe partyauras)".
- why it matters: if the same holds here, "Yours" equals "Anyone's" on every frame but your own: with two druids in a raid your Rejuvenation indicator lights up for the other druid's Rejuvenation, and a "missing" indicator stays hidden although your own buff is not on the unit. The settings offer a choice that does nothing on the frames it is meant for.
- fix: check with two casters of the same HoT on a third player (which of them pass `HELPFUL|PLAYER` in an engine group with `includeSpellIDs`, and in `GetAuraDataByIndex` out of combat). If own casts cannot be told apart, treat "mine" as "any" on frames that are not the player and say so under the "Yours" control in `src/Units/BuffIndicators.wowlua`, rather than showing a choice with no effect. If the engine does tell them apart for spell-list groups, record it in `Docs/test-notes/ui-units.md` and close this.

#### HUD-UF-4: UpdateHealth runs in full, with allocations, on every health, heal-prediction and absorb event
- severity: high
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed on 2026-11-16 (branch `high-perf`; UI/UnitFrame: the four health events mark what they changed, and one driver draws each frame's health at most once a frame, a heal-prediction or absorb change only those bars; the bars that take the range are a list kept on the frame and get it only on a maximum change; the text's font and colour are set only when they change; the ghost's hold is a time on the frame (`ghostDue`) moved by the same driver, no closure or timer. Frames with `incoming = false` still take the two incoming events, each now a mark and two empty bars set)
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:1433-1552 (the function), 1036-1041 and 2232-2236 (four events mapped to it),
  1407-1420 (`Tapped`); src/UI/Text.wowlua:48-52 (`SetStyle`); src/UI/Bar.wowlua:54-59
- known: no
- what: `UNIT_HEALTH`, `UNIT_MAXHEALTH`, `UNIT_HEAL_PREDICTION` and `UNIT_ABSORB_AMOUNT_CHANGED` each run the whole of `UpdateHealth`. Per call:
  - lines 1444-1454 build a seven-element table
    (`for _, b in ipairs({ self.health, self.healthLow, self.ghost, self.incoming, self.absorb, self.absorbReach, self.absorbOver }) do b:SetMinMaxValues(0, amount(max)) end`)
    and set seven ranges, whether or not the maximum changed;
  - lines 1495-1496 (and 1491-1492 for a dead unit) call `self.right:SetStyle("numeric")` every time; `SetStyle` is `fonts.apply(self, style)` plus `self:Changed()` with no check for the style already set (`SetColor` is cheap now);
  - lines 1533/1535 format a new string for the text when the values are readable;
  - `trail` allocates a closure and a timer roughly every 0.15 s while health moves;
  - `isOffline`, `UnitIsDeadOrGhost`, `Tapped()` (two `errors.tryValue` calls on frames with `opts.tapped`), two or three `UnitHealthPercent` curve evaluations and both prediction reads, also when only the absorb changed.
  Frames with `opts.incoming == false` still register the prediction and absorb events and run all of it.
- why it matters: one heal landing raises three of the four events for the same unit, so the work is done three times; in a 40-player raid in combat that is many hundreds of calls per second on the raid frames alone, each leaving a table (and often a string) behind. This is the hottest Lua path of the group frames.
- fix: (1) keep the seven bars in a field built once in the constructor and set the range only from `UNIT_MAXHEALTH` and `Refresh` (a secret maximum cannot be compared, so split by event, not by value); (2) remember the text's mode (`"gone"`/`"numeric"`) on the frame and call `SetStyle`/`SetColor` only when it changes (or give `Text:SetStyle` an early return when `self.style == style`, which fixes every caller); (3) split the handler: the prediction and absorb events update only `incoming`, `absorb`, `absorbReach` (lines 1476-1488) and are not registered when `opts.incoming == false`; (4) give `trail` one callback per host, created once. Optionally coalesce to once per frame per unit with a dirty flag. Tests: tests/unit/UI/UnitFrame.test.wowlua (count calls on the bars per event).

#### HUD-1: Every SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN re-reads the interrupt's cooldown once per active cast bar, nameplates included
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CastBar.wowlua:205-226 (`refreshKicks` and its `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` listener), 763-778
  (`UpdateKick`), 181-186 (`ready`), 908 (`interrupt.bars[self] = true`); src/Units/Nameplates.wowlua:478
  (every plate's bar is built with the default `kick`), 1617-1622 (activated per plate)
- known: no
- what: `events.onGame("SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN", refreshKicks, "Interrupt")` runs
  `for bar in pairs(interrupt.bars) do bar:UpdateKick() end` over every *activated* bar, casting or not. `UpdateKick` calls `self:KickReady()` → `ready()` → `readyFrom(C_Spell.GetSpellCooldown(interrupt.spell))` (a new table from the game each call), then `draw.paint(k.glyph, …)` (which sets nothing when the colour is unchanged, src/UI/Draw.wowlua:181-185) and two `SetShown`. A nameplate's bar is built as `UI.CastBar(self, "none", { size = "plate", width = w, icon = false, target = true })`, so `opts.kick ~= false` holds, each plate has a `KickMark` and sits in `interrupt.bars`.
- why it matters: SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN fires several times per cast (the action bars' own comment at src/UI/ActionBar.wowlua:408-413 measured it). With 20 to 40 plates in a pull, a class with an interrupt does 20 to 40 identical cooldown reads (as many garbage tables) per event, for bars that are hidden because nothing is cast. The handler is registered at file load under the owner "Interrupt" and never removed, so it also runs with the cast bar modules off (then over an empty set).
- fix: in `refreshKicks` read `ready()` once and hand the result to the bars (`bar:UpdateKick(isReady)`; keep `KickReady()` as the default when no value is given, since tests stand in for it), and skip bars with no cast (`bar.duration == nil`): `Start` already calls `UpdateKick` when a cast begins. Do the same in the loop of the `UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED` handler (lines 198-200). Extend tests/unit/UI/CastBar.test.wowlua: with three activated idle bars, one SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN reads the cooldown at most once.

#### HUD-UF-15: An aura button's art is built when it first shows, which is usually in a fight, where the game's aura buttons refuse addon code
- severity: medium
- category: bug

The watcher failed at a dungeon fight's end: it compared an engine aura button's `IsShown()` with `true`, and that value is a secret boolean to SuuUI's code ("attempt to compare local 'isShown' (a secret boolean value, while execution tainted by 'SuuUI')"). The item counts as done and needs its watcher fixed and a re-run (`Docs/plans/open-probes.md`).
- where: src/UI/Auras.wowlua:375-390 (`build`: unguarded `button:CreateTexture`, `CreateFrame(…, button)`,
  `button:GetFrameLevel()`), 479-515 (registrations, each in a `pcall`), 517-536 (the deferral); the notes
  that contradict it: src/UI/Draw.wowlua:1649-1651, src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:934-936,
  src/UI/Auras.wowlua:363-364
- known: no
- what: the initializer now only sizes a hidden button and builds its art later:
  ```
  local built = false
  button:HookScript("OnShow", function()
      if not built then
          built = true
          build(button)
      end
  end)
  ```
  The engine makes ten buttons per group up front and shows one more each time the unit has one more aura, so for nameplate debuffs and group-frame debuffs the first show of most buttons happens in combat. NEW's own notes say what the game does with these buttons then: "The game's aura buttons refuse addon code in a fight while answering IsForbidden false (probed 2026-11-12)" (Draw.wowlua:1648), "writes to these buttons are refused once auras are secret" (UnitFrame.wowlua:935), "reachable once the game has made the button forbidden" (Auras.wowlua:364). `build` starts with unguarded calls on the button (`button:CreateTexture(nil, "ARTWORK")`), and everything that registers art with the engine (`SetIcon`, `SetApplicationCount`, `SetDurationText`, `SetDurationBar`, the dispel textures) is in a `pcall` that swallows a refusal. `built` is set before `build` runs, so a failed build is never tried again.
- why it matters: if the refusal applies to a button's first show in a fight (dungeon combat is where the notes saw it), the fourth debuff on a plate or the first debuff on a raid member in an instance either raises a Lua error from the `OnShow` hook or, where only the pcall'd registrations are refused, leaves a sized, empty button in the row for the rest of the session. It would not show in open-world testing, where the lazy build was measured.
- fix: probe first: in a dungeon fight, log from the hook whether `pcall(build, button)` succeeds for a button that first shows in combat, and whether its icon draws. If it fails: build ahead instead of on show, but out of the hot path: after a group is added, build its buttons a few per frame out of combat (a queue drained by a timer, also flushed on `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`), and build in the hook only as the fallback; set `built = true` only after `pcall(build, button)` succeeded so a refused build is retried on the next show. If it works in fights, record that next to the three notes above, which say otherwise. Test: tests/unit/UI/Auras.test.wowlua ("a hidden button is sized now, its art made when it first shows": add a build that throws once and expect a second show to build).

- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:1673-1680

  `local dragon = self.opts.dragon and crest.dragonArt(c, boss and boss(u) or nil)` and

If either happens in combat, `UpdateIdentity` errors on every identity event and every `Refresh`: Fault catches it, but the function stops before the meta text, the "you" badge and `LayoutRow`, and `Refresh` (lines 2211-2214) never reaches `UpdateHealth`, `UpdatePower` and `UpdateRaidMarker`.

Probe: `UnitClassification("target")` and `UnitIsBossMob("target")` on a hostile elite in dungeon combat.

#### HUD-UF-6: A unit change rebuilds every listener of the frame, and the frame is redrawn two or three times
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)

The target, focus, pet and boss frames' few game listeners are still made on each `Activate`)
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:2097-2127 (`SetUnit`), 2217-2365 (`Activate`), 2367-2386 (`Deactivate`);
  src/Core/Events.wowlua (what one `onUnit` allocates); src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1214-1236 (the header
  hook: `btn:Activate()` then `btn:Refresh()`)
- known: no
- what: `SetUnit` on an active frame calls `Deactivate()` and then `Activate()`, which creates 17 listener closures (the theme message, 4 health, 3 power, 4 identity, connection, 4 game events), and for each the bus adds an entry table, a guard closure, a unit list and a subscription. `Activate` ends with `self:Refresh()`. The raid header's hook then does
  `if not btn.active then btn:Activate() end  btn:Refresh()` (RaidFrames.wowlua:1237-1240), a second full redraw, and the frame's own `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` listener calls `Refresh` a third time for the same roster change (UnitFrame.wowlua:2281-2286). Each `Refresh` runs `FitRow` → `LayoutRow` and then `UpdateIdentity` → `LayoutRow` again.
- why it matters: a raid header re-assigns many buttons at once (someone joins or leaves, sorting by role, a sub-group move), also in combat. With 40 buttons that is some 2,700 short-lived objects and up to 120 full redraws in one frame: a hitch at the moment the raid changes.
- fix: keep the listeners for the frame's life and re-point them: the stdlib has `watchUnit` with `setUnit(unit)` "without subscribing again" (wowlua `std/events.wowlua`); expose it through `/Core/Events` with an owner and Fault reporting, register the unit events on one watch per frame with methods rather than closures, and have `SetUnit` call `watch:setUnit(unit)`. The unit-specific game events (target, focus, pet, boss) only need re-registering when the unit's kind changes. Drop the `Refresh` at the end of `Activate` when `SetUnit` called it and the caller refreshes, or drop the caller's `btn:Refresh()`.

- category: performance

  src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1952-1985
- known: no
- what: every active frame registers its own `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` and `PLAYER_ROLES_ASSIGNED` listeners. A party or raid frame answers the first with `self:Refresh()` (identity, row layout twice, health, power, marker); every other frame (player, target, focus, pet, target of target, the boss frames) with `UpdateIdentity()` + `UpdatePower()`. Separately each `UnitAuras` created for a `party`/`raid` unit registers its own `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` listener that calls `UpdateAllAuras`, and `RaidFrames` then rescans the containers again by hand (`auras:Refresh()`, every dispel container, every indicator container) and calls `UpdateIndicatorPresence` on every button.

- fix: one roster listener per module (or one in this file for all frames), coalesced to the next frame (`timer.after(0)` with a pending flag), which redraws the frames whose unit exists; drop the per-frame `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`/`PLAYER_ROLES_ASSIGNED` listeners for units that cannot change with the roster. #### HUD-UF-8: An aura container chooses its rescan event once, at construction, and parked indicator containers keep theirs
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Auras.wowlua:623-659 (constructor), 664-673 (`SetUnit`), 679-691 (`Release`), 886-900
  (`listen`); src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:959, 1901-1904, 1932-1936, 1949, 2190;
  src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1952-1972 (the hand-written container rescans)
- known: no
- what: `listen(unit)` runs in the constructor and when a released container comes back; a plain `SetUnit` never re-evaluates it:
  ```
  self.unit = unit
  pcall(self.container.SetUnit, self.container, unit)
  if self.released then … self:listen(unit) … end
  self:Refresh()
  ```
  So the rescan event belongs to the unit the container was created with:
  - created with `"none"` (a raid button's containers: `f.unit or "none"`, the header gives the unit later) → never rescans on `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` by itself; `RaidFrames` works around it with explicit `Refresh` calls (1946-1965);
  - created later with a unit set (an indicator added in the settings, a dispel set built on the first switch to "removable") → does listen, and is rescanned twice;
  - created for `target` and pointed elsewhere → keeps rescanning on `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED` and gets none for its new unit.
  `UnitFrame.SetIndicators` parks unused containers with `c.container:Hide(); c:SetUnit("none")` instead of `c:Release()`, so each parked container keeps its roster listener (and the engine rescan it triggers) for the session.
- why it matters: identical containers behave differently by creation order, the module has to know and compensate (a `UnitFrame` user that does not, such as a plugin's group frames through `SuuUI.UI.UnitFrame`, shows the previous person's debuff border after the roster changes until the next aura event), and listeners pile up with every indicator edit.
- fix: in `UnitAuras.SetUnit`, when the unit's rescan event differs from `self.rescan`, `events.off` the old one and `listen(unit)` for the new one (for `"none"`: no listener). In `UnitFrame.SetIndicators` park with `c:Release()` and let `SetUnit` revive (it already shows the container). Then remove the hand-written container rescans in RaidFrames.wowlua:1954-1964. Tests: tests/unit/UI/Auras.test.wowlua (`events.bus:count(c)` after `SetUnit("raid1")` on a container made with `"none"`, and after parking).

#### HUD-UF-9: Each group frame's decoration containers build all ten engine buttons' decorations up front
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: likely (that the engine makes and initializes ten buttons per group up front is stated twice in NEW's Auras.wowlua; the count was not measured for these containers)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:951-971 (four containers per dispel set, up to two sets), 2132-2153
  (`DispelDecoration`), 1002-1023 (`WardDecoration`), 2186-2199 (ward slot), 1937-1968 (one container per
  indicator), 2157-2165 (the unused set stays bound); src/UI/Auras.wowlua:517-536, 902-905, 914
- known: no (the cost is noted for the standard icons only)
- what: Auras.wowlua now says "The engine makes every button of a group up front (ten), most never shown" and defers its own buttons' art to their first show. That deferral is only in `makeInitializer`; a group with its own `initialize` is handed to the engine as it is (`local init = group.initialize or makeInitializer(…)`), and the unit frame's containers all use one:
  `local init = function(button: AuraButton) quietButton(button) f:DispelDecoration(button, kind) end`.
  Every one of them has `max = 1`. So per raid frame and per dispel set the engine runs `DispelDecoration` 40 times (a frame, a four-texture border, a state badge, a `measureText`), `WardDecoration` 10 times (two frames, a border, a badge, a shadow), and an `indicatorLook` 10 times per square, border or fill indicator; only one button of each group can ever show. - fix: probe which button the engine shows for a `max = 1` group (count the `init` calls and note the index of the button that shows). If it is always the first one made, decorate only that one (`quietButton` for the rest); otherwise defer the decoration to the button's first show as `makeInitializer` does, subject to HUD-UF-15's probe (decorations must exist before a fight). Also: build "removable" as a type list on one set (HUD-UF-1) instead of a second set, unbind the unused set (`SetUnit("none")`) if two remain, and keep only the badge of a button that can show in `edgeBadges`.

#### HUD-CD-2: Pool keys hold everything about a container, so settings edits leak engine containers and cells for good
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the growth; likely for the fix (the live setters exist, their behaviour on a parked-and-revived container is unprobed)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker/Pool.wowlua:17-40 (`containerKey`), 57-70 (`Take`);
  src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:300-309 (`Aura`), 343 (cell key `"cell|" .. size`), 363-389 (effect
  container), 417-424 (slot key), 594-625 with 635-708 (packed containers, group keys `"b" .. i`, `"p" .. i`,
  `"d" .. i`); src/UI/Auras.wowlua:729-830 (`SetGroupSize`, `SetGroupMax`, `SetGroupFilter`,
  `SetGroupSpells`), 902-905; src/Units/CooldownManager.wowlua:584-586 (`WatchAll` rebuild on `essentialSize`)
- known: no
- what: `containerKey` concatenates the unit, size, anchor, growth and, per group, `g.key`, the filter, `g.max`, every included spell ID, dispel types, border, glow, drain, digits, stacks, expiring and size. `Pool:Take` (1420-1432) reuses a spare only under the identical key, and the comment at 1372-1377 says "an engine aura container can never be freed". So any edit that changes one of those values (a rank added to an entry, source, border, max, size, or the order of packed entries, whose group keys are `"b" .. i`, `"p" .. i`, `"d" .. i` by list position) makes a new engine container and parks the old one for the session. The packed containers have one group per entry, and `src/UI/Auras.wowlua:902` records "The engine makes ten buttons for every group up front", so one edit to a list with 12 packed entries strands a container with about 120 buttons. Cells are keyed by size alone (`self.cellPool:Take("cell|" .. size, …)`), and an effect container's key contains `size`; the caller rebuilds on every `essentialSize` change (`self:WatchAll({ "setups", "essentialSize", … }, function() self:Apply() end)`), so every size value applied creates a full set of cells plus an effect container per cell with an effect.
- why it matters: memory and frame count grow without bound during a settings session (each control change in the Behaviour panel is a rebuild), and none of it comes back until `/reload`. Released containers are hidden and deaf, but their buttons exist.
- fix: key pools by what cannot change after creation and set the rest on reuse. `UnitAuras` has `SetUnit`, `SetGroupSpells(key, ids)`, `SetGroupFilter(key, filter)`, `SetGroupMax(key, n)` and `SetGroupSize(key, size)`. Slots and effect containers (fixed group keys "e", "e2", "fx"): key by the number of groups and the looks the initializer bakes in (border, glow, drain, digits, stacks, expiring, `warn`), then on Take call the setters (and resize the slot frame for `max`). Packed containers: key by anchor, growth and number of groups, name groups by ordinal ("g1".."gN") instead of list position, reconfigure each on reuse; baked-in looks become a per-group sub-key or get a live setter in `UnitAuras`. Cells: one pool; `SetSize` the cell and its icon on Take and set the countdown font again. Probe first that the engine's candidate and filter setters take effect on a parked-and-revived container (`/suu probe`); the rebuild is out of combat anyway. Test in `tests/unit/UI/CooldownTracker.test.wowlua`: editing an entry's ids and rebuilding does not raise the number of containers made.

#### HUD-CD-3: UNIT_AURA rescans up to 40 auras per reminder, unthrottled, and for the wrong unit
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:1038-1047 (handler), 791-810 (`UpdateReminders`);
  src/UI/CooldownTracker/Slots.wowlua:194-209 (`auraUp`)
- known: no
- what: the handler is registered for both units and ignores which one fired:
  ```
  events.onUnit("UNIT_AURA", { "player", "target" }, function()
      if not (t.inFight or InCombatLockdown()) then
          t:UpdateReminders()
      end
  end, t)
  ```
  `UpdateReminders` allocates a `ctx` table and an `update` closure per call (also with no reminders at all), then for each reminder calls `auraUp`, which per check walks `for i = 1, counted and 40 or 0 do local ok, a = pcall(C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDataByIndex, r.unit, i, check.filter)` (an aura table per call) until the list ends. A target's aura event rescans every buff reminder on the player; a player's aura event rescans the target for every debuff reminder. Several `UNIT_AURA` in one frame each run the full scan.
- why it matters: out of combat in a city or raid with a buffed target, `UNIT_AURA` fires constantly; with R reminders and B auras that is R x B aura-table reads per event. Out of combat only, so it costs smoothness while buffing and travelling, not in fights.
- fix: return at once when `#self.built.remindBuffs + #self.built.remindDebuffs == 0`; pass the event's unit and update only that unit's list; coalesce with a flag handled in the driver's OnUpdate (`self.remindDirty[unit] = true`); scan each unit once per pass into a reused set of readable spell IDs per filter string (at most three: plain, `|PLAYER`, `|!PLAYER`) and test every reminder against that set. Test in `tests/unit/UI/CooldownTracker.test.wowlua`: N `UNIT_AURA` events in a frame make one scan per unit.

- severity: medium

- confidence: confirmed (from code)

#### HUD-CD-5: "Only yours" / "only others'" splits (PLAYER, !PLAYER) on the target contradict what was probed for player targets

So on a mob the split holds for others' debuffs, as IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md recorded on 2026-10-12; the 2026-10-16 rule ("`X` and `!X` alike") is about other players' auras on players. In fights the probe's reads failed ("Auras cannot be accessed when secret while tainted", 2,212 times), so the answer is from reads out of combat, through plain `C_UnitAuras` calls, not an engine group with a spell list. Still waiting for own debuffs on a mob (`Docs/plans/open-probes.md`).
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker/Slots.wowlua:214-223 (`sourceFilter`), 233-270 (`auraParts`: one engine group
  per source in the same slot); src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:374 (effect filter), 442-457 (reminders use the

- what: an entry's source maps to a filter:
  ```
  if source == "mine" then return { kind, "PLAYER" } end
  if source == "others" then return { kind, "!PLAYER" } end
  return { kind }
  ```
  and a shared slot whose members have different sources gets one engine group per source, all in the same slot. The debuff side and `effect = "target"` (`filter = { fx == "player" and "HELPFUL" or "HARMFUL", "PLAYER" }`) always use the unit `target`.
- why it matters: when the target is another player (PvP, duels, a friendly target for a "target" effect), the probe says auras on them have a hidden caster and pass PLAYER and !PLAYER alike. Then "your debuffs on the target" slots show other players' debuffs of the same spells as yours; a slot with members of both sources shows one aura twice (two engine groups, each with the slot's max, overflowing the slot's width); a reminder with an "others" member reads as up regardless of caster. The spell lists limit this to tracked spells. On NPC targets the 2026-10-12 observation says the split works.
- fix: probe first (on a hostile player target and on a mob: which of `HARMFUL|PLAYER`, `HARMFUL|!PLAYER` a tracked debuff from you and from someone else passes). If player targets fail as recorded: on `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED`, when `UnitIsPlayer("target")` is known true, set the `!PLAYER` groups of target containers to max 0 for slots that also have a PLAYER group (the `liveGroups` mechanism does this kind of switch), and say in the editor that "only others'" cannot be told apart on player targets. Record the outcome in `Docs/wowlua-port-notes.md` either way.

#### HUD-CD-6: Aura sounds are module-level state shared by every tracker

- known: no

#### HUD-DM-1: The spell breakdown indexes a secret `combatSpells` table
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- status: withdrawn (not a problem on this client for your own source: in 2 fights its `combatSpells` was never secret; `RefreshSpells` still has no secret guard, one line should a later client change this)
- probe (2026-11-15, build 70888): your own damage meter source's `combatSpells` was never secret in combat, in 2 fights.
- where: src/UI/DamageMeter.wowlua:1190-1199 (compare `RefreshList`, 1121-1125)
- known: no (`Docs/test-notes/ui-hud.md:95` records the same bug as fixed for the list only)
- what: `RefreshSpells` guards with
  `if not data or not spells or (not isSecret(spells) and #spells == 0) then self:ShowEmpty("No spells to show.") return end`.
  A secret `spells` passes that guard, and line 1199 then runs
  `local top: number | Secret<number> = ps and spells[1].amountPerSecond or spells[1].totalAmount`.
  Indexing a secret table is an error. `RefreshList` in the same file handles it:
  `if isSecret(sources) then self:ShowEmpty("The list is secret until combat ends.") return end`
  (1122-1125), and `RefreshRecap` does the same with `issecrettable(given)` (1259-1262). `RefreshSpells` is the only view without it.
- why it matters: your own row is always openable in combat (`local guid = you and UnitGUID("player") or src.sourceGUID`, 1086-1088). If the client hands back `combatSpells` as a secret table in combat, clicking your row raises a Lua error, and again every second from the module's refresh while the window stays drilled in. Whether the client ever does that is the open question; the two sibling views guard against it.
- fix: after fetching, `if isSecret(spells) then self:ShowEmpty("The breakdown is secret until combat ends.") return end`, then the plain `not data or not spells or #spells == 0` check. Add a test next to the list's secret test in `tests/unit/UI/DamageMeter.test.wowlua` (a source whose `combatSpells = mock.secret({})`). Probe in combat: `issecretvalue(C_DamageMeter.GetCombatSessionSourceFromType(Enum.DamageMeterSessionType.Current, Enum.DamageMeterType.DamageDone, UnitGUID("player")).combatSpells)`.

#### HUD-DM-2: The saved totem set is dropped for the session if its Call spell is not known yet at the first Refresh
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- status: open (unverified: needs a cold-login probe of `knows(SUMMONS[2])` when the totem bar is built)
- where: src/UI/ClassBars.wowlua:956 (`self.page, self.onPage = opts.page or 1, opts.onPage`), 1050
  (`self:Refresh()` in the constructor), 1095-1097 (`Refresh` overwrites `self.page`);
  src/Units/ActionBars.wowlua:940-948
- known: no
- what: the module builds the bar with the character's saved page (`page = type(saved) == "number" and saved or 1`, ActionBars.wowlua:926) and the constructor calls `self:Refresh()` at once. `Refresh` does
  `if self.page ~= 1 and not knows(SUMMONS[self.page]) then self.page = 1 end`.
  That overwrites the only in-memory copy of the wanted page. Later `SPELLS_CHANGED` / `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` refreshes see `self.page == 1` and keep it. `onPage` is not called, so `char.totemPage` still holds 2 or 3 and the same thing repeats at the next login.
- why it matters: a shaman who chose Call of the Ancestors or Spirits. If the spellbook answers false when the module enables (a cold login, before the first `SPELLS_CHANGED`), the bar shows and casts set 1 for the whole session while the saved setting says otherwise. After a `/reload` it may work, which makes it look random.
- fix: keep the wanted page apart from the page in use: a field `wanted` set in the constructor (`opts.page or 1`) and in `SetPage`; in `Refresh`, `self.page = (self.wanted == 1 or knows(SUMMONS[self.wanted])) and self.wanted or 1`. Add a case to the pages test in `tests/unit/UI/ClassBars.test.wowlua`: not known at the first Refresh, known at a later `SPELLS_CHANGED`, the page comes back. Probe: log `knows(SUMMONS[2])` in the constructor on a cold login.

#### HUD-DM-3: The totem bar redraws everything on each cooldown and usable event, uncoalesced; the stance bar still updates ten buttons for classes without forms
- severity: medium
- category: performance

- known: no
- what:

    `self.known = #elementSpells(self.element.slot) > 0`, and `elementSpells` is
    `local ok, list = pcall(function(): number[] return { G.GetMultiCastTotemSpells(slot) } end)`: a closure, a `pcall` and a new table, only to learn "more than zero". Then `ShowSpellCooldown`, `IsSpellUsable`, `ShowEmptyLook` (a loop over the 16 dashes with `draw.paintFill` and `SetAlpha` each), `ShowActive`, `count:SetText`, `UpdateHotkey`, `UpdateEmpty`. `UpdateAll` ends with `self:UpdateTimers()`, which for all four slots calls `pcall(G.GetTotemDuration, …)`, `totemIsChosen` and `SetTimerDuration` plus the text binding's `SetDuration`/`SetEnabled` again, although no totem changed.
  - `StanceBar` is made for every class. Its coalesced `UpdateAll` (ClassBar's, 186-190) still runs `StanceButton.Update` on all `SLOTS` buttons once per frame in which `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN`, `ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` or a shapeshift event fired: for an empty slot that is `GetShapeshiftFormInfo`, `art:Hide`, `cooldown:Clear`, `ShowActive`, `ShowUsable`, `count:SetText`, `UpdateHotkey`, `UpdateEmpty`, whether the class has forms, the bar is enabled or the header is shown. (`UpdateState` does return early for empty slots.)
- why it matters: these events fire together on every cast, several times a second in combat. The stance bar's own comment records what the same pattern cost before it was coalesced ("58,000 updates and 19 MB of garbage in five minutes"); a shaman's totem bar still pays it per event: 4 closures, 4 tables and 4 `pcall`s of garbage plus four timer re-sets, on each of three or four events per cast. - fix:
  1. Give `TotemBar` the stance bar's flusher (a hidden frame whose `OnUpdate` runs the due pass once; lift the one in `StanceBar`'s constructor, 261-285, into a small shared helper in this file and use it for both).
  2. `TotemButton.Update`: take `known` from a field set in `Refresh` (which already walks `elementSpells` per slot at 1100-1102) instead of calling `elementSpells` per update.
  3. Take `UpdateTimers` out of `UpdateAll` for the cooldown/usable events; `PLAYER_TOTEM_UPDATE`, `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`, `Refresh` and the picker paths call it (keep it for `ACTIONBAR_SLOT_CHANGED`, which changes what `totemIsChosen` compares).
  4. In `ShowEmptyLook`, return when `hasAction` did not change since the last call (keep the paint in `Layout` after `Resize`, where the comment at 1166 puts it).
  5. In `StanceBar`, update only the first `self.count` buttons (clear the rest once in `UpdateForms`) and skip the pass when `not self.enabled` or the count is 0.
  Tests: `tests/unit/UI/ClassBars.test.wowlua` (three cooldown events in a frame make one totem pass; with no forms an event calls `GetShapeshiftFormInfo` zero times).

#### HUD-DM-4: Every pet UNIT_AURA rewrites 20 secure attributes, with a string and a global lookup per button
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)

- where: src/UI/ClassBars.wowlua:464-496 (`all` and what calls it, `UNIT_AURA` of the pet at 489), 513-527

- known: no
- what: `all()` is `self:UpdateAll(); self:UpdateAutocastClicks()` and is bound to `PET_BAR_UPDATE`, `PET_UI_UPDATE`, `PET_BAR_UPDATE_USABLE`, `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD`, the control events, `UNIT_PET`, and

  `UpdateAutocastClicks` goes through `combat.run("classbar:autocast:" .. self.name, function() … end, "Action bars")`. Out of combat it runs, for each of the ten buttons,

Dragging a settings slider that writes a CVar runs `lock` per step.

- what: `Tick` runs every frame while the timer is shown, for all three rows, and builds a `"%.1f"` string per live row per frame; `Text:SetValue` then drops it when equal (src/UI/Text.wowlua:69-71), so the value reaches the game ten times a second but the string is made every frame. With "always" visibility `Tick` also runs out of combat with no live row.
- why it matters: one or two string formats per frame for the whole fight; small, but it is the widget's only per-frame Lua work and easy to remove.
- fix: keep the last shown tenth per row (`local tenth = math.floor(left * 10)`; format only when it changes), and set the `OnUpdate` script only while a row is live or flashing (`Swing` sets it; `Tick` clears it when no row is live and no `flashAt` is left).

#### HUD-12: Buttons pop and flash "ready" when a hidden bar shows, for cooldowns that ended while it was hidden
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/ActionBar.wowlua:416-426 (the cooldown pass skips buttons that are not visible),
  src/UI/ActionButton.wowlua:236-241 (`OnShow` reads the stale cooldown), 433-438 (`ShowCooldown`: the pop and
  flash)
- known: no
- what: since the cooldown pass skips hidden buttons (`else b.cooldownStale = true`), a hidden button keeps `self.coolingDown = true` from its last read. When it shows, the hook runs `self:UpdateCooldown()`, and `ShowCooldown` sees
  `if self.coolingDown and not active then motion.pop(self.face); self.flash:SetAlpha(1); motion.alphaTo(self.flash, 0, T.duration["dur-slow"]) end`,
  the "came off cooldown just now" effect.
- why it matters: a bar set to "In combat" (a secure visibility driver, src/UI/Visibility.wowlua:53, so its buttons are truly hidden out of combat): cooldowns used in one fight end between fights; at the next pull the bar appears and every such button pops and flashes at once, although they have been ready for minutes. The same on a bar the player turns back on. Before this change the effect played unseen while hidden.
- fix: in the `OnShow` hook, when `cooldownStale` is set, clear `self.coolingDown` (and `self.onGCD`) before `self:UpdateCooldown()`, or give `UpdateCooldown`/`ShowCooldown` a `quiet` flag that skips the pop. Test in tests/unit/UI/ActionButton.test.wowlua: cooling down → hide → cooldown ends → cooldown pass → show: `flash:GetAlpha() == 0`.

#### HUD-10: A digit font object is created for every distinct action text size and never reused for another size
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/ActionButton.wowlua:110-124 (`digitFont`), 603-614 (`SetTextSize`), 140-150 (the theme handler
  re-sets every one)
- known: no
- what: `digitFont(px)` creates a global `Font` named `"SuuUIActionDigits" .. key` per size (to a tenth of a pixel: `local key = math.floor(px * 10 + 0.5)`) and keeps it in `digitFonts` for the session.
- why it matters: font objects cannot be freed. Dragging the text size setting creates one per value passed through. Bounded by the setting's range, so a small permanent cost.
- fix: every button uses the same `actionTextSize`, so one shared font object is enough: keep a single `SuuUIActionDigits` font and call `SetFont` on it when the size changes; or, if bars may differ, round the key to whole pixels.

#### HUD-11: Resizing an action button abandons its autocast dash textures and creates new ones
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/ActionButton.wowlua:493-507 (`Resize`), 510-541 (`ShowAutocast`)
- known: no
- what: `Resize` hides every texture in `self.dashes`, sets `self.dashes = nil`, and, if autocast is on, calls `ShowAutocast(true)`, which creates a full new set (`self.over:CreateTexture(nil, "OVERLAY", nil, 2)` per dash, four edges, one dash every 4 px). The old textures stay on the frame, hidden, for the session.
- why it matters: textures cannot be freed. Each step of the pet bar's size setting leaves about `size - 4` dead textures per autocasting pet button. Bounded by how often the size is changed, so a small permanent cost.
- fix: keep the textures and re-place them: in `ShowAutocast`, reuse `self.dashes[i]` in order (`ClearAllPoints`, `SetPoint`), create only the ones missing for a larger size and hide the surplus for a smaller one; `Resize` then calls that placing step without dropping the list. Test: tests/unit/UI/ActionButton.test.wowlua (the region count of `b.over` does not grow over two resizes).

#### HUD-UF-16: A deferred aura button is built outside the pixel-unit scope its container was made in
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the lost scope; likely for the visible effect
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Auras.wowlua:908-929 (`addGroup`'s wrapper), 520-536 (the deferral), 395 and 409
  (`draw.border` in `build`); src/UI/Draw.wowlua:1067-1090 (`scoped`, `withPixelUnit`, `pixelUnit`), 1125
  (`self.unit = scoped`), 1141-1143, 1680-1688
- known: no
- what: a container remembers the pixel unit it was made under (`self.pixelUnit = draw.pixelUnit()`, a nameplate's) and wraps the initializer so the buttons' lines take it:
  ```
  init = function(button: AuraButton)
      draw.withPixelUnit(unit, function()
          build(button)
      end)
  end
  ```
  Here `build` is the function `makeInitializer` returns, which for a hidden button only sizes it and hooks `OnShow`. The real `build` (which calls `draw.border`) runs later from that hook, after `withPixelUnit` has restored `scoped` to nil, so `Border.unit` is nil for every button that was hidden when the engine made it, which is nearly all of them.
- why it matters: such a border is laid with `pixel.size(self.frame)` at the moment it first shows instead of the plate's fixed unit, and is not in the "has a unit of its own" group that the `SUUUI_ROOT_SCALED` handler leaves alone (Draw.wowlua:1684: `if not b.unit then pcall(b.Layout, b) end`). The fixed unit was added because nameplate debuff borders "came out under one pixel and vanished" when laid at another scale; for lazily built buttons that protection is not in effect.
- fix: capture the unit where the deferral is made: in the function `makeInitializer` returns, `local unit = draw.pixelUnit()` at call time, and in the `OnShow` hook `draw.withPixelUnit(unit, function() build(button) end)` (or do the same once in `addGroup` by passing the unit into `makeInitializer`). Test in tests/unit/UI/Auras.test.wowlua: a container made inside `withPixelUnit(u, …)`, a hidden button shown later, expect its `StyledButton.edges[1].unit == u`.

#### HUD-UF-5: Power events wake every frame, including those that never show a power line
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:1042, 2237-2241 (registration), 1554-1595 (`UpdatePower`);
  src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:85-99 (`powerFor`)
- known: no
- what: `Activate` registers `UNIT_POWER_UPDATE`, `UNIT_MAXPOWER` and `UNIT_DISPLAYPOWER` for every frame. `UpdatePower` then decides:
  `if not u or self.offline or self.opts.power == false or (powerFor and not powerFor(u, A)) then self.power:Hide() self.powerLow:Hide() self.powerSpend:Hide() return end`.
  For raid frames `powerFor` reads a setting (`M:Get("power")`) and the unit's role on every call. When the line shows, each event reads `UnitPowerType`, `UnitPowerMax`, `UnitPower`, sets the range and value (twice for mana) and evaluates a curve.
- why it matters: `UNIT_POWER_UPDATE` fires for every rage, energy and mana tick. In a raid whose power setting is "tanks and healers" or "none", 30 to 40 frames handle every tick only to hide three bars that are already hidden.
- fix: register the power events only when the line can show (`opts.power ~= false`; for `powerFor` frames re-evaluate on `Refresh`/roster/role changes and register or drop the three events). In `UpdatePower`, set the range and colour only from `UNIT_DISPLAYPOWER`/`UNIT_MAXPOWER`/`Refresh`/a cast-cost change; on `UNIT_POWER_UPDATE` only set the value(s) and the low-mana alpha.

#### HUD-UF-10: UpdateIndicatorPresence allocates per call and walks the raid per frame
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:2009-2074, 680-701 (`inYourGroup`); callers
  src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1976-1980, 2015-2025, src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:1464, 1491-1509
- known: no
- what: called for a unit on each of its `UNIT_AURA` events out of combat, and for every frame on each `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`. Each call creates the `inScope` closure; for each "missing" indicator it builds a set of the spell IDs (`local set: { [number]: boolean } = {}` …) and reads up to 40 auras through `pcall(C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDataByIndex, u, i, filter)`, each a new table. An indicator limited to "my group" calls `inYourGroup`, which walks the raid with `A.UnitIsUnit("raid" .. i, "player")` to find the player: for 40 frames up to 1,600 calls and string concatenations per roster update. All of this also runs when the frame has no missing look and no group- or role-limited indicator.
- why it matters: out of combat only; but buffing a raid before a pull raises `UNIT_AURA` constantly and each event pays this on its frame, and the roster path is quadratic.
- fix: return at once when `#self.missingLooks == 0` and no indicator in use has `on == "group"` or roles (compute the flags in `SetIndicators`, next to `roleLimited`); build each indicator's ID set once in `SetIndicators` and keep it on the `MissingLook`; find the player's sub-group once per roster update (a cached value in this file, invalidated by the roster event) and pass it in.

#### HUD-UF-11: The indicator, missing-look and preview caches only grow
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:656-669 (`indicatorKey`), 1894-1972 (`SetIndicators`), 2076-2095
  (`SetPreviewIndicators`)
- known: no
- what: `indicatorCache`, `missingCache` and `previewCache` are keyed by the indicator's whole look (kind, point, size, colour, source, spell IDs; for the missing look also the mode and colour). Any change to one of them makes a new engine container (or frame) on every group frame and keeps the old one ("The engine never frees a container"). Most of the key is not needed: size, point and colour are properties of the look, and `SetGroupSpells` / `SetGroupFilter` exist for the spell list and the source.
- why it matters: editing indicators during a session (trying sizes, colours, corners) leaves a container with its ten buttons and their looks (HUD-UF-9) behind per step and per frame, 40 times over in a raid, until the next reload.
- fix: reuse by kind and position in the list instead of by look: one container per indicator slot and kind, re-pointed with `SetGroupSpells`, `SetGroupFilter` and (for icons, out of combat) `SetGroupSize` and a new anchor; for squares, borders and fills keep the look frame on the cache entry and restyle it. Park the rest with `Release()` (HUD-UF-8).

#### HUD-UF-13: The unit recorded for plugins never follows SetUnit
- severity: low

#### HUD-UF-14: The row is laid out twice per Refresh, with temporary tables and a closure each time
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:1717-1805 (`LayoutRow`), 1842-1856 (`FitRow`), 2202-2215 (`Refresh`),
  1826-1840 (`SetState`)
- known: no
- what: `LayoutRow` allocates `{ self.role, self.classDot }`, the `badges` list and (for small frames or a secret name) the `place` closure, measures the meta text and re-anchors the name, meta and badges, whether or not anything changed. `Refresh` calls `FitRow`, which re-anchors the row and the health text and calls `LayoutRow`, and then `UpdateIdentity`, which calls `LayoutRow` again. It also runs from every identity event, each roster/role event per frame, and `SetState` when the aggro state flips.
- why it matters: not a per-frame cost by itself, but it multiplies with HUD-UF-6 and HUD-UF-7 (40 frames, up to three `Refresh` per roster event, two layouts each) and with threat flips on a tank swap.
- fix: call `FitRow` from the constructor, `Resize`, `PlaceByTheme` and the option setters only, not from `Refresh`; cache `LayoutRow`'s inputs on the frame (marker, meta text, whether the state badge and "you" show, whether the name is secret, row width) and return early when none changed.

#### HUD-CD-1: The usability pass still runs for every cell on almost every frame in combat, also while the tracker is hidden
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the size of the cost needs an in-game measure
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:1005-1037 (what marks which flag), 266-293 (driver), 845-859
  (`UpdateCooldowns`); src/UI/CooldownTracker/Cell.wowlua:138-223 (`TrackerCell:Update`), 227-240
  (`ReadCooldown`); src/UI/Icon.wowlua:57-70; src/UI/Draw.wowlua:181-185
- known: no (`src/Diagnostics/GarbageProbe.wowlua:106` measures `CooldownTracker:UpdateCooldowns`)
- what changed: the pass is now split. `SPELL_UPDATE_USABLE`, `ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_USABLE`, `UNIT_POWER_FREQUENT` (player) and `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED` set `usableDirty`, and the driver then runs `UpdateCooldowns(nil, true)`: `Update(opts, light)` keeps the last `onCooldown` and skips `ReadCooldown`, so no cooldown table and no duration object are made on power events. `Draw`'s `keep` now returns early when the kind, token and alpha are the ones already kept (`if p and kind ~= "gradient" and p.kind == kind and p.token == token and p.alpha == alpha then return p end`), so an unchanged `border:SetColor(token)` is four table lookups instead of four repaints.
- what remains: the light pass still runs on practically every frame in combat (`UNIT_POWER_FREQUENT`), for every cell, and applies everything undiffed: `C_Spell.IsSpellUsable(id)`, then `self.icon:SetBorder(…)`, `self.icon:SetState(…)` (which calls `self.art:SetDesaturated(dim)` and `self.art:SetVertexColor(…)` every time, and `border:SetColor` a second time), `SetGlow`, `self.pulse:IsPlaying()`, `self.ring:SetShown(useNow)` and `self:SetAlpha(alpha)`: about 20 calls per cell per frame for a state that changes a few times a second. The full pass (`SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN`, `SPELL_UPDATE_CHARGES`, `UPDATE_SHAPESHIFT_FORM`, a cell's `OnCooldownDone`) still makes a table and a duration object per cell and calls `SetCooldownFromDurationObject` again for a cooldown the cell already shows; `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` comes several times per cast. The driver is its own frame (comment at 1526-1528), so all of it runs while the tracker is hidden or faded out.
- why it matters: with 15 to 20 cells that is 300 to 400 widget calls per frame in combat with no visible effect, and 30 to 40 short-lived objects per cooldown event. No longer a likely frame-time problem by itself; it is steady waste on the hottest path of the widget.
- fix: (1) keep the cell's look and apply only on change: compute one key (for example `"cd-grey"`, `"cd-dim"`, `"useNow"`, `"unsure"`, `"rest|" .. border .. "|" .. ready`) plus the alpha, store them on the cell, and skip `SetBorder`/`SetState`/`SetGlow`/`ring:SetShown`/`SetAlpha` when both are equal (reset the stored key in `CooldownTracker:Cell`, 1608). (2) Throttle the light pass to about 10 per second (accumulate `elapsed` in the driver). (3) In `ReadCooldown`, remember `active`/`gcd` and call `SetCooldownFromDurationObject` only on a transition or when `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` marked the pass (not for `UPDATE_SHAPESHIFT_FORM` or `OnCooldownDone` of another cell). Test in `tests/unit/UI/CooldownTracker.test.wowlua`: a second `UNIT_POWER_FREQUENT` with unchanged state calls no setter on the cell's art (count `SetDesaturated`).

#### HUD-CD-7: A shared slot whose members all override the source the same way gets the slot's source instead
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker/Slots.wowlua:233-270
- known: no
- what: `auraParts` builds one part per distinct member source (`local source = m.source or own`), then returns
  `return (#out > 1 or (first and first.when)) and out or single`,
  where `single` is `{ { filter = sourceFilter(kind, entry, default), ids = entry.ids or {} } }`, built from the group's own source (`entry.source or (entry.group and "mine")` in `sourceFilter`).
- why it matters: a group with `source` unset or "mine" whose members all carry `source = "others"` (or all "any") yields exactly one part, with the members' filter and no live `when`, so `single` is returned and the engine group filters by PLAYER: the slot never shows the auras its members asked for. The file header says a member's own source wins.
- fix: return `out` whenever `#out >= 1` (it holds the right filter and the deduplicated ids) and `single` only when `out` is empty. Test: a group with one member `{ source = "others" }` builds a slot whose group filter is `HELPFUL|!PLAYER`.

#### HUD-CD-8: The ready pop and sound fire for cells that are not shown, and possibly when a cooldown read turns secret
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for hidden cells; needs in-game probe for the secret case
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker/Cell.wowlua:147-161 (pop and sound), 172-185 (visibility decided afterwards),
  30-37 (`cooldownFlags`)
- known: no
- what: `if was and not onCooldown then … self.icon:Pop() … if e.sound then trackerSound(e.sound) end end` runs before `self.wantShown = want and self.condOK ~= false` is computed, and looks at neither `condOK` nor `e.show`/`e.unusable`. `cooldownFlags` returns `false, false` when the info table is secret (`if issecretvalue(info) or not info then return false, false end`) and `known(info.isActive, false)` for a secret field, so a cell on cooldown whose next full read is secret looks like "came ready". (The light pass keeps the previous `onCooldown`, so this can only happen on a full pass.)
- why it matters: a cooldown with a stance or combat condition plays its ready sound while the cell is hidden by that condition (Overpower with a battle-stance condition coming off cooldown in defensive stance); a cell with `unusable = "hide"` likewise. If the client ever returns a secret cooldown read mid-cooldown, every such cell pops and plays its sound then, and again when it really ends.
- fix: compute `want` first and gate the pop and sound on it (`if was and not onCooldown and want and self.condOK ~= false`). Make `cooldownFlags` return a third value "unknown" and keep the previous `onCooldown` in that case. Test: a cell with `condOK == false` coming ready does not call `trackerSound`.

#### HUD-CD-9: An effect's aura stays at a closed-up cell's old place
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: likely
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:359-389 (the effect container hangs on the tracker, anchored to the
  cell); src/UI/CooldownTracker/Layout.wowlua:44-52 (which cells keep their place);
  src/UI/CooldownTracker/Cell.wowlua:181-183 (`unusable == "hide"`), 175-177 (`show == "cooldown"`)
- known: no
- what: the effect's container is anchored to the cell (`c:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", f, "TOPLEFT")`), and `Layout` keeps a hidden cell in its row only when
  `f.condOK ~= false and (f:IsShown() or (f.container ~= nil and f.onCooldown == true))`.
  A cell hidden for another reason (not usable with `unusable = "hide"`, or `show = "cooldown"` while ready) leaves the row; the others close up over its old anchor, and the hidden cell is not re-anchored, so its effect container keeps the stale position.
- why it matters: an effect that is up while its spell is hidden as unusable (out of rage or mana during the effect) draws on top of whichever cell moved into that place. Conversely a cell with `show = "ready"` and an effect holds an empty gap for its whole cooldown, long after the effect ended.
- fix: in `Layout`, treat a hidden cell with a container as placed in every case where its effect can be up (`f.container ~= nil and f.condOK ~= false`), or set the effect group's max to 0 through `liveGroups` whenever the cell is hidden for a reason other than "on cooldown". Add a layout test for `unusable = "hide"` with an effect.

In debuffs or procs it becomes an aura group with `include = {}` (the editor makes enchant entries with `ids = {}`), and `candidates({})` returns `includeSpellIDs = {}`; the Build comment at 1763-1764 says "an empty spell list would let the engine show every aura". A packed group's max is taken unclamped from saved settings while a fixed slot's is clamped to 1..4. The editor's drag rule keeps enchants in buffs (`if from.enchant then return to.path.key == "buffs" and …`), so only an imported or hand-edited profile gets there. In a cooldown list an enchant entry is harmless (`knownRank` of no IDs is nil: no cell).

- what: `targetKind` treats `UnitExists("target")` as possibly secret, but `UpdateMissing` and `UpdateReminders` put it straight into an `and`, a truth test. The debuff slots' alpha from hostility is applied only at build and on `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED`.
- why it matters: if `UnitExists` can come back as a secret boolean on this client, every target change in that state raises an error inside the handler (caught by Fault; the slots keep their old alpha, and the `markUsable()` after it in the same handler is skipped). A target whose attackability changes without a target change (a duel starting or ending, a PvP flag, mind control: `UNIT_FACTION`) keeps the wrong grey slots and reminders until the player retargets.
- fix: use `known(UnitExists("target"), false)` at both places; probe whether `UnitExists` is ever secret and make the file uniform either way. Listen to `UNIT_FACTION` for `target` (and the duel events the probe suggests), calling `UpdateMissing` and `UpdateReminders`.

#### HUD-CD-14: SPELLS_CHANGED does three jobs through two listeners, each allocating
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:1091-1103 (`KnownSignature` per event), 1125-1141 (`forgetTalents` +
  `static`), 910-932, 937-962; src/UI/CooldownTracker/Entries.wowlua:120-133
- known: no
- what: `SPELLS_CHANGED` has two handlers for the same owner. The first builds `KnownSignature()` at once on every event: `knownRank` for every listed entry and member (an `IsPlayerSpell` and now a `rankNumber` per known rank), a `tostring` per part, then `table.concat`. The second drops the talent cache and arms the half-second look, which builds `ConditionSignature()` and, when an entry has a talent condition, reads the talent tree again. The file's own comment (2548-2549) says the spellbook "changes" with every shapeshift.
- why it matters: a druid or warrior switching forms in combat pays both walks per switch, and `SPELLS_CHANGED` comes in bursts at login and zone changes; the first handler is not coalesced. Small, but on a path that runs in fights.
- fix: one handler: set `t.spellsDirty = true` and let the existing half-second `static()` look compute both signatures once; drop the talent cache only on the trait and talent events, not on `SPELLS_CHANGED` (the `IsPlayerSpell` fallback in `TEST.talent`, line 952, covers learned spells). Concatenate numbers directly instead of `tostring` per part.

#### HUD-CD-15: The rank lookup re-reads the subtext of every rankless spell on each call, and falls back to the old choice while subtexts are not loaded
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (the cache gap is confirmed from code; whether `GetSpellSubtext` answers empty before spell data loads needs an in-game probe)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/CooldownTracker/Entries.wowlua:98-113 (`rankNumber`), 120-133 (`knownRank`); callers
  src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:564, 683, 910-932
- known: no
- what: `rankNumber` caches only a positive result:
  ```
  local ok, sub = pcall(C_Spell.GetSpellSubtext, id)
  if not ok or type(sub) ~= "string" or secret.isSecret(sub) then return 0 end
  local n = tonumber(sub:match("(%d+)")) or 0
  if n > 0 then rankNumbers[id] = n end
  return n
  ```
  A spell without a rank (most cooldowns: trinket-like abilities, talents, racials) is never cached, so each `knownRank` does a `pcall(C_Spell.GetSpellSubtext, id)` and a `match` for it again. `knownRank` runs for every entry and member in `KnownSignature` (every `SPELLS_CHANGED` and `LEARNED_SPELL_IN_SKILL_LINE`), several times per entry in `Build`, and in `iconFor`. And when the subtext is not available yet (nil or `""`, which the client can return until a spell's data is loaded), every known rank reads as 0, the tie rule picks the last known ID in the list, which is the choice the new code was written to replace (the comment: Consecration's Rank 1 has the highest ID, "the cell checked its mana cost and range"). `knownSig` then records that ID, and nothing rebuilds when the subtexts arrive unless a later `SPELLS_CHANGED` happens to come.
- why it matters: the wrong-rank cell (usability and mana check of Rank 1) can come back after a cold login for spells whose IDs do not climb with their ranks, until some later spellbook event; and the signature walk on a hot-ish event (HUD-CD-14) got a `pcall` per rankless spell.
- fix: cache "no rank" too, but only for an answer that is a readable, non-empty string or once the spell's data is loaded (`C_Spell.IsSpellDataCached(id)` where the client has it; otherwise cache 0 after `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` plus one `SPELLS_CHANGED`), using a sentinel (`rankNumbers[id] = 0`, test `cached ~= nil`). When a read gave nil or `""` for a known ID during `Build`, mark the tracker to look again (`self.rebuild = true` on the next `SPELL_DATA_LOAD_RESULT`/`SPELLS_CHANGED`, or a single `after(1, …)` re-check of `KnownSignature`). Probe: log `C_Spell.GetSpellSubtext(26573)` at the first `Build` after a cold login. Test in `tests/unit/UI/CooldownTracker.test.wowlua`: subtexts empty at build, filled later, the cell's `spellID` becomes the highest rank; and a rankless spell's subtext is read once.

#### HUD-6: Weapon enchants scan at file load and tick every second for the whole session, whoever uses them
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/WeaponEnchants.wowlua:194-266 (`scan`), 255-263 (the 1 s ticker), 268-286 (file-level
  listeners), 641 (`scan()` at load), 577-583 (a new `OnUpdate` closure per `Refresh`)
- known: no
- what: the module registers its listeners at load under the owner "WeaponEnchants" (`WEAPON_ENCHANT_CHANGED`, `PLAYER_EQUIPMENT_CHANGED`, `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD`, `UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED`, `UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED`) and calls `scan()` at file level. While any weapon has an enchant, `ticker = every(1, function() scan() end)` runs for good. Each scan does a `read(s.ws)` (a `pcall` and a list table) and `G.GetInventoryItemID` for three slots, and per enchanted slot a new `info` table (`local info = { slot = slot, enchantID = id, … }`), a `slot .. ":" .. id` key, `itemName(s.inv)` and `G.C_Spell.GetSpellName`. The cast listener allocates `lastCast = { id = spellID, at = GetTime() }` for every successful cast of every class. `WeaponEnchantIcon:Refresh` sets a new closure with `self:SetScript("OnUpdate", function(_: Frame, elapsed: number) … end)` on every call while an enchant is up.

Small each time, but permanent garbage that cannot be turned off, against the rule that a disabled feature leaves nothing behind.
- fix: count consumers: `weaponEnchantIcon`'s `SetSlot` and a new `Release`, plus an exported `watch(owner)`/`unwatch(owner)` pair for the Cooldown Tracker; register the listeners and the ticker with the first consumer and remove them with the last (`events.offAll("WeaponEnchants")`, `ticker:Cancel()`). In `scan`, update the existing `state[slot]` table in place when the enchant is the same (only `expires`, `charges`, `weapon` change), cache the item name per weapon ID, reuse one `lastCast` table, and drop the load-time `scan()` in favour of the first consumer's. In `Refresh`, set one `OnUpdate` function defined once (a method). Tests: `tests/unit/UI/WeaponEnchants.test.wowlua`.

#### HUD-DM-7: Remaining garbage and repeated work on each meter refresh
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/DamageMeter.wowlua:73-91, 1135-1146, 615-628, 1047 and 1062-1098, 1406-1415 with 1368;
  src/Units/DamageMeter.wowlua:564-565, 649-650
- known: no
- what: per window and per refresh (once a second in combat, up to three windows):
  - `meterTypeOf` builds a ten-entry table on each call to look up one key (`local byKey: { [string]: DamageMeterType } = { DamageDone = E.DamageDone, … } return byKey[key]`).
  - `RefreshList` copies `sources` into `list` (`for i = 1, #sources do list[i] = sources[i] end`) also when it is not reversed.

- why it matters: at one refresh a second this is not a frame drop; it is steady garbage in raid combat (some dozens of short-lived tables and closures per window per second) with no purpose.

Give `SetMaxRows`/`SetOptions` an optional "no refresh" argument, or add one `Configure(rows, options)` that refreshes once, and use it in the module's `Layout` and preview.

#### HUD-DM-9: No way to see entries beyond the row count; deaths lose the newest

Deaths are reversed to "the order they happened" and are in `NO_PIN`, so with more deaths than rows the newest are cut. The spell breakdown is cut the same way.
