### Fixed since the first pass

- HUD-2 (a nameplate's cast bar registered ten bus listeners per plate): the unit's cast events are now on one frame per bar, registered with `RegisterUnitEvent` and dispatched by a table (`src/UI/CastBar.wowlua:427-431`, 953-988), and `events.offAll` looks only at the owner's entries (`src/Core/Events.wowlua:72-76`, 178-194).
- HUD-3 (an action button kept its out-of-range veil after its action was removed): the empty branch of `Update` now calls `self:SetOutOfRange(false)`, which hides the veil and reruns `UpdateArt` (`src/UI/ActionButton.wowlua:358-360`, 577-586).

Partly fixed, restated among the findings with what remains:

- HUD-UF-4 and HUD-UF-5 (`draw.paint` skips an unchanged colour, src/UI/Draw.wowlua:181-185), HUD-UF-6 (`offAll` by owner, src/Core/Events.wowlua:72-76 and 178-189).

- HUD-CD-1 is largely fixed (see its "what changed"): the light pass at src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:532-540 and 2468-2486, and the unchanged-paint early return at src/UI/Draw.wowlua:182-184.

- HUD-DM-3 (stance bar coalesced and split into "all"/"states", src/UI/ClassBars.wowlua:261-298, commit bbe0a7e8), HUD-DM-7 (`SetFill` diffed, src/UI/DamageMeter.wowlua:557-565; fight select rebuilt only on a changed signature, 1362-1380; commit bbe0a7e8).

### Withdrawn

None in full.

- HUD-DM-10, one part only: "a double update on a picker click". `ClosePicker` returns before its `UpdateAll` in combat (src/UI/ClassBars.wowlua:1273-1276), so the explicit `self:UpdateAll()` in `PostClick` (1246) is needed there; the double call out of combat is harmless.

### Cross-cutting observations

#### From: Lead files (ActionBar, ActionButton, CastBar, SwingTimer, ResourceBar, PowerCost, Readiness, RestedSign, LevelUp)

- **Skipping work while hidden needs the "edge" state reset too.** HUD-12 is the general shape: a pass that is skipped for hidden widgets leaves flags (`coolingDown`) that the catch-up read then treats as a fresh transition. Check other "stale, read on show" paths added since (cooldown tracker cells, class bars).
- **File-level listeners with no consumer count** are unchanged in `CastBar` ("Interrupt": SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN, SPELLS_CHANGED, PLAYER_LOGIN, UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED) and `ActionBar` (about 35 events gated on `#bars == 0`).
- **Raw event frames beside the bus.** `CastBar.ListenUnit` now registers on its own frame with `fault.call("CastBar", …)`: right for a widget whose unit changes per plate, but such listeners are invisible to `events.bus:count(owner)` and to `offAll`; any test or disable path that proves "nothing left" by the bus count will not see them. `Deactivate` does call `UnregisterAllEvents`.
- **`x or {}` in iteration** (`pairs(bySlot[slot] or {})` at src/UI/ActionBar.wowlua:129, `ipairs(INTERRUPTS[class] or {})` at src/UI/CastBar.wowlua:113 and 132) still allocates an empty table per call on event paths.
- **Two power events for one change** (`UNIT_POWER_FREQUENT` and `UNIT_POWER_UPDATE` on the same handler): check the player frame's power line and the cooldown tracker for the same pairing.

#### From: UnitFrame, Auras, HealthFill, CombatBadge

- **Filter tokens on other players**: the modules' comments (src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:127-136, src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:106-112, src/Units/Auras.wowlua:95-98) now state the rule for `RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE`, `PLAYER` and the defensive filters, and the modules' own groups follow it. `src/UI` was not swept with it: the unit frame's dispel sets and buff indicators (HUD-UF-1, HUD-UF-2) still select by those tokens on any unit. Sweep `src/UI` for `"PLAYER"` and `RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE` in filters.
- **Work deferred to "first show" lands in fights.** The lazy aura-button build (HUD-UF-15) trades login cost for work at the moment an aura appears; anything deferred that way on engine-owned or secure frames needs a check that it is still allowed then, and should record a failure for a retry rather than set its "done" flag first.
- **Scoped state does not survive a deferral.** `draw.withPixelUnit` is a dynamic scope; any callback registered inside it (an `OnShow` hook, a timer) runs outside it (HUD-UF-16). Look for other closures created inside `withPixelUnit` bodies (the nameplates build at src/Units/Nameplates.wowlua:496 and 947).
- **Custom `initialize` on aura groups bypasses what the standard initializer learned** (lazy art). Other users of `group.initialize` (grep `initialize =` in `src/UI` and `src/Units`) build ten decorations per group up front as the unit frame does.
- **`Text:SetStyle` has no "already this" check**, while `draw.paint` now has one; a one-line early return there removes a `fonts.apply` per health event on every frame and likely elsewhere.
- **Module-side workarounds for widget gaps remain**: RaidFrames still rescans containers by hand and refreshes after `SetUnit` (HUD-UF-6, HUD-UF-8).
- **Inline `ipairs({ a, b, … })` over fixed fields** in handlers (src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:1444, 1720, 1871) allocates a table per call.
- Outside this group, for the PowerCost reviewer: `CastCost:Amount` returns nil unless `UnitPowerMax` is a readable number (src/UI/PowerCost.wowlua:124-126); the plan notes say power is secret even out of combat on Forever, so it is worth confirming in game that the player's maximum is readable, or the cast-cost line never shows.

#### From: CooldownTracker, WeaponEnchants

- `Draw`'s `keep` now skips an unchanged paint (src/UI/Draw.wowlua:182-184), which removes the repaint cost from every caller that paints by token on an event. `Icon:SetState` and `Icon:SetBorder` (src/UI/Icon.wowlua:57-70) still have no early return: `SetState` calls `SetDesaturated` and `SetVertexColor` every time. A "same state" check there would finish the job for every icon user.
- Split-by-meaning dirty flags (`dirty` / `usableDirty`) are the right shape; the same split is missing where one handler serves several events elsewhere (the reminder scan here, HUD-CD-3).
- Caches that store only "found" answers (`rankNumbers` keeps `n > 0` only) re-do the read for every miss; sweep for `if n > 0 then cache[id] = n end` and similar where the miss is the common case.
- Reads that depend on lazily loaded client data (`C_Spell.GetSpellSubtext`, item names, tooltips) used at build time with no re-check when the data arrives.
- Module-level registrations behind a public constructor (`soundIDs`) and state written only by events and not on Start/Stop (`inFight`) are unchanged patterns; both are worth a sweep in other `SuuUI.UI.*` constructors.
- File-level listeners and tickers with no consumer count (WeaponEnchants) remain; a disabled module still leaves UI-layer work behind.

#### From: DamageMeter, ClassBars, ThreatMeter

- **A fix applied to one sibling only.** The stance bar got a once-per-frame flusher and an "all"/"states" split; the totem bar in the same file and the pet bar listen to the same kind of events and got neither. The secret-table guard exists in `RefreshList` and `RefreshRecap` but not `RefreshSpells`; the "hide the rows above the count" loop likewise. When a performance or guard fix lands, sweep the siblings in the same file.
- **The once-per-frame flusher is now written per widget** (`StanceBar`'s constructor here, the action bars' `due` set). A shared helper (Core, keyed "run once next frame") would let the totem bar, pet bar and others take it without a copy.
- **Setters with no "same as before" check that callers hit on a timer**: `StateBadge:SetState` (measures text each call) and `Border:SetColor` in `DamageRow:Set`. `draw.paint`/`paintFill` do have the check now (`src/UI/Draw.wowlua:181-185`), so the remaining cost sits in the widget-level setters above them.
- **`combat.run("prefix:" .. self.name, function … end, …)` in event handlers** still allocates a key string and a closure per call (and a job table in combat): `UpdateAutocastClicks`, `lock`, `UpdateForms`, `Refresh`, `Layout` in ClassBars. Build the key and the function once where the handler is hot.
- **Refresh-on-every-setter**: `DamageMeter.SetMaxRows`, `SetOptions` and `SetView` each refresh, and callers call two in a row (module `Layout`, preview). `ThreatMeter.SetMaxRows` goes the other way (it only hides rows and relies on the caller's next `SetRows`); the two meters should agree on one convention.
- **Preview instances go through the same constructor as live ones** and so register with `extend` under the live kind (both meters).

## Area: UI window bodies


All file:line references are for the 0.17.0 export (`36f5f407`), repo-relative.

### Coverage

**First-pass findings re-checked on the new code:** all 18 (UIW-1 to UIW-18).
Each was re-read at its place in the new files; the owners' sides were
re-checked in `src/Units/GroupFinder.wowlua`, `Social.wowlua`,
`RaidPlanner.wowlua`, `Bags.wowlua`, `LootRolls.wowlua`, `ObjectiveTracker.wowlua`,
`Spellbook.wowlua`, and `src/UI/Inputs.wowlua` (TextField) and
`src/UI/Draw.wowlua` (`layout`, `relayout`).

**New code read:**
- `src/UI/LootRollTray.wowlua`: in full (1,187 lines).
- The complete diff `4c6ea485..36f5f407` of every changed file of the area:
  `Spellbook`, `Inventory`, `Professions`, `Legacy`, `ObjectiveTracker`,
  `Social`, `Guild`, `GuildControl`, `GroupFinder`, `GroupFinderListed`,
  `GroupFinderListing`, `GroupFinderWho`, `TalentTree`, `TalentBuilds`,
  `RaidPlanner`, `Timeline`, `MicroMenu`, `Loot`, plus the surrounding new
  code wherever a finding or a new feature depended on it. For `Social`,
  `Guild`, `GuildControl`, `GroupFinder*`, `Legacy` the changed lines were
  read with the unchanged context lines filtered out (the changes there are
  almost all the same three mechanical edits, see the summary).

**The forward-reference scan (UIW-2's pattern) was run again over all of the
new `src/`** (two scripts: module-level `local X = …`, `local X: T = …`,
`local function X`, `const X`, each searched for on earlier indented lines,
outside comments and strings). 19 raw hits, every one checked by hand: all
are a parameter, a loop variable, a class method or a type field of the same
name. **No module local is used above its declaration in 0.17.0.**

**Not done:** no build, check or test was run (as instructed). The unchanged
parts of the 18 old files were not read a second time start to end; only the
places the findings and the diffs touch.

### Summary

The area changed in three mechanical ways since the first pass, in every
file: glyph and texture paths became theme tokens (`draw.glyph`, `draw.skin`),
load-time spacing constants became functions (`PAD()`, `slotPx()` …), and
spacing-dependent anchors moved into `draw.layout(self, function() … end)` so
a theme's spacing can be applied again. The first of these fixed UIW-2 (no
file builds a path from `GLYPHS` any more). Real fixes: the recipe pane
scrolls (UIW-3), the tracker no longer lays out twice and skips unchanged
quests (UIW-16, most of it), the bags skip an unchanged layout (UIW-11, most
of it), `MicroMenu:SetItems` follows a changed item (UIW-13, most of it),
Legacy's row heights follow the theme (UIW-15, half).

Still open and unchanged in substance: the Group Finder ad text thrown away
(UIW-1, the one high finding), all three hand-written drags (UIW-8, 9, 10),
the rename field (UIW-4), the per-frame timeline (UIW-5), no virtual list
(UIW-6), the write on the game's category buttons (UIW-7), the duplicated
widgets (UIW-12, now one more copy each in `LootRollTray`).

The new code is in good shape. `LootRollTray` follows the view contract
(data in, callbacks out, rows reused, `SetRemaining` without a layout) and
has only two small issues. The spellbook's bind mode adds eager cover frames
and more secure work to the lazily built cells (UIW-17 grows a little).

### Findings

#### UIW-1: The ad text's edits are never reported (gated on `userInput`), so the generated text replaces them
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code; rests on the owner-confirmed fact that `OnTextChanged`'s `userInput` is never true on Forever)
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (an edit is any change of the text while the field has focus that differs from the text last set by code; "From my listing" clears the focus first)
- where: src/UI/GroupFinderListed.wowlua:263-268 (the gate), 389-392 (the reset in SetData); owner
  src/Units/GroupFinder.wowlua:715-717, 850-855, 1033 (the 15 s `M:Every`)
- known: no
- what: the ad's edit box (a hand-made `EditBox`, not a `TextField`) reports
  typing only when the script's second argument is true:
  ```
  e:SetScript("OnTextChanged", function(obj, user)
      self:Count()
      if user and self.onText then
          self.onText(obj:GetText())
      end
  end)
  ```
  On Forever `user` is never true, so `onText` never runs. The owner's
  `onText` is the only place that sets `self.adText, self.adEdited = t, true`.
  With `adEdited` still false, every `RenderListed` (the 15 s ticker at
  GroupFinder.wowlua:985, a channel change, a listing change) runs
  `if not self.adEdited then self.adText = self:AdFromListing(listing) end`,
  and the view's `SetData` then does
  ```
  if not a.edit:HasFocus() and a.edit:GetText() ~= (A.text or "") then
      a.edit:SetText(A.text or "")
  ```
- why it matters: a player edits the ad and presses Escape to get the
  keyboard back (the field's `OnEscapePressed` clears focus). Within 15
  seconds the text snaps back to the generated one; posting after that posts
  the generated text, not theirs. Only a post made while the field still has
  focus keeps the edit (`onPost` reads `e:GetText()`). "From my listing"
  (`onRewrite`) does nothing useful, since the text is always regenerated.
- fix: do what `TextField` does (src/UI/Inputs.wowlua:784-791): drop the
  `user` gate and compare, e.g. keep `self.lastTyped`, and in the handler
  `local t = obj:GetText(); if obj:HasFocus() and t ~= self.lastTyped then self.lastTyped = t; if self.onText then self.onText(t) end end`;
  set `self.lastTyped` wherever the code itself calls `SetText` (SetData,
  line 390). Extend `tests/unit/UI/GroupFinderListed.test.wowlua` with a
  typing case that fires `OnTextChanged` with `userInput = false` while the
  field has focus and expects `onText`, then a `SetData` after focus is lost
  with the owner's kept text and expects the field unchanged.

#### UIW-4: Any data refresh while renaming a setup ends the rename (and may commit half a name)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (rests on a focused edit box losing focus when hidden, the game's normal behaviour)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/RaidPlanner.wowlua:1131-1149 (the field and its after(0) hook), 1437-1486 (DrawLeft,
  `renameField:Hide()` at 1448), 1730-1733 (Rename); src/UI/Inputs.wowlua:757-774 (commit on focus lost);
  triggers in src/Units/RaidPlanner.wowlua:382 (Render), 500-545 (events)
- known: no
- what: `DrawLeft` starts with `self.renameField:Hide()` on every draw and
  shows the field again over the row being renamed. Hiding the focused field
  fires `OnEditFocusLost`, where `TextField` commits: if the text differs
  from the stored value it calls the planner's `onChange`, which sets
  `self.renaming = nil` and calls `onRename(id, strtrim(text))` with whatever
  was typed so far (and that callback renders again from inside the running
  draw). If nothing was typed yet, the planner's own hook queues
  `after(0, function() if self.renaming then self:Rename(nil) end end)`,
  which ends the rename a frame later even though the same `DrawLeft`
  re-showed and re-focused the field.
- why it matters: the module renders on `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`,
  `PLAYER_ROLES_ASSIGNED`, `UNIT_CONNECTION`, `INSPECT_READY`, addon messages
  and combat start/end. In a raid these arrive constantly, so typing a setup
  name with the planner open is cut off after a few letters and the half
  name is saved.
- fix: in `DrawLeft`, don't hide the field while `self.renaming` is set and
  its row is still in the list: only re-anchor it (hide it after the loop
  when no row matched). Make the `after(0)` hook check
  `not self.renameField.edit:HasFocus()` before ending the rename. Guard
  `Draw` against re-entry (a `drawing` flag that marks dirty and redraws once
  at the end). Test in `tests/unit/UI/RaidPlanner.test.wowlua`: `Rename(id)`,
  type two letters, `SetData` again, expect the field shown, focused, its
  text kept and `onRename` not called.

#### UIW-5: The encounter timeline allocates and re-lays every event every frame
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed on 2026-11-16 (branch `high-perf`; the same fix as X-2.1: per frame no tables, closures or strings beyond a changed time text; the list variant sets icon, name and badge per row only on a layout)
- where: src/UI/Timeline.wowlua:119-187 (layoutTrack), 271-303 (layoutList), 400-419 (Layout, SetEvents'
  OnUpdate)
- known: no
- what: `SetEvents` installs `OnUpdate → self:Layout()` whenever there is at
  least one event. Each frame `layoutTrack` builds two tables (`inWin`,
  `later`), one `{ e = e, r = r }` table per event, two sort closures, sorts
  both, formats a time string per event (`fmtTime`), and per event calls
  `ClearAllPoints`, `SetPoint`, `SetValue`, `SetColor` ×3 and `Show`; with
  later events it also formats `"then %s in %s%s"`. `layoutList` is heavier
  and has no `id` check at all: per row per frame `ClearAllPoints`,
  `SetPoint` ×2, `icon:SetArt`, `name:SetValue`, `badge:SetState`,
  `time:SetValue`, `draw.paintFill`, `drain:SetWidth`, then
  `panel:SetHeight` and `t:SetHeight`.
- why it matters: this runs for the whole of every boss fight, when frame
  time matters most. With 8 events at 120 fps it is about 3,000 short-lived
  tables and strings a second and a few thousand widget calls.
- fix: keep one sorted array on the timeline, rebuilt in `SetEvents` only
  (the order by end time doesn't change between calls) and reuse its records.
  Per frame: one loop computing `r`; move a frame only when its rounded pixel
  changed; set the time text only when the shown string changed (compare
  with the last one kept on the frame); set colours only when `soon` flips.
  In the list variant set icon, name and badge only when the row's event id
  changes (the track already does this with `f.id`), set the panel height
  only when the row count changes, and throttle the list to about 20 Hz.
  Test file: `tests/unit/UI/Timeline.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-6: No list is virtualised: one frame per entry, every entry re-laid on every refresh
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed in db302207 (the guild roster, the contacts and the Who results are VirtualLists now; the Group Finder's browse list, the recipe list and the people list still make a row per entry and re-lay all of them, and the people list still sets a new OnClick closure per action button per draw)
- where: src/UI/GroupFinder.wowlua:423-545 (drawRow), 901-966 (browse Draw);
  src/UI/Professions.wowlua:1261-1322 (DrawList); src/UI/Social.wowlua:1223-1330 (PeopleList, the per-draw
  closure at 1299)
- known: no
- what: each `Draw` walks the whole data list and, per entry, takes
  `rows[n] or makeRow()` and sets every anchor, width, text and colour again,
  whether or not the row is inside the scroll window. A roster row is a
  Button with 6 font strings, 5 textures and a badge frame; its draw makes
  about 45 widget calls. A click on a row (select) goes back through the
  owner and redraws the whole list. `PeopleList.Draw` creates a new `OnClick`
  closure per action button per draw
  (`b:SetScript("OnClick", function() local onClick = a.onClick …`), and
  `GroupFinderWho.Draw` a `place` closure per row. New since the first pass:
  rows that use `draw.layout` (ContactRow, PeopleRow, BrowseRowFrame,
  RecipeRow, SectionHead, …) also keep 1 to 7 layout closures each in
  `Draw.wowlua`'s registry for the theme's relayout.
- why it matters: a 500-member guild with offline members shown creates 500
  row frames (about 6,500 regions) on first show and makes about 22,000
  widget calls per render; the owner renders on each `GUILD_ROSTER_UPDATE`
  while the page shows, on each search keystroke (coalesced) and on each
  selection, so the window hitches on every click. The recipe list with
  "All" shown has 300+ rows per profession. The owners' coalescing limits
  how often, not how much.
- fix: one shared virtual list in `src/UI` (fixed row height, a pool the
  size of the window plus one, `OnVerticalScroll` re-binds rows, headings as
  a row kind). Roster (24 px), Who (24 px), recipes (20 px), contacts (40 px
  plus heads) and browse (44 px plus heads) all have fixed heights, so all
  five fit. Selection should repaint the two affected rows without going
  through `SetData`. Until then, cheap wins: skip a row whose data table and
  column layout are the same as last time, and bind the people list's button
  handler once (`b.action = a` and one fixed `OnClick` that reads it).

#### UIW-7: The listing skin writes `fixedWidth`/`fixedHeight` on the game's category buttons
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (in game: the write); no taint effect observed
- status: open (the write is confirmed in game, with no harm seen: nothing else became addon-written and the post went through; the width going stale after a resize was not checked)
- probe (2026-11-15, build 70888): after a listing was posted, 8 of the category buttons' `fixedWidth`/`fixedHeight` read as addon-written, as the finding says; no other new addon-written values, and the post was not blocked.
- where: src/UI/GroupFinderListing.wowlua:1023-1024 (the write), 2-7 (the header's rule), 984-1035
  (LayoutCategories' loop)
- known: no (`Docs/port-notes/ui-social.md` records the opposite: that this file avoids writing to the game's frames)
- what: the header says "What the game keeps on its frames is read, never
  written: SuuUI's parts live in tables of their own", and everything else in
  the file keeps to it (weak tables `cards`, `rows`, …). The one exception,
  inside `if not p then` (so only the first time a card is skinned, with the
  width of that moment):
  ```
  -- a ResizeLayoutFrame: its own size, not its children's
  b.fixedWidth, b.fixedHeight = cw, 132
  ```
  on each of Blizzard's `CategoryButtons`.
- why it matters: (1) taint: these buttons belong to Blizzard's secure group
  finder addon, the panel whose Post button lists you. Their layout code
  reads `fixedWidth`; from then on that read is tainted and so is what the
  layout writes. Whether that reaches the listing call can't be seen from
  the code. (2) the value goes stale: after the window is resized or the
  number of shown categories changes, the game's next `Layout()` of the
  button snaps it back to the first width while the skin has set a new `cw`.
- fix: probe with `/suu probe taint` after choosing a category and posting a
  listing. If `b:SetSize(cw, 132)` after the game's layout is enough (the
  skin already re-lays after the game's category update), drop the write. If
  the fields are needed, set them on every pass of the loop, not only once.

#### UIW-8: Raid page drag: the drop uses the roster index from the drag's start; the ghost has no cleanup on hide
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the stale index; needs in-game probe for the ghost
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Social.wowlua:759-788 (drag scripts), 906-956 (StartGhost, StopGhost), 958-1022 (Draw; no
  OnHide in the file); owner src/Units/Social.wowlua:1060-1095
- known: no
- what: `OnDragStart` keeps `r.dragMember = m`. `OnDragStop` then does
  ```
  if not (to and to.group and to.pos) or to.member == member then … return end
  local other = to.member
  if other then r.onSwap(member.index, other.index) elseif r.onMove then r.onMove(member.index, to.group) end
  ```
  with that kept member's `index`; the owner passes it straight on
  (`pcall(SwapRaidSubgroup, a, b)`, `pcall(SetRaidSubgroup, index, group)`).
  `to.member == member` compares table identity, which is false after any
  redraw during the drag (each `SetData` brings new member tables), so a drop
  on one's own slot becomes a swap with oneself. `Draw` sets
  `b:SetAlpha(m.online and 1 or …)` on every slot, so the dragged slot loses
  its 0.5 alpha on a redraw. The ghost is hidden only in `StopGhost`, called
  only from `OnDragStop`; `Social.wowlua` has no `OnHide` at all.
- why it matters: if someone leaves or joins during the drag, raid indices
  shift and the drop moves a different player than the one dragged. If the
  window closes mid-drag (Escape, another window) and the client doesn't
  deliver `OnDragStop` to a hidden frame, the ghost card stays on screen
  following the cursor (its `OnUpdate` keeps running) until the next drag.
- fix: at the drop, find the dragged member again by name in
  `r.data.members` and use that entry's index (no move if gone); compare
  names for "dropped on itself". Add `OnHide` on `RaidGroups` that calls
  `StopGhost()` and clears `dragging`/`dragMember` without acting. In `Draw`
  keep 0.5 alpha on the slot whose member's name is `dragMember.name`. Test
  file: `tests/unit/UI/Social.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-9: Raid planner drag: hiding the window performs the drop; the target scan allocates per frame
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/RaidPlanner.wowlua:1265-1268 (OnHide), 1302-1329 (Targets, TargetUnderCursor), 1353-1369
  (StopDrag), 798-813 (the ghost's OnUpdate)
- known: no
- what: the window's `OnHide` hook does `if self.dragging then self:StopDrag() end`,
  and `StopDrag` is the same function as a real drop: it takes
  `self:TargetUnderCursor()` and calls `drop(what, where)`. `Targets()` tests
  `g:IsShown()` / `c:IsShown()` (a frame's own flag, still true while its
  parent is hidden) and `IsMouseOver()` (geometry). Separately, during a
  drag the ghost's `OnUpdate` calls `planner:TargetUnderCursor()` every
  frame, which builds a new array of every shown card, Add slot and the
  unplaced zone (about 50 entries at 40 players) and walks it.
- why it matters: pressing Escape while dragging a player over a slot places
  them there (or swaps two players) instead of cancelling. The per-frame
  table is garbage during every drag.
- fix: give `StopDrag` a `cancel` argument; `OnHide` passes `true` and only
  hides the ghost, clears the highlight and `self.dragging`. In
  `TargetUnderCursor` iterate `self.groupFrames` directly (no table) and use
  `IsVisible()`. Test file: `tests/unit/UI/RaidPlanner.test.wowlua` (start a
  drag, hide the window, expect `onDrop` not called).

#### UIW-10: Talent order drag survives the panel hiding and fires a move on the next show
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/TalentTree.wowlua:505-513 (press and release on a line), 608-610 (the panel's OnUpdate),
  621-638 (Finish), 642-684 (Drag), 865-901 (SetOrder)
- known: no
- what: a press stores
  `o.press = { index = self.index, y = …, line = self }`; the order panel's
  `OnUpdate` runs `Drag()`, which ends the drag when the mouse button is up.
  The panel has no `OnHide`. If it hides while a line is dragged (window
  closed, tab changed), `OnUpdate` stops and `OnMouseUp` never reaches the
  hidden line, so `press`/`dragging` stay set and the plate and drop rule
  stay shown. On the next show the first `OnUpdate` sees the button up and
  calls `Finish()`, which computes the slot under wherever the cursor is now
  and calls `move(press.index, before)`. `SetOrder` during a drag (a talent
  event refreshing the page) also leaves `press.index` pointing into the old
  order.
- why it matters: a build's order changes without the player doing it; in
  the build editor that is a saved change.
- fix: `OrderPanel` gets an `OnHide` that cancels (clear `press`/`dragging`,
  hide plate and drop rule, `press.line.dragged = false`, redraw the line, no
  move). In `SetOrder`, cancel a running drag the same way. Test file:
  `tests/unit/UI/TalentTree.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-11: `Inventory:LayoutSlots` moves the game's bag buttons with no combat rule of its own
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe (whether Forever's bag item buttons are protected)
- status: open (unverified: needs a probe of `button:IsProtected()` on a bag slot while `InCombatLockdown()`)
- probe (2026-11-15, `/suu probe all`, in a fight; read 2026-11-19): recorded "error" for SuuUI's bag slot button (`SuuUIBag2Slot1`); Blizzard's first bag slot did not exist. The watcher writes `ok and show(prot) or "error"`, which turns a readable `false` into "error", so the likeliest reading is "not protected", but a failed call looks the same. Not settled; the watcher needs fixing and a re-run.
- where: src/UI/Inventory.wowlua:712-757 (LayoutSlots), 759-774 (LaidOut, SetSectionMetas); owner
  src/Units/Bags.wowlua:628 (the skip), 548-670 (`Fill`, the full path at 668)
- known: no
- what: what changed: `Bags` builds a key from the bags' sizes and, when it
  matches the last layout (`laid.key == key and inv:LaidOut() == laid.list`),
  only calls `inv:SetSectionMetas(sections)` and `inv:SetMeta(meta)`. So an
  item moving or a stack changing no longer re-anchors every button. What is
  left: when the key does change (a bag swapped, a key looted so the keyring
  shows another slot), `LayoutSlots` still does `ClearAllPoints`, `SetPoint`,
  `SetSize`, `Show` on every button, and neither it nor that path of the
  owner checks `InCombatLockdown()`. The buttons are Blizzard's own bag slot
  buttons (file header, lines 24-28).
- why it matters: if the item button template is protected on Forever,
  looting a key (or a bag filling a bag slot) in combat with the bags open
  makes about 100 blocked calls and leaves the grid half laid out.
- fix: probe `/suu probe` for `button:IsProtected()` on a bag slot while
  `InCombatLockdown()`. If protected: `LayoutSlots` returns false in combat
  without touching anything and the owner queues the layout through
  `/Core/Combat` `run` (as `MicroMenu:SetItems` does). Test file:
  `tests/unit/UI/Inventory.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-13: `MicroMenu:SetItems` updates a reused button's click target but not its glyph or its `onClick`
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open (the part left: a plain button's OnClick and glyph still come from the first item, and a kind change reuses the global frame name)
- where: src/UI/MicroMenu.wowlua:116-136 and 146 (constructor), 240-275 (SetItems)
- known: no
- what: what changed: `SetItems` now sets `b.item = item` on reuse, updates
  the secure `clickbutton` when `item.click` changed, and makes a new button
  when an item changes between secure and plain. What is left: a plain
  button's handler is still the constructor's closure over the first item,
  ```
  self:SetScript("OnClick", function()
      if item.onClick then item.onClick() end
  end)
  ```
  and the glyph is set only in the constructor
  (`draw.glyph(self.glyph, item.glyph)`). Also, when the kind changes, the
  new button is created under the same global frame name
  (`menu.name .. item.key`) as the old one, which stays alive, hidden.
- why it matters: a plugin item registered again under the same key with
  another handler or glyph (a plugin turned off and on) shows the old glyph
  and calls the old function, which may belong to a disabled module.
- fix: have `OnClick` read `self.item.onClick`; on reuse call
  `draw.glyph(b.glyph, item.glyph)` when the glyph differs. For a kind
  change give the new button a distinct name (a counter suffix). Test file:
  `tests/unit/UI/MicroMenu.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-14: `TalentTree:SetSpecs` ignores changed labels and locks unless the count changes
- severity: low

#### UIW-15: Legacy: rows with one step or already done still toggle; the view imports `/Core/API` to write its heights back
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed in a5082e2d (Legacy no longer imports /Core/API: Core/API refreshes the two heights from `legacy.heights()` on a theme change; one-step and done rows still toggle open without a chevron)
- where: src/UI/Legacy.wowlua:469-477 (click) vs 480-489 (Fill) and 566-569 (GroupPanel.Fill)
- known: no
- what: `DetailRow`'s click toggles `view.expanded[id]` for any item with
  `stepsN` set (`local id = item and item.stepsN and item.id`), but `Fill`
  only treats `stepsN > 1` as having steps and hides the chevron when the
  item is done (`self.chevron:SetShown(steps and not item.done)`).
  `GroupPanel.Fill` then lays the steps out anyway
  (`if item.stepsN and id and view.expanded[id] and steps then`). Separately,
  the file is the only window body that imports `SuuUI from "/Core/API"`, to
  write `public.LEGACY_CARD_H, public.LEGACY_TRACK_H = cardHeight(), trackH`
  on a theme change, because both are exported as `const` values computed at
  load (lines 277, 885) and copied into the API table.
- why it matters: clicking a one-step or finished challenge opens a step
  list with no chevron to show it is open or to close it by. The import is a
  UI → API dependency going the wrong way.
- fix: one `hasSteps(item)` used by the click, `Fill` and `GroupPanel.Fill`
  (decide whether done items may open; if yes, show their chevron). Export
  the two heights as functions (`legacyCardHeight()`), or have `Core/API`
  refresh its copies on `SUUUI_THEME_CHANGED`, and drop the import. Test
  file: `tests/unit/UI/Legacy.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-16: Objective tracker: frozen order is lost after folding the quests; recipe rows are drawn on every layout
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open (the part left: the frozen order is lost after folding the quests, and recipe rows are drawn on every layout)
- where: src/UI/ObjectiveTracker.wowlua:614-666 (LayOut's entries; the drop at 650, `self.entries = entries`
  at 666), 700-710 (recipe rows, `r.drawnKey = nil` at 707)
- known: no
- what: the frozen path (combat) rebuilds from `self.entries` so quests keep
  their places, but `LayOut` stores the list after dropping every quest
  entry while the quests are folded:
  ```
  for _, e in ipairs(entries) do
      if not (e.section or e.recipe) and not self.questsCollapsed then kept[#kept + 1] = e end
  end
  entries = kept … self.entries = entries
  ```
  After folding and unfolding in combat, `before` holds no quest, so every
  quest counts as new and is appended in the given order, with new zone
  headings. Separately, recipe rows share the row pool but are never cached:
  `local h = self:DrawQuest(r, rcp); r.drawnKey = nil` runs for every
  tracked recipe on every `LayOut`, although `questKey` would work for them.
- why it matters: quests jump in combat, which freezing is there to prevent;
  a tracker with many tracked recipes pays their full draw on every quest
  log update.
- fix: keep the full frozen entry list in its own field (`self.frozenEntries`)
  and filter a copy for drawing. Cache recipe rows with `questKey(rcp)` like
  quest rows (set `r.drawnKey` instead of clearing it; the key must differ
  from a quest's, e.g. prefix it). Test file:
  `tests/unit/UI/ObjectiveTracker.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-17: Spellbook builds secure parts lazily with no combat guard of its own; bind mode adds a cover frame per cell for everyone
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: likely
- status: open
- where: src/UI/Spellbook.wowlua:192-200 (`cell()`), 109-128 (the cell's secure button and its attributes),
  752-800 (SetSpells: the combat check at 778, `cell` called outside it), 897-957 (SetSchools builds a tab and
  its secure overlay), 1065-1075 (SetCovers); caller src/Units/Spellbook.wowlua:1104
- known: no
- what: `SetSpells` guards its layout with `local layout = not InCombatLockdown()`
  but calls `cell(self, i)` for `1..rows * COLUMNS` unconditionally; a new
  cell creates a `SecureActionButtonTemplate` button and sets attributes on
  it (`useOnKeyDown`, new: `type2`, `_ondragstart`). `SetSchools` creates a
  `SchoolTab` and its secure overlay (`secureOver`: `SetSize`,
  `SetFrameLevel`, `SetFrameRef`, `SetAttribute`) for any index it hasn't
  seen, before its own combat check. Today the owner builds the book out of
  combat, so the cells exist; a school tab that first appears during combat
  would be built in combat. New: `SetCovers(on, live)` does
  `local cover = c.cover or makeCover(self, c, i)` for every cell even when
  `on` is false, and the owner calls it on every render
  (`book:SetCovers(self.bindMode, live)`), so every player gets one extra
  Button with a border per cell on first open, whether or not they ever
  enter bind mode.
- why it matters: blocked-action errors in the rare case, and the widget is
  public API (`SuuUI.UI.Spellbook`), where a plugin won't know the rule. The
  covers are about 14 to 20 frames of waste per book.
- fix: in combat, skip indexes without a cell or tab (they can't be shown
  then anyway) and return a flag so the owner redoes it after combat. In
  `SetCovers`, create a cover only when `on` is true; when off, hide the
  ones that exist. Test file: `tests/unit/UI/Spellbook.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-19: Loot roll tray: a row scrolled out while hovered keeps its hover fill
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (the file's comment says no `OnLeave` reaches a frame hidden under the mouse; CD-27's probe found it does fire during `Hide()`, so this now rests on `IsMouseOver()` reading true there)
- status: open (unverified: `OnLeave` does fire during `Hide()` on this client (CD-27's probe), so the stuck fill needs `IsMouseOver()` to still read true inside that `OnLeave`, which `Hover` asks first; check in game by scrolling the tray with the mouse on the edge row)
- where: src/UI/LootRollTray.wowlua:519-526 (Hover), 976-981 (the tray's OnHide), 1000-1006 (SetData's tail),
  1105-1116 (Layout)
- known: no
- what: a row's hover state is kept in `row.hovered` and shown by
  `row.hoverBg`. The tray resets both when the tray itself hides and for
  rows past the end of the data, but `Layout` hides rows outside the
  scrolled window with a bare `row:Hide()`:
  ```
  if row.data and i >= self.first and i <= last then … row:Show() … else row:Hide() end
  ```
  The wheel scrolls while the mouse is over a row, so the row at the edge is
  the one both hovered and hidden.
- why it matters: with more than six open rolls (a raid boss), scrolling
  down and back shows a row with a stuck highlight until the mouse passes
  over it again. Cosmetic.
- fix: in `Layout`'s else branch (and wherever a row is hidden) set
  `row.hovered = false` and `row.hoverBg:Hide()`; a small `row:Unhover()`
  used by all three places. Test file:
  `tests/unit/UI/LootRollTray.test.wowlua`.

#### UIW-20: Theme spacing is followed by halves: parts placed once at construction sit beside parts placed again
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/UI/LootRollTray.wowlua:818-820, 837-840, 878, 884, 895-896, 919, 944 (placed once with `PAD()`),
  against 834-836, 879-881, 920-922 (`draw.layout`) and 1078-1099; src/UI/Loot.wowlua:58 against 168 and 175;
  src/UI/TalentTree.wowlua:83-84, 88 against 1133-1147; src/UI/Inventory.wowlua:226-232
- known: Docs/API.md, "Spacing and sizes that follow the theme", the "Not live" list (it says these windows "keep what they were laid out with"; it does not say they end up mixed)
- what: the port to theme spacing turned constants into functions and moved
  some anchors into `draw.layout`, but not consistently inside one widget.
  In `LootRollTray` the title, fold button, divider, foot buttons, foot
  note, ask text and tab icon are anchored once with `PAD()` in the
  constructor, while `Layout()` computes the rows' and columns' offsets from
  `PAD()` on every call and three anchors re-run through `draw.layout`. In
  `Loot`, `LootRow` does `self:SetSize(BODY_W(), SLOT())` once, while
  `SetItems` places rows at `(i - 1) * (SLOT() + GAP())` and sizes the body
  from the current values. `TalentTree` exports widths computed once from
  `PAD()`/`GAP()` but lays panels out with the live `GAP()`.
- why it matters: after switching to a theme with other spacing or slot size
  without a reload, these windows are not simply "as before": new rows
  overlap or gap against old-sized ones, and heads sit at the old inset over
  rows at the new one. Low, since a `/reload` cures it and the doc tells
  players these windows are not live.
- fix: per widget choose one: either everything from load-time values (then
  it honestly keeps its layout until reload), or put every `PAD()`-dependent
  anchor in one `Place()` method called from the constructor and from
  `draw.onLayout(self, …)`, followed by `self:Layout()`. For `Loot`, set the
  row's and its slot's size in `SetItems`. For `TalentTree`, make
  `PANEL_W` a function and compute the two exported widths in the API on
  demand.

### Fixed since the first pass

- **UIW-2** (`GlyphButton` and `BrowseEmpty` read a global `GLYPHS`): fixed.
  No file builds glyph paths any more; `src/UI/GroupFinder.wowlua:108` and
  `:146` call `draw.glyph(self.glyph, glyph)` / `draw.glyph(self.glyph, "search")`
  and the `GLYPHS` local is gone (line 170 onward). The scan over all of the
  new `src/` found no other module local used above its declaration.
- **UIW-3** (the recipe pane's tools, source, reagents and cooldown didn't
  scroll): fixed. `src/UI/Professions.wowlua:1422, 1444, 1450, 1461, 1469,
  1477, 1495` now anchor to the scroll child `c`
  (`line:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", c, "TOPLEFT", 0, -y)`); the new Market section
  (`DrawMarket`, 1325-1371) anchors to `c` as well.

Partly fixed, listed above as "changed": UIW-11 (the bags skip an unchanged
layout, `src/Units/Bags.wowlua:1134-1140`), UIW-13 (`b.item = item`,
`clickbutton` updated, `src/UI/MicroMenu.wowlua:252-262`), UIW-15 (heights as
functions, `src/UI/Legacy.wowlua:203-205, 338-343, 517-522`), UIW-16 (one
layout pass and `questKey`, `src/UI/ObjectiveTracker.wowlua:111-133, 596-607,
722-733`).

### Withdrawn

None. One correction to UIW-1's first-pass wording: changing the channel
select does not by itself reset the text; the reset needs the field to have
lost focus (Escape), after which the next render (15 s at most) replaces it.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Module locals used above their declaration** (the UIW-2 pattern): none
  left in 0.17.0, checked by script over all of `src/` and by hand for each
  hit. `wowlua check` still would not catch a new one when a global of that
  name is declared; a lint for it remains worthwhile, since this refactor
  turned many constants into `local function NAME()` and moved code around.
- **Hand-made edit boxes** bypass the `userInput` rule that `TextField`
  solved (UIW-1). In this area the ad field is the only one left
  (`GroupFinderListing.wowlua:828` hooks the game's box without the
  argument, which is fine).
- **Drag state without an `OnHide` cancel** (UIW-8, 9, 10): three copies,
  none fixed. Anything that sets an `OnUpdate` or a cursor ghost on press
  needs one; `RaidPlanner` has the hook but uses it to drop, not cancel.
- **`Draw` that hides a focused edit box** (UIW-4): any view that re-lays an
  inline editor on every data refresh drops the player's typing.
- **`draw.layout` closures per row.** Every list row now registers one to
  seven closures in `Draw.wowlua`'s `layouts` table, and `draw.relayout()`
  (on a theme change) walks every registered frame, climbs its parents in a
  `pcall` with a new closure per frame, and sorts them all. With several
  hundred pooled rows across the windows this is a visible hitch on a theme
  change and a steady memory cost. Rows whose owner re-places them on every
  draw don't need a kept layout; for the reviewer of `Draw.wowlua`.
- **Theme handlers redraw hidden pages** (`Social`, `Guild`, `TalentTree`,
  `Professions`, `Legacy`): only `RaidPlanner` and `GuildControl` check
  `IsShown()`. `MicroMenu`'s handler now also re-runs `SetItems` through
  `combat.run` for every menu ever made.
- **`MicroMenu:UpdateEnabled`** (new, `src/UI/MicroMenu.wowlua:278-293`) runs
  for every menu on each call of the game's `UpdateMicroButtons` (hooked at
  372-378) and repaints every glyph unconditionally; cheap, but it could
  compare with the button's last `off` state first.
- **View contract is good and uniform**, and the new `LootRollTray` keeps
  it: data in, callbacks out, rows reused, a separate `SetRemaining` for the
  ticking parts so the 0.1 s tick does no layout. Worth keeping as the
  stated rule; UIW-18 lists the exceptions.
- **`SetData` replaces whole selects' options every refresh**
  (`GroupFinderListed:SetData` → `a.channel:SetOptions`, line 387, every
  15 s). Whether `Select` rebuilds its rows or closes an open list on
  `SetOptions` is for the `Select` reviewer.

findings touch only); unchanged regions of those files were not reviewed again
beyond the first-pass findings. The widgets `UI/ThreatMeter`, `UI/DamageMeter`,
`UI/CombatBadge`, `UI/HealthFill` and `Core/Ahead` were not read. Nothing was
run.

### Summary

Between 0.6.0 and 0.17.0 the area grew by pets on party and raid frames, the
"typed and crowd control" debuff choice, role-limited indicators, aura filter
lists (the new module), nameplate pooling in steps, and more "shows" choices for
the meters. Some of the first pass's cost was removed on the way: the aura
widget's setters now skip unchanged values, the raid hook updates one button's
offline state instead of all, and the threat meter reuses its row tables.

None of the 22 findings is fully fixed. The two high ones stand: raid roster
changes are still handled at once and in full (UF-1), and Readiness still sends
addon messages regardless of its panel (UF-2, file unchanged). Game state is
still not put back (UF-3, UF-5, UF-6). The layer rule is broken by seven files
now, two more than before (UF-11), and the party/raid duplication grew with
every feature added to both (UF-10).

New: forty raid pet buttons with their indicator containers are built at login
for every player (UF-23); the Noise list attached by default to party and raid
debuffs cannot work on friendly units by the code's own probe notes (UF-24);
the new debuff choice splits other players' debuffs by a filter word and its
negation (UF-25).

### Findings

#### UF-1: A roster change in a raid re-scans and redraws everything at once, with no coalescing
- severity: high
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed on 2026-11-16 (branch `high-perf`; Units/RaidFrames: `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`, role changes and the header's reassignments queue one pass on the next frame; a button is drawn and its containers re-scanned only when its token shows someone else (by GUID; one it cannot read counts as someone else), the others only follow a role or raid group change; the buttons' own roster listeners are gone (`rosterRefresh = false`). `UpdateIndicatorPresence` still reads the auras per "while missing" indicator, now only for a button drawn anew or limited to your raid group. Unprobed: whether `UnitGUID("raidN")` is secret in combat on Forever; if it is, a pass in combat redraws every visible button, still once per burst)
- where: src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1952-1997 (`GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`), 1213-1235 (the `OnAttributeChanged`
  hook, still `SetUnit` then `btn:Refresh()`), 1252-1295 (pet buttons); src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:2009-2074
  (`UpdateIndicatorPresence`), 2098-2128 (`SetUnit`), 2281-2292 (each frame's own roster listener)
- known: no
- what: What changed since 0.6.0: `UnitAuras:SetGroupMax`, `SetGroupFilter` and `SetGroupSpells` return early on an unchanged value (src/UI/Auras.wowlua:773-830), and the hook calls `self:UpdateOfflineOf(btn)` for its own button instead of looping over all. What remains: on every `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` the handler runs, for each button with a unit, `UpdateIsMe`, `ApplyWho`, `auras:Refresh()`, a `Refresh()` of every dispel container and every indicator container (each an engine `UpdateAllAuras`), then `UpdateStates`, `UpdateSelected`, `UpdateRange`, and `f:UpdateIndicatorPresence()` on all buttons. `UpdateIndicatorPresence` still builds a set table and reads up to 40 auras through `pcall(C_UnitAuras.GetAuraDataByIndex, u, i, filter)` per "while missing" indicator per unit (UnitFrame.wowlua:2043-2062). Each active `UnitFrame` also has its own listener: `if grouped then self:Refresh()` (2281-2292; `grouped` is true for `raidN` and for `raidpetN`, so the up to 40 pet buttons redraw too). In the hook, `btn:SetUnit(unit, true)` deactivates, re-registers every listener and refreshes when the button was active, and then the hook calls `btn:Refresh()` a second time (line 1240). New in the handler: `lastGroup()` (a `GetRaidRosterInfo` loop over the raid) whenever `laidGroup` is set. Nothing is delayed or merged; the game fires this event in bursts.
- why it matters: forming a raid, someone going offline, a subgroup move or a role change costs, per event, about 40 full frame redraws twice over plus several engine aura re-scans per button, in combat too. The default Protection warrior list has a "while missing" indicator (BuffIndicators.wowlua:68-80), so the aura-read loop is in the shipped default.
- fix: (1) Coalesce: on `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` set a flag and run the body once after 0.1 s (`after`), one pending timer. (2) In the hook drop the second `btn:Refresh()` when `SetUnit` re-activated the button. (3) In the roster handler skip a button whose person did not change: keep `f.guid` (when `UnitGUID` is readable) and skip the container refreshes when it and `isMe` are unchanged. (4) Give `UpdateIndicatorPresence` one aura pass per unit that fills one set of spell IDs, shared by all missing indicators. (5) Either remove the per-frame `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` listener for frames owned by a group module (an option `rosterRefresh = false`), or remove the module's own redraw, not both. Test: `tests/unit/Units/RaidFrames.test.wowlua`, count refreshes over a burst of three roster events.

#### UF-2: Readiness broadcasts addon messages constantly, also while its panel is off
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (shares go out only when they changed, through Core/Comm's unlessSame, and nothing for a class without the cooldowns; RDYQ is sent only while the panel is wanted, for newcomers not heard from, at most once per 10 s; answers come once per 10 s with jitter; messages are taken from the group's channels only and the panel update is coalesced)
- where: src/Units/Readiness.wowlua:27 (default `shows = "off"`), 280-300 (`Share`, `ShareSoon`), 302-327 (`OnMessage`), 442-456 (`GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`, `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN`), 484-490 (heartbeat), 103-111 (`encodeShare`), 57-67 (`MAJOR`)
- known: no
- what: Nothing that sends looks at the `shows` setting. With the module enabled (panel "off" is the default) every client sends `"RDYQ"` to the group on every `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` (`if channel() then self:Send("RDYQ"); self:ShareSoon() end`, no debounce); every receiver of `RDYQ` queues a share (`OnMessage` → `ShareSoon`); `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` queues a share out of combat, so casting between pulls sends one message every 2 s; the heartbeat sends every 30 s. `Share` never compares with what was sent last. Classes with an empty list (`WARLOCK`, `ROGUE`, `HUNTER`) send `"RDY\t"` with nothing in it at the same rate. `OnMessage` ignores its third argument (the distribution) and runs `self:Update()` per message.
- why it matters: with N SuuUI clients in a raid, one roster event produces N requests and N answers, and roster events come in bursts; idle traffic is N messages every 2 s while people cast out of combat. The game throttles addon messages per client; the same prefix carries other SuuUI messages, which are then delayed or dropped with these.
- fix: keep the last sent text and time and skip an equal share (compare "ready or not, and end time within 2 s", not raw seconds); send nothing when the own list is empty. Send `RDYQ` only when the roster gained a member, at most once per 10 s, and only when this client shows the panel. Answer `RDYQ` after a few seconds plus random jitter. React to `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` only when the ready state of a `MAJOR` spell flipped. In `OnMessage` accept only `PARTY`/`RAID` distribution and coalesce `Update()` to once per 0.5 s. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Readiness.test.wowlua` (messages counted over a roster burst and a cast sequence).

#### UF-3: Turning SuuUI's focus, pet or boss frames on mid-session leaves Blizzard's showing beside them
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (a watcher on showToT/showFocus/showPet/showBoss stands Blizzard's frames down through RunOutOfCombat)
- where: src/Units/UnitFrames.wowlua:177-205 (`standDownBlizzard`), 981-993 (`UpdateVisibility`), 1091 (only call site, in `OnEnable`)
- known: no
- what: `standDownBlizzard()` runs once and suppresses `FocusFrame`, `PetFrame` and the boss frames only `if M:Get("showFocus")` (and so on) at that moment. The `show*` settings are live: `UpdateVisibility` starts following the unit for SuuUI's frame, but nothing suppresses Blizzard's frame then. The module is `reloadToToggle` (line 794), but these settings are not.
- why it matters: a player who logged in with "Focus" off and turns it on sees two focus frames (pet frames, sets of boss frames) until the next reload.
- fix: call `standDownBlizzard()` from the watcher of the `show*` keys through `self:RunOutOfCombat("standDown", …)` (suppressing is idempotent). Test: `tests/unit/Units/UnitFrames.test.wowlua`: start with `showFocus = false`, set it true, expect `FocusFrame` suppressed.

#### UF-4: The threat meter polls five times a second, out of combat too, and re-raises its alert every tick
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Threat.wowlua:31 (default `shows = "always"`), 131-218 (`sample`, `add`, `readRows`),
  82-105 (`readyDrop`), 235-238 (`alert`), 421-536 (`MeterOpts`, `Warn`, `Update`), 545-552 (`Refresh`),
  598-611 (driver); src/Units/Alerts.wowlua (`Show`)
- known: no
- what: Changed since 0.6.0: the rows and unit tokens are pooled (`rowPool`, `rowList`, `RAID[i]`), so the per-tick tables for rows are gone; `shows` gained "group" and "instance". Remaining: the driver is shown `inCombat() or self:ShowsOutside(shows)` and "always" is still the default, so `Update()` runs every 0.2 s for the whole session; without a hostile target it still calls `meter:SetTarget(nil)`, `meter:SetRows(entries(rows), self:MeterOpts(hidden))` (a new options table) and `meter:Show()` each tick. With a hostile target `readRows` still walks 40 raid units and 40 raid pets whatever the "who" setting is (per unit `UnitExists`, `UnitIsUnit`, `UnitThreatSituation`, `pcall(UnitDetailedThreatSituation…)`, `UnitClass`, `UnitName`, the role). While a warning holds, `Warn` calls `readyDrop()` and `alert(...)` every tick, and `alert` calls `SuuUI.ShowAlert` each time with the same content. No threat event is used.
- why it matters: about 500 API calls per second through a raid fight and a permanent idle tick for every player on the default; the alert module re-formats and re-presents the same alert five times a second.
- fix: register `UNIT_THREAT_LIST_UPDATE` (unit "target") and `UNIT_THREAT_SITUATION_UPDATE`, set a dirty flag, and let the driver call `Update()` only when dirty (a 1 s safety tick in combat). Out of combat without a hostile target draw the empty meter once on `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED`/`PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` and hide the driver. Skip other units when `who == "self"` and no alert needs a holder. In `alert()` remember the last `(key, tone, formatted arguments)` and call `ShowAlert` only on a change. Keep one options table in `MeterOpts`. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Threat.test.wowlua` (driver stopped out of combat without a target; `ShowAlert` once while the state holds).

#### UF-5: Nameplates changes game CVars and never puts them back
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed (the CVars go through M:SetCVar in db302207, with upgraders' defaults seeded in 68ae02ee, and are given back at the next login with the module off; the plate size set with `C_NamePlate.SetNamePlateSize` is still neither recorded nor put back)
- where: src/Units/Nameplates.wowlua:1824-1835 (`ApplyGameSettings`: `SetNamePlateSize` at 1829), 2174
  (`OnDisable`)
- known: no
- what: On enable (and now on every theme change) the module writes the nameplate alpha and scale CVars in `CVARS` and `C_NamePlate.SetNamePlateSize`; it also writes `nameplateShowEnemies`, the friendly player CVars and `nameplateShowFriendlyNPCs`. The previous values are recorded nowhere, and `OnDisable` only releases plates and restores Blizzard's unit frames. Because the module toggles on reload, nothing of it runs once it is off.
- why it matters: a player who set "Nameplates: off" (writes `nameplateShowEnemies = 0`) and later turns the module off has no enemy nameplates and no SuuUI setting left to bring them back; Blizzard's plates keep SuuUI's scale and alpha values for good; uninstalling leaves all of it behind.
- fix: record each CVar's value before the first write in data outside profiles (`self:CharData()`, written only when no entry exists), and restore where the module is known to be off: in `OnDisable` through `RunOutOfCombat`, and at load when the module is disabled and the record is not empty. The same for the plate size. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Nameplates.test.wowlua` (after a stop the CVars read as before the start).

#### UF-6: Blizzard's meter CVar is remembered in the profile, so a profile switch loses it
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (Blizzard's meter CVar goes through M:SetCVar, kept per character outside profiles; the old profile value is migrated out by "blizzardWas-cvar")
- where: src/Units/DamageMeter.wowlua:41 (`blizzardWas` in `DEFAULTS`), 455-471 (`BlizzardOff`, `BlizzardBack`)
- known: no
- what: `BlizzardOff` stores the CVar `damageMeterEnabled` in the module setting `blizzardWas` (profile data) when that is `""`, then writes `"0"`. In another profile whose `blizzardWas` is still `""`, the next `BlizzardOff` reads the `"0"` SuuUI wrote and records that as Blizzard's own value; `BlizzardBack` then "restores" `"0"`.
- why it matters: a player with two profiles (profiles switch by role) who later turns the module off never gets Blizzard's meter back; the value also travels in profile exports.
- fix: keep it in `self:CharData()` (never a profile), remove `blizzardWas` from `DEFAULTS`, and move an existing non-empty value over in a `M:Migrate`. Test: `tests/unit/Units/DamageMeter.test.wowlua` (switch profile between enable and disable; the CVar comes back).

#### UF-7: "Only yours" and "what you can remove" filters on other players' auras show everything
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (the rule is recorded from a probe of 2026-10-16; these call sites were not probed)

  RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE`), 1683-1720 (the friendly group made once `HARMFUL|RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE` returns
  anything); src/Units/Auras.wowlua:105 (`myBuffs`), 126 (`mine`), 159 (focus `mine`), 173 (boss `mine`)
- known: no (the rule is in the comments at Auras.wowlua:95-98 and 117-119)
- what: The project's recorded finding is that on Forever another player's auras have a hidden caster and pass `PLAYER` and `!PLAYER`, `RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE` and its negation alike. Party and raid frames were changed for it. The same filter words are still used on units that can be other players: the friendly nameplate's `removable` group, the target's "only yours" buffs and debuffs when the target is a player, the focus's debuffs, enemy players' plates. Changed in NEW: the friendly plate's group is now created only for classes in `REMOVERS` and only after the first matching aura; by the rule, any debuff on a friendly player matches, so the group is created for any debuffed friendly player and then shows that debuff with a dispel edge.
- why it matters: on a friendly player's plate every debuff shows as if you could remove it; with "Target's buffs: only yours" a player target shows anyone's buffs; in PvP enemy players' plates show everyone's debuffs as yours. The lazy creation meant to spare cities (Nameplates.wowlua:1695-1700) is also defeated for debuffed players.
- fix: confirm with `/suu probe` on a friendly player carrying a debuff you cannot remove and a buff someone else cast. Then: on friendly players' plates use dispel-type candidates (the types your class removes; `dispelCandidates` in src/UI/Auras.wowlua matches by type in the engine, as the unit frames' badge sets do) instead of `RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE`; for target and focus set the "only yours" group's max to 0 when the unit is another player, or say in the setting's description that it applies to NPCs.

The ward slot is missing. The new pet buttons have indicator containers too (`f:SetIndicators` at 1282) and are not in the loop at all.

- known: no
- what: In a raid the holder is hidden by `[group:raid] hide`, but the five frames, and in NEW the five pet frames, stay active and unit-watched. `player`, `party1-4`, `pet` and `partypetN` exist in a raid, so each hidden frame still handles health, power and identity events, keeps its engine containers bound, runs `Refresh()` on every `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`, `UpdateIndicatorPresence` on `UNIT_AURA` and `UpdateState` on threat events. Only the range ticker checks `holder:IsVisible()`. Both group modules register a `UNIT_AURA` and a `UNIT_THREAT_SITUATION_UPDATE` handler for all units that does string finds and a linear search over the frames for every unit in the game.

#### UF-11: Seven modules import UI and Core internals; the public API cannot express what they need
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in a5082e2d (the seven files import only /Core/API: `UnitFrameClass`, `PanelClass`, `UI.GameUnits`, `UI.CurveAmount`, `UI.WithPixelUnit`, the health fill helpers, `BuildAhead` and `Services.ALERTS` are exported, and UnitFrames uses `UI.CurveAmount` instead of its copy)
- where: src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:36 and RaidFrames.wowlua:32 (`import UnitFrame from "/UI/UnitFrame"`, subclassed); Nameplates.wowlua:38 (`gameUnits, curveAmount` from `/UI/UnitFrame`), 43 (`import * as draw from "/UI/Draw"`, for `draw.withPixelUnit`), 53 (`import * as healthFill from "/UI/HealthFill"`); BuffIndicators.wowlua:22 (`import Panel from "/UI/Panel"`); Alerts.wowlua:26 (`import ALERTS from "/Core/ServiceKeys"`); Threat.wowlua:28 and DamageMeter.wowlua:20 (`import * as ahead from "/Core/Ahead"`)
- known: no
- what: `CLAUDE.md` says feature modules use only `import SuuUI from "/Core/API"`. Type-only imports and `Module` as the base class are used everywhere and are harmless. The value imports above are real dependencies a plugin could not have; NEW added four (`/UI/Draw`, `/UI/HealthFill`, `/Core/Ahead` twice). The headers of Threat (line 3), Nameplates (3), DamageMeter (7) and RaidFrames (4) still say "written against the public API only". `UnitFrames.wowlua:210` has its own copy of `curveAmount`.
- why it matters: the built-in modules are the proof that the plugin API is enough; a plugin cannot build ahead of combat, draw plate-pixel lines or subclass the unit frame.
- fix: export what is used and document it in `Docs/API.md` under the current API version: the `UnitFrame` and `Panel` classes to extend, `SuuUI.UI.GameUnits()`, `SuuUI.UI.CurveAmount`, `SuuUI.UI.WithPixelUnit`, the health fill's `paint`/`classToken`/`reactionToken`, `SuuUI.BuildAhead(name, step)` for `/Core/Ahead`, and a way to provide the alerts service. Switch the seven files, delete the copy in UnitFrames, correct the headers, and state in the conventions that `import Module` and `import type` are the two allowed exceptions.

#### UF-12: Setting changes and pet show/hide in combat write to frames the engine's aura containers hang on
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- status: open (unverified: in combat, re-anchoring a frame an aura container hangs on and hiding a player-buff container were both allowed, on a probe-owned container with no buttons shown; still to see: the same with buttons shown (auras on the unit). The code paths are unchanged)
- probe (2026-11-15, build 70888): in combat, `ClearAllPoints`/`SetPoint` on the frame an aura container hangs on and `SetShown(false)` on a player-buff container were both allowed. Tried on a container of the probe's own with no aura buttons shown; a container with shown buttons was not tried.
- where: src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1422-1450 (`ApplyOptions` → `f:ApplyAuraCount()`, `f:ApplyWho()`), 347
  (`ApplyAuraCount`), 1898-1910 (watchers that call `ApplyOptions` at once);
  src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:1120-1131 (`PlaceOwnerAuras`); src/Units/Auras.wowlua:447 (`SetParent` on
  containers) and 805-870 (watchers)
- known: no
- what: A settings row's `combat = true` only adds a sentence; every setting can change in combat. Layout settings go through `RunOutOfCombat`, but the cosmetic ones (`healthText`, `nameColor`, `raidMarkers`, `lowHealth`, `incoming`, `rangeAlpha` on raid frames; the show toggles in Auras) call `ApplyOptions` at once. In RaidFrames that re-anchors and resizes `auraClip`, the frame the engine container is anchored to, and in NEW also sets group filters; in Auras it shows, hides and re-parents the engine's containers. New in NEW: a party pet's frame shows and hides in combat by its unit watch, and its hooks re-anchor the owner's `auraClip` each time (the comment at PartyFrames.wowlua:1124-1127 assumes this is allowed because the clip is not secure). The project's own notes say the engine may refuse writes to its containers in combat. None of these sites has a combat check or `pcall`.
- why it matters: if the client refuses, a pet appearing in a fight, or changing "Health text" during one, raises a Lua error from a frame script or settings watcher and leaves the rest undone.
- fix: probe in combat: `ClearAllPoints()`/`SetPoint` on a party frame's `auraClip` with a bound container, and `SetShown(false)` on a player-buff container; record with `/suu probe`. Independently: move `f:ApplyAuraCount()` and `f:ApplyWho()` out of RaidFrames' `ApplyOptions` into the layout path (they only depend on settings that already wait for combat's end); in Auras route container writes through `RunOutOfCombat` when `InCombatLockdown()`; in `PlaceOwnerAuras` wrap the two writes in `pcall` and redo them on `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` if the probe shows a refusal.

#### UF-14: Threat drops and readiness cooldowns are looked up by English spell name
- severity: medium

The widget's own note says the engine makes ten buttons per group up front (src/UI/Auras.wowlua:903). With three indicators that is 120 more containers on top of the forty group buttons' own.

- known: no
- what: Filters become `excludeSpellIDs`/`includeSpellIDs` on the engine's aura groups. The comments in both group modules record a probe of 2026-11-08: "The game won't leave a debuff out by spell on a friendly unit unless the spell is never secret; on Forever none of the noisy ones is". So the block list shipped on party and raid debuffs (Forbearance, Weakened Soul, Resurrection Sickness, Boosted Rest…) leaves nothing out there; the `debuffKinds = "kinds"` setting was added to do that job. The editor's note says so in its last sentence, but the defaults, the list's description and the module's description present Noise as working. The same note states that an allow list on such frames hides every secret spell, which by the probe is all of them.

#### UF-25: The "typed and crowd control" debuff choice splits other players' debuffs by DISPELLABLE and its negation
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (in game, 2026-11-15: see the probe line)
- status: open (confirmed in game: the negation cannot split crowd control on another player; the code is unchanged at `3dcdc41e`)
- probe (2026-11-15, `/suu probe all`, out of combat; read 2026-11-19): on 3 party members under crowd control (each aura without a dispel type), the same aura passed `HARMFUL|CROWD_CONTROL|DISPELLABLE` and `HARMFUL|CROWD_CONTROL|!DISPELLABLE`, and `HARMFUL|DISPELLABLE` too. So it shows in both of the frame's groups. A typed crowd control effect was not seen. The fix below applies as written.
- where: src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:154 (`OTHERS_BY_KIND = { "HARMFUL", "DISPELLABLE" }`), 165-172 (group
  `cc` with `!DISPELLABLE`); src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:168 (`kinds`), 175-178 (group `cc`)
- known: no
- what: With the default setting, another player's frame has two debuff groups: the typed ones (`DISPELLABLE`) and crowd control without a type (`CROWD_CONTROL`, `!DISPELLABLE`). The project's recorded rule is that another player's auras pass many filter words and their negations alike, and that such pairs must not be used to split them; the probe behind it covered `PLAYER`, the defensive words and `RAID_PLAYER_DISPELLABLE`, not `DISPELLABLE`. The comment says "these filter words work in combat" (probed 2026-11-08) but does not say the negation was checked on another player.
- why it matters: if `!DISPELLABLE` also passes for typed auras on other players, a typed crowd control effect (a Magic polymorph) shows twice on party and raid frames, once in each group.
- fix: probe with a party member under a typed crowd control effect and under a typeless one: record what `HARMFUL|DISPELLABLE`, `HARMFUL|CROWD_CONTROL` and `HARMFUL|CROWD_CONTROL|!DISPELLABLE` list. If the negation is unreliable, drop `!DISPELLABLE` from the `cc` group on other players' frames and keep the split on your own frame only (the pattern the other groups use with `who = "me"`).

  polled four times a second at 1509-1514); src/Units/BuffIndicators.wowlua:209 (`knownBuffs`) and 999 (in
  every editor `Refresh`); src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1506-1517 and src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:1238-1250
  (`ApplyDefensives` → `groupSpells` per group per button); src/Core/AuraFilters.wowlua:335-388 (`filterFor`,
  `groupSpells`), 142-147 (`version`)
- known: no
- what: (a) `UpdateRange` allocates a ten-entry table on each call. (b) `knownBuffs()` now walks the whole spellbook with a `pcall` per line and item and builds a `seen` set and a temporary array per spell, then the editor asks `C_Spell.GetSpellTexture` for every option; this runs on each change to the list, not once. (c) On every `SUUUI_AURA_FILTERS_CHANGED` and `SUUUI_DEFENSIVES_CHANGED`, RaidFrames calls `SuuUI.AuraFilterSpells` for each of four groups on each of forty buttons; each call walks the attached lists, builds sets and sorts, although the answer depends only on the frame kind, the set and the group's own list. `Core/AuraFilters` counts a `version` that nothing uses for caching.
- why it matters: steady garbage from the range ticker; a visible pause in the indicator editor on classes with a large spellbook; 160 filter computations per filter or defensives edit in the raid module.
- fix: (a) keep one `all` array filled in `build`. (b) cache `knownBuffs()` per session and clear it on `SPELLS_CHANGED` and `SUUUI_COOLDOWN_PRESETS`-type changes. (c) in `ApplyDefensives` compute each group's lists once before the button loop; or memoise `groupSpells` in Core per `(kind, set, own)` until `version` changes.
