#### UF-28: Aura filters: an edit can publish twice with a half-applied state, and the editor redraws while hidden
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/AuraFilters.wowlua:148-153 (`mutate`: `M:Set("lists", …)` then `M:Set("attached", …)`),
  1118-1145 (`DeleteList`), 1280-1290 (`WatchAll` → `Publish`; `SUUUI_AURA_FILTERS_CHANGED` → `Refresh`),
  1059-1063 (`Refresh`); src/Core/AuraFilters.wowlua:264-272 (`setState` → `changed()`)
- known: no
- what: `mutate` writes two settings one after the other; each write that differs fires the watcher, which publishes the whole state and emits `SUUUI_AURA_FILTERS_CHANGED`. `DeleteList` changes both, so the first publish carries the lists without the deleted one and the attachments still naming it; every frame module re-applies its filters for that state and again for the final one, and the editor refreshes twice. Separately, the module's `Refresh` redraws the editor on every such message (a plugin registering a list, a profile's lists changing) whether or not the settings page is shown; the editor already refreshes on `OnShow`.
- why it matters: two rounds of filter work on every frame for one click, the first with an attachment that resolves to nothing; needless layout of a hidden page. No wrong end state.
- fix: publish once per edit: let `mutate` set a flag that suppresses `Publish` during the two writes and publish after, or coalesce `Publish` with `after(0, …)`. In `Refresh` return when the editor is not visible.

### Fixed since the first pass

None in full. Partial fixes are described in UF-1 (setters skip unchanged
values, src/UI/Auras.wowlua:773-830; `UpdateOfflineOf`,
src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1465-1478) and UF-4 (pooled rows and unit tokens,
src/Units/Threat.wowlua:164-218).

### Withdrawn

None.

### Cross-cutting observations

- `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` is still handled everywhere at once; NEW added Threat (line 676) and more work in RaidFrames. A core-level coalesced roster message would remove most of the burst cost in one place.
- Game state changed without a record of what it was: nameplate CVars (UF-5), the meter CVar in a profile (UF-6). Worth sweeping every `SetCVar` in `src/`.
- `combat = true` on a settings row is only a sentence; each watcher has to defer by itself (UF-12). NEW added frame-script paths that write near engine containers in combat (pet `OnShow`/`OnHide`).
- The layer rule erodes with each performance fix: the build-ahead queue, pixel units and the health fill were reached by direct import instead of an export (UF-11). Other areas' modules probably did the same with `/Core/Ahead`.
- Probe notes live in code comments ("probed 2026-11-08") and decide behaviour, but the settings text and defaults do not always follow them (UF-24). A sweep of comments containing "probed" against the nearest setting description would find more.
- The Forever aura rule (another player's auras pass a filter word and its negation) is applied on group frames but not on nameplates, target and focus (UF-7), and a new negated split was added (UF-25). One helper that says "may this group split by this word on this unit kind" would make the rule checkable.
- Raw frame scripts bypass fault isolation: `OnUpdate` drivers, the plates' `OnEvent`, `HookScript` closures (pet `OnShow`/`OnHide`, `OnAttributeChanged`, the new editor's `OnClick`/`OnMouseUp` in `Units/AuraFilters`).
- Per-event `M:Get` in hot paths (nameplate health and threat, the threat tick, range tickers) remains; cache in locals refreshed by the watcher, or use `Peek`.
- Spell names as keys (UF-14) may exist in other modules' tables; a sweep for name lookups with a literal is cheap.

## Area: Units: cooldowns, action bars, mouse bindings


All file:line references are for the 0.17.0 export (NEW), repo-relative.

### Coverage

First-pass findings re-checked on NEW: all 26 (CD-1 to CD-26). Each one was
re-read in the NEW code named under "where".

Read in full in NEW:
- `src/Units/MouseBindings.wowlua` (2,499 lines, start to end).
- `src/Units/RankUpgrade.wowlua` (245 lines).

Diffs read in full (`4c6ea485..36f5f407`), plus the surrounding NEW code where
a finding depends on it: `ActionBars.wowlua`, `MicroMenu.wowlua`,
`CooldownManager/Migrations.wowlua` (the whole NEW file), `Campsite.wowlua`,
`Minimap.wowlua`, `Marks.wowlua`, `GameMenu.wowlua`, `CooldownManager.wowlua`,
`Support.wowlua`, `Convergences.wowlua`, `CooldownManager/Conditions.wowlua`.

Unchanged between the two commits (no diff), so the first pass's full read
stands and only the cited places were re-read: `Timeline.wowlua`,
`MicroBags.wowlua`, `CooldownManager/Lists.wowlua`.

Read to check claims: `src/Core/Modules.wowlua` (`RunOutOfCombat`,
`releaseAll`), `src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua` (the secure frame list, 1185-1215,
2385-2400), `src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua` (the headers' `INIT`, the buttons
made ahead, 1835-1856), `src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua` (the driver 1525-1552,
the event wiring 2452-2490, `UpdateCooldowns` 2304-2318), the stdlib's
`secure.overlay`.

Not done: nothing was run (no `wowlua`, no tests). `src/UI/ActionButton.wowlua`,
`src/UI/Timeline.wowlua`, `src/UI/MicroMenu.wowlua` and the Spellbook's side of
the mouse bindings (`src/Units/Spellbook.wowlua`, `src/UI/Spellbook.wowlua`)
were not read. The test files of the new modules were not read.

### Summary

- Two first-pass performance findings are fixed in 0.17.0: the tracker no
  longer re-reads every cooldown on a power tick (CD-7), and the micro menu no
  longer rebuilds its item list seven times a second (CD-13). Marks' minimap
  pins now stand still while you do (CD-8, partly).
- Everything else from the first pass is still there, most of it in unchanged
  code: the `/quit` cover that survives a dialog closed in combat (CD-1), the
  addon messages taken from anyone (CD-2, now four receivers: Campsite's shared
  fires joined), Timeline's leftovers after disable (CD-3, CD-4), state kept in
  profile settings (CD-5), uncoalesced talent events and action bar watchers
  (CD-6, CD-12).
- The new mouseover bindings module is careful about combat (every secure
  write is out of combat or queued, the boxes close when a fight starts,
  `OnDisable` clears every attribute and puts the game's click bindings back).
  Its weak spots: a unit frame that hides under the mouse leaves its keys bound
  to a dead unit (CD-27, needs an in-game check), and every apply clears and
  rewrites every attribute on every unit frame (CD-29).
- The new rank upgrade places spells into action slots without checking that
  the cursor holds the spell or that the slot still holds what was read; with
  an empty cursor `PlaceAction` picks the slot's action up and `ClearCursor`
  deletes it (CD-28).
- The three new CooldownManager migrations are idempotent, keyed per class and
  safe on missing tables; they repeat the older gap (the lists from before
  setups are skipped) (CD-22).
- MicroMenu's new handling of the game's menu button leaves hooks that keep
  hiding that button's tooltip after the module is turned off (CD-30).
- Structure: MouseBindings is a new 2,500-line file holding pure input logic,
  two dialogs, a list and the secure part; three modules now walk the spellbook
  for ranks on `SPELLS_CHANGED`, each with its own code (CD-33).

### Findings

#### CD-1: The secure /quit cover of "Exit the game?" stays active when the question closes in combat
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (a cover the lockdown keeps is hidden after combat through RunOutOfCombat, the question and its cover close at PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED (StandDownQuit), and a PostClick closes the question a frame later)
- where: src/Units/GameMenu.wowlua:432-457 (`ConfirmQuit`), 461-492 (`PlaceSecure`, for comparison), 598-606; stdlib `secure.overlay` (`show`, `hide` and `set` start with `if InCombatLockdown() then` and return false); src/UI/Panel.wowlua:714 (`confirm`, one shared dialog)
- known: no
- what: `ConfirmQuit` puts a secure button (`secure.overlay(d.ok, { strata = "FULLSCREEN_DIALOG" })`, `macrotext1 = "/quit"`) over the shared confirm dialog's OK button and hides it only from the dialog's `OnHide`:
  ```
  d:HookScript("OnHide", function()
      made.hide()
  end)
  ```
  `made.hide()` does nothing in combat and returns false. Nothing reads the result and nothing retries after combat. The menu's own covers have a `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` handler (598-606) and a `PostClick`; the quit cover has neither.
- why it matters: open Exit Game out of combat, get attacked, press Esc or Cancel. The dialog hides, the cover does not: an invisible button that runs `/quit` stays in the middle of the screen until the next `ConfirmQuit`. `UI.Confirm` is one shared dialog, so any other question shown afterwards has its OK button under the `/quit` cover: confirming it exits the game and never runs its own `onConfirm`. Also, the hook is added to the shared dialog once and fires for every later question (harmless out of combat).
- fix: (1) In the `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` handler (it runs before lockdown, as `PlaceSecure` relies on) call `self.quitOver.hide()` and hide the confirm dialog if it is the quit question. (2) In the `OnHide` hook, when `made.hide()` returns false, queue it: `self:RunOutOfCombat("quitOver", function() made.hide() end)`. (3) Add a `PostClick` that hides the dialog next frame, as the menu's covers do. Test in `tests/unit/Units/GameMenu.test.wowlua`: dialog open, combat starts, dialog closes, the cover is hidden; a second `UI.Confirm` has no cover.

#### CD-2: Addon messages are taken from any channel and any sender; Marks and Timeline validate too little
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the `C_Map.GetMapInfo` error on a bad map id needs in-game probe
- status: fixed in db302207 (Core/Comm takes MARK, PULL, CONV and FIRE from the group's channels only, plus the guild for Convergences and Campsite, with per-sender rates; PULL only from the leader or an assistant; Marks checks the map with `SuuUI.Comm.Map`, cleans and caps the name, keeps 30 per sender and never pushes out an own mark; Campsite drops shared fires before own ones)
- where: src/Units/Marks.wowlua:163-173 (`decodeMark`), 777-802 (`OnMessage`), 70-81 (`makeRoom`), 770-773 (`MapName`); src/Units/Timeline.wowlua:886-903 (`OnMessage`); src/Units/Convergences.wowlua:586-631 (`OnMessage`); src/Units/Campsite.wowlua:504-535 (`OnMessage`), 167-186 (`addFire`)
- known: no
- what: all four listen to `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` for prefix `SuuUI` and ignore the channel argument (`_channel`, `_`), so a `WHISPER` (or a custom channel) message from any player is handled like a group member's.
  - Marks: `decodeMark` checks only `0 <= x,y <= 1`. The map id is any number (fractional, negative, huge); the name is kept as sent (the sender-side `clean` is not applied on receipt: `|` escapes and any length go into the saved mark, the tooltip and the card); there is no limit per sender. `MapName` calls `C_Map.GetMapInfo(mark.map)` unprotected. Every new position is a new saved mark, up to `MAX_MARKS` = 200 per character. `makeRoom` removes "the oldest shared, then the oldest": with 200 marks of your own, each incoming shared mark deletes one of yours.
  - Timeline: `PULL\t<n>` from anyone starts `StartPull` (alert, ticker, countdown voice), with no check that the sender is in your group or leads it.
  - Convergences validates the payload well (integer map, `GetMapInfo`, 30 per sender a session) but accepts whispers, so strangers can add spots (200 saved account-wide).
  - Campsite (new): validates the payload (integer map, `GetMapInfo`, 10 per sender a minute) but accepts whispers. `addFire` drops the oldest fire past `MAX_FIRES` = 100 whoever found it, so shared fires push out your own. `self.taken[sender]` is never pruned (one small table per sender name for the session).
- why it matters: a stranger can fill a character's saved marks and world map with junk (persistent), push out your own marks and fires, and pop a "Pull in 10" alert with voice on your screen at will. If `C_Map.GetMapInfo` raises on a non-integer or out-of-range id, one bad MARK message makes the pin tooltip and the mark card error on every use until the mark is removed.
- fix: one shared receiver (CD-9) that drops a message unless the channel is `PARTY`, `RAID` or `INSTANCE_CHAT` (and `GUILD` for Convergences and Campsite, which send there), and that checks every argument for secrets before comparing (CD-26). Marks: require an integer map with `C_Map.GetMapInfo(map)` in `pcall`, run `clean` and a length cap (40) on the received name, cap marks per sender, and when the list is full drop the incoming shared mark instead of evicting an own one. Campsite: evict shared fires before own ones. Timeline: accept `PULL` only from the group's leader or an assistant (`UnitIsGroupLeader(sender)` / `UnitIsGroupAssistant(sender)`). Tests: `tests/unit/Units/Marks.test.wowlua`, `Timeline.test.wowlua`, `Convergences.test.wowlua`, `Campsite.test.wowlua` (whisper refused; bad map refused; a full list keeps own entries).

#### CD-27: A unit frame that hides under the mouse leaves its mouseover keys bound to a dead unit
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe (whether `OnLeave` runs for a secure unit frame hidden while the mouse is over it on Forever; in other clients it does not)
- status: fixed in 68ae02ee (a secure OnHide wrap resets the frame state, and `_refresh` ignores the frame state unless the hovered frame is visible and its unit exists; the probe found that `OnLeave` fires as a frame hides under the mouse, so the stuck state could not arise on this client and the fix is a safety net)
- probe (2026-11-15, build 70888): `OnLeave` fires during `Hide()` when a frame hides under the mouse (tried on a plain frame of the probe's own; a secure unit frame with wrapped scripts was not tried).
- where: src/Units/MouseBindings.wowlua:2394-2405 (the `OnEnter` / `OnLeave` wraps), 690-717 (`refreshSnippet`), 2201-2204 (the state handlers)
- known: no
- what: the frame's state is set only by the two wraps:
  ```
  SecureHandlerWrapScript(f, "OnEnter", owner, [=[ ... owner:SetAttribute("state-frame", r) ]=])
  SecureHandlerWrapScript(f, "OnLeave", owner, [=[ owner:SetAttribute("state-frame", "off") ]=])
  ```
  and `_refresh` gives the frame state priority over the world's mouseover state:
  ```
  local r = self:GetAttribute("state-frame")
  if r and r ~= "off" then
  <frame keys: SetBindingClick(true, key, frameButton, …)>
  else
  r = self:GetAttribute("state-mo")
  ```
  Nothing else ever resets `state-frame`. If the hovered frame hides (target cleared with the mouse on the target frame, a party or raid member leaves, target-of-target goes, a boss frame ends) and no `OnLeave` runs, `state-frame` stays `help`/`harm`/`other`, the frame's keys stay as priority override bindings on `SuuUIMouseBindingsFrame`, whose `unit` attribute is still the old frame's, and the world keys are never bound (the `else` branch is not reached) until the mouse next enters and leaves a SuuUI unit frame.
- why it matters: a healer binds the wheel or a key on frames, hovers the target frame and the target dies or is dropped (in combat, where it matters): from then on that key or the wheel casts at a unit that is gone ("target", "party3") everywhere on screen, its normal job (camera zoom, an action button) is dead, and mouseover casting in the world is off, with no visible cause.
- fix: probe first (`/suu probe mouseover`: hover the target frame, clear the target, read `state-frame`). If `OnLeave` does not run: keep the hovered frame in the owner's restricted environment (`hovered = self` in the `OnEnter` wrap, `hovered = nil` in `OnLeave`), and at the top of `_refresh` drop a stale one: `if hovered and not (hovered:IsVisible() and hovered:IsUnderMouse(true)) then hovered = nil; self:SetAttribute("state-frame", "off"); return end` (the attribute change runs `_refresh` again). `_refresh` already runs on every `state-mo` change, which a hiding unit frame causes; add a second driver that changes when frames commonly hide (`[@target,exists] 1; 0`) for the case where the mouseover state does not move. Test in `tests/unit/Units/MouseBindings.test.wowlua`: enter a frame, hide it, the frame keys are gone and the world keys bind.

#### CD-28: The rank upgrade places into action slots blind: an empty cursor deletes the slot's action, and a delayed upgrade writes into slots that may have changed
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the missing checks; likely for how often `C_Spell.PickupSpell` leaves the cursor empty (needs in-game probe: a spell ID the book lists but that cannot be picked up)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/ActionBars/RankUpgrade.wowlua:144-174 (`Place`), 208-255 (`Apply`);
  src/Units/ActionBars.wowlua:1361-1365 (`onConfirm`), 1473-1478 (`placePending` retried at
  `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` only), 1305-1314 (`SpecMaybeSwitched` keeps it)
- known: no
- what: both paths do
  ```
  C_Spell.PickupSpell(s.id)
  PlaceAction(s.slot)
  ClearCursor()
  ```
  with no check that the cursor holds a spell after `PickupSpell`. With an empty cursor, `PlaceAction(slot)` picks up what is in the slot, and `ClearCursor()` then throws it away. `Place(list)` also never re-reads the slots: the list was built by `Stale()` when the popup opened. If `Place` returns false (cursor busy, or the popup answered in combat), ActionBars keeps the list in `placePending` and tries again only at the next `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`, which for a busy cursor out of combat can be minutes later, after the player rearranged bars or switched spec back: the slot numbers then belong to other buttons, which are overwritten with the remembered spell.
- why it matters: action bar contents are lost or replaced without the player doing anything: a button vanishes when a pickup fails, or a remembered rank lands on a slot of the other spec's bars.
- fix: in both loops, after `PickupSpell` require `GetCursorInfo()` to return `"spell"` (and skip the slot, counting nothing, otherwise); before each placement re-read the slot (`GetActionInfo(slot)` is a spell whose name is `s.name` and whose rank is `s.from`) and skip it when it changed. In ActionBars drop `placePending` when the spec group changes (`SpecMaybeSwitched`), and retry a busy cursor with a short timer as `RankUpgrader:Apply` does (213-221) instead of waiting for a fight to end. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/RankUpgrade.test.wowlua` (a pickup that leaves the cursor empty changes nothing; a slot changed since `Stale` is left alone), `tests/unit/Units/ActionBars.test.wowlua` (a pending upgrade is dropped on a spec switch).

#### CD-29: Every apply of the mouse bindings clears and rewrites every attribute on every unit frame
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the cost in a raid needs the dev profiler in game
- status: open
- where: src/Units/MouseBindings.wowlua:586-742 (`Apply`), 598-609 (clearing), 666-681 (per frame, per
  binding); src/Units/MouseBindings/Secure.wowlua:22 (`castAttributes`);
  src/Units/MouseBindings.wowlua:746-756 (`ApplySoon`), 787-791 (the events), 508 (`UnitFrames`)
- known: no
- what: `Apply` runs 0.2 s after every `SPELLS_CHANGED`, `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` and `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`, and on every change. Each run sets every attribute it set before to nil on every frame, then sets them all again:
  ```
  for _, f in ipairs(frames) do
      ...
      for _, kv in ipairs(castAttributes(prefix, suffix, n, fAny, fHelp, fHarm)) do
          f:SetAttribute(kv[1] :: string, kv[2])
  ```
  `castAttributes` (a list of 2 to 7 small tables) is built again for every frame although its arguments do not depend on the frame. The frame list is every secure SuuUI unit frame: player, target, party, boss and the raid's 40 buttons plus 40 pet buttons, all made ahead (src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1835-1856). Each `SetAttribute` on a secure unit button also runs the frame's `OnAttributeChanged`.
- why it matters: with 8 click bindings and about 100 frames one apply is about 800 `castAttributes` calls (some 4,000 short-lived tables and 3,000 concatenated strings) and 3,000 to 5,000 `SetAttribute` calls to clear plus as many to set, for a result that is identical almost every time. `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` comes in bursts while a raid forms and whenever someone moves, goes offline or changes role; the apply queued during a fight lands in the frame combat ends, with everything else that waits for it. The comment at 2211-2212 records that the earlier frame walk alone cost up to 39 ms there.
- fix: (1) build the attribute list once per binding, outside the frame loop. (2) keep per frame a map `name -> value` of what was applied, build the wanted map once, and write only the differences (a frame new to the list gets everything; an unchanged frame gets nothing). (3) skip `Apply` when nothing it depends on changed: a signature of the bindings with their cast IDs, the clicks and the frame count; `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` then costs one list length compare. (4) `SPELLS_CHANGED` only matters when a bound spell's top rank changed: compare `castID` per binding. Test in `tests/unit/Units/MouseBindings.test.wowlua`: a second `Apply` with the same bindings makes no `SetAttribute` call (count them through a hook on one frame).

#### CD-3: The encounter timeline shows again after the module is turned off
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (`Refresh` and the three `AddonTimer*` methods return while the module is off; `OnDisable` clears `addonTimers` and `refreshToken`)
- where: src/Units/Timeline.wowlua:392-431 (`AddonTimer`, `AddonTimerStop`, `AddonTimerPause`), 513-586 (`HookSources`), 645-677 (`Refresh`), 1046-1059 (`OnDisable`)
- known: no
- what: `HookSources` registers callbacks with the boss mods once for the session (`pcall(register, dbm, event, fn)`); they are not module events, so disabling does not remove them. They call `self:AddonTimer(...)`, which ends in `self:Refresh()`. Neither checks `self:IsEnabled()` (the only checks in the file are at 442 and in the delayed re-read at 672). `Refresh` ends with `timeline:SetShown(shown and true or false)`. `OnDisable` hides the timeline and leaves `addonTimers` as it is.
- why it matters: with a boss mod chosen as the source, turn the Timeline module off: the next boss timer fills `addonTimers` and shows the timeline frame again, with no mover and no settings.
- fix: `Refresh` returns at once when `not self:IsEnabled()`; the three `AddonTimer*` methods too (so the table does not grow); `OnDisable` sets `self.addonTimers = {}` and `self.refreshToken = nil`. Test in `tests/unit/Units/Timeline.test.wowlua`: disabled, a source callback fires, the frame stays hidden.

#### CD-4: The other addon's "hide warnings" option is remembered in the profile, so a profile switch leaves it on for good
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (the player's value is kept in the character's data, given back at PLAYER_LOGOUT, and the old profile value is moved over at enable)
- where: src/Units/Timeline.wowlua:44 (`dbmWarningsWas` default), 445-459 (`ApplySuppression`), 1049-1053 (`OnDisable`)
- known: no
- what: while a boss mod feeds the timeline and "Hide their bars" is on, SuuUI writes `true` into that addon's own options table and keeps the previous value in the profile setting `dbmWarningsWas` (`""`, `"true"` or `"false"`):
  ```
  if want and was == "" then
      self:Set("dbmWarningsWas", options.HideDBMWarnings and "true" or "false")
      options.HideDBMWarnings = true
  ```
  The other addon's option is not per SuuUI profile.
- why it matters: profile A suppresses (was = `"false"`, their option now `true`). Switch to profile B, where `dbmWarningsWas` is `""`: if B also suppresses, the current value (SuuUI's own `true`) is recorded as the user's and later "restored"; if B does not suppress, nothing restores it. Either way the other addon's warnings stay hidden with no hint why. The same happens with Reset on the Timeline settings, and when SuuUI is disabled at the character screen while suppressing.
- fix: keep the remembered value outside profiles (`SuuUI.AccountData("timeline")`), restore it on `PLAYER_LOGOUT` and apply it again at login, so the other addon never saves SuuUI's value. Move the existing profile value over in a migration. Test in `tests/unit/Units/Timeline.test.wowlua`: suppress, switch profile, their option is back.

#### CD-5: Run-time state is kept in profile settings; "Seen recently" is rewritten on casts in combat
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed (db302207: "Seen recently" and `viewerOff` moved to the character's data with migrations, so a cast in combat no longer writes a setting; MicroMenu's `seenPluginButtons` is still a profile setting)
- where: src/Units/MicroMenu.wowlua:42 (`seenPluginButtons` default), 380-398
- known: no
- what: these are not choices the player makes, but they are registered as settings, so they are part of the profile: exported, imported, reset and swapped with it, and every write goes through `M:Set` (watchers, `SUUUI_SETTING_CHANGED` to every listener; Marks now listens to that message too, src/Units/Marks.wowlua:1138).
  - `recent`: `remember` runs on the player's casts: `M:Get("recent")` (a deep copy of every class's lists), `copy(all)` again, then `M:Set("recent", changed)`, in combat, whenever the cast spell is not already near the top of the list.
  - `viewerOff`: "this module switched Blizzard's Cooldown Manager off". Reset the module's settings or switch profile and the flag is gone; turning the module off then no longer switches Blizzard's manager back on.
  - `seenPluginButtons`: a new profile has an empty list, so every plugin button is "new" again and is re-added to `buttons` even if that profile had hidden it.
- why it matters: wrong restores after a profile switch or reset, profile exports that carry one character's cast history, and a settings write with a global broadcast in the cast path during combat.
- fix: move `recent` to `M:CharData()` (kept in memory, written when the editor opens or on `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`); move `viewerOff` to `M:CharData()` (the CVar is the client's, not the profile's); keep `seenPluginButtons` in account data. One migration each that moves the old profile value. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/CooldownManager.test.wowlua`, `MicroMenu.test.wowlua`.

#### CD-6: Talent events are not coalesced: every one schedules its own full walk of the talent trees
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/CooldownManager.wowlua:614-625 (`respec`), 95-120 (`treePoints`), 437-448 (`UpdateSpec`)
- known: no
- what:
  ```
  local function respec()
      after(0.2, function()
          self:UpdateSpec()
      end)
  end
  ```
  is registered for seven events, among them `TRAIT_NODE_CHANGED` (one per node) and `CHARACTER_POINTS_CHANGED`. There is no pending flag, so N events make N timers and N calls of `treePoints`, each of which calls `C_Traits.GetTreeNodes` and `GetNodeInfo` for every node of every tree and builds a table per node. The timer does not check `self:IsEnabled()` either.
- why it matters: a respec or a talent loadout fires dozens of node events in one frame; 0.2 s later the same full walk runs dozens of times in one frame, a visible hitch with the talent window open. ActionBars (new `SpecMaybeSwitched`) and MouseBindings (`ApplySoon`, with a flag) listen to the same bursts; only this one walks the trees per event.
- fix: one pending flag (`if self.specPending then return end; self.specPending = true; after(0.2, function() self.specPending = false; if self:IsEnabled() then self:UpdateSpec() end end)`). Test in `tests/unit/Units/CooldownManager.test.wowlua`: ten events, one `DetectSpec`.

#### CD-9: Marks, Convergences, Campsite and Timeline each carry their own messaging; Marks and Convergences duplicate the minimap layer and world positions
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed (db302207: one receiver and sender for SuuUI's addon messages, Core/Comm, with the channel, rank, rate, own-sender, secret and name checks; Marks and Convergences still each keep a world position cache, a map-to-map conversion and a minimap layer with its own 0.1 s `OnUpdate`)
- where: src/Units/Marks.wowlua:189-209 (`worldOf`), 660-680 (`PlaceOn`), 833-923 (minimap layer);
  src/Units/Convergences.wowlua:99-117 (world cache), 742-770 (`UpdateMinimap` and its `OnUpdate`)
- known: no
- what: the same code several times, with drift: "which group channel" (three versions), "is this sender me" (three: Marks' `isOwnSender`, Campsite's `fromMe`, Timeline with `Ambiguate`), cleaning a name (Convergences and Campsite cap at 40 characters, Marks does not clean on receipt), a per-sender cap (per session in Convergences, per minute in Campsite, none in Marks and Timeline), the secret checks in a different order in each. Four modules register the `SuuUI` prefix and parse `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` themselves, so every addon message of the prefix runs four handlers. Marks and Convergences also each have a weak-keyed world position cache, a map-to-map conversion, and a child frame of `Minimap` with its own 0.1 s `OnUpdate`.
- why it matters: the fixes in CD-2, CD-8 and CD-26 have to be made two to four times, and the drift is already there. Two timers place pins on the same minimap.
- fix: two public API pieces, documented in `Docs/API.md` under the next API version:
  1. `SuuUI.Comm`: `Register(tag, handler, { channels = … })` and `Send(tag, payload, channels)`, which owns the prefix, the secret checks, the channel filter, the own-sender check, name cleaning and a per-sender rate cap. Marks (`MARK`), Convergences (`CONV`), Campsite (`FIRE`) and Timeline (`PULL`) keep only their payload checks. Wire formats must stay as they are (other players run older versions).
  2. `SuuUI.MinimapPins` (or a `UI.MinimapLayer`): one layer and one tick, `Add(owner, { world = …, make/update pin })`, the player's position read once per tick, the layer hidden while it has no pins. Marks and Convergences register sources.

#### CD-11: Turning the XP bar or the totem bar on does not stand Blizzard's down until a reload; the stance bar's text promises a return that never happens
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (`ApplyOptions` stands down the XP and totem bars through RunOutOfCombat when turned on, the PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD re-suppress is always registered with the check inside, and the stance row now says off means no stance bar)
- where: src/Units/ActionBars.wowlua:352-384 (`standDownBlizzard`), 340-350 (`suppressTracking`), 772-837 (`ApplyOptions`), 1418-1420, 501, 539, 546 (the rows' descriptions)
- known: no
- what: `standDownBlizzard` runs once, in `start()`. It suppresses the tracking bars only `if M:Get("showXP")` and the totem bar only `if M:Get("showTotem")`, both read at that moment; the `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` re-suppress is registered only if `showXP` was on at enable (`if self:Get("showXP") then self:OnGameEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD", suppressTracking) end`). `ApplyOptions`, which the watchers of `showXP` and `showTotem` call, never suppresses. The stance and pet bars are suppressed always (`extras` at 362), whatever `showStance` says, yet the "Stance and form bar" row says "Blizzard's own comes back after a reload".
- why it matters: log in with the XP bar off, turn it on: SuuUI's bar and Blizzard's both show until the next reload (same for a shaman's totem bar). Turn the stance bar off and reload: there is no stance bar at all, against what the setting says.
- fix: in `ApplyOptions` (out of combat, through `RunOutOfCombat`), call `suppressTracking()` when `showXP` is on and suppress the totem bar when `showTotem` is on; register the `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` handler always, with the check inside. For the stance bar decide one way: suppress Blizzard's only while `showStance` is on, or change the row's description. Test in `tests/unit/Units/ActionBars.test.wowlua`: `showXP` false at enable, then true, Blizzard's manager is suppressed.

#### CD-12: Every watched action bar setting runs the whole `ApplyOptions`
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open

#### CD-14: A Skysight cast is forgotten if any aura changes before the blessing arrives; "Share all" silently stops at 30 per receiver
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (the event order between the cast and the blessing needs an in-game probe); the cap is confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Convergences.wowlua:461-500 (`OnCast`, `Resolve`), 176-191 (`blessing`), 818-822 (the
  `UNIT_AURA` handler), 69 and 598-607 (`MAX_PER_SENDER`), 552-590 (`ShareAll`), 318-329 (the Share all
  description)
- known: no
- what: `Resolve` reads the long blessing; out of combat a missing aura reads as `nil` (`blessing` returns false only in combat or when unreadable), and the next line is `self.pending = nil`. `Resolve` is called from every player `UNIT_AURA` while a cast is pending (`if self.pending and not InCombatLockdown() then self:Resolve() end`) and from a 0.5 s timer. So the first aura event after the cast that is not the blessing's (a proc, a buff from someone else, the timer on a slow connection) drops the pending cast and the convergence is never learned. Separately, a receiver takes at most 30 new spots from one sender per session, while "Share all" sends every one (up to 200) and gives no feedback.
- why it matters: learning convergences is the module's core; a missed one costs the player the save and the share. A player with more than 30 spots cannot hand them all to a guild mate without both knowing to reload.
- fix: in `Resolve`, when the aura is absent and `GetTime() - p.cast < 3`, keep `pending` and return (the existing `PENDING_FOR` and the start-time check keep it safe); clear it only after that window. For sharing, a cap per minute (as Campsite's `PER_MINUTE`) instead of per session, or say in the "Share all" description that receivers take 30 per session. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Convergences.test.wowlua` (an unrelated aura event between cast and blessing).

#### CD-32: Mouse bindings: what stays when the module is off, and small gaps
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code), except (e) needs in-game probe
- status: partly fixed (db302207: `OnDisable` closes both boxes, the mouseover state driver is unregistered while off, and the game's clicks come back at the next login with the module off; still open: the file-level `bookWatch` frame, a new rank switch per `CaptureBox:Open`, `commit` returning silently in combat, no message for secure frames made later, no restore at logout or with SuuUI itself off, and `Apply` trusting the saved shape)
- where: src/Units/MouseBindings/Ranks.wowlua:33-35 (`bookWatch`);
  src/Units/MouseBindings/Boxes.wowlua:295-301 (`rankSeg`); src/Units/MouseBindings.wowlua:397-404 (`commit`),
  529-581 (`SyncClickBindings`), 836-856 (`clicksBack`), 610-620 (`slot[b.react] = b`)
- known: no
- what:
  - (a) `OnDisable` only calls `Apply()` (which clears the attributes and the snippet and puts the game's click bindings back, correctly, queued when in combat). It does not close the capture box, the click box or a pending confirm; the box's `OnKeyDown` returns early in combat without touching `SetPropagateKeyboardInput`, and the `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` handler that closes the boxes is gone with the module, so a box left open with the last key not passed on swallows the keyboard in the next fight.
  - (b) the `mo` state driver (`RegisterStateDriver(owner, "mo", …)`) is never unregistered: with the module off, every mouseover change still runs the restricted `_refresh`. The file-level `bookWatch` frame listens to `SPELLS_CHANGED` whether the module is on or not.
  - (c) `CaptureBox:Open` makes a new `UI.Segmented` for every ranked spell opened (`self.rankSeg:Hide(); self.rankSeg = nil`, then a new one): frames are never freed.
  - (d) `commit` in `Press` returns silently when a fight started while the question was open: `done` is never called, so the Spellbook's bind mode gets no answer. Unit frames made later (anything not made by login or followed by `SPELLS_CHANGED`, `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` or `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`) get no bindings until one of those events: `secureUnitFrames` has no "frame made" message.
  - (e) the moved Target and Menu clicks are written into the game's own click-binding profile (`C_ClickBindings.SetProfileByInfo`), which the game saves. They are put back only by this module's `OnDisable`. If SuuUI is switched off in the addon list (or removed) while they are moved, the game's own unit frames no longer target on a left click, and nothing in the game says why. The setting's text says "on unit frames … In the world the game's own clicks stay", but the game's profile is one for every unit button of every addon.
  - (f) `Apply` trusts the saved shape: a saved binding without `react` or `input` raises "table index is nil" at `slot[b.react] = b` / `byInput[b.input]` in `OnEnable`, which fails the module. The module writes only complete bindings today; a hand-edited or future-version file is the risk.
- fix: (a) `OnDisable` closes both boxes; the boxes' `OnKeyDown` checks `self.owner:IsEnabled()`. (b) `UnregisterStateDriver(owner, "mo")` when the apply runs disabled, registered again on enable. (c) keep one rank switch and change its label (or pool by rank). (d) call `done("In combat", …)` in `commit`; emit a message from `UnitFrame`'s constructor when a secure frame is added (`SUUUI_SECURE_UNIT_FRAME`, documented in `Docs/API.md`) and `ApplySoon` on it. (e) probe (`/suu probe mouseover`: move Target, disable SuuUI, left click a Blizzard unit frame); at least restore the defaults on `PLAYER_LOGOUT` and apply them again at login, so the game never saves SuuUI's values, and say in the row's text that the click moves for all unit frames. (f) drop bindings that lack `input`, `spell`, `reach` or `react` when the store is first read. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/MouseBindings.test.wowlua`.

- what: `slotUids` walks only the top level of each list (`for i, raw in ipairs(list(l))`), so a shared slot saved inside a collection before uids existed stays without one. `slotUids` and `missingPerEntry` also handle `values.lists` (the shape from before setups); the five later migrations go through `eachSetup` only (`values.setups`), while `MigrateLists` copies those unmigrated lists into a setup afterwards, when the migrations are already marked done. `addRacials` gives the copied Racials collection the uid a preset copy would get, but its entries are copied as the preset has them, without the per-entry uids `copyLists` gives; and it collects "names the setup already holds" from top-level entries and collection entries only, not from a shared slot's `members`, so a racial already inside a shared slot is added a second time.
  The three new migrations themselves are sound: each is keyed per class (`"racials-" .. CLASS`), touches only that class's setups, guards every level with `tableOf` / `list`, and running one twice changes nothing (`addRacials` stops at an existing Racials collection, `presetIDs` adds only missing IDs, `untanglePresetIDs` removes only IDs another preset spell owns). Their order (`preset-ids-eclipse` before `preset-ids-untangle`) is right.
- why it matters: only old profiles: a slot that loses its open Behaviour panel on reorder, a shaman's old Shields slot that keeps its fixed icon, a setup made from pre-setup lists without the Racials collection or the mended IDs, a racial shown twice.
- fix: `slotUids` recurses into `e.entries` (uid `tag .. key .. i .. "." .. j`, as `copyLists`); the later migrations also run over `values.lists` when `values.preset` belongs to the class (or `MigrateLists` runs before the settings migrations, as its own first migration); `addRacials` builds its copy with `copyLists`' uid scheme and also reads `members` names. Correct them under new migration ids (all are idempotent). Extend `tests/profiles/cooldowns-migrations.json` and `tests/unit/Units/CooldownManager/Migrations.test.wowlua` with a slot inside a collection, an old `lists` with the Shields slot, and a setup holding a racial inside a shared slot.

#### CD-23: Minimap: the clock can be ten seconds late, the invisible cluster's children keep their mouse, other addons' buttons are not handled
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the clock; needs in-game probe for the cluster's children
- status: open

  (`alphaOff`), 731 (`GetMinimapShape`)
- known: no
- what: (a) `UpdateClock` runs from `every(10, …)` started whenever the module started, so the minute changes up to 10 s late (the settings preview, new in 0.17.0, reads its clock every second: 641-648). (b) `alphaOff` turns the mouse off on the frame it is given, not on its children; anything in the invisible cluster that is not listed by name still takes the mouse and shows tooltips. (c) the module publishes `GetMinimapShape` for other addons' minimap buttons but does nothing else for them.

(b) probe (`/suu probe` listing mouse-enabled descendants of `MinimapCluster`), then turn the mouse off on those that are not SuuUI's or the queue button. (c) a design decision for the owner: gather them into a drawer, or leave as is and say so in the settings text.

#### CD-26: The addon message prefix is compared before the arguments are checked for secrets
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe (can `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` arguments be secret on Forever, for example in an instance?)
- status: fixed in db302207 (Core/Comm checks all four CHAT_MSG_ADDON arguments for secrets before comparing anything; no module in this area listens to CHAT_MSG_ADDON itself any more)
- where: src/Units/Marks.wowlua:778-781; src/Units/Convergences.wowlua:587-590; src/Units/Campsite.wowlua:505-508; src/Units/Timeline.wowlua:887
- known: no
- what: all four start with `if prefix ~= PREFIX or …` and check `text` and `sender` for secrets after it. If the prefix can be secret too, that comparison is the error the later checks were meant to avoid, once per addon message from any addon, in four handlers.
- fix: check `secret.readable(prefix)` first (in the shared receiver of CD-9). Probe by logging `issecretvalue` of the four arguments in a dungeon and a battleground.

### Fixed since the first pass

- CD-7 (The tracker re-reads every cooldown on every power tick): `UNIT_POWER_FREQUENT`, `SPELL_UPDATE_USABLE` and `ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_USABLE` now set `usableDirty` and the driver runs a light pass that keeps the cooldowns as read (src/UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:2466-2486, 1540-1551, `TrackerCell:Update(opts, light)` at 529-536).
- CD-13 (The micro menu rebuilds its item list seven times a second): `Layout` keeps the list in `self.laidItems` and `UpdateActive` walks it (src/Units/MicroMenu.wowlua:410-433). What is left is minor: `Items()` still reads the two modules inside its loop, at layout time only (346-355).

### Withdrawn

- None. Every other first-pass finding was found again in the NEW code.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Hooks on Blizzard frames that outlive the module** need a check at their top, every one of them. 0.17.0 added several (MicroMenu's menu button, the help tips, ActionBars' Quick Keybind); most check `IsEnabled()` or an "adopted" flag, some do not (CD-30). The same sweep as for Timeline's callbacks (CD-3).
- **"Hook once" guards that also guard module listeners**: a `self:On(...)` or `self:OnGameEvent(...)` registered inside an `if self.hooked then return end` block is lost on the first disable (CD-31). Sweep for `self:On` / `self:Watch` calls outside `OnEnable`'s straight path.
- **A frame read once at enable** (`HelpFrame`, `QuickKeybindFrame`, a boss mod's table): if it loads later, the feature is silently off for the session (CD-18, CD-20, CD-31). A small helper "when this frame exists" (now or on `ADDON_LOADED`) would remove the class.
- **Secure state that depends on `OnLeave`**: any restricted state set in an `OnEnter` wrap and cleared only in `OnLeave` is stuck when the frame hides under the mouse (CD-27). Worth checking other secure hover logic (mouseover fade of bars, nameplates).
- **"Clear everything, set everything" applies** on bursty events: MouseBindings' `Apply` (CD-29), ActionBars' `ApplyOptions` (CD-12), CooldownManager's `setups` watchers (CD-16). Diffing against what was applied, or a signature to skip identical applies, fits all three.
- **Writing into state the game or another addon saves** (the game's click-binding profile, another addon's option, a CVar): the restore lives in `OnDisable` only, so it is lost when SuuUI is switched off at the character screen, on a profile switch, or on a crash (CD-4, CD-5 `viewerOff`, CD-15, CD-32e). Restoring on `PLAYER_LOGOUT` and re-applying at login keeps SuuUI's value out of what gets saved.
- **Addon messages**: one prefix, now four parsers, no shared validation and no channel filter (CD-2, CD-9, CD-26). Any other module that sends or receives on `SuuUI` should go through one receiver.
- **Placing things with the cursor** (`PickupSpell` + `PlaceAction` + `ClearCursor`): always check what the cursor holds between the steps (CD-28). Sweep other uses of `PickupSpell`, `PickupItem`, `PickupMacro` and `PlaceAction` outside this area.
- **Run-time state in profile settings** (CD-4, CD-5): the newer modules do this right (`CharData` in MouseBindings, ActionBars' `rankDeclined`, Campsite's fires); the older keys are still in `DEFAULTS`.
- **Spellbook walks on `SPELLS_CHANGED`**: MouseBindings, RankUpgrade and CooldownManager's candidates each read the whole book on their own (CD-33). One shared index would serve all.

## Area: Units: chat, notifications, loot rolls


All file:line references are for the 0.17.0 export (NEW), repo-relative.

### Coverage

First-pass findings re-checked on NEW: all 22 (CHAT-1 to CHAT-22).

Read in full in NEW:

- `src/Units/LootRolls.wowlua` (1,777 lines, new)
- `src/Units/Loot.wowlua` (357 lines; the rolls moved out of it)

Read as diff (`git diff 4c6ea485 36f5f407`) plus the surrounding NEW code needed to judge it:

- `src/Units/Chat.wowlua`, `ChatCommands.wowlua`, `ChatCommands/Match.wowlua`, `Notifications.wowlua`, `Tooltips.wowlua`, `Welcome.wowlua`, `Addons.wowlua`, `Legacy.wowlua` (every hunk)
- `src/Units/Chat/Lines.wowlua`, `Search.wowlua`, `Input.wowlua`, `Tabs.wowlua` have no changes between the two commits; the lines the findings cite were re-read in NEW.
- `src/Core/Ahead.wowlua` (to judge its new use in ChatCommands and Notifications), the export lines of `src/Core/API.wowlua`.

Not done:

- Nothing was executed (no `wowlua`, no tests, no game).
- `src/UI/LootRollTray.wowlua` was not read (another reviewer's); findings that depend on it say so.
- The unchanged parts of `Chat.wowlua`, `ChatCommands.wowlua` and `Notifications.wowlua` were not re-read line by line, only the places the first-pass findings cite and the changed hunks.
- Blizzard's Forever UI source was not consulted. Findings that depend on its behaviour (StaticPopup reuse and anchoring, the wording of loot lines, the number in the loot history link) are marked `likely` or `needs in-game probe`.

Still true from the first pass: Chat, Notifications, Tooltips, Addons, Legacy, Loot and the new LootRolls are `reloadToToggle = true`, so their `OnDisable` never runs in a session. ChatCommands and Welcome toggle live.

### Summary

- The two polling problems in Chat are fixed: the tab row is now refreshed by what changes it (hooks on Blizzard's window code, show and hide of windows), and the 0.2 s tick only handles the idle fade.
- The command palette now draws its rows over several frames with a time budget, builds its catalog ahead of use in steps, and reads the emotes once.
- Group loot rolls are a new module with their own tray. It never accepts a Bind on Pickup confirmation by itself: `ConfirmLootRoll` is called only from a click on the row's own button, and "Greed on all" only calls `RollOnLoot`. The declined-confirmation lock from the first pass is fixed.
- The new module's main defect: rolls are found by item id, so two open rolls for the same item are confused. The player's own vote can lock the wrong row, and a decided roll can remove the row of one that is still open.
- The roll tray rebuilds every open row on every vote line, with a class lookup that walks the group per name. This is heavier than the old roll card in a raid.
- Unchanged and still present: the welcome panel's keyboard capture in combat, the per-line cost of the chat mirrors (combat log included), presence lines hidden without a card, timed notes expiring in combat, hosted request windows left off screen, the 0.1 s Notifications tick, and the layer violations (two more imports of `/Core/Ahead` and one of `/UI/Draw` were added).

### Findings

#### CHAT-23: Two open rolls for the same item are confused: your vote locks the wrong row, and a decided roll removes one that is still open
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (LootRolls/Rolls: your vote line goes to the roll you answered with that choice, else to the item's only roll without your vote, else to none; another player's vote to the oldest roll of the item they haven't voted on; a result removes a row only when it is certain which roll it is about, or once every open roll of the item has one. The lines and the loot history carry no roll key, so it rests on these rules, which never answer, lock or remove a row you haven't answered)
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/LootRolls.wowlua:1328-1349 (`RollFor`), 1364-1415 (`OnLootLine`), 1278-1304
  (`DropDecided`), 880-905 (`Choose`), 187-188 (the loot history link taken off the line)
- known: no
- what: every chat line and every loot history drop is matched to a roll by item id only: `RollFor(link)` returns "the oldest open one for that item". With two open rolls A (older) and B for the same item:
  1. Your own vote line always lands on A:
     ```
     if short(who) == me() then
         roll.choice = choice
         roll.confirm = nil
     end
     ```
     If you answer B first (for example Pass on B), `Choose` sets `B.choice` and the game's line then sets `A.choice = "pass"` too. `Choose` returns early for a roll with a choice (`if roll.choice or … then return end`), so A can no longer be answered in the tray.
  2. A "won" or "everyone passed" line, and `DropDecided`, end the oldest open roll: `if roll and self.rolls[roll.id] == roll then self:EndRoll(roll.id) end`. If B is decided while you have not answered A, A's row is removed.
  3. Other players' votes for B are all written into A (the earlier vote of the same player is removed first), so B shows no votes and everyone as "Choosing".
- why it matters: Blizzard's roll frames are off screen (`HideBlizzardRolls`), so the tray is the only place to roll. A boss that drops the same item twice (tokens, recipes, crafting materials) leaves the player unable to roll on one of them, and it times out as a pass.
- fix: identify the roll exactly instead of by item.
  - The line starts with `|HlootHistory:<n>|h`, which `OnLootLine` strips (`HISTORY_LINE`). Probe in game whether `<n>` is the roll id of `START_LOOT_ROLL` (or the loot history's key). If so, capture it and look the roll up by it; keep the item match only as a fallback.
  - For `DropDecided`, probe what `C_LootHistory.GetSortedInfoForDrop` returns that ties a drop to a roll (roll id, or `lootListKey` matched to the order of `START_LOOT_ROLL` within one `lootHandle`), and store that key on the roll.
  - Until a key is available, make the fallback safe: for your own vote line prefer the open same-item roll whose `choice` equals the line's choice and that has no vote of yours yet; for others prefer the oldest same-item roll that player has not voted on; for "won"/"all passed" never end a roll you have not answered while another same-item roll is answered. Never set `roll.choice` from a line when another same-item roll already carries that pending choice.
  - Test: `tests/unit/Units/LootRolls.test.wowlua` (two rolls of one item: Pass on the second, then Need on the first must still work; a "won" line for the second leaves the first open).

#### CHAT-1: The welcome panel swallows all keyboard input if combat starts before a key is pressed
- status: fixed in db302207 (the panel's keys go through UI.Dismissable, which passes every key on and lets the keyboard go as a fight starts; the dim takes no clicks in a fight; the probe confirms the design: in combat lockdown `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` is refused and `EnableKeyboard` allowed)
- probe (2026-11-15, build 70888): `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` is refused in combat lockdown on an addon's own frame, `EnableKeyboard` is allowed (tried on a hidden frame of the probe's own in the first fight). So the finding was real: a handler that waits for the fight to call `SetPropagateKeyboardInput` cannot, and UI/Dismiss's design (let go before the lockdown, call nothing during it) is the one that works. The fix no longer waits on the game for this point.
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: likely
- where: src/Units/Welcome.wowlua:588-620 (`Build`), 724-736 (`Show`), 786-795 (the combat events), 815-828 (opened by itself)
- known: no
- what: `Build` calls `p:EnableKeyboard(true)` and sets
  ```
  p:SetScript("OnKeyDown", function(frame: Frame, key: string)
      if InCombatLockdown() then
          return
      end
      if key == "ESCAPE" then
          frame:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(false)
          self:Close()
      else
          frame:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(true)
      end
  end)
  ```
  Propagation is never switched on before the first key. A keyboard-enabled frame consumes keys until `SetPropagateKeyboardInput(true)` is called, and in combat the handler returns before calling it. The `dim` frame covers the whole screen with `EnableMouse(true)`. The `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` handler only redraws the Start button.
- why it matters: the welcome opens by itself two seconds after the first login with SuuUI. If the player is attacked before pressing a key, movement and ability keys do nothing and clicks on the world are taken by the dim. The only way out is clicking Skip. This is the first thing a new user sees.
- fix: call `p:SetPropagateKeyboardInput(true)` in `Build` and again in `Show` (both run out of combat on the automatic path), so only Esc ever switches it off. In the `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` handler hide `dim` (or disable its mouse) and restore it on `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` if the welcome was not closed. Probe whether `EnableKeyboard`/`SetPropagateKeyboardInput` are refused in combat on Forever; if so, `/suu welcome` typed in combat before the panel exists errors in `Build`: route the command through `self:RunOutOfCombat`. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Welcome.test.wowlua` (show, enter combat, send a key, expect it to propagate).

#### CHAT-2: Every chat line, the combat log's included, pays an O(500) shift and work whose result is never used
- status: open
- severity: high
- category: performance
- confidence: likely (the per-line work is confirmed from code; how many lines ChatFrame2 gets while its tab is not shown needs an in-game probe)
- where: src/Units/Chat/Mirrors.wowlua:214-236 (`newLine`), 238-256 (`put`, `append`), 310-331
  (`keepWhisper`), 379-393 (the `AddMessage` hook); src/Units/Chat/Kept.wowlua:212-213 (`fillWhispers`);
  src/Units/Chat.wowlua:1112-1113 (the combat log loaded on enable)
- known: no
- what: `OnEnable` loads `Blizzard_CombatLog` for everyone, and `Mirror` hooks `AddMessage` on every window including `ChatFrame2` (a raw mirror). Per line the hook does:
  1. `NewLine`: a new table per line (for a raw mirror too).
  2. `Append`: `lines[#lines + 1] = line; if #lines > MAX_LINES then table.remove(lines, 1) end`. With 500 lines held, every further line shifts 500 entries.
  3. `self:ShowTimes()` (a settings read), `Draw`, and a second `AddMessage` on SuuUI's frame.
  4. `self:KeepWhisper(text, r, g, b, (select(4, ...)))`: the combat log passes no event, so `isWhisperLine` falls back to colour comparisons per line.

  For a raw mirror the `lines` list is never read: `Redraw` returns at once (`if m.raw or m.drawnWithTime == withTime then return end`).
- why it matters: in a raid the combat log produces hundreds to thousands of lines a second. Each costs a table, a 500-entry shift and the whisper test, on top of Blizzard's own formatting, whether or not the Combat Log tab is shown.
- fix: (a) for `m.raw` mirrors skip `NewLine`, `m.lines` and `KeepWhisper`: the hook becomes `m.frame:AddMessage(text, r, g, b)`. (b) For the others, replace `table.remove(lines, 1)` with a ring (head index) or trim in blocks (when `#lines > MAX_LINES + 100`, drop the oldest 100 in one pass). Do the same in `KeepWhisper` (line 1967) and `FillWhispers` (line 3003). (c) Probe whether ChatFrame2 receives lines while hidden; if it does, mirror the combat log only while its tab is selected and refill from `GetMessageInfo` on select. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Chat.test.wowlua`.

#### CHAT-3: The roll tray rebuilds every open row on every vote line, with a class lookup that walks the group for each name
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (a vote line marks only its roll's row, drawn at most once a frame through the tray's new `SetRow`, and nothing while the tray is folded or hidden; names and classes come from one map of the group read once per roster change (LootRolls/Group); your own name is read once)
- severity: high
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the size of the frame cost needs in-game measurement
- where: src/Units/LootRolls.wowlua:277-307 (`me`, `classOf`, `classColored`), 316-339 (`roster`), 341-403
  (`waitingOn`, `nameList`, `whoLine`), 636-705 (`Row`), 755-815 (`Data`), 820-842 (`Refresh`), 1373-1392 (a
  vote line calls `Refresh`)
- known: no
- what: each "X has selected Need for: Y" line calls `self:Refresh()`, which calls `Data()`, which calls `Row(roll)` for every open roll. `Row` colours every name through `classColored(name, roll.classes)`. `roll.classes` is set only on test rolls, so for a real roll `classOf` runs:
  ```
  for i = 1, n do
      local unit = prefix .. i
      local un = SuuUI.FullName(unit)
      if secret.readable(un) and short(un) == short(name) then
  ```
  (and `me()`, another `FullName`, first). Per row this is called for every voter (the choice tooltips), for every voter and every waiting member (the "Who chose what" tooltip), and up to 5 times 4 names per group in `whoLine`. `waitingOn` builds the roster (`FullName` per member) twice per row (`Row` and `Data`). Then `tray:SetData` redraws the tray.
- why it matters: in a 40-player raid one row costs roughly 80 `classOf` calls of up to 40 `FullName` calls each. With five items open, one vote line rebuilds all five rows: on the order of 15,000 `FullName` calls and a few hundred strings per line. A boss's loot produces about 200 vote lines in a few seconds, often still in combat (the tray shows in combat by design).
- fix:
  1. In `StartRoll`, fill `roll.classes` and `roll.roster` once (one pass over the group: `short(FullName(unit))` to class). Refresh them on `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` while rolls are open.
  2. Cache `me()` in a module local (the player's name does not change).
  3. Coalesce `Refresh` from loot lines: set a dirty flag and redraw once on the next frame (the driver's `OnUpdate` already runs while the tray shows).
  4. Rebuild only the row of the roll the line was about, if the tray widget allows a single-row update.
  - Test: `tests/unit/Units/LootRolls.test.wowlua` (a raid roll with many vote lines; count `SetData` calls and `FullName` calls).

#### CHAT-4: Online and offline lines are hidden from chat even when no card is shown for them
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Notifications/Presence.wowlua:468-476 (the filter in `hookPresence`), 292-300
  (`queuePresence` returns when the setting is off), 183-245 (`whoIs`), 442-466 (`systemLine`), 174
  (`isPresenceLine`); src/Units/Notifications.wowlua:700-703 (the roster asked for once);
  src/Units/Notifications/Settings.wowlua:28 (defaults)
- known: no
- what: the `CHAT_MSG_SYSTEM` filter hides every presence line whenever `presenceHideChat` is on (the default):
  ```
  return self:IsEnabled() and self:Get("presenceHideChat") and isPresenceLine(msg)
  ```
  Whether a card follows is decided separately: `Presence` returns when that kind's setting is off (`presenceGuildOffline = false` by default), and `SystemLine` drops the line when `WhoIs` finds neither a friend nor a guild member. `WhoIs` walks the guild roster, which is requested exactly once in `OnEnable` although the comment says "asked for now and then".
- why it matters: with the defaults, "X has gone offline" for guild members disappears from chat and no card is shown. The same happens for any member the roster does not hold yet (the first seconds after login, someone who joined since).
- fix: make the filter hide a line only when a card will be shown. Share one function `presenceFor(msg)` between `SystemLine` and the filter that returns kind, online and person and checks `self:Get(setting .. "Online"/"Offline")`; cache the last result by message text, since the filter runs once per chat frame. Request the roster again when `WhoIs` misses in a guild, at most every few minutes. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Notifications.test.wowlua` (guild offline with the default settings: the line stays in chat).

#### CHAT-5: Timed notes raised in combat run out while they are held back
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Notifications.wowlua:363-370 (`Rebuild` passes the combat state), 406-441 (`Tick`, the
  timed branch); src/UI/Notification/Stack.wowlua:155-163, 220
- known: no
- what: `SetItems(items, inCombat)` leaves `timed` and `sticky` notes out during combat (`if inCombat and (kind == "sticky" or kind == "timed") then`) and shows "N waiting for the end of combat". `Tick` keeps counting every timed note against `endsAt[id]` and removes it at zero, held or not:
  ```
  elseif d.kind == "timed" and ends then
      local remaining = ends - now
      d.remaining = remaining
      if remaining <= 0 then
          self.notes[id] = nil
  ```
- why it matters: a timed note raised in a fight (the group finder's notes, any plugin's `SuuUI.Notify` with a duration) is gone before the fight ends unless the fight is shorter than its duration, although the footer promised it. Only presence cards are held properly, by their own queue.

#### CHAT-9: The Global tab's channels are moved again after every fight; a closed Global window is not handled
- status: open

- category: bug

- where: src/Units/Chat/GlobalTab.wowlua:78-135 (`applyGlobalTab`), 53-65 (`windowNamed`);
  src/Units/Chat.wowlua:1162-1182 and 1201-1203 (its triggers); src/Units/Chat/Windows.wowlua:190-201
  (`closeWindow`)
- known: no
- what: `ApplyGlobalTab` runs on every `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`, on each channel event (0.5 s later), three seconds after login and on the setting. Each run takes "everything General was set to show, and every channel you're in" and, for each, calls `AddChannel` on Global and `RemoveChannel` on General, without checking what is already set:
  ```
  for _, list in ipairs({ windowChannels(idOf(general)), joinedChannels() }) do
  ...
      channelCall(global, "AddChannel", name)
  ...
  channelCall(general, "RemoveChannel", name)
  ```
- why it matters:
  1. A player who unticks a channel in the Global tab's own chat settings (to stop seeing Trade) gets it back after the next fight, because joined channels are always added to Global.
  2. Each run makes two channel calls per channel after every fight for nothing.

Then `windowNamed("Global")` either still finds the closed window by its kept name (channels go to a window nobody sees and leave General), or finds none and a new Global tab appears after the next fight. Probe which: close Global, then `/dump GetChatWindowInfo(n)`.
- fix: move only what General shows (`windowChannels(idOf(general))`), plus channels joined since the last run. Keep a per-character set `CharData().globalMoved[name] = true` and skip names in it. In `CloseWindow`, when the closed window is the Global one, set `globalTab` to false (or ask first), and make `windowNamed` ignore windows that are neither shown nor docked. #### CHAT-11: The AddOns window reports changes that were not made after switching "This character / All characters"
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Addons.wowlua:394-410 (`Snapshot`, `Changes`), 461-464 (the select's `onChange`), 734
  (`DrawRow`)
- known: no
- what: `Snapshot()` records the enable state once in `Open`, under the scope chosen then. The select's `onChange` does `self.perChar = v == "me"; self:Draw()` without a new snapshot. `Changes()` (`if self:Enabled(e.index) ~= self.start[e.index]`) and `DrawRow` (`local changed = enabled ~= self.start[e.index]`) then compare the state under the new scope with the snapshot taken under the old one.
- why it matters: an addon enabled on another character only (or disabled for this one only) reads differently under the two scopes. After switching, such rows show as changed, the footer counts "N changes" and offers a reload, though the player changed nothing.
- fix: take two snapshots in `Open` (`start.me[index]`, `start.all[index]`) and compare against the one for the current scope. Count a change when either scope differs from its own snapshot, so a change made under "me" still counts after switching. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Addons.test.wowlua`.

#### CHAT-24: Another player's automatic pass is read as a pass by "Name automatically"
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (the patterns are tried by how much of their text is fixed, so the automatic pass lines come before "%s passed on: %s")
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (depends on the client's format strings; the English ones are "%s passed on: %s" and "%s automatically passed on: %s because he cannot loot that item.")
- where: src/Units/LootRolls.wowlua:242-250 (the order of the lines), 167-180 (`match`), 1364-1393
- known: no
- what: `OnLootLine` takes the first pattern that matches. The general line is added before the automatic ones:
  ```
  add("LOOT_ROLL_PASSED", function(c: Captures)
      return "vote", c[1], c[2], "pass"
  end)
  add("LOOT_ROLL_PASSED_AUTO", function(c: Captures)
  ```
  `LOOT_ROLL_PASSED` becomes `^(.+) passed on: (.+)$`, which also matches "Brannoc automatically passed on: [Item] because he cannot loot that item." with who = "Brannoc automatically". The file's own comment states the rule ("The specific lines before the general ones") and applies it to the "You"/"Everyone" lines, but not here.
- why it matters: the pass is listed under the name "Brannoc automatically", and the real member stays under "Choosing", so the row's count and the "waiting on N players" line stay wrong until the roll ends. The item id is still found (the link is inside the second capture), so the wrong name is recorded on the right roll.
- fix: add `LOOT_ROLL_PASSED_AUTO` and `LOOT_ROLL_PASSED_AUTO_FEMALE` before `LOOT_ROLL_PASSED`. As a general guard, when two patterns match prefer the one with the longer literal part. Test: `tests/unit/Units/LootRolls.test.wowlua` (an automatic pass line with the game's real formats: the vote is under the member's name).

#### CHAT-25: Several Bind on Pickup confirmations at once, and other popups while one is hosted
- status: open (unverified: needs in game Greed on all with two Bind on Pickup rolls, and a party invite while a roll's confirmation is hosted with requests off)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- where: src/Units/LootRolls.wowlua:912-930 (`GreedAll`, `AskAnswered`), 932-992 (`ConfirmAsked`,
  `HostConfirm`), 1062-1083 (`HookDialog`); src/Units/Notifications.wowlua:485-496 (the re-anchor of popups
  under its own hosts only)
- known: no
- what: two cases the code does not cover, both depending on how Forever's StaticPopup behaves.
  1. "Greed on all" calls `Choose(roll, "greed")` for every unanswered roll in one frame. Each Bind on Pickup roll raises `CONFIRM_LOOT_ROLL`. If the game shows only one such popup at a time (it hides the shown one to show the next, as StaticPopup does for a popup of the same kind), the hosted popup's `OnHide` hook runs for the earlier roll:
     ```
     after(0, function()
         self.lastHosted, self.lastYes = nil, nil
         self:Answered(id, false)
     end)
     ```
     and `Answered(id, false)` sets `roll.choice = nil`. Only the last Bind on Pickup roll keeps its question; the earlier ones silently go back to unanswered. The ask's note promises otherwise: "the game still asks about it on its own row".
  2. While a confirmation is hosted, the popup sits off screen (`dialog:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", UIParent, "TOPLEFT", -200, 200)`). If Blizzard anchors the next popup under the last shown one, that popup is off screen too. Notifications corrects this only for its own hosts (`if under and self.hosts[under] then`), and it hosts new popups itself only while its `requests` setting is on and the module is enabled.
- why it matters: (1) after "Greed on all" on a boss with several Bind on Pickup items the player believes all are answered or asked; all but one time out as passes unless noticed. (2) With Notifications off or `requests` off, a resurrection, summon or invite popup arriving while a roll's confirmation is open cannot be seen or answered.
- fix: probe both in game (`/suu lootroll` does not exercise the real popup): Greed on all with two Bind on Pickup rolls; a party invite while a confirmation is hosted with `requests` off.
  - For (1): when a hosted popup hides because another `CONFIRM_LOOT_ROLL` replaced it (the next `ConfirmAsked` arrives in the same frame), keep `roll.confirm` on the earlier roll instead of taking the choice back; its row then answers through `Confirm` → `ConfirmLootRoll`, which is already the path for "a row the popup isn't for". Or have "Greed on all" skip Bind on Pickup rolls and say so in the note.
  - For (2): in `LootRolls:Tick`, re-anchor any shown `StaticPopupN` whose first point is relative to the hosted dialog (the same check as `Notifications.wowlua:2391-2402`), or move that check into one shared helper used by both modules.
  - Test: `tests/unit/Units/LootRolls.test.wowlua`.

#### CHAT-26: A roll whose item name cannot be read is dropped while Blizzard's roll frames are off screen
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (a roll whose name can't be read yet is kept under the link's name or a placeholder and named once the item's data arrives; whether the client ever gives no name at `START_LOOT_ROLL` was not probed, and the fix holds either way)
- probe (2026-11-16 to 18, `/suu probe all`, in fights; read 2026-11-19): in 5 rolls (3 Bind on Pickup) the item's name was never missing and never secret at `START_LOOT_ROLL`. The fallback is not needed on this client; it stays as a safety net.
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: needs in-game probe (whether `GetLootRollItemInfo` can return no name or a secret one on Forever at `START_LOOT_ROLL`)
- where: src/Units/LootRolls.wowlua:1182-1190 (`StartRoll`), 1435-1460 (`HideBlizzardRolls`)
- known: no
- what:
  ```
  local itemName = secret.asString(name)
  if not itemName then
      return
  end
  ```
  The roll then has no row in the tray, and Blizzard's own roll frame is off screen and see-through for the whole session.
- why it matters: if the name is ever missing (item data not yet loaded) or secret, the player cannot roll on that item at all and gets no sign that a roll exists.
- fix: do not drop the roll. Use the link's name or a placeholder ("Item") and fill the name in from the `item.load` callback that `Add` already registers (line 1256). Probe once in game with an item never seen before in the session.

#### CHAT-27: Narrowing the command matches can leave a command that now fits only by an alias ahead of commands that fit by name
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/ChatCommands/Match.wowlua:165-184 (`narrow`), 116-161 (`ordered`, `matches`)
- known: no
- what: `narrow` keeps each list's order and only recomputes the score: "a match by name stays one". That does not hold. A command whose main name is a prefix of what is typed so far, and which has a longer alias, matches by name for the shorter text and by alias for the longer one: for an item with `cmd = "/w"` and alias `"/whisper"`, typing `/w` gives score 1; typing `/wh` gives `matchOf` = 2 (alias). `narrow` leaves it at its old place among the name matches, while `matches("/wh")` puts it after every name match (`/who`). `matches` sorts when `ordered(list)` is false; `narrow` never checks.
- why it matters: the palette's order, and so which command the first row and Tab offer, depends on whether the text was typed key by key or arrived at once (paste, backspace and retype). The stated rule "a command whose own name fits comes before one that fits by an alias" is broken on the common path.
- fix: in `narrow`, after building `kept`, apply the same check as `matches`: `if not ordered(kept) then table.sort(kept, before) end`. Test: `tests/unit/Units/ChatCommands/Match.test.wowlua` (narrowing from `/w` to `/wh` equals `matches` for `/wh`).

For `BN_WHISPER` the target is the session-only `|K…|k` token, saved to the character's history and meaningless after a relog. Fix: do not keep `BN_WHISPER` lines.

#### CHAT-22: Modules import `/UI` and `/Core` values that the public API does not offer
- status: partly fixed in a5082e2d (the modules import only /Core/API, with IsColor, Hex, InlineMark, OpenRoot and BuildAhead exported; Tooltips still finds the Bags window by its global name, and ChatCommands' Tab wrapper and its unforced Unfocus on disable are unchanged)
- severity: low

Fix: give `Unfocus` a `force` argument for `OnDisable`.

### Fixed since the first pass

- CHAT-7: Declining a bind-on-pickup roll confirmation leaves the roll card locked. Fixed in the new module: the hosted popup's `OnHide` hook calls `Answered(id, false)`, which clears `roll.choice` (src/Units/LootRolls.wowlua:1117-1131, 927-941); the row's own Cancel does the same through `Confirm` (909-924).
- CHAT-8: The chat rebuilds its whole tab row five times a second. Fixed: `Tick` only handles the idle fade (src/Units/Chat.wowlua:3408-3440); the tabs are refreshed by `RefreshWindows` through `WindowsChanged`, `WatchWindow` and `HookWindowCode` (3314-3393), and the edit boxes are cached in `self.boxes`.
- CHAT-14, parts: the per-minute synchronous catalog rebuild (now built ahead in steps, `RebuildSoon`, src/Units/ChatCommands.wowlua:929-949; emotes read once, `emoteNames`, 636-667) and the single-frame draw of all rows (`Room`, `Add`, `DrainRows`, 1262-1306). The rest is restated above.
- CHAT-16, part: the action's `onClick` ran on press and release. Fixed: `PostClick` returns when `down` (src/Units/Notifications.wowlua:867-870).
- CHAT-21, item 6: which of two commands sharing an alias is kept differed between sessions. Fixed: the keys are sorted before the catalog is built (src/Units/ChatCommands.wowlua:792-796).

### Withdrawn

None. (CHAT-3 and CHAT-20 are not withdrawn: their code moved to `LootRolls.wowlua` and they are restated there.)

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Matching by a non-unique key** (CHAT-23: rolls by item id). Other places that pair a game event or chat line with a tracked object by name or item id deserve the same question: can two be open at once?
- **Pattern lists built from the game's format strings must put the specific format first** (CHAT-24). Any other code that turns `%s … %s` globals into `(.+)` patterns and takes the first match has the same risk; a helper that orders by literal length would remove it.
- **Blizzard frames moved off screen** is now written four times (Loot, LootRolls twice, Notifications `HostFrame`), with different care: LootRolls saves and restores the popup's points, Notifications does not (CHAT-6), and only Notifications corrects popups anchored under a hosted one (CHAT-25). One helper would settle all of them.
- **Full rebuild per data change**: the roll tray (`Refresh` → every row, CHAT-3) repeats the pattern the first pass saw in the notification stack. A dirty flag drawn once per frame, plus per-row updates, applies to both.
- **Per-name group walks** (`classOf` in LootRolls) instead of a name-to-class map built once per roster change. Worth a grep for loops over `"raid" .. i` inside functions that are themselves called per member.
- **Session-long tickers** remain in Notifications (0.1 s) and Addons (`every(15)`, src/Units/Addons.wowlua:873). Chat's is now cheap. LootRolls does it right: its driver is shown only while the tray has content.
- **`table.remove(list, 1)` as a queue** on lists of several hundred entries is still in the chat mirrors and whispers (CHAT-2).
- **Chat filters that hide Blizzard's line on the assumption that SuuUI shows the same thing elsewhere** (CHAT-4).
- **Parsing localized game text with English literals** (Legacy, CHAT-18). LootRolls and Notifications build patterns from the game's format globals, which is the pattern to follow.
- **`/Core/Ahead` is used by modules but not exported** (CHAT-22): the build-ahead pattern is spreading, so it should become public API before more modules import it directly.
- **Raw truthiness tests on unit API results** that sibling code wraps in `secret.flag` (LootRolls `roster`; Notifications `WhoIs` compares `GetGuildRosterInfo` values directly where ChatCommands `Names` guards the same calls).
