Nothing was run.

### Summary

Much of the first pass's performance and combat material was dealt with between 0.6 and 0.17: the big data tables are built lazily in steps (`Core/Data`), the world map keeps its filters, its judged quests and the completed-quests set between refreshes, the tracker skips a redraw that would draw the same, and the "map opened from addon code" problem was found in game and fixed three ways (the flight master has its own window, pins defer `SetPassThroughButtons` out of combat, the tracker opens the quest log through a secure click).

What remains:

1. NpcDialogue can still leave the whole UI at a partial alpha (unchanged code), and the new AutoQuests module makes the close-and-reopen timing that triggers it routine.
2. AutoQuests itself is careful (no gossip option is ever selected, a reward with more than one choice is never taken, gold and item turn-ins, dailies, shared and PvP quests are opt-in, each quest is opened once per conversation, Shift pauses a conversation). Its problems are at the edges: it runs under SuuUI's dialogue, which fades the UI out and back for each automated step; its gold check depends on an earlier event; it builds the whole quest table in one frame for a level it mostly does not need.
3. QuestAnnounce sends to raid chat as well as party, with no throttle, no repeat guard and no setting to limit it.
4. Unchanged from the first pass: zoom rebuilds every map pin per frame, the flight map redraws the network per hover, quest item buttons missing after unfolding in combat, Train all buying beyond the confirmed list, Durability's consumers stale after it is turned off.
5. The two map files grew (2,959 and 2,651 lines) and gained another copied helper (`PassThrough`).

### Findings

#### MAP-1: NpcDialogue can leave the whole UI dimmed until a reload
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); how often the timing is hit needs an in-game check
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (`HideUI` keeps the alpha it read while its own fade back runs, plus a quarter second, so a conversation that opens again mid-fade returns to the right alpha; steps AutoQuests answers no longer show the dialogue at all, MAP-20)
- where: src/Units/NpcDialogue.wowlua:1567-1593 (`HideUI`), 661-663 (root `OnHide`), 1252-1263 (`Draw`);
  src/Core/Motion.wowlua:155 (`alphaTo`)
- known: no
- what: `HideUI(true)` records the alpha to return to at the moment it runs:
  ```
  if on then
      self.uiAlpha = UIParent:GetAlpha()
  end
  ...
  SuuUI.Motion.AlphaTo(UIParent, on and 0 or (self.uiAlpha or 1), T.duration["dur-base"] or 0.2)
  ```
  `alphaTo` fades over time from an OnUpdate driver, so `UIParent:GetAlpha()` returns intermediate values while SuuUI's own fade back runs. The root's `OnHide` calls `HideUI(false)` (fade back); if a conversation is drawn again before that fade has finished, `HideUI(true)` reads the half-restored alpha (for example 0.4) and stores it as the value to return to. Every later conversation records the same wrong value again.
- why it matters: with "Hide the rest of the UI" on, a conversation that closes and reopens within the fade (about a fifth of a second) leaves UIParent at a partial alpha until `/reload`. In 0.17.0 the new AutoQuests module makes this sequence common: it accepts or turns in a quest as its page opens, the game closes the page and the NPC shows its list again a server round trip later (see MAP-20).
- fix: never read the return value during SuuUI's own fade. In `HideUI(true)` use `self.uiAlpha = self.uiAlpha or UIParent:GetAlpha()`; in `HideUI(false)` start the fade and clear `self.uiAlpha` with `after(duration, …)` only if `self.uiHidden` is still false then. Test in tests/unit/Units/NpcDialogue.test.wowlua: hide, show again after `mock.advanceTime(0.05)` and a frame, close, advance, expect UIParent's alpha 1.

#### MAP-20: AutoQuests runs under SuuUI's dialogue: the UI fades out and back, and the minimap blinks, for every quest it handles
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (follows from the code; how visible it is needs a look in game)
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (AutoQuests provides the `autoquests` service: `Handling()` is true from just before it answers a step until the conversation moves on, closes, or a second passes; NpcDialogue then draws no scene, fade or minimap change for that step and looks again 0.1 s later)
- where: src/Units/AutoQuests.wowlua:290-317 (`OnDetail`), 319-360 (`OnProgress`, `OnComplete`);
  src/Units/NpcDialogue.wowlua:1454-1463 (`QueueDraw`), 1252-1263 (`Draw`), 1567-1593 (`HideUI`, the minimap
  at 1585-1591)
- known: no
- what: the two modules do not know about each other. AutoQuests acts inside the event (`try(AcceptQuest)` in `QUEST_DETAIL`, `try(CompleteQuest)` in `QUEST_PROGRESS`, `try(GetQuestReward, …)` in `QUEST_COMPLETE`). The game's quest frame still shows for that event, NpcDialogue's hook on the panel's `OnShow` queues a draw for the next frame, and `Draw` then shows the scene and calls `HideUI(true)`: `Minimap:Hide()` at once and UIParent fading to 0. When the server's answer closes the quest frame a moment later, the scene hides, `Minimap:Show()` runs and the UI fades back. With an NPC offering three quests this happens three times in a row (list, page, closed, list, …).
- why it matters: with both modules on (the defaults), every automatically handled quest gives a flash of the dialogue, a dip of the whole UI and a minimap blink, and the quick close/reopen is the timing that triggers MAP-1.
- fix: let NpcDialogue know a step is being automated. For example AutoQuests provides a service (`Busy()`: true from the moment it called `AcceptQuest`/`CompleteQuest`/`GetQuestReward`/`Select…Quest` until the next quest or gossip event or a short timeout), and `NpcDialogue:Draw` does not show the scene (or at least skips `HideUI(true)`) while it is true. Simpler alternative: delay `HideUI(true)` by about 0.15 s after the scene shows and cancel it when the scene hides first. Tests: tests/unit/Units/NpcDialogue.test.wowlua and AutoQuests.test.wowlua (a quest accepted automatically leaves UIParent's alpha at 1 and the minimap shown throughout).

#### MAP-21: Quest announcements go to raid chat too, with no throttle, no repeat guard and no way to limit them
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/QuestAnnounce.wowlua:133-165 (`Read`), 21-24 and 84-109 (settings); wowlua stdlib
  `chat.sendToGroup` / `groupChannel`
- known: no
- what: `Read` sends one line per objective that turned done and one more when the quest is complete:
  ```
  if o.done and not before.done[i] and o.text ~= "" then
      chat.sendToGroup(("SuuUI: %s: %s"):format(name, o.text))
  ...
  if self:Get("complete") and complete and not before.complete then
      chat.sendToGroup(("SuuUI: %s is ready to turn in."):format(name))
  ```
  `sendToGroup` picks `INSTANCE_CHAT`, else `RAID`, else `PARTY`, and has no rate limit (it only holds messages during the game's chat lockdown and then sends them all). The module's only settings are the two toggles, both on by default. Nothing remembers what was already announced: `seen` holds only the last state, so an objective that goes done → not done → done (quest items put in the bank or mailed and taken back, a count that drops when an item is used) is announced again each time, with "ready to turn in" again.
- why it matters: (1) in a raid, every player with SuuUI announces into raid chat; a quest objective completed by a boss kill gives up to one or two lines per such player at the same moment, right after the lockdown lifts. (2) A single-objective quest always gives two lines (the objective, then "ready to turn in"). (3) Repeats when items move. Other players read this as addon spam under SuuUI's name, and the player cannot restrict it to parties.
- fix: add a setting for where (party only by default; raid and instance group opt-in) and check `chat.groupChannel()` before sending; when the last objective completes the quest, send only the "ready to turn in" line; keep a per-quest record of what was announced (objective index and "complete") until the quest leaves the log (`QUEST_REMOVED` already clears per quest) so nothing is said twice; cap the lines per second (a small queue drained by a timer). Tests in tests/unit/Units/QuestAnnounce.test.wowlua (in a raid nothing by default; done → undone → done says it once; one line for a quest completed by its only objective).

#### MAP-3: The world map rebuilds and repaints every pin on every frame of a zoom
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/WorldMap.wowlua:613-623 (provider callbacks); src/Units/WorldMap/Canvas.wowlua:377-396
  (`queueLayout`), 286-365 (`layout`, `pinAlpha` read per pin at 339), 274-284 (`clearPins`);
  src/Units/WorldMap/Arrange.wowlua (`arrange`); src/UI/MapPin.wowlua (`SetData`)
- known: no
- what: `provider.OnCanvasScaleChanged` queues `Layout` (once per frame). `Layout` releases every pin (`ClearPins`), runs `arrange` over all items (merging, spreading with pair checks, a sort), then for every group takes a pin from the pool and calls `pin:SetData(data)`, `pin:SetBaseAlpha(self:Get("pinAlpha") / 100)` (a settings read per pin), frame levels and points; then walks the game's quest pins (`FitQuestPin`). A merged group also builds a new data table per layout. On a city map with several filters on this is a few hundred items per frame while the zoom animates.
- why it matters: zooming the map in a city or a busy zone with more than the default filters drops frames; the hovered pin is released and re-acquired on each of those frames.
- fix: split layout into "arrange" and "place". Arrange only when the items or the zoom's end state change: key the result by the rounded canvas scale and skip when unchanged, or arrange once the scale has stopped changing (a short trailing timer) and during the animation only rescale and re-point the existing pins (`pin:SetScale(grow / cs)` and the same normalized position). Skip `SetData` when the group's look is unchanged, read `pinAlpha` once per layout. Extend tests/unit/Units/WorldMap.test.wowlua (a scale change keeps the same pin objects) and WorldMap/Arrange.test.wowlua.

#### MAP-4: Quest item buttons are not placed while the quests are folded, so they are missing after unfolding in combat
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/ObjectiveTracker.wowlua:732-768 (`LayoutItems`, comment at 740-741), 1076-1140 (`Refresh`);
  src/UI/ObjectiveTracker.wowlua:614-654 (`LayOut` drops the quests at 650), 832-843 (`QuestTop`), 870-873
  (`SetQuestsCollapsed`)
- known: no
- what: `LayoutItems` says "placed even while collapsed: the holder hides them, and shows them in place when the tracker opens again, in combat too". But the head's toggle folds only the quests, and `LayOut` then drops every quest entry:
  ```
  if not (e.section or e.recipe) and not self.questsCollapsed then
      kept[#kept + 1] = e
  ```
  so `tops` stays empty, `QuestTop(q.questID)` returns nil for every quest, and `LayoutItems` places no button (`local top = item and parts.tracker:QuestTop(q.questID)`; the buttons left over are hidden and their `item` attribute cleared; `itemsShown = 0`). The secure toggle then shows the holder in combat, but nothing is in it; `Refresh` in combat only sets `pendingItems`.
- why it matters: fold the quests out of combat, enter a fight, unfold: the quests come back without their item buttons until the fight ends. Quest items usable in combat is the point of the secure holder.
- fix: keep the quests' tops while folded: have `LayOut` compute `tops` for the quests even when `questsCollapsed` (lay the entries out, only not show the rows), or have `LayoutItems` place the buttons from a layout taken with the quests unfolded. Test in tests/unit/Units/ObjectiveTracker.test.wowlua: a tracked quest with an item, `collapsed` on, `LayoutItems`, expect the button shown in the holder with its `item` attribute.

#### MAP-5: Train all buys more than it asked to confirm, and paces by a fixed 0.35 s instead of the trainer's answer
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); how often new services unlock mid-run depends on the trainer
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Trainer.wowlua:610-652 (`TrainAllList`, `TrainAll`), 768-790 (the confirmation)
- known: no
- what: the confirmation shows a count and total computed once ("Learn %d skills for %s."). `TrainAll` then loops up to 60 times:
  ```
  local list = self:TrainAllList()
  local e = list[1]
  ...
  BuyTrainerService(e.index)
  after(0.35, next)
  ```
  Two effects: (a) services that become available because of what was just learned (the next rank, recipes that need a skill) are bought too, although they were not in the confirmed count or cost; (b) when the server has not answered within 0.35 s the list is unchanged, so the same service is requested again (an error line from the game per repeat, and steps used up; on a slow connection the 60 steps can run out before the list is done).
- why it matters: gold spent beyond what the player confirmed; error spam and an incomplete run on a slow connection.
- fix: fix the list at confirmation: keep the confirmed services by `keyOf(e)` (name and rank, the function the module now has at line 96) and buy only those, looking each one's current index up again before buying. Drive the loop by `TRAINER_UPDATE` (the module listens to it at 1124) with a timeout as fallback, instead of a fixed delay. #### MAP-6: The objective tracker still reads everything again on every quest or bag event and every 10 seconds (the redraw is now skipped when nothing changed)
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/ObjectiveTracker.wowlua:1076-1104 (`Refresh`), 255-310 (`keyOf`, `drawnKey`), 1146-1155
  (`QueueRefresh`), 1219-1229 (the 10 s resort), 1295-1335 (events)
- known: no
- what: each queued refresh still calls `self:TrackedQuests()` (every tracked quest's info, objectives, distance, special item), `self:TrackedRecipes()`, and builds the signature (`drawnKey`: a string per quest plus a recursive walk of the recipes table with a sorted key list per table) before it can decide to skip. It is queued by `QUEST_LOG_UPDATE`, `QUEST_WATCH_UPDATE`, `QUEST_POI_UPDATE`, `ZONE_CHANGED`, `BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED` (every loot, also with no recipe tracked and nothing with an item) and unconditionally every 10 s by the OnUpdate, coalesced to one per frame only.
- why it matters: less than before (the 3 ms redraw is gone in the common case), but still steady garbage while questing and a full read every 10 s while standing still.
- fix: (1) a trailing throttle of 0.1-0.2 s instead of one frame; (2) `BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED` only when a recipe is tracked or a tracked quest has an item (flags kept from the last refresh); (3) the 10 s resort should only read distances and compare the resulting order with the shown one. Tests in tests/unit/Units/ObjectiveTracker.test.wowlua (count `TrackedQuests` calls).

#### MAP-7: The world map's refresh after quest events is not coalesced

#### MAP-22: AutoQuests builds the whole quest table in one frame to read a level it usually does not need
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/AutoQuests.wowlua:58-62 (`dataLevel`), 343 (`OnDetail`)
- known: no
- what: `OnDetail` computes `local level = id and (self.levels[id] or dataLevel(id))` for every quest page that did not come from a list (an NPC with one quest, a follow-up offered straight after a turn-in, an item's quest, a shared one). `dataLevel` calls `SuuUI.QuestStarts()`, which is `data.questStarts:Get()`: "the table, built now if it isn't" (`while self:Step() do end`). The level is only used by `tooLow` when `levelRange > 0`; with the default 0 only `trivial` counts, so the table is built for nothing.
- why it matters: `Core/Data` exists because building this table (3 MB, per its header) in one frame was a stutter; the first directly offered quest of a session, before the map or an NPC tooltip has finished preparing the data, brings that frame back.
- fix: read the level only when `self:Get("levelRange") > 0`, and then without forcing the build: add a public way to ask whether the data is there (for example `SuuUI.QuestStartsReady()`, documented in Docs/API.md) and use the data only when ready (falling back to `trivial`), or start `Prepare` and decide when it is done. Test in tests/unit/Units/AutoQuests.test.wowlua (a directly offered quest with range 0 leaves the quest data unbuilt).

#### MAP-23: AutoQuests' gold and item guard rests on an earlier event, and it reports what it did without checking
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the code paths; items marked "probe" need the game
- status: open
- where: src/Units/AutoQuests.wowlua:358-401 (`OnProgress`, `OnComplete`), 350-355 and 396-400 (the chat
  lines), 403-409 (`OnAcceptConfirm`), 229-235 (`PageRepeats`), 336-338
- known: no
- what:
  - `OnComplete` never looks at the cost itself. A turn-in that takes gold or items is left alone only because `OnProgress` recorded it earlier in the same conversation: `if id then self.leftAlone[id] = true end`, then in `OnComplete` `if (id and self.leftAlone[id]) or self:PageRepeats(id) then return end`. If `GetQuestID` answered nil or a secret at either event, or the reward page arrives without a progress page, `GetQuestReward` is called. Forever's own complete button checks at this step (`QuestRewardCompleteButton_OnClick`: `local money = GetQuestMoneyToGet(); if money and money > 0 then … StaticPopup_Show("CONFIRM_COMPLETE_EXPENSIVE_QUEST")`), and AutoQuests skips that confirmation.
  - "Accepted: <title>" and "Turned in: <title>" are printed right after `try(AcceptQuest)` / `try(GetQuestReward, …)`, whether or not the game accepted (quest log full, bags full, a unique reward already owned).
  - `OnAcceptConfirm` hides only the `QUEST_ACCEPT` popup; the game shows `QUEST_ACCEPT_LOG_FULL` when the log is full, which stays.
  - probe: `PageRepeats` reads `QuestIsDaily` and `QuestIsWeekly`; Forever's own UI code never references either (nor `GetAvailableLevel`, used at 272). If they are missing, a daily opened directly or from the older greeting list as a turn-in is only caught by `C_QuestLog.IsRepeatableQuest`.
  - probe: a shared quest is recognised by `UnitIsPlayer("npc")` on `QUEST_DETAIL`; if "npc" is not the sharing player on Forever, shared quests are accepted with "Quests others share" off.
  - probe: Forever's `QuestFrame_OnEvent` closes an item-started quest at once (`questStartItemID ~= nil and ~= 0` → `CloseQuest()`); whether AutoQuests' `AcceptQuest` in the same event lands before or after that decides whether such quests are accepted, and the header comment does not list them either way.
- why it matters: the first item is the only place where gold could leave without the player's opt-in; the others are wrong chat lines and settings that may not hold on this client.
- fix: in `OnComplete`, check `GetQuestMoneyToGet()` and `GetNumQuestItems()` directly against the `gold` and `items` settings (keep `leftAlone` as well). Print from `QUEST_ACCEPTED` and `QUEST_TURNED_IN` for a quest AutoQuests acted on (remember the id), not after the call. Hide `QUEST_ACCEPT_LOG_FULL` too, or leave both to the player when the log is full. Add the three probes to `/suu probe` (which of the functions exist, what "npc" is for a shared quest, an item quest's event order) and record the results in the file's header. Tests in tests/unit/Units/AutoQuests.test.wowlua.

#### MAP-12: Durability does all of its work on every durability event before it knows whether anything changed
- severity: low

- known: no
- what: `UPDATE_INVENTORY_DURABILITY`, `UPDATE_INVENTORY_ALERTS`, `PLAYER_EQUIPMENT_CHANGED` each call `Update` directly (several per frame on a gear swap or a death). `Update` reads every slot, builds a table per piece, sorts, builds the summary including the coloured tooltip lines, then the signature string, and only then returns when the signature is unchanged (`if not force and sig == self.signature then return end`).
- why it matters: garbage on a combat event for no visible change.

#### MAP-13: The repair report decides who paid from the money difference
- severity: low

- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Durability.wowlua:500-507 (`repairReport`), 810-860 (`AutoRepair`, `ReportRepair`)
- known: no
- what: one second after `RepairAllItems`, the report computes `local paid = moneyBefore - moneyNow` and `local from = paid > 0 and "" or " from the guild bank"`, whatever `guild` was. Money that came in during that second (junk sold in the same merchant window, loot) makes a repair paid from the player's gold read as paid by the guild bank, with the amount `cost - left`; a server answer slower than a second reads as "The game didn't let SuuUI repair by itself here".
- why it matters: a wrong chat line about where gold went, on a feature that spends gold without asking.

#### MAP-15: Flight times and the learned speed can never recover from a change of more than 20%
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/FlightMap/Flights.wowlua:100-125 (`learn`, `TRUST` at 64), 174-206 (`flightEnded`)
- known: no
- what: `Learn` returns before touching the route's time or the character's speed when `expected and math.abs(seconds / expected - 1) > TRUST`. That guards against early landings, but `FlightEnded` already tells those apart by where the player landed. If flights become more than 20% faster or slower, every later flight is rejected, for timed routes and estimates alike, so nothing updates until the player uses "Forget".
- why it matters: permanently wrong times and landing clocks after such a change, with no visible reason.
- fix: remember the last rejected measurement per route; when the next one agrees with it (within a few percent), accept it and replace the record (and move the speed). Test in tests/unit/Units/FlightMap.test.wowlua.

### Fixed since the first pass

- MAP-2 (map pins call a protected function when first made; the map opened from addon code in combat): confirmed in game by the owner ("Blocked in combat: SetPassThroughButtons") and fixed on all three paths. Pins defer the call out of combat (`PassThrough`, src/Units/WorldMap.wowlua:1930-1944 and src/Units/FlightMap.wowlua:1567-1580); the flight master's map is SuuUI's own window instead of the world map (src/Units/FlightMap.wowlua:1164-1228, commit 78d397cf); `OpenWith` no longer opens the map (src/Units/WorldMap.wowlua:1045-1061) and the tracker opens the quest log through a secure click (`QuestLogOn`, src/Units/ObjectiveTracker.wowlua:850-894, commit 19ab6a80); the game's quest filters are set by CVar only (WorldMap 1021-1036).
- MAP-10 (the quest data built at login whether or not the map is on): the data files are now lists of build steps run on first use, a few per frame (src/Core/Data.wowlua, `LazyData`; src/Core/API.wowlua:1021-1026; commit 5a4a8cb9). Note: with the world map module on, the first NPC tooltip starts the build (src/Units/WorldMap.wowlua:1415-1418), so the memory is saved only for players who turn the module off; and see MAP-22 for a caller that still builds it in one frame.

### Withdrawn

None.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Two modules acting on the same Blizzard frames without knowing of each other** (MAP-20: AutoQuests and NpcDialogue). Worth a sweep for other pairs where one module automates what another presents (auto-repair and the merchant window, auto-loot and the loot window, sell junk).
- **Sending to group chat**: `chat.sendToGroup` has no rate limit and includes raid chat; any other caller (map marks share the group channel) inherits MAP-21's exposure.
- **Lazy data used through the eager accessor**: `SuuUI.QuestStarts()`, `MapPlaces()` and the other `data.*:Get()` accessors build the whole table in one frame. Sweep `src/Units` for calls not preceded by a `Ready()` check or a `Prepare` (AutoQuests is one; Nameplates, Tooltip and Collections are worth checking).
- **Guards that depend on state recorded at an earlier event** (MAP-23's `leftAlone`): where a decision spends gold or items, re-read the game's state at the moment of the call.
- **Success reported right after a request to the server** (AutoQuests' chat lines, Durability's repair report, Train all's pacing): each has an event that says the answer arrived.
- **Hooks placed in `OnEnable` without a guard** (MAP-11): events and watches are released by the registry, hooks are not; sweep for `hook(` / `hookScript(` / `HookScript(` inside `OnEnable` bodies of modules that are not `reloadToToggle`.
- **Layout on every zoom frame** (MAP-3, MAP-9): any data provider whose `OnCanvasScaleChanged` rebuilds instead of rescaling.
- **Saved-and-restored global state captured while SuuUI animates it** (MAP-1's UIParent alpha): look for other reads of a Blizzard frame's alpha, scale or position "to put back later".
- **A module that provides data to others should emit its changed message in `OnDisable`** (MAP-8); check Marks, Convergences, Campfires and the other service providers.
- **Copied helpers** (`coins` in at least nine files, the quality table in about fourteen, `continentOf`, `PassThrough`, the NPC title from its tooltip, keep-away of a Blizzard frame).

### Summary

Mail, Merchant, Macros and the sort are unchanged in logic, so their findings stand as they were:
Collect all still retries a refused take forever, and the merchant queue, the COD confirmation and
the delete confirmation still act on a captured index.

The auction house grew by a third. A single auction's buyout now goes through secure clicks on the
game's own hidden page, and the game's own popup asks. That path is guarded by auction ID and is
safe for money. Three things around it are not finished:
- Bid, Bid again and the Bids tab's Buy out still call `C_AuctionHouse.PlaceBid` directly, the call
  the file's own header says Forever blocks; a blocked call reads as success.
- Bid still takes its auction by row index. NEW never re-maps `self.chosen` by auction ID.
- The secure overlays are never released when combat starts, and only rows the game's hidden list
  has a frame for can be bought.

Search history is bounded (5 entries per character). The price memory is still per character,
unpruned and read across realms, and now also feeds Professions' new cost and profit.

Bags: the per-update cost is largely fixed (a light path on `BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED`, cooldown-only
updates). The snapshot a second after every bag event and the tooltip scan over every saved slot
remain. The new secure item use is careful about combat (hidden on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` and by a
visibility driver); only small points there.

One first-pass finding is withdrawn (BAG-22), two changed (BAG-7, BAG-15), none fully fixed.

### Findings

#### BAG-1: Auction house Bid acts on a row index that goes stale when the list is re-read, and places the typed amount unchecked
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (the chosen auction is held by its auctionID, found again in the list at the moment of bidding and compared with the prices the player saw; Bid is disabled with the reason and refuses an amount under the least bid, at or above the buyout or above the player's money; a bid is asked about first and checked again at the answer; `RememberBid` runs on `BID_ADDED`. Whether Forever takes the bid at all is BAG-32)
- where: src/Units/AuctionHouse/ItemView.wowlua:270-277 (list rebuilt), 351-369 (row click stores
  `row.index`), 381-384 (`chosenAuction`), 387-411 (`drawItemFoot`), 462-475 (`bid`);
  src/Units/AuctionHouse.wowlua:890-897
- known: no
- what: The chosen auction of an item's view is `self.chosen`, an index: `local i = self.chosen; return i and self.auctions[i] or nil`. `DrawItemView` rebuilds `self.auctions` from `GetItemSearchResultInfo` on every refresh (`ITEM_SEARCH_RESULTS_UPDATED/ADDED`, `PLAYER_MONEY`, `ITEM_KEY_ITEM_INFO_RECEIVED`, theme change, the sell tab's search for the same key) and keeps the index. I traced every write of `self.chosen` in NEW: `OpenItem` (nil), a row click (`self.chosen = row.index`), and `AUCTION_HOUSE_PURCHASE_COMPLETED` (nil). Nothing re-maps it by `auctionID` after a re-read, so the index can point at another auction. `Bid()` then does `pcall(AH.PlaceBid, a.auctionID, amount)` with `a = self.auctions[self.chosen]`: no confirmation, no check that `amount >= least`, none against the player's money, none against the buyout. `DrawItemFoot` also raises the typed bid to the new row's least bid (`if (v.bid:GetCopper() or 0) < least then v.bid:SetCopper(least) end`), and the Bid button is never disabled (only `v.buyout:SetEnabledState` is set). `RememberBid` is called before the house answers.
- why it matters: The player chooses auction 3 and types a bid. The results refresh (someone buys or bids; the list is sorted by price). Index 3 is now another auction: the highlight moves and the bid field is raised to that auction's least bid. A click on Bid bids on an auction the player did not choose. An amount at or above that auction's buyout buys it outright, without the confirmation Buy out has. (Whether the call goes through at all on Forever is BAG-32; if it does, this is the money path with the least protection in the module. The new Buy out is not affected: `DrawBuyOver`, 2546-2558, shows its secure click only while the game's page has the same `auctionID`.)
- fix: Keep the chosen auction as its `auctionID` (as `AuctionsPage.chosen` already does, 3734-3740). After each re-read in `DrawItemView` find it again; if it is gone clear the selection and the bid field. In `Bid()` and `BidAgain()` refuse an amount below the least bid or above `GetMoney()` (disable the button with a reason, as `DrawAuctionsFoot` 3801-3809 does), and send an amount at or above the buyout through the buyout path. Call `RememberBid` on `BID_ADDED`, not before. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/AuctionHouse.test.wowlua` (choose a row, change the result order, Bid).

#### BAG-32: Bid, Bid again and the Bids tab's Buy out call `PlaceBid` directly, which the header says Forever blocks; a blocked call is reported as placed
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (the header at `36f5f407` recorded the block for a buyout; the 2026-11-17 probe saw a buyout from SuuUI's own button taken, and a confirmation's OK refused; a bid under the buyout needs a probe)
- status: partly fixed in 740e3d27 (a call no longer counts as placed: `PlaceBid` runs in `SuuUI.ExpectRefusal`, a refusal or the house's error says nothing was placed, and a bid or buyout counts only on `BID_ADDED` or `AUCTION_HOUSE_PURCHASE_COMPLETED`, with a 10 s backstop. Left: whether Forever takes a bid under the buyout from SuuUI's code is still not probed (`/suu probe ahbid` exists, no answer recorded); Bid and Bid again are not routed through the game's page; the Bids tab's Buy out still calls the single-auction buyout the header says Forever refuses, and now says so when it is refused. Since, at `3dcdc41e`: the probe answered for a buyout (see the probe line) and the Buy page's Buy out places `PlaceBid` itself (`06ef3747`: the price asked on the first click, placed within a second click on the same button; its message records that a buyout placed from a confirmation's OK was refused in game). Left: Bid (Buy page), Bid again and the Bids tab's Buy out still place from `UI.Confirm`'s `onConfirm`, the confirmation's OK; a bid under the buyout was never tried)
- probe (2026-11-17, `/suu probe ahbid`, by another session; `SuuUIProbe.ahBid`, read 2026-11-19): from SuuUI's own button, `PlaceBid` with an auction's buyout was not refused: `AUCTION_HOUSE_PURCHASE_COMPLETED` came and the money went. The auction took no bids, so no bid under the buyout was placed. The header of `src/Units/AuctionHouse/Bidding.wowlua` records the same (not from `/run` or `/script`).
- where: src/Units/AuctionHouse.wowlua:11-17 (header); src/Units/AuctionHouse/Bidding.wowlua:107-142 (`placeBid`);
  src/Units/AuctionHouse/ItemView.wowlua:540-597 (`bid`), 512-527 (`buyOut`); src/Units/AuctionHouse/Auctions.wowlua:593-632
  (`bidAgain`), 638-667 (`buyOutBid`)
- known: no (`Docs/wowlua-test-findings.md` V48 only says the emulator's `PlaceBid` is a no-op and the tests stub it)
- what: The header says: "A single auction's buyout (C_AuctionHouse.PlaceBid) Forever takes only from the game's own code (found in game: \"Blocked\", also typed in chat), so it goes through the game's hidden page". The Buy tab's Buy out was reworked for that (0aac4856). Three callers were left: `Bid()` (`pcall(AH.PlaceBid, a.auctionID, amount)`), `BidAgain()` (`pcall(AH.PlaceBid, e.auctionID, amount)`) and `BuyOutBid()` (`pcall(AH.PlaceBid, id, buyout)`, exactly the blocked buyout, behind SuuUI's own confirmation). A protected call blocked by the client does not raise a Lua error, so `pcall` returns true: `Bid` and `BidAgain` go on to `self:RememberBid(...)` and `self:Note("Bid " .. coins(amount) .. ".")`.
- why it matters: On Forever a bid from either place most likely does nothing except the client's "blocked" message, while the foot says "Bid 5g" and the amount is stored as the player's bid. The Bids tab's Buy out asks "Buy out X? For 12g", and confirming does nothing. Players believe they bid or bought.
- fix: Probe first (`/suu probe` topic: `PlaceBid` with an amount under the buyout from addon code; then a secure click on the game's `ItemBuyFrame.BidFrame.BidButton` after choosing the auction on its row, with the game's prefilled amount and with an amount set from addon code). Then either route Bid through the game's page like Buy out (`Over("bid", …)` on the game's Bid button; if an addon-set amount taints it, offer only the game's least bid) or remove Bid where it cannot work and say so in the foot. Until then, do not report success from the `pcall`: wait for `BID_ADDED` / `AUCTION_HOUSE_PURCHASE_COMPLETED`, and listen for `ADDON_ACTION_FORBIDDEN`/`ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` naming SuuUI to say "the game refused". Give `BuyOutBid` the same treatment as `BuyOut`. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/AuctionHouse.test.wowlua`.

#### BAG-2: Collect all retries a refused take forever
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); how often the game refuses is in-game behaviour
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (Mail/Collect: one take at a time, moved on by the game's answer (`MAIL_INBOX_UPDATE`, `MAIL_SUCCESS`, `MAIL_FAILED`, `UI_ERROR_MESSAGE`) with a 5 s backstop; a refused take is skipped for the rest of the run; an item the bags have no room for (by bag family, part stacks and the reagent bag) is not asked for; the run ends by saying what was left and why)
- probe (2026-11-16 and 17, `/suu probe all`; read 2026-11-19): 3 refusals with the mailbox open came as `UI_ERROR_MESSAGE` only, never `MAIL_FAILED` (one `ERR_BANK_FULL`; the two others, `ERR_INVALID_ATTACK_TARGET` and `ERR_TOO_FAR_TO_INTERACT`, likely not takes: the watcher counts any red error then). The fix holds: Collect moves on by the error text and its short backstop. The header of `Mail/Collect` still says `MAIL_FAILED` comes with the error.
- where: src/Units/Mail.wowlua:157-174 (`nextTake`), 605-628 (`CollectAll`)
- known: no
- what: Each 0.25 s tick takes the first thing `nextTake` finds (`TakeInboxItem(i, a)` or `TakeInboxMoney(i)`). The only stops are: mailbox closed, nothing left, or `local full = a and (asNumber(try(C_Container.CalculateTotalNumberOfFreeBagSlots)) or 1) == 0`. Nothing checks that the previous take changed anything, and there is no `UI_ERROR_MESSAGE` listener. (NEW added `Closed()` at 1540-1551, which cancels the ticker on `MAIL_CLOSED` and on `PLAYER_INTERACTION_MANAGER_FRAME_HIDE`; the loop itself is unchanged.)
- why it matters: If the game refuses the item (a unique item already owned; the only free slots are in a quiver, ammo pouch, soul or profession bag, which that count includes), `nextTake` returns the same mail and attachment every tick: `TakeInboxItem` four times a second, the red error text repeating, the button on "Collecting…", and no mail after the stuck one is ever collected, until the mailbox closes.
- fix: Track progress: remember the last (sender, subject, attachment) asked for; when the same one comes back twice without the inbox having changed, add that mail to a `skipped` set passed to `nextTake` and go on; stop when nothing is left to try. Use the general bags' free slots (Bags exports `isSpecialBag`, src/Units/Bags.wowlua:247) instead of the total. Say in the foot what was left ("2 mails left: bags full or unique"). Tests: `tests/unit/Units/Mail.test.wowlua` (a mail whose item the engine refuses).

#### BAG-33: The auction house's secure overlays are not released when combat starts or the house closes in combat
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the overlays staying; needs in-game probe for what the client then blocks
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (the secure overlays hang off a holder under a `[combat] hide; show` state driver and are hidden on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`; after the fight they come back only where their view shows, and the house closing hides them all. Point (3), a shown overlay above another window dragged over Buy out out of combat, is unchanged)
- where: src/Units/AuctionHouse/GamePage.wowlua:61-111 (`placeOver`, `hideOver`, `hideStaleOvers`), 194-223
  (`drawBuyOver`); src/Units/AuctionHouse.wowlua:710-716 (`Refresh`), 826-833 (`AUCTION_HOUSE_CLOSED`)
- known: no
- what: Four `SecureActionButtonTemplate` overlays ("result", "auction", "buyout", "back") hang off `UIParent` at DIALOG strata, anchored with `SetAllPoints` to SuuUI's rows and buttons while shown. "back" is shown whenever an item's view is open and the game's page is on an item; "buyout" while an auction is chosen. `HideOver` does nothing in combat (`if over and not InCombatLockdown() then over.hide() end`) and nothing retries: there is no `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` or `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` handler in this module. `HideStaleOvers` runs only from `Refresh`, which returns while the window is hidden.
- why it matters: (1) Combat starts with an item's view open (a duel, a flagged player, a city raid): the protected overlays stay anchored to the window's buttons. The stdlib's own comment says a window with a protected frame anchored to it "would no longer open or close in combat"; if so, `window:Hide()` on `AUCTION_HOUSE_CLOSED` and the row layout in `Refresh` are blocked with "interface action failed". Probe: open an item, choose an auction, enter combat, walk away; watch the error list and `/suu probe taint`. (2) The house closes in combat: the overlays stay shown over where Buy out and Back were, invisible, at DIALOG strata, taking clicks there (and clicking the game's hidden Buyout or Back) until the next visit's first `Refresh` out of combat. (3) Out of combat too, a shown "buyout" overlay sits above any other window dragged over the Buy out button (bags, a dialog), the kind of covered click `Docs/wowlua-test-findings.md` V47 records.
- fix: As Bags does for its own overlays (src/Units/Bags.wowlua:3044-3053): on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` (lockdown is not active yet) hide every overlay in `self.overs`; on `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` hide them all if the window is hidden, else `Refresh()`. Also parent the buttons to a holder with `secure.visibility(holder, "[combat] hide; show")` as `Bags.UseButton` does (src/Units/Bags.wowlua:1565-1567). Tests: `tests/unit/Units/AuctionHouse.test.wowlua` (overlay shown, combat starts: hidden and unanchored).

#### BAG-34: Only items and auctions the game's hidden list has a row frame for can be bought out; the foot's advice does not help
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code); how many rows the hidden list makes needs in-game probe
- status: partly fixed in 740e3d27 (the note after a click on Buy out now says why it can't buy: the game's page is on another item (search for its name), the auction's row is there (click it again), or the game lists only an item's first auctions and this one is not among them; Buy out is still enabled for an auction it cannot buy, and results and auctions beyond the game's first rows still cannot be bought out)
- where: src/Units/AuctionHouse/GamePage.wowlua:47-60 (`gameRow`), 146-230 (`overResult`, `overAuction`);
  src/Units/AuctionHouse/ItemView.wowlua:512-527 (`buyOut`); src/Units/AuctionHouse/Buy.wowlua:697-728
  (`sortedResults`)
- known: no
- what: A buyout needs three secure clicks on the game's own frames: its result row (opens its item page), its auction row (selects the auction), its Buyout button. `gameRow` finds a row only among the frames the game's virtual list currently has, i.e. its first screenful; nothing scrolls that list. For a result without a frame, `OverResult` falls back to the game's Back button or hides the overlay, and the plain click opens the item in SuuUI only. `BuyOut()` then says "Go back and open the item again to buy it out." or "Choose the auction again to buy it out (only the first ones listed)."
- why it matters: Results beyond the game's first rows (after "More results", or scrolled down), results placed first by SuuUI's own item-level or Available sort (`SortedResults` reorders locally; the game's list keeps the house's order), and auctions further down an item's list cannot be bought, and "go back and open it again" gives the same result every time. With the game's page on another item, every result needs two opens (the first click only sends the game's page back).
- fix: Probe whether the game's `ScrollBox` can be scrolled from addon code without tainting the later secure click (`ScrollToElementDataByPredicate` on hover, then find the frame). If yes, scroll before placing the overlay in `OverResult` and `OverAuction`. If not: when a result has no game row, send a browse query narrowed to that item (its exact name and the same filters) so it is the game's first row, and open it from there; for auctions, say in the row's tooltip and the foot which ones can be bought ("the cheapest N") and disable Buy out with that reason for the others instead of a note after the click. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/AuctionHouse.test.wowlua`.

#### BAG-3: A COD confirmation takes from whatever mail is at the index when it is confirmed
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in 740e3d27 (Mail/Inbox: a mail is known by its content (sender, subject, money, COD, attachments); the COD confirmation, Delete, Return, Take and row clicks find it again at the moment of acting and do nothing when it is gone or changed; the COD question closes with the mailbox and checks the visit and the money again)
- where: src/Units/Mail.wowlua:771-797 (`Take`); the open mail's Delete and Return:
  src/Units/Mail.wowlua:271-291
- known: no
- what: `Take` captures the inbox index: `onConfirm = function() TakeInboxItem(i, a) end`, with `i = self.openIndex` read when the dialog opened. Inbox indexes shift when a mail above is removed (Collect all, an expired mail, the game delivering more). The dialog text ("Pay %s to %s for this?") is not re-checked on confirm, and the dialog is not closed by `Closed()` (1540-1551).
- why it matters: Collect all is running (it skips COD mails but removes others), the player clicks a COD attachment, the dialog opens, mails above are removed, the player confirms: `TakeInboxItem(i, a)` addresses another mail. If that one is COD too, its amount is paid without having been shown.
- fix: In `onConfirm` read `header(i)` again and compare sender, subject and `cod` with what the dialog showed; if they differ, find the mail by those fields or cancel with a note. #### BAG-4: The merchant's Buy queue and its confirmation use an index that can point at another item
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed in db302207 (each step finds the item again by link and a visit counter stops the queue and a late confirmation; the queue still sends every step after a refused purchase, bags full or money gone)
- where: src/Units/Merchant.wowlua:410-461 (`Locate`, `Buy`), 463-488 (`ConfirmBuy`), 1035-1053
  (`MERCHANT_SHOW`, `MERCHANT_CLOSED`)
- known: no
- what: `Buy` queues chunks and calls `BuyMerchantItem(e.index, n)` every 0.3 s; the only guard is `if not n or not self.open then return end`. `ConfirmBuy`'s dialog calls `self:Buy(e, items)` whenever it is confirmed. `e.index` is the merchant index at draw time. Nothing checks that the index still holds the same item, and nothing stops the queue after a failed purchase.
- why it matters: (1) Changing the merchant filter (`SetMerchantFilter`, 641) during a multi-step purchase renumbers the list; the remaining steps buy whatever is at that index. (2) The confirmation for a dear or currency purchase stays open after the vendor closes; confirmed at the next vendor (`self.open` is true again) it buys that vendor's item at the same index, with no price check. (3) When the bags fill or the money runs out mid-queue, every remaining step is still sent: an error line per 0.3 s. NEW also enables Buy for items the game marks not purchasable (`r.buy:SetEnabledState(not e.known and purchases > 0)`, line 521, wanted), so refusals mid-queue are more likely.
- fix: Give each merchant visit a token (a counter raised on `MERCHANT_SHOW`, `MERCHANT_CLOSED` and filter change); `Buy` and the confirmation capture it and stop when it differs. Before each `BuyMerchantItem` compare `GetMerchantItemLink(e.index)` with `e.link` (the name when there is no link). Stop the queue when the item count did not rise after a step or on `UI_ERROR_MESSAGE`. Close the confirmation on `MERCHANT_CLOSED`. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/Merchant.test.wowlua`.

#### BAG-5: A post that is never confirmed leaves Post disabled until a reload
- severity: medium

#### BAG-6: Auction prices are saved per character, never pruned, and read across realms; Professions' cost and profit now build on them
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/AuctionHouse.wowlua:195-207 (`CharStore`), 292-301 (`Saved`, `AllSaved`), 999-1008 (the
  `Price` service); src/Units/AuctionHouse/Prices.wowlua:38-81 (`recordSeen`, `lowestSeen`, `lastPosted`);
  src/Units/AuctionHouse/Scan.wowlua:279-283; src/Units/AuctionHouse/Sell.wowlua:350-352;
  src/Units/Professions.wowlua:317-325 (`auctionPrice`), 658-670 (`VendorPrice`), 692-700 (`UnitCost`)
- known: no
- what: `Seen` writes `{ price, at, qty, n, most }` into this character's `CharData().seen[itemID]`; Scan all writes one entry per item on the house. `LowestSeen`/`LastPosted`/`LastScan` take the newest entry over `AllSaved()`, i.e. every character in `SuuUIDB.charData`, whatever its realm or faction. Nothing removes an entry. `AllSaved()` builds a table per call on top of `allCharData`'s own. NEW adds a service `Price(itemID)` = `LowestSeen`, which Professions calls for every reagent and product.
- why it matters: (1) Growth: each scanning character keeps its own full copy (thousands of small tables), loaded at every login and written at every logout. (2) Wrong prices: a price seen on another realm shows in tooltips, fills the sell price (`sell.price:SetCopper((last and last.price) or (low and low.price) or 0)`) and now decides crafting cost, profit and the profit sort. (3) Two tables per lookup, per tooltip, per sell row and per reagent of every recipe (BAG-12).
- fix: Keep the price memory once per realm (and faction if the houses are separate on Forever), outside `charData` (the account store or a `wowlua:saved` table), with `posted`, `bids` and `history` left per character. Prune on login and after a scan (entries older than N days; 30 or a setting). Migrate the per-character `seen` by taking the newest per item among characters of the same realm. Cache the list of stores instead of building it per lookup. The new search history needs nothing: it is capped at five (`HISTORY_MAX`, `RememberSearch` 2080-2091). Tests: `tests/unit/Units/AuctionHouse.test.wowlua`, `tests/compat` for the old shape.

#### BAG-8: The character snapshot is rebuilt in full a second after every bag or equipment event, in combat too

- known: no
- what: `BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED`, `BAG_CONTAINER_UPDATE`, `BANKFRAME_OPENED`, `PLAYER_EQUIPMENT_CHANGED` and `PLAYER_LEVEL_UP` call `QueueSave`, which runs `SaveMe` one second later, window open or not (`self.saveTimer = after(1, …)`; a leading timer, not a debounce): `snapshot` reads every slot of every bag and builds a saved table per item, plus 19 inventory links, replacing `d.bags` whole. NEW adds `isSpecialBag(bag)` per bag to it (several API calls each).
- why it matters: Anything that changes a bag once a second or more (ammo per shot, reagents per cast, looting, crafting runs) makes this a once-a-second job for the whole fight: a few hundred short-lived tables per second for data that only matters at logout or when another character's view or a tooltip count asks for it.

Or restart the timer on each event (a trailing debounce) and skip it in combat. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/Bags.test.wowlua`.

Build the overview's cards only when the overview shows. Drop the caches on `TRADE_SKILL_DATA_SOURCE_CHANGED`/`NEW_RECIPE_LEARNED`. #### BAG-14: The sort marks items as "don't stack" when more than six kinds have part stacks

The round limit (`STACK_ROUNDS`) also ends stacking early for an item with many part stacks.

#### BAG-15: Any red error text during a sort still stops it; in the bags it can now also take a special bag out of sorting for the session
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Bags.wowlua:1119-1133 (`UI_ERROR_MESSAGE`); src/Units/Bags/SortRun.wowlua:356-388
  (`SortTick`), 166-187 (`Refused`), 415-428 (`StopSort`)
- known: no
- what: What changed: for the bags an error during a wave no longer stops the sort at once; it is kept (`st.refused = text or ""`) and looked at when the wave lands: `if not self:Refused(w.moves) then return self:StopSort("the game refused a move" …) end`. `Refused` blames, for each move that did not land, both the target and the source bag when they are not plain bags, adds them to `self.refusingBags` (never cleared in the session) and prints "Sorting leaves your %s as it is". What did not change: the handler takes every `UI_ERROR_MESSAGE`, whatever its text. An unrelated message ("Out of range", "Not enough mana", "You are too far away") with all moves landed makes `Refused` return false, and the sort stops with that text as its reason. For the bank the sort still stops at once, and in its first wave `StopSort` runs the game's bank sort instead (`why:find("^the game")`).
- why it matters: Unrelated errors stop a sort half-way with a misleading reason, or give the bank Blizzard's order instead of the chosen one. If an unrelated error coincides with a move that has not landed, a quiver, soul or profession bag is left out of every later sort until a reload, though it refused nothing.
- fix: React only to inventory errors: compare the message (or the message type, the argument the handler skips) with a small set built at load from the game's strings (`ERR_INV_FULL`, `ERR_BAG_FULL`, `ERR_ITEM_LOCKED`, `ERR_WRONG_BAG_TYPE*`, `ERR_BANK_FULL`, `ERR_ITEM_NOT_FOUND`, the "Only %s can be placed in that" family); ignore the rest. In `Refused` blame only the target bag. Clear `refusingBags` for a bag when `BAG_CONTAINER_UPDATE` changes that slot. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/Bags.test.wowlua` (an unrelated error leaves the sort running and no bag blamed).

#### BAG-23: Macros: the first of two macros with the same name cannot be opened, edited or deleted
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Macros.wowlua:698-707 (`Refresh`), 834-842 (`Select`), 878-898 (`Delete`)
- known: no
- what: `Refresh` looks the chosen macro up again by name only: `for _, m in ipairs(list) do if m.name == chosen.name then current = m end end` (the last match wins). The delete confirmation captures the loaded macro's index and deletes it without checking that the index still holds that macro.
- why it matters: The game allows macros with equal names. Clicking the first always loads the last; Save and Delete then act on the last. If the list shifts while the delete dialog is open, another macro is deleted.
- fix: In `Refresh` prefer the entry whose index equals `chosen.index` when its name still matches; fall back to the name. In `Delete`'s `onConfirm` check that `GetMacroInfo(m.index)` returns `m.name` and `m.body` first. Tests: `tests/unit/Units/Macros.test.wowlua`.

### Fixed since the first pass

None in full. Parts of BAG-7 are fixed (the full re-layout per `BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED` and the full redraw per `BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN`; src/Units/Bags.wowlua:1056-1182, 1007-1028, commits 5a4a8cb9 and 17d80d4d); what remains is restated under BAG-7 as low. BAG-15 changed form (735368bd) and is restated.

### Withdrawn

- BAG-22 (the buy cell's secure overlay stays anchored when hidden): the first pass read the stdlib wrongly. `overlay.hide` in wowlua's `std/secure.wowlua` does `button:Hide(); button:ClearAllPoints()` and has since the overlay was added (8467a560, in v0.10.0), and Bags hides the overlay on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` (src/Units/Bags.wowlua:3044-3050), before lockdown. Nothing stays anchored in combat.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Calls Forever blocks, wrapped in `pcall` and read as success.** A blocked protected call raises no Lua error. Sweep `src/Units` for `pcall(`/`try(` around functions the game restricts (`PlaceBid`, `UseContainerItem`, `CancelAuction`, `PostItem`, `PickupContainerItem` in the sort) and make each wait for its confirming event instead of trusting the call's return. `Blizzard_APIDocumentationGenerated` (`HasRestrictions`) on the `forever` branch lists them.
- **Secure overlays need one combat policy.** Bags has it (hide on `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`, a `[combat] hide` driver, hide on `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`); the auction house's four overlays have none. Best placed in `secure.overlay` itself (an option `hideInCombat`), so every user gets it.
- **Index as identity.** Auction rows (Bid), merchant indexes, inbox indexes and macro indexes are captured and used later from a timer, a queue or a confirmation. Sweep every `UI.Confirm({ onConfirm = … })` and every `after`/`every` callback in `src/Units` for a captured index.
- **Confirm dialogs outlive their context.** `UI.Confirm` has no owner; a dialog opened by a window stays when that window or the NPC conversation closes. An `owner = window` option (closed with it) would remove a class of stale confirmations.
- **Tickers and queues without a progress check**: Sell junk (twice), Collect all, the merchant's Buy queue. A small shared helper ("repeat a step until done, stop when a step changes nothing twice") fits all of them.
- **Per-character stores read with `AllCharData()` in hot paths** (tooltips, sell rows, and now every reagent of every recipe): Bags, AuctionHouse, Professions. `allCharData` builds a table per call; a cached list invalidated on a character being added or forgotten would serve all three.
- **Data that is per realm stored per character and read account-wide**: auction prices, now vendor prices too.
- **`QueueRefresh` on closed windows** and **full redraw as the only redraw** are the same in Merchant, Mail, AuctionHouse and Professions, and probably in the other window modules.
- **Session-long listeners for a short-lived need** (`GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN` for a dropdown, `CURRENT_SPELL_CAST_CHANGED` for a hidden button): register while the thing is open.

### Summary

Talents, Inspect and the dressing room are nearly unchanged since the first pass (layout and theme
calls, a per-tree row gate in Talents), so every first-pass finding there is still in the code:
the shared `learned` baseline, the 120 s rollback window, the planned notice, Use build dropping
planned points, the full redraw per item event in Inspect.

The Spellbook was reworked for cost: a closed book is now drawn once, half a second after a burst,
out of combat, and the train count comes from the lists the render already made. What is left is
smaller: pet events still force a full render of the closed book, the count is still worked out a
second time a second later, and every page flip rebuilds every school. A Pet school was added
(the first pass's gap is closed).

Collections grew most (pets, gifts, drag to the bars, secure tabs for combat). Its rebuild cost got
worse: every refresh now builds four whole lists (the tab's, and mounts, pets and toys again for the
foot), on each keystroke. The toy shelf still shows other toys over the old secure `Use` in combat,
and the stage's Summon button has the same drift across tabs. The micro menu now opens the window
through the secure toggle.

The Character window gained a Pet tab that calls Blizzard's `ToggleCharacter`,
`PaperDollFrame_SetSidebar` and `PaperDollFrame_SetPet` from addon code; the file's own notes say a
tainted stats update failed on secret values, so this needs a probe.

- known: no
- what: `self.learned` holds each node's learned rank "while nothing is planned", because the game's rank counts planned points on Forever. It is one table for whatever config `Collect` was last called for:
  ```
  local staged = errors.tryValue(C_Traits.ConfigHasStagedChanges, configID) == true
  if not staged or self.learnedFor ~= configID then
      self.learnedFor = configID
      if not staged then
          self.learned = {}
      end
  end
  ```
  A call for a config that is not staged (the other spec group, `INSPECT_CONFIG`) empties the table and fills it with that config's ranks (`learned[nodeID] = current`, line 727). The next call for your staged config sees `learnedFor ~= configID`, sets `learnedFor`, and keeps the table (it is staged), which now holds the other config's ranks. `base = math.min(learned[nodeID], current)` (729-733) then uses them. While the window shows an inspected player, `Render` calls `Collect()` and then `Collect(INSPECT_CONFIG)` (lines 902, 913, 920) on every pass.
- why it matters: plan a point (not applied), click the Secondary spec, click back to Primary: every talent learned in Primary but not in Secondary now shows as planned (`pending = current - base`), the pending total and the points line are wrong, right-click offers a refund of learned ranks, Undo and Apply are enabled by counts that are not real, and `Fit` (Use build) takes the wrong ranks as learned. The same after View Talents on an inspected player of your class (same node IDs). For another class the IDs miss and `base` falls back to `min(activeRank, current)`, which the comment at 707-709 says is wrong on Forever.
- fix: key the baseline by config: `learned: { [configID]: { [nodeID]: rank } }`; reset `learned[configID]` only when that config is not staged; never record for `INSPECT_CONFIG` (nothing is planned there: use `current`). Remove `learnedFor`. Extend `tests/unit/Units/Talents.test.wowlua`: stage a point, view the other group, view the first again, expect the same `rank` and `pending`; the same with an inspect render in between.

#### CHAR-6: Collections builds four whole lists per refresh, on every keystroke, and two or three refreshes on opening
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code); how often `COMPANION_UPDATE` fires near other players needs in-game probe
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Collections.wowlua:469-512 (`Refresh`), 435-454 (`Entries`), 601-628 (`DrawFoot`), 636-648
  (`Toggle`), 935-942 (`COMPANION_UPDATE`); src/Units/Collections/Strip.wowlua:201 (search `onTextChanged`);
  src/Units/Collections/Catalog.wowlua:238-291, 316-406, 423-462, 529-579 (the list builders)
- known: no
- what: `Refresh` calls `Entries()`, which rebuilds the tab's whole list from the game and only then filters; `self.all` is stored and never reused. `DrawFoot` then builds three more lists just to count them:
  ```
  { label = "Mounts", entries = self:Mounts() },
  { label = "Pets", entries = self:Pets() },
  { label = "Toys", entries = self:Toys() },
  ```
  `Mounts()` is two journal calls, `wrapped()` and a `Learned()` store lookup per mount, then a sort; `Pets()` is `GetPetInfoByIndex` per row plus `GetPetInfoBySpeciesID` and `GetPetModelSceneInfoBySpeciesID` per kind, then a sort; `Toys()` is `GetToyInfo`, `PlayerHasToy`, `IsToyUsable`, `NeedsFanfare` per toy, then a sort; `Appearances()` is `GetAppearanceSources`, `GetItemIconByID`, `GetAppearanceCameraID` per visual. The search's `onTextChanged` calls `Refresh` per character typed. Opening runs `Refresh` from `OnShow`, again from its `after(0)`, and a third time when opened through `Toggle` (`SetTab` always calls `onTab`, src/UI/Panel.wowlua:1048-1057). `COMPANION_UPDATE` calls a full `Refresh` while the Pets tab shows, not coalesced; every favourite toggle schedules its own `after(0.1)` refresh.
- why it matters: typing in the search costs four list builds per key (on Appearances a category has hundreds to thousands of visuals). Opening costs eight to twelve. With the Pets tab open in a town, each companion event from other players rebuilds everything.
- fix: build `self.all` per tab only when the tab, slot, class or weapon kind changes or a collection event arrives (`NEW_MOUNT_ADDED`, `NEW_PET_ADDED`, `PET_JOURNAL_LIST_UPDATE`, `TOYS_UPDATED`, `TRANSMOG_COLLECTION_UPDATED`, `PLAYER_EQUIPMENT_CHANGED`, names arriving, the sources data ready); the search and filters call `filterEntries(self.all, …)` only. Keep the foot's three counts in a cache invalidated by the same events (counts need no entries: `GetNumMounts`-style loops without tables). Queue refreshes from events through one `after(0)` flag (as `petRefreshQueued` does for one event). On open, keep one `Refresh`; the `after(0)` only needs `self.showing = nil; self:DrawStage()`. Test: count `C_MountJournal.GetMountInfoByID` calls across three keystrokes.

#### CHAR-13: The spells window's per-tab sizing is written twice, in Talents and in Spellbook, and each can record the other's size as "Blizzard's"

- category: architecture

  src/Units/Spellbook.wowlua:1574-1617 (`Shorten`, `Place`), 1839-1854 (`Restore`), 1321-1330 (`again`),
  1071-1074 (`Render` calls `Shorten`)
- known: no
- what: both modules remember "Blizzard's size" in their own `blizzHeight`/`blizzWidth`, set the window's size under their own `sizing` flag, hook `SetHeight`/`SetWidth`/`SetSize` on the same frame, and register a tab size with `UI.SecurePlacement`. Neither knows the other's flag. One concrete path: `Spellbook:Render(true)` runs with the book hidden (0.5 s after any spell change, or on a pet event) and does

If SuuUI's Talents tab is showing (applying talents teaches spells), Talents' `again` hook answers with `Size()`, which reads the Spellbook's size and stores it as `self.blizzHeight`/`blizzWidth`; `Talents:Restore` later sets that size for Blizzard's other tabs. With the Talents module off, the window stays at the Spellbook's size under Blizzard's tab.
- why it matters: two copies of protected-frame sizing that must stay in step, with a wrong window size as the failure; any further page in this window adds a third copy.
- fix: one helper in `src/UI` beside `SecurePlacement` (for example `placer:TabSize(key, tabFrame, width, height)`) that owns the remembered Blizzard size, the single set of hooks and the re-assertion, and applies a size only while its tab frame is shown; both modules call it. Export it and document it in `Docs/API.md`. Until then: `Shorten` returns unless `bookPage(f):IsShown()` (keep `Place()` before the check).

#### CHAR-19: Collection dates: your first of a kind reads "before SuuUI", and others get the day the window first saw them, per character
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Collections.wowlua:258-278 (`Learned`), 944-984 (`NEW_PET_ADDED`, `NEW_MOUNT_ADDED`,
  `NEW_TOY_ADDED`), 205 (`Saved` → `CharData`); src/Units/Collections/Catalog.wowlua:157 (`day`)
- known: no
- what: `Learned` returns before making the kind's store when the item is not collected, and treats everything seen within 5 s of the store's making as owned before SuuUI:
  ```
  if not collected then return nil end
  …
  if not seen then
      seen = { first = time() }
      learned[kind] = seen
  end
  local at = seen[id]
  if at == nil then
      at = (time() - seen.first < 5) and 0 or time()
  ```
  With no mount (pet, toy) yet, the store for that kind is first made when the first one is seen collected, so that one gets `0`. Later items are stamped when a list is next built with them (the new-item events only call `NoteLast` and `Refresh`, which does nothing while the window is closed). The store is per character although the collections are account-wide.
- why it matters: on a fresh character the first mount reads "Collected · before SuuUI", has no fresh mark and sorts last under Recent. A mount learned on Monday with the window closed reads Thursday when the window is next opened. On a second character everything learned since its first look shows as new today.
- fix: make the kind's store on the first list build whether or not anything is collected (`Learned` called once per kind before the loop, or create `seen` before the `collected` check); in the three new-item events write `seen[id] = time()` directly; keep the store in `SuuUI.AccountData` with a migration that merges the characters' tables, earliest date first. Test: empty collection, build the list, add one mount, expect a date.

#### CHAR-20: Smaller Collections costs: cooldown lines rebuilt every second, the names loop, the class filter left set, a hidden mount's star does nothing
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for (a) and (d); needs in-game probe for (b) and (c)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Collections/Shelf.wowlua:204-226 (`DrawCooldown`); src/Units/Collections.wowlua:1003-1012,
  1041-1045, 1013-1024 (`namesPending`); src/Units/Collections/Catalog.wowlua:444, 548;
  src/Units/Collections/Wardrobe.wowlua:328 (`SetClassFilter`); src/Units/Collections/Actions.wowlua:188-237
  (`toggleFavourite`, `mountIndex`) against 244-267 (`pickup`)
- known: no
- what: (a) every second, and on every `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` and `BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` (each global cooldown in combat), each shown toy card calls `GetItemCooldown` and, when not on cooldown, rebuilds its source line (`sourceLine`: pattern matches on the NPC string, concatenations) and sets two texts and the button's state. (b) A toy or appearance whose name never arrives sets `namesPending` on every refresh, so any `GET_ITEM_INFO_RECEIVED` triggers a full refresh 0.3 s later for as long as the window is open. (c) The class select calls `C_TransmogCollection.SetClassFilter(id)` and nothing restores the player's class when the window closes. (d) A mount's favourite is set by its place in the game's displayed list (`MountIndex`); a mount hidden by the game journal's own search or filters has no place, and `ToggleFavourite` then does nothing, silently. `Pickup` handles the same case with `SetSearch("")` and `SetDefaultFilters()`.
- why it matters: (a) steady work in combat with the Toys tab open; (b) a refresh loop (four list builds each, see CHAR-6) for an item the client does not have; (c) the game's own wardrobe or a transmogrifier may open on another class's list; (d) the star does nothing.
- fix: (a) keep `start`, `duration` per card and update only on a change; set the source line once in `DrawToyCard`; (b) stop after a few tries per item ID; (c) restore the class filter in the window's `OnHide`; (d) move the clear-and-look-again from `Pickup` into `MountIndex` (a `clear` flag) and use it in `ToggleFavourite` and `DrawStage`.

#### CHAR-22: The stats pane's rows are reskinned twice per ScrollBox update, with tables and closures per row, and unguarded geometry reads
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the cost; needs in-game probe for the geometry (open the Character window in combat)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/CharacterWindow.wowlua:1099-1185 (`SkinStatRow`), 1192-1220 (`skinAll` on both `Update` and
  `OnDataRangeChanged`), 1106 (`r:GetSize()` compared), 1300 (`row:GetWidth() - 6`), 1178 (`GetTextColor` read
  back), 312 and 1023 (`STATS_BOX_H`)
- known: no
- what: each stats refresh runs `skinAll` twice. Since `BuildGear` makes Blizzard's list 3,000 px tall ("makes a row for every stat"), that is every stat row, not only the visible ones. Per row `SkinStatRow` creates two closures and two or more tables (`{ row:GetRegions() }`, `texts`, each child's regions), applies fonts and paints. `row:GetHeight()` and `t:GetLeft()` go through `secret.asNumber`, but `local w, h = r:GetSize()` is compared directly (`w > 0 and w <= 24`), as is the sidebar row's `GetWidth()`; `AlignSetList` notes that edges here are "secret in combat". The value's colour is read back with `GetTextColor()` after SuuUI painted it on the last pass, so a reused row keeps a bonus or malus colour if Blizzard does not set the colour again.
- why it matters: with the window open in a fight, every stat change (buffs, procs) reskins all rows twice and leaves garbage; a possible error if a texture's size is secret there; a stat value in the wrong colour.
- fix: skin a row once per data change (remember per row what was skinned in a weak table and skip unchanged rows), hoist `texture`/`take` out of the per-row call, register one of the two triggers, read sizes through `secret.asNumber`, and remember Blizzard's colour before painting (hook the value's `SetTextColor`).

#### CHAR-15: The game's talent string is imported without checking its tree hash or version, and only each class's first spec ID is known
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the hash; needs in-game probe for the spec IDs
- status: open
- where: src/Units/Talents/Share.wowlua:478-514 (`readPasted`, the game's string: no hash or version check);
  src/Units/Talents/Trees.wowlua:367-397 (`readClasses`: spec 1 only); src/UI/TalentBuilds.wowlua
  (`readGameTalentString`)
- known: no
- what: `readGameTalentString` returns `version` and `hash`; `ReadPasted` ignores both (`GameString`, lines 2347-2348, writes them from `GetLoadoutSerializationVersion` and `GetTreeHash`). The string has no node IDs: it is a run of bits in `GetTreeNodes` order, so a string made on another build of the tree decodes onto the wrong talents with no error. The class is found by `c.specID == specID`, where `c.specID` is the class's spec 1.
- why it matters: a string from before a talent change imports as a plausible but wrong build. If the game writes the player's actual spec ID (2 or 3) into its string, the import says "for a class without talents here".
- fix: compare `read.hash` with `C_Traits.GetTreeHash(tree.treeID)` and `read.version` with `GetLoadoutSerializationVersion()`; on a mismatch set the note "Made for another version of the talents." as the SuuUI format does (line 2426). In `Classes`, record every spec ID of a class (`GetNumSpecializationsForClassID`) and map each to it. Tests: the sharing group in `tests/unit/Units/Talents.test.wowlua`.

#### CHAR-17: Tree and class caches are never invalidated, and an empty class list is cached for the session
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (needs in-game probe: can `GetClassInfo`/`GetTraitTreeForSpec` or spell names answer nothing early at login)
- status: open

  (`BuildTree`: `self.buildTrees[file] = tree`), 980-982 (the `NextTalent` service)
- known: no
- what: `Classes()` stores its result on the first call even when `list` is empty. `BuildTree` stores a tree for the session with the names and icons read at that moment, and nothing clears it on `TRAIT_TREE_CHANGED`, a hotfix, or a level that makes nodes visible (`placedNode` drops invisible ones).
- why it matters: if the first call comes before the game has the data, the New build dialog has no classes or the order panel shows wrong names until `/reload`. A saved active build whose nodes left the tree gives `NextTalent` nil silently: no ring and no notice that the build no longer fits.
- fix: do not cache an empty `Classes` result; drop `self.buildTrees[CLASS]` on `TRAIT_CONFIG_LIST_UPDATED`/`TRAIT_TREE_CHANGED`; when the active build fails `UI.TalentOrderCheck` against the current tree, post a notice once.

#### CHAR-18: Talents renders twice per click and reads every node again each time; the reset check is not coalesced
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open

  src/Units/Talents/Trees.wowlua:32-115 (`gateOf`, `talentOf`), 202-340 (`collect`);
  src/Units/Talents.wowlua:1032-1042 (one 0.5 s timer per event)
- known: no
- what: a click renders at once and again a frame later from `TRAIT_NODE_CHANGED`/`TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED`. Each render calls `GetNodeInfo`, `GetEntryInfo`, `GetDefinitionInfo`, the spell's name and texture and now `GetConditionInfo` per condition for every node, `NextTalent` reads `GetNodeInfo` again per step, and `PickerOptions` rebuilds and sorts every build. With a reset pending, each of three events starts its own `after(0.5)` timer that runs `CheckReset` → `Collect`.
- why it matters: only while the window is open; a visible hitch on slower machines when clicking quickly.
- fix: cache `talentOf` and `gateOf` per `(configID, nodeID, entryID)`; let the click paths only `QueueRender`; one pending reset timer behind a flag.

### Fixed since the first pass

- CHAR-8: No pet spellbook. A Pet school now lists the pet's book, casts by name, and turns autocast through the pet bar's buttons: src/Units/Spellbook.wowlua:627-730 (`PetSchool`, `PetBarSlots`, `PetLearned`), 1032-1036 (commits 21f0472e, 49a9a3ea).

### Withdrawn

None.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Secure buttons whose look follows data in combat.** Three places now: the toy cards (CHAR-2), the stage's Summon button across tabs (CHAR-29), the Spellbook's cells (CHAR-7). The pattern is always "redraw the look, set a flag for the attributes"; the safe pattern is "in combat, do not re-map". Worth one rule in the conventions and a sweep of other pooled secure lists.
- **Two ways to coalesce in one file.** The Spellbook has `RenderOrMark`/`RenderAhead` for `SPELLS_CHANGED` and direct `Render(true)` for the pet events beside it; Collections has `petRefreshQueued` for one event and direct `Refresh` for nine others. A module helper ("draw once next frame while shown, else mark dirty") would remove CHAR-1(a), CHAR-6's event part, CHAR-9, CHAR-23 and CHAR-26.
- **Counting by building.** `DrawFoot` builds three sorted entry lists to print three counts; `CountToTrain` builds every school's lists to return two numbers the render already has. Look for the same wherever a tooltip, a badge or a foot shows a count.
- **Blizzard functions called from addon code.** The Pet tab (CHAR-28) calls `ToggleCharacter`, `PaperDollFrame_SetSidebar`, `PaperDollFrame_SetPet`; `FitSidePane` calls the pane's `Content:Layout()`; the Spellbook calls `PlayerSpellsUtil.OpenToSpellBookTab` and `HideUIPanel(ClickBindingFrame)`. On Forever a tainted Blizzard update can fail on secret values, as CharacterWindow's own note records. Each such call deserves a line saying it was probed in combat.
- **"Blizzard's size" remembered by each module that resizes a shared window** (CHAR-13). The same shape is likely wherever two modules restyle tabs of one Blizzard window.
- **"Public API only" is not true** (CHAR-21): besides the four value imports, all six files import `/Core/Modules`, three import `/Core/ServiceKeys`, Talents extends `/UI/Panel`, Inspect extends `/UI/Inventory`'s `ItemSlot`. Either export what built-in modules need or say in the conventions that they may use it.
- **Windows built in `OnEnable`** (CHAR-12). `/Core/Ahead` now exists for exactly this; these four modules do not use it for their windows.
- **English text matched in game strings**: `^Use:` (Collections 1559), `"Rank " .. n` and `"Passive"` (Spellbook 898, 605), the possessive `className .. "s"` (Collections 3594), `"^Toy %d"` as the marker for a missing name (Collections 2238). Fine for an English client only.
- **Quiet calls hide API changes.** Nearly every game call goes through `try`/`tryValue`/`tryMethod`/`pcall` and falls back to nil; Collections added many more (gifts, pets, the present's placement). A debug-level report on the first failure per function would make a client update visible.
