  (GRP-20), the same pattern as Guild's overlays (GRP-1, GRP-2).
- Addon messages: six modules receive on the one prefix `SuuUI`, each with its own
  listener and parser. None checks the channel, so every one of them accepts an
  addon whisper from any player. Timeline (a stranger starts or cancels your pull
  countdown, with voice) and Marks (a stranger fills your saved marks) are the
  worst; RaidPlanner and Readiness answer questions from anyone with a RAID/PARTY
  broadcast. Convergences and Campsite validate the payload well and limit per
  sender, but not who sends. The full table and a shared helper are in GRP-26.
- foreverlfg receives no addon messages (public chat and the game's tool only), and
  no other module (LootRolls, QuestAnnounce, MouseBindings, Chat) listens to
  `CHAT_MSG_ADDON`.
- Windows is larger (2,528 lines) and more coupled than before: it now also imports
  `reskinPart` and `moneyText` from `/UI` and calls the FlightMap and WorldMap
  modules' methods by name (GRP-6).

### Findings

#### GRP-21: Timeline: anyone can start or cancel your pull countdown with an addon whisper
- status: fixed in db302207 (PULL goes through Core/Comm: group channels only, the sender must lead or assist in a raid, two a sender per 2 s, and OnPull ignores it in combat)
- probe (2026-11-15 and 16, `/suu probe all`, COMM-senders; read 2026-11-19): `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` names a group member "Name Surname", equal to `GetUnitName(unit, true)` and never to plain `UnitName(unit)`. At `3dcdc41e` the rank check (`GameComm:membership` → `names()` in src/Core/Comm.wowlua) compares the sender with `GetUnitName(unit, true)` first, so it finds the member and the "assist" rule holds: in a raid only the leader or an assistant, in a party anyone in it, nobody outside the group. The record calls the case "a sender of another realm" (from `UnitName`'s second return, which holds the surname): WoW Forever has no realms. Comm's comments still call the form unverified and speak of other realms.
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Timeline.wowlua:886-903 (OnMessage), 731-782 (StartPull), 692-710 (ScheduleVoice), 997-999 (listener)
- known: no
- what: the receiver checks the prefix, that the text is `PULL\t<int>`, and that the
  sender is not you. It ignores the channel (`_`) and never asks whether the sender
  is in your group, leads it or assists:
  ```
  function OnMessage(prefix: unknown, text: unknown, _: unknown, sender: unknown)
      ...
      local seconds = text:match("^PULL\t(%-?%d+)$")
      ...
      self:StartPull(tonumber(seconds), Ambiguate(sender, "short"))
  ```
  `StartPull` first calls `CancelPull(true)`, then for `seconds > 0` adds the timeline
  event, schedules the countdown voice (`PlaySoundFile`, channel Master) and shows the
  "Pull in N" alert every 0.25 s; for `seconds <= 0` it only cancels. There is no
  combat check here (the game's own countdown path, `OnCountdown` at 849, returns in
  combat) and no rate limit.
- why it matters: any player on the realm can send `PULL\t10` by addon whisper to a
  SuuUI user, solo, in a city or in the middle of a boss fight: an alert in the
  middle of the screen "Pull in 10 … from <name>" and a spoken countdown, as often
  as they like. `PULL\t0` cancels the display of a real countdown the raid leader
  started. In a raid any member, not only the leader or an assistant, can do the same
  over RAID.
- fix: accept `PULL` only when the channel is `PARTY`, `RAID` or `INSTANCE_CHAT` (the
  channels `Pull` sends on, line 816), the sender is the group's leader or an
  assistant (in a party: anyone in it), and not in combat (as `OnCountdown`). At most
  one accepted start per sender per 2 s. Best through the shared receiver of GRP-26
  (`channels = group`, `rank = "assist"`). Tests in
  `tests/unit/Units/Timeline.test.wowlua`: a whisper is ignored; a raid member
  without rank is ignored; the leader's message starts it.

#### GRP-22: Marks: shared marks are accepted from anyone, without limit, and saved
- status: fixed in db302207 (MARK only from the group's channels, ten a minute and thirty kept per sender, map checked with C_Map.GetMapInfo, name cleaned and cut, symbol from the known set, and a shared mark never pushes out one of yours)
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the map ID part is likely
- where: src/Units/Marks.wowlua:777-802 (OnMessage), 163-173 (decodeMark), 69-81 (makeRoom), 627-636 (Add), 1167-1172 (listener)
- known: no
- what: the comment says "A shared mark from a group member", but the code checks
  only the prefix, string types and "not me". The channel is ignored
  (`_channel`). Each message with a new place calls
  `self:Add(map, x, y, { name = name or "", symbol = symbol, from = who })`, which
  writes into the character's saved marks (`store(self).marks`, `CharData`) and emits
  `SUUUI_MARKS_CHANGED`. There is no limit per sender and none per minute; the only
  bound is `MAX_MARKS = 200` in `makeRoom`, which then drops the oldest shared mark
  (and, when there is no shared one yet, the player's own oldest: `table.remove(list, 1)`).
  `decodeMark` checks x and y for 0..1 but takes any number as the map
  (`tonumber(map)`: 1.5, 1e300 and negative numbers pass; nothing asks
  `C_Map.GetMapInfo`). The name is not cleaned or shortened on receipt (`clean` at
  151 is used only when sending), so it can carry `|` escape sequences. A sender on
  the same place can rename and re-symbol only its own mark (`m.from == who`), which
  is fine.
- why it matters: a stranger whispering `MARK\t<map>\t<x>\t<y>\tstar\t<text>` in a loop
  fills the player's marks up to 200, saved with the character: pins on the world map
  and the minimap with any text, each one to be removed by hand, and a real group
  member's shared marks pushed out. A player with 200 marks of their own loses the
  oldest. A map that is no map ID is stored and later passed to `C_Map.GetMapInfo`
  and the world-position functions on every map draw.
- fix: accept only channels `PARTY`, `RAID`, `INSTANCE_CHAT` (what `Post` sends on,
  `GroupChannel`); validate the map as Convergences does (integer, 1..99999,
  `C_Map.GetMapInfo(map)` not nil); clean the name with `clean` and cut it to 40
  characters, and take the symbol only from the known set (`SYMBOL`); at most 10 new
  marks per sender per minute and, say, 30 per sender per session; `makeRoom` must
  never drop one of the player's own marks for a shared one (refuse the shared one
  instead). Through the shared receiver of GRP-26. Tests in
  `tests/unit/Units/Marks.test.wowlua`: a whisper is ignored; the 11th mark of a
  minute is ignored; a full list of own marks stays whole; a bad map is refused.

#### GRP-3: The raid planner's spec messages are accepted from anyone on any channel
- status: fixed in db302207 (RPSPECQ and RPSPEC only on RAID, the question answered at most once per 30 s, specs rate-limited, and the bare-name alias written and read only for a name without another realm)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/RaidPlanner.wowlua:1772-1789 (OnMessage), 1598-1609 (NoteSpec), 1746-1757 (ShareSoon), 1295-1306 (KnownTree), 2914-2918 (listener)
- known: no
- what: `OnMessage(prefix, text, _, sender)` ignores the channel and never checks that
  the sender is in the raid:
  ```
  if message == "RPSPECQ" then
      if key(from) ~= key(asString(SuuUI.FullName("player")) or "") then
          self:ShareSoon()
      end
      return
  end
  local tree = tonumber(message:match("^RPSPEC\t(%d)$") or "")
  ...
  self:NoteSpec(from, tree, "message")
  ```
  1. `RPSPECQ` from anyone makes this client answer to RAID (`Send` uses only
     `"RAID"`, line 1733), coalesced only to one answer per 2 s (`ShareSoon`).
  2. `RPSPEC\t<1-3>` from anyone is stored. `NoteSpec` writes `specs[key(name)]` and,
     when different, `specs[Ambiguate(name, "short")]`. For a sender from another
     realm the short key is the bare name, which is also the key of a same-realm raid
     member of that name (`KnownTree` reads `specs[key(name)] or
     specs[Ambiguate(name, "short")]`). The entry is saved (`self:Data().specs`) and
     counts for a day (`SPEC_FRESH`).
- why it matters: (1) a player outside the raid can whisper `RPSPECQ` in a loop and
  make every SuuUI user they pick send a RAID addon message every 2 s (while in a
  raid and out of combat), out of the addon message budget that all six SuuUI
  protocols share on the prefix `SuuUI`. A raid member can do the same to everyone at
  once. (2) a same-named character from another realm can overwrite a raid member's
  known spec, so the planner fills and arranges that member by the wrong tree and
  does not inspect them. Table growth is small (one or two keys per sender name), but
  a stranger's keys are saved too.
- fix: accept both verbs only when the channel is `"RAID"` (the server delivers RAID
  messages only from raid members, so this is the membership check; do not rely on
  `self.byKey`, which is only filled while the roster is read). Answer `RPSPECQ` at
  most once per 30 s (as `AskSpecs` limits asking, line 1765). In `NoteSpec` write the
  short alias only when the name carries no other realm. The wire format stays.
  Through the shared receiver of GRP-26. Tests in
  `tests/unit/Units/RaidPlanner.test.wowlua`: a whisper is ignored; repeated
  questions give one answer; a cross-realm name does not write the short key.

#### GRP-23: Readiness: answers `RDYQ` from anyone, asks on every roster event, and keeps what strangers send
- status: fixed in db302207 (group channels only, RDYQ answered at most once per 10 s, asking coalesced and only for newcomers not heard from, spell list capped at 20 with ranges checked, heard pruned on roster changes, panel update coalesced)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Readiness.wowlua:302-327 (OnMessage), 115-128 (decodeShare), 289-300 (ShareSoon), 439-448 (listener, GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE)
- known: no
- what:
  1. `OnMessage(prefix, text, _, sender)` ignores the channel. `RDYQ` from any sender
     other than you calls `self:ShareSoon()`, which 2 s later sends your cooldowns to
     RAID or PARTY.
  2. `RDY\t…` from any sender is stored: `heard[who] = { at = now, spells = spells }`,
     `who = Ambiguate(sender, "short")`. `heard` is never pruned (not when the group
     changes or ends), so it keeps one entry per sender name of the session. Spell IDs
     and seconds are not range-checked (`(%d+):(%d+)`, any length), and every accepted
     message calls `self:Update()` (a full rebuild of the panel's rows when shown),
     not coalesced.
  3. On every `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`, while in a group, each client sends `RDYQ` at
     once (`self:Send("RDYQ")`, not coalesced; only the share after it is).
- why it matters: (1) a whisper loop makes the victim broadcast to its raid every
  2 s. (2) rows are only drawn for group members (`roster()`), so a stranger's data
  is not shown unless the short name equals a member's: then a character of that name
  on another realm sets that member's cooldown rows (any spell, any time left). (3)
  without any attacker: roster events come in bursts when a raid forms; ten events
  give ten `RDYQ` per SuuUI client within a moment, and every other client answers.
  All of it comes out of the one budget of the prefix `SuuUI`, so pull countdowns and
  marks sent in that moment can be dropped by the client's throttle.
- fix: accept only `PARTY`, `RAID`, `INSTANCE_CHAT`; answer `RDYQ` at most once per
  10 s; ask (`RDYQ`) through a coalesced "ask soon" with the same 10 s floor; cap the
  list at about 20 spells, IDs at 1..2^31 and seconds at 0..86400; clear `heard` for
  names no longer in the group on `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`; coalesce `Update` after a
  message. Through the shared receiver of GRP-26. Tests in
  `tests/unit/Units/Readiness.test.wowlua`.

#### GRP-1: Guild invite's secure button keeps a stale name when combat starts while the dialog is open
- status: fixed in db302207 (PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED calls StandDownInvite: the invite question closes and its secure cover is hidden and released before the lockdown)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Guild.wowlua:791-817 (InviteOverlay), 819-835 (Act), 1825-1839 (PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED)
- known: no
- what: `InviteOverlay` puts a secure macro button over the confirm dialog's Invite
  (`secure.overlay(p.ok, { strata = "FULLSCREEN_DIALOG" })`) and rewrites its macro as
  the name is typed:
  `made.set("macrotext1", "/ginvite " .. strtrim(box:GetText() or ""))`. The stdlib's
  `set` and `hide` return false in combat without doing anything
  (`secure.wowlua:122-147`). Combat is checked only when the dialog opens (`Act`,
  line 821). The PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED handler hides `self.overs`, `self.infoOvers`,
  `self.noteOvers` and `self.rowOver`:
  ```
  for _, list in ipairs({ self.overs, self.infoOvers, self.noteOvers }) do
      for _, over in pairs(list) do
          over.button:Hide()
  ...
  local row = self.rowOver
  ```
  `self.inviteOver` is not in it.
- why it matters: open "Invite to the guild", type part of a name, combat starts,
  finish typing, click Invite: the secure button is still shown and runs `/ginvite`
  with the text as it was when combat began, a shorter and different name. If that is
  a real character, the wrong player gets a guild invite. After the click the dialog
  hides, but `made.hide()` in its `OnHide` hook is refused in combat, so the secure
  button stays shown where Invite was (it hangs off UIParent). `UI.Confirm` is one
  shared dialog: the next confirm any module opens in that fight has this button over
  its OK, and a click runs the stale `/ginvite` instead of confirming.
- fix: in the PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED handler (lockdown has not begun, `over.hide()`
  still works) call `self.inviteOver.hide()` and close the dialog (or disable its
  Invite with "Not in combat"). More robust, and the pattern NEW already uses for the
  world map's title (`src/Units/Windows.wowlua:1840-1842`): parent the secure button
  to a holder frame with `secure.visibility(holder, "[combat] hide; show")`, and
  still release its anchors at PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED. Test in
  `tests/unit/Units/Guild.test.wowlua`: open the dialog, type, enter combat, expect
  the overlay hidden and released.

#### GRP-2: Guild's secure overlays are hidden at combat start but stay anchored to the window's parts
- status: partly fixed (the row overlay and the invite cover are now released with their anchors at combat start, 68ae02ee and db302207; the Promote/Demote/Remove, info and note overlays still get only button:Hide() and keep their anchors)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- where: src/Units/Guild.wowlua:1849-1863 (PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED), 402-416 (the comment and show/hide rule),
  1785-1800 (OnHide)
- known: no
- what: the module's own comment (409-413): "Anchored only while shown: a secure
  button anchored to the roster made the whole guild window protected (it couldn't
  open in combat then)". The stdlib's `over.hide()` does `Hide()` and
  `ClearAllPoints()`. At PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED the handler calls
  `over.button:Hide()` directly on every overlay (and `row.button:Hide()`), which
  leaves the anchors. Every later release in that fight (`OnHide` of the window at
  1773-1775, the row and note overlay hides) goes through `over.hide()`, which
  refuses in combat.
- why it matters: roster open with a member selected (Promote, Demote, Remove
  overlays shown, or the row overlay), combat starts, the player closes the window
  with J and opens it again in the fight. If the comment is right, the window is
  anchoring-restricted then and the game blocks placing it ("Interface action
  failed"), the case the design set out to avoid.
- fix: in the PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED handler call `over.hide()` (allowed: lockdown
  starts after the event) for `overs`, `infoOvers`, `noteOvers`, `rowOver` and
  `inviteOver` instead of `over.button:Hide()`. Probe: roster open, a member
  selected, enter combat, close and reopen the guild window; record whether the open
  is blocked and what `CommunitiesFrame:IsProtected()` returns.

#### GRP-20: The world map's secure "up" button is not let go when combat starts while the mouse is on the title
- status: fixed in db302207 (upOff runs on PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED and releases the secure button, and placeUp does not move the title while a shown secure button hangs on it in combat)
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- where: src/Units/Windows.wowlua:1798-1808 (placeUp), 1821-1854 (upOff, upOn), 1869-1876 (OnHide, MapSet)
- known: no
- what: hovering the map's title out of combat shows a secure click button over it
  (`secure.overlay(up)`, anchored with `SetAllPoints(up)`; `up` hangs on the header,
  the header on `WorldMapFrame`). It is parented to a holder with
  `secure.visibility(holder, "[combat] hide; show")`, so it disappears in combat, but
  it is only released by `upOff()` → `over.hide()`, called from its `OnLeave`, its
  `PostClick` and the map's `OnHide`. In combat `over.hide()` returns false and does
  nothing. Nothing releases it at PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED. Meanwhile `placeUp()` (on
  the map's `OnShow` and on every `MapCanvas.MapSet`) calls `up:ClearAllPoints()`,
  `up:SetPoint(...)`, `up:SetSize(...)` with no combat check.
- why it matters: the mouse rests on the map's title (reading the map while
  travelling) and a fight starts. For that fight a protected button stays anchored
  to `up`, and through it to the header and the map window. By the module's own
  finding for the guild window (a secure button left anchored "made the whole guild
  window protected (it couldn't open in combat then)", `src/Units/Guild.wowlua:411-413`),
  the world map may then refuse to open or move in that fight, and `placeUp` moves a
  frame a protected one hangs on (a blocked action on each map change). After the
  fight the button is shown again over the title, with the old `clickbutton1`, until
  the mouse next enters and leaves it.
- fix: register `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` in Windows and call `upOff()` there (lockdown
  has not begun, so `over.hide()` works); return early from `placeUp` when
  `InCombatLockdown()` and `self.upOver` is shown. Probe: hover the title, enter
  combat, close and reopen the map with M, change the zone shown; record blocked
  actions (`/suu probe taint`). Test in `tests/unit/Units/Windows.test.wowlua`:
  overlay shown, combat starts, expect it hidden and without points.

#### GRP-19: The maximize button centres the map without `overCastBar`, so the enlarged map rises to the screen's top
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Windows/WorldMap.wowlua:556-563 (setEnlarged: UI.CenterWindow(f, on) without overCastBar)
  vs 597; src/UI/WindowSkin/Row.wowlua:168-182 (centerWindow)
- known: no
- what: at load the map is centred with the option:
  `UI.CenterWindow(f, enlarged(), { overCastBar = true })`, with the comment
  "(enlarged: in the exact middle, over the cast bar as the game's fullscreen map;
  risen above it, it went to the screen's top)". The buttons' path does not pass it:
  ```
  local function setEnlarged(on: boolean)
      self:Set("mapEnlarged", on)
      look(on)
      fit()
      UI.CenterWindow(f, on)
  end
  ```
  `centerWindow` stores what the last call gave:
  `local over = opts ~= nil and opts.overCastBar == true … chrome.overCastBar = over or nil`.
  So a click on maximize sets `centered = true, overCastBar = nil`; a click on
  minimize and maximize again does the same.
- why it matters: a player who starts with the small map and clicks maximize (or
  toggles the size once in a session) gets the enlarged map pushed up to keep above
  the cast bar: at 80% of the screen's height it goes to the top, over the micro
  menu, the fault the option was added for (WindowSkin's comment dates it
  2026-11-13). It is right again only after a reload.
- fix: pass the option in `setEnlarged` too: `UI.CenterWindow(f, on, { overCastBar = true })`
  (it has no effect while `on` is false). Test in
  `tests/unit/Units/Windows.test.wowlua`: click the maximize button, expect
  `chromeOf(WorldMapFrame).overCastBar == true`.

#### GRP-4: Social's Raid page reads the raid roster unguarded and redraws in combat
- status: withdrawn (not a problem on this client: in raid combat every `GetRaidRosterInfo` field read was readable, see the probe line; `RaidMembers` still reads them raw and the page still redraws in combat, harmless while they stay readable. Seen in a raid group of 5, not a full raid instance: reopen if a larger raid shows otherwise)
- probe (2026-11-17, `/suu probe all`, in fights; read 2026-11-19): in 2 fights in a raid group of 5, no `GetRaidRosterInfo` field the watcher read was secret, nor the member count.
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- where: src/Units/Social.wowlua:979-1013 (RaidMembers), 1015-1032 (RenderRaid), 1094 (onMember), 1316-1332
  (events)
- known: no
- what: `RaidMembers` calls `GetRaidRosterInfo(i)` raw and uses the values directly:
  `leader = rank == 2`, `assistant = rank == 1`, `online = online and true or false`,
  `group = group`, and `for i = 1, GetNumGroupMembers()`. Only `name` and
  `combatRole` go through `secret.readable`. The page redraws on GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE,
  PARTY_LEADER_CHANGED, PLAYER_ROLES_ASSIGNED, UNIT_CONNECTION, PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED
  and PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED, so also during combat. `onMember` tests
  `UnitIsGroupLeader("player")` raw. RaidPlanner reads the same function only out of
  combat and wraps every value: "The roster itself out of combat only (its values may
  be secret in combat)", with `if InCombatLockdown() then return self.roster end`.
- why it matters: if the roster's values are secret in combat on Forever, as the
  planner assumes, then with the Raid page open in a raid fight either the page shows
  an empty raid (the name is secret, so every member is skipped) or the comparison on
  a secret rank raises on every roster event of the fight.
- fix: probe `GetRaidRosterInfo` in raid combat. Then keep the last roster read while
  in combat (as the planner does) or read every value through
  `secret.asNumber/asString/flag`. Better: one roster reader shared by Social and
  RaidPlanner in the public API (see GRP-6). Test:
  `tests/unit/Units/Social.test.wowlua` with a raid in combat.

#### GRP-26: Six modules each receive addon messages on the prefix `SuuUI` with their own listener and rules; one receiver in Core should check them
- status: fixed in db302207 (Core/Comm: one prefix registration and one CHAT_MSG_ADDON listener, per-verb channels, rank, rate, replyEvery and maxLength, field readers, M:OnAddonMessage/M:SendAddonMessage owned by the module; all six protocols use it)
- probe (2026-11-15 and 16, `/suu probe all`, COMM-senders; read 2026-11-19): the question below ("how senders are named for members of other realms") has its answer, without realms (Forever has none): a group member's sender is "Name Surname", equal to `GetUnitName(unit, true)`, which `names()` compares first (see GRP-21).
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: the six `OnMessage` functions and their `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` registrations in the table below
- known: no
- what: every receiver of addon messages in NEW `src/` (Diagnostics left out). All use
  prefix `SuuUI`; every one registers the prefix and its own `CHAT_MSG_ADDON`
  listener, so each message runs six handlers. None looks at the channel argument.

  | Module | Receiver | Verb(s) | Channels accepted | Sender accepted | What it validates | What a hostile sender can cause | Finding |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Timeline | src/Units/Timeline.wowlua:886 (listener 997) | `PULL\t<int>` | any, whisper included | anyone but you | exact pattern; seconds capped at 60 in `StartPull` | alert and spoken countdown at any time, also in combat; cancels a real countdown; no rate limit | GRP-21 |
  | Marks | src/Units/Marks.wowlua:777 (listener 1170) | `MARK\t<map>\t<x>\t<y>\t<symbol>\t<name>` | any | anyone but you | x, y in 0..1; nothing on map, name, symbol | fills the saved marks to 200 (per character), pushes out shared marks and one own; unlimited rate; a redraw per message; text with `\|` escapes | GRP-22 |
  | RaidPlanner | src/Units/RaidPlanner.wowlua:1772 (listener 2915) | `RPSPECQ`, `RPSPEC\t<1-3>` | any | anyone (the question: anyone but you) | exact pattern, tree 1..3 | a RAID reply every 2 s on demand; a saved spec for any sender name; overwrites a same-named member's spec across realms | GRP-3 |
  | Readiness | src/Units/Readiness.wowlua:302 (listener 439) | `RDYQ`, `RDY\t<id>:<left>,…` | any | anyone but you (short name) | pattern only; no ranges | a RAID/PARTY reply every 2 s on demand; `heard` grows by one entry per sender name; a panel rebuild per message; a same-named stranger sets a member's rows | GRP-23 |
  | Convergences | src/Units/Convergences.wowlua:586 (listener 780) | `CONV\t1\t<map>\t<x>\t<y>\t<by>\t<at>` | any | anyone but you | version; map an integer 1..99999 known to `C_Map.GetMapInfo`; x, y in 0..1; `at` sane; names cleaned to 40; not near a known spot; 30 per sender per session; list capped at 200; `receive` setting | up to 30 false spots per sender name, saved for the whole account, a toast each; `taken` grows per sender | GRP-24 |
  | Campsite | src/Units/Campsite.wowlua:504 (listener 581) | `FIRE\t1\t<map>\t<x>\t<y>` | any | anyone but you | version; map as above; x, y in 0..1; 10 per sender per minute; list capped at 100; fires go out after 10 min; `showShared` setting | up to 10 false fires a minute per sender name on the map; keeps any fire alive; `taken` grows per sender | GRP-25 |

  Not receivers: `foreverlfg` (used through `SuuUI.LFG`, `src/Core/API.wowlua:90`)
  listens to `CHAT_MSG_CHANNEL`, `CHAT_MSG_SAY`, `CHAT_MSG_YELL` and
  `CHAT_MSG_WHISPER_INFORM` only and has no addon message code; Campsite's, LootRolls',
  QuestAnnounce's and MouseBindings' other code, Chat and Notifications do not listen
  to `CHAT_MSG_ADDON`. The stdlib's `wowlua:comm` is not used anywhere (it has its own
  wire format with chunking, so switching would break the protocol with older
  versions).

  The same small things are written four to six times with small differences: "is
  this sender me" (`isOwnSender` in Marks 177, `fromMe` in Convergences 237 and
  Campsite 222, `Ambiguate(…, "short")` compares in Readiness 309 and Timeline 898,
  `key()` compare in RaidPlanner 1778); the group channel choice (Convergences 207,
  Campsite 192, Readiness 84, Timeline 816, Marks `GroupChannel`); map and coordinate
  checks (Convergences 595-603 and Campsite 513-521 are the same lines; Marks has
  half of them); per-sender limits (two different shapes, both never pruned).
- why it matters: the two modules written last (Convergences, Campsite) have most of
  the checks, the four older ones have nearly none, and every new protocol has to
  remember all of it again. All six also draw on one send budget (the client
  throttles addon messages per prefix), so one module's replies starve the others.
- fix: one receiver in Core, `src/Core/Comm.wowlua`, exported through
  `src/Core/API.wowlua` as `SuuUI.Comm` and on the module class
  (`src/Core/Modules.wowlua`) as `M:OnAddonMessage(verb, opts, handler)` and
  `M:SendAddonMessage(verb, payload, where)`, so listeners go away with the module
  like `OnGameEvent`. Core because it needs the module owner and the event bus, and
  because plugins should get the same checks; document it in `Docs/API.md`.
  - One `RegisterAddonMessagePrefix("SuuUI")` and one `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` listener. It
    drops anything that is not the prefix, not a readable string (text and sender,
    `secret.readable`), longer than 255, or from the player (one `isOwnSender` that
    knows "Name", "Name-Realm" and Forever's "Name Surname"). It dispatches on the
    text up to the first tab (`PULL`, `MARK`, `RPSPEC`, `RPSPECQ`, `RDY`, `RDYQ`,
    `CONV`, `FIRE`): the wire formats stay as they are.
  - `opts.channels`: the set the verb accepts; default the group channels (`PARTY`,
    `RAID`, `INSTANCE_CHAT`); `GUILD` only where asked (CONV, FIRE); `WHISPER` and
    `CHANNEL` never unless a verb names them. The server delivers PARTY, RAID,
    INSTANCE_CHAT and GUILD messages only from members, so the channel is the
    membership check and needs no roster lookup.
  - `opts.rank = "assist" | "lead"`: the sender must lead or assist the group (PULL).
    This needs the sender matched to a unit: walk the roster comparing
    `SuuUI.FullName(unit)` as Readiness's `roster()` does (probe first how senders
    are named for members of other realms on Forever).
  - `opts.perMinute` and `opts.perSession`: a count per sender and verb, kept in one
    table that is emptied of senders no longer seen (older than a minute for the
    minute counts; on GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE for the rest) and capped in size (drop
    all when over, say, 500 senders).
  - `opts.replyEvery`: for question verbs (`RPSPECQ`, `RDYQ`), the handler runs at
    most once per that many seconds whoever asks.
  - Field readers for handlers, each returning nil on bad input: `Comm.int(s, lo, hi)`,
    `Comm.unit(s)` (0..1), `Comm.map(s)` (integer, 1..99999, known to
    `C_Map.GetMapInfo`), `Comm.name(s, maxLen)` (tabs, newlines and `|` to spaces,
    cut).
  - Sending through it too: one place for the group channel choice, the combat and
    chat-restriction checks (`Readiness:Send` and `RaidPlanner:Send` have them, the
    others do not), and a small queue so the six protocols share the budget in order.
  Tests: `tests/unit/Core/Comm.test.wowlua` (channel set, own sender, rank, limits,
  reply floor, each field reader), and each module's test file for its verb.

- status: partly fixed (the UI helpers now come through the public API, a5082e2d, and Windows is split into parts, bcd11307; the guild, social and group finder skins still live in Windows, it still reaches Guild, WorldMap and FlightMap by field and method name, and Social and RaidPlanner keep two raid roster readers)
- severity: medium

  src/Units/Windows/WorldMap.wowlua:453, 516-527 (QueueLayout, PlaceSide, UpdateBar by name),

  src/Units/RaidPlanner/Fill.wowlua:119 (readRoster)
- known: no
- what:
  1. Windows holds the skin of ten Blizzard windows (`SkinSpells` 863, `SkinLegacy`
     940, `SkinProfessions` 999, `SkinFriends` 1023, `SkinSocial` 1080,
     `SkinCommunities` 1185, `SkinGroupFinder` 1298, `SkinWorldMap` 1756,
     `SkinTrainer` 2268, `SkinCollections` 2438). The world map and quest log alone
     are lines 185-420 and 1432-2260, more than 1,000 lines: title, the secure way
     up, quest list rows, quest details layout and money, coordinates line, enlarging
     by scale.
  2. It reaches into other modules by ID and by field or method name:
     `field(guild(), "ownPage")` and `tryMethod(guild(), "ShowOwn", key)` (Guild's
     internals); it builds the Guild module's Log and Settings tabs itself (1258-1262);
     `SuuUI.GetModule("legacy")` (961); `SuuUI.GetModule("trainer")` (2274);
     `SuuUI.GetModule("worldmap"):Get("enlargedSize")` (2104) while the sibling
     setting `mapEnlarged` lives in Windows; new in 0.17.0:
     `tryMethod(wm, "QueueLayout")` and `tryMethod(fm, "QueueLayout")`,
     `"PlaceSide"`, `"UpdateBar"` on the WorldMap and FlightMap modules (2168-2178),
     calls by string that the checker cannot follow when those methods are renamed.
  3. Value imports of UI internals in `src/Units`: `import chromeOf from
     "/UI/WindowSkin"`, `import markOwn, leave, reskinPart from "/UI/Reskin"`,
     `import moneyText from "/UI/Inventory"` (Windows 21-25; the last two names are
     new), and `chromeOf`, `markOwn`, `isOwn` in Guild 16-17. None of `chromeOf`,
     `markOwn`, `isOwn`, `leave`, `reskinPart`, `moneyText` is exported in

     `Social:RaidMembers` (GRP-4).
- why it matters: a change to the guild window touches Guild, Windows and
  UI/WindowSkin; a change to FlightMap's layout methods silently stops the enlarged
  map from laying out the flight pins; a plugin cannot build what Guild or Windows
  build (the functions are not exported).
- fix: split along the windows: each window's skin next to its owner
  (`SkinCommunities` and the Log/Settings tabs into Guild, `SkinGroupFinder` into
  GroupFinder, `SkinSocial`/`SkinFriends` into Social, the world map and quest log
  block into `src/Units/WorldMap/`, the trainer skin into Trainer as its "off"
  fallback, collections into Collections), leaving Windows with spells, Legacy and
  professions. Replace the calls by name with an event the map modules listen to
  (`self:Emit("SUUUI_WORLDMAP_SCALED", k)`) and give Guild's own pages a service
  (`ShowOwn`, `OwnPage`). Export `UI.WindowChrome(frame)`, `UI.MarkOwn`, `UI.Leave`,
  `UI.ReskinPart`, `UI.MoneyText` in `src/Core/API.wowlua` and `Docs/API.md`. Tests
  move with the code (`tests/unit/Units/Windows.test.wowlua` → the owners' files).

#### GRP-7: Two CVars are changed for good and never put back
- status: fixed in db302207 (both CVars go through M:SetCVar with seedDefault: the player's value is remembered per character and given back when the module turns off, also at the next login for a reloadToToggle module)
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Guild.wowlua:1813-1817 (`communitiesShowOffline` = 1 on every enable); src/Units/Windows.wowlua:2232-2236 (`miniWorldMap` = 1)
- known: no
- what: `try(field(C_CVar, "SetCVar") or field(_G, "SetCVar"), "communitiesShowOffline", "1")`
  runs in Guild's `OnEnable`; `if not GetCVarBool("miniWorldMap") then
  SetCVar("miniWorldMap", 1) …` runs when the world map is skinned. The client saves
  both. Guild and Windows are `reloadToToggle` (Guild 240, Windows 858), so
  `OnDisable` never runs in a session and nothing restores them; neither module
  remembers the old value.
- why it matters: a player who turns the Guild module off (or removes SuuUI) keeps
  offline members shown in Blizzard's communities list, and one who used the game's
  fullscreen map keeps the small one. `communitiesShowOffline` is also rewritten at
  every login even if the player unticked it in Blizzard's own list.
- fix: remember the first-seen value in the module's saved data before writing, and
  restore it at the next load when the module is off (a small "CVars a module owns"
  helper in Core would serve every module). Tests:
  `tests/unit/Units/Guild.test.wowlua`, `tests/unit/Units/Windows.test.wowlua`.

#### GRP-8: Group Finder notes have no overall rate limit, and `noted` grows for the session
- status: open
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: likely
- where: src/Units/GroupFinder.wowlua:1322-1345 (Note), 1357-1386 (OnMatch), 340 (noted)
- known: no
- what: every post in a public channel that foreverlfg parses and that matches the
  player's interest raises a note, and plays a chime where the kind's `sound` is on
  (`UI.TrackerSound("chime")`, 1294-1296). The only limit is per poster:
  `self.noted[e.key]` within `AGAIN`. `noted` is keyed by the entry's key and is never
  pruned. Held notes are capped at 5 (1285); shown ones are not.
- why it matters: the input is public chat, written by strangers. Many different
  posters with the same kind of line (a busy channel, or one account cycling
  characters) give one toast and one chime each, back to back; `noted` collects
  every matching poster of a long session.
- fix: a global budget in `Note` (for example at most 3 match notes per 30 s, the

  `tests/unit/Units/GroupFinder.test.wowlua` (ten posters in a second give three
  notes).

#### GRP-24: Convergences: shared spots are accepted from anyone (whispers too), per sender name, account-wide
- status: fixed in db302207 (spots only from the group's channels and the guild, rate-limited per sender, a shared spot never pushes out one you found or confirmed, one notice per sender's burst)
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Convergences.wowlua:586-631 (OnMessage), 69-70, 145-160 (makeRoom), 365-366 (`taken`)
- known: no
- what: the payload is checked well (see the table in GRP-26), but the channel
  argument is never read and the sender only has to be someone else. The section's
  header says "Sharing: your group and your guild" (204). The limit is
  `MAX_PER_SENDER = 30` per sender name per session, with no limit over time and none
  over all senders; `self.taken` is never emptied. An accepted spot is saved for the
  account and, while the feature shows, raises a toast "Convergence of Elements
  shared … Shared by <name>, saved for all your characters". When the list is full
  (`MAX_SPOTS = 200`) and no unconfirmed shared spot is left, `makeRoom` drops the
  oldest spot that is not seed data, which can be one the player found.
- why it matters: a stranger can whisper 30 false spots per character name (more with
  more characters, or after the victim's reload), each a saved pin on the world map
  that sends the player to an empty place, and 30 toasts at once.
- fix: accept only `PARTY`, `RAID`, `INSTANCE_CHAT`, `GUILD`; at most 5 per sender
  per minute besides the session count; never drop a spot the player found or
  confirmed for a shared one; one toast for a burst ("3 spots shared by …"). Through
  the shared receiver of GRP-26. Test: `tests/unit/Units/Convergences.test.wowlua`.

#### GRP-25: Campsite: shared fires are accepted from anyone (whispers too) and refresh any known fire
- status: fixed in db302207 (fires only from the group's channels and the guild, ten a minute per sender through Core/Comm's swept rate, and a shared report no longer refreshes a fire you found)
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Campsite.wowlua:504-535 (OnMessage), 167-186 (addFire), 313-314 (`taken`)
- known: no
- what: the payload is checked well, the channel is not (`_channel`), and the sender
  only has to be someone else; the header says "to your group and guild". The limit
  is 10 per sender name per minute; `self.taken` keeps one entry per sender for the
  session. `addFire` treats a fire within 1% of the map as the same one and sets
  `f.seen = time()` whoever reports it, also for a fire the player found.
- why it matters: a stranger can keep 10 false fires a minute on the player's map
  (they go out after 10 minutes, so about 100 at a time, the list's cap, which then
  pushes out real ones), and can keep a fire that has gone out on the map for as long
  as they repeat it. Low: nothing outlives 10 minutes after they stop.
- fix: accept only `PARTY`, `RAID`, `INSTANCE_CHAT`, `GUILD`; a shared report must
  not refresh `seen` of a fire the player found (`f.by == nil`); prune `taken`.
  Through the shared receiver of GRP-26. Test:
  `tests/unit/Units/Campsite.test.wowlua`.

#### GRP-10: RaidPlanner: renders and inspect retries are not coalesced
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/RaidPlanner.wowlua:500-518 (GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE: an after(1) per event),
  src/Units/RaidPlanner/Specs.wowlua:218-279 (inspectNext; 229-236 the unguarded 5 s retry while InspectFrame
  shows, 244-246 Render)
- known: no
- what: with the planner open, every GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE starts its own
  `after(1, … self:AskSpecs(); self:InspectNext())`. When nobody can be inspected,
  `InspectNext` ends in `self:Render()` (1665), a full view build. A burst of ten
  roster events gives ten full renders a second later, besides the coalesced
  `RefillSoon`. While the game's `InspectFrame` is shown, each `InspectNext` call
  re-arms itself every 5 s with no guard (1645-1653), so every caller starts another
  chain until that frame closes. `inspectFailed` is never pruned (session only).
- why it matters: a hitch when a raid forms or reshuffles with the planner open; a
  growing number of 5 s timers while the player inspects someone.
- fix: one queued flag for the "ask and inspect" follow-up (as `refillQueued`), one
  `waitingForInspectFrame` flag for the 5 s retry (as `retryQueued` at 1667), and let
  `InspectNext` call `Render` only when `inspectRound` actually changed.

#### GRP-11: Arrange groups runs delayed moves by raid index without checking them again
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/RaidPlanner/Arrange.wowlua:151-162 (runMoves: the delayed SetRaidSubgroup/SwapRaidSubgroup
  by raid index)
- known: no
- what: the plan is a list of raid indices; each move runs from its own timer
  (`after((i - 1) * 0.1, …)`), up to about 4 s after planning for 40 moves. The timer
  checks only `InCombatLockdown()` before `SetRaidSubgroup(p.a, p.g)` or
  `SwapRaidSubgroup(p.a, p.b)`: not that the module is still on, that you still lead,
  or that index `p.a` is still the same player.
- why it matters: when someone leaves the raid during those seconds the indices
  shift and the remaining moves act on the wrong players. Turning the module off
  mid-arrange still moves people.
- fix: keep the member's name in the move and resolve the index when the timer fires
  (compare `GetRaidRosterInfo(p.a)`'s name, out of combat); stop when
  `not self:IsEnabled()` or the roster count changed. Test:
  `tests/unit/Units/RaidPlanner.test.wowlua` (a member leaves between plan and move).

#### GRP-12: Guild reads the whole roster for the Info page on every roster and group event
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- where: src/Units/Guild.wowlua:250-291 (Members), 1157-1176 (RenderInfo), 1868, 1880-1910 (events)
- known: no
- what: `RenderInfo` calls `self:Members()` only to count members per rank. `Members`
  makes one `GetGuildRosterInfo` call per member, builds a 16-field table for each
  and, for every offline member, calls `lastOnline(i)`. `RenderInfo` runs uncoalesced
  on GUILD_ROSTER_UPDATE, PLAYER_GUILD_UPDATE, GUILD_RANKS_UPDATE,
  GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE (unrelated to it), GUILD_MOTD and PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED, while
  the roster's own render is coalesced (`QueueRender`).
- why it matters: in a guild of several hundred, each event costs hundreds of API
  calls, tables and strings while the Info page is open.
- fix: count ranks in a small loop of its own (rank index only), coalesce
  `RenderInfo` like `QueueRender`, drop GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE for the Info page, and
  fill `lastOnline` only for the rows shown.

#### GRP-13: Guild's SkinTextEdit walks all of `_G` when the edit dialog has no known name

#### GRP-14: World map status line works 20 times a second and reads the player's position unguarded
- status: open
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the secret part needs in-game probe
- where: src/Units/Windows/WorldMap.wowlua:396-433 (the status line's OnUpdate; 414-419 the unguarded
  pos:GetXY())
- known: no

  runs at most once a frame (1441-1455) and reskins the whole log once, then only new
  rows (1467-1489).
- what remains: while the map is open the status line's OnUpdate, every 0.05 s,
  calls `C_Map.GetPlayerMapPosition` (a new position object each call) when the
  cursor is off the map, formats a string, measures it (`UI.MeasureText`), sets the
  text and `status:SetWidth(...)`, even when nothing changed. The cursor's
  coordinates go through `secret.asNumber` (2060); the player's do not:
  `x, y = pos:GetXY()` and then `if x and y and (x > 0 or y > 0)`.

  here, and moves it away again on the next frame.
- why it matters: a roster burst redraws the 40-member page many times; a probe that
  asks for Blizzard's own friends list never sees it.
- fix: a queued flag for `RenderRaid`; pass `when = function() return not
  (SuuUI.ProbeShowsBlizzardSocial and SuuUI.ProbeShowsBlizzardSocial()) end` to
  `keepAway`, and call the handle's `apply` when the probe ends.

None in full. Partly fixed, restated above as "changed":

- GRP-5: `f:SetMapID` and `f:OnFrameSizeChanged()` are gone
  (src/Units/Windows.wowlua:1809-1854 and 2184-2206 replace them).
- GRP-14: `RestyleQuestLog` is coalesced and incremental
  (src/Units/Windows.wowlua:1441-1489).

### Withdrawn

None.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **No receiver reads the channel argument of `CHAT_MSG_ADDON`.** That one check
  (group channels, plus GUILD where meant) removes the stranger-by-whisper case for
  all six protocols; rank, limits and reply floors come after it (GRP-26).
- **Question verbs amplify**: `RPSPECQ` and `RDYQ` make every client answer to the
  whole raid, and the askers are not coalesced either (Readiness asks on every roster
  event). All SuuUI protocols share one prefix and so one client throttle.
- **Per-sender tables are never pruned** (`taken` in Convergences and Campsite,
  `heard` in Readiness, `noted` in GroupFinder, `inspectFailed` in RaidPlanner, the
  saved `specs` in RaidPlanner).
- **Secure overlays must be let go at PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED** with the full release
  (`over.hide()`: hide and clear points), not a bare `Hide()`, and every overlay must
  be in that handler: Guild misses `inviteOver` (GRP-1) and keeps the anchors
  (GRP-2), Windows' new `upOver` has no handler at all (GRP-20). The holder with
  `[combat] hide; show` in Windows is a good second line and worth using for every
  overlay; a sweep for `secure.overlay(` across `src/` would find the rest.
- **Options passed at one call site and not at its twin**: `UI.CenterWindow` stores
  what the last call gave, so every caller has to pass `overCastBar` (GRP-19). An
  option that belongs to the window would be safer set once (at `UI.SkinWindow`).
- **Module methods called by string** (`tryMethod(module, "QueueLayout")`,
  `"PlaceSide"`, `"UpdateBar"`, `"ShowOwn"`) and module fields read with `field`
  cross module borders without the checker seeing them (GRP-6); events or services
  would.
- **`reloadToToggle` modules never run `OnDisable`**, so anything that outlives a
  reload (CVars, saved data) needs a restore at the next load (GRP-7).
- **Uncoalesced `after(x, render)` per event** next to a coalesced `QueueRender` in
  the same file (Social's raid page, RaidPlanner's follow-up, Guild's `RenderInfo`,
  Readiness's `Update` per message).
- **Raw comparison on values a sibling treats as possibly secret** (Social's roster
  against RaidPlanner's; Windows' `pos:GetXY()` against its own cursor read).

### Summary

- **CI now runs the suite** on every pull request and push to `main`, and a tag's `wowlua publish` runs it before uploading; the compiler version is pinned. That removes the worst part of the first pass's top finding. What is still not automated: the coverage minimums (neither `wowlua test` in CI nor the test run inside `publish` passes `--coverage`), the identity scan, a publish dry-run, and anything from `tests/perf`.
- **The perf scenarios are real and well built** (23 scenarios, per-frame Lua instruction counts and allocated bytes attributed to SuuUI, deterministic by design, a committed baseline, a tool that names the worst frame and its events). They measure exactly the kinds of cost reviewers look for. But **nothing enforces them**: there is no threshold, the comparison only prints "WORSE", the snapshots are always rewritten, they are outside `wowlua test` and outside CI, and the baseline is three compiler versions and 22 source commits old.
- The perf scenarios are also the only place where a 40-player raid, a roster change in a fight, more nameplates than the pool and a hunter's pet fight are played with the whole addon live, and **none of them checks for errors or refused protected calls**.
- **The module lifecycle is still not tested**: `tests/smoke` is unchanged, 39 modules only toggle after a reload, 28 test files call `OnDisable()` directly, and 22 module test files have no disable test, among them the new `MouseBindings` (secure key overrides and click attributes on unit frames).
- **Old saved data**: two fixtures of pre-migration data exist (`cooldowns-migrations.json`, new `lootrolls-off.json`), so the first pass's "no migration ever runs on old data" was too strong; 13 of the 22 migrations still have no such fixture, and three migration unit tests still cannot fail.
- The new unit tests that were read (`Core/Ahead`, `Core/Data`, `Core/AuraFilters`, `Units/MouseBindings`, `Units/QuestAnnounce`, `Units/RankUpgrade`) are behaviour tests of good quality, several end to end through the emulator's own state. `Units/AutoQuests` and `Units/LootRolls` are driven mostly through faked globals.
- `Docs/Testing.md` and `Docs/HANDOFF-tests.md` have not changed and mention neither CI's test run nor `tests/perf`.

### Findings

#### TEST-2: The smoke "every module off and on" does nothing for 39 modules, checks only for errors, and only one module is ever tested as off at login
- severity: high
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed (tests/helpers' cycle() checks what a live-toggling module leaves behind and is used in 22 module tests, and Nameplates and MouseBindings now log in turned off; the smoke cycle still checks only for errors and no reloadToToggle module is turned off and reloaded)
- where: tests/smoke/modules.test.wowlua:8-25; src/Core/Modules.wowlua:859-862, 1100 (reloadToToggle);
  tests/smoke/login.test.wowlua:13-23; tests/compat/legacy.test.wowlua:58 (the only `mock.reloadUI`)
- known: no
- what: `tests/smoke/modules.test.wowlua` is unchanged: for every enabled module it runs `mock.slash("/suu disable " .. m.id)`, `mock.slash("/suu enable " .. m.id)`, two frames, and compares `#errorsSoFar()`. For a module with `reloadToToggle = true` the registry only notes the wish (`ownOf(m).pendingReload = …; return` at Modules.wowlua:698-703) and the command prints "turns off after a /reload" (920-921); nothing is torn down. 39 files under `src/Units` set that flag (ActionBars, AuctionHouse, Auras, Bags, CastBars, CharacterWindow, Chat, Collections, GameMenu, Guild, Loot, LootRolls, Mail, Minimap, Nameplates, Notifications, ObjectiveTracker, PartyFrames, RaidFrames, Talents, Tooltips, UnitFrames, Windows, …). For the modules that toggle live the only assertion is "no new error": nothing checks that listeners, timers, hooks, shown frames, CVars or hidden Blizzard frames are gone, or that they are not doubled after the re-enable. `mock.reloadUI` is used once in the suite (`tests/compat/legacy.test.wowlua:58`, for a setting). One test now logs in with a module off: `tests/compat/lootRollsOff.test.wowlua` (through the `loot/rolls` migration) asserts `lootrolls` is disabled and `GroupLootContainer` keeps alpha 1. No other profile or test starts SuuUI with any module's `enabled` saved as false, which for the 39 is the only way they are ever off.
- why it matters: The project's central rule (every feature can be turned off and then leaves nothing behind) has no test that could fail for 38 of the 39 reload-only modules, and only an error check for the rest. A module that still hides Blizzard's frame when off, leaves a `hooksecurefunc` hook acting, or breaks another module that reads its service passes the whole suite; the players who turn a module off are the ones who meet it.
- fix: (1) In `tests/smoke/modules.test.wowlua`, for each module that toggles live, record before the cycle and compare after it: `events.bus:count(module)` (`src/Core/Events.wowlua:197`) must be 0 while off and equal to the first count after on; add the same for settings watchers, commands, settings sections, movers (`editMode.movers()`) and services (add `count(owner)` where missing). (2) Add `tests/compat/modulesOff.test.wowlua` in the shape of `lootRollsOff.test.wowlua`: profiles `tests/profiles/off-<batch>.json` with `"<id>": { "enabled": false }` for about ten modules each (four or five files cover all 39 reload-only modules plus the rest), asserting per module `IsEnabled() == false`, Blizzard's counterpart frame shown and usable (press its binding as `tests/smoke/blizzard.test.wowlua` does), every other module not `errored`, and `expectNoErrors()`. (3) One test that disables a `reloadToToggle` module with `/suu disable`, calls `mock.reloadUI()` and asserts the same after the reload.

#### TEST-3: Unit tests turn modules off by calling `OnDisable()` directly; what the registry releases and the re-enable are not tested, and 22 module test files have no disable test
- severity: high
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed (cycle() in tests/helpers goes through the registry and compares holdings, used in 22 module test files; 17 files still call OnDisable directly and 16 of the 22 named module files still have no disable test)
- where: tests/unit/Units/Nameplates.test.wowlua:952, LootRolls.test.wowlua:707,
  Notifications.test.wowlua:188, Bags.test.wowlua:383, Loot.test.wowlua:227 (17 direct `OnDisable` calls in 17
  files); no disable in tests/unit/Units/ CharacterWindow, DeathRecap, Guild, Legacy, MicroBags, Minimap,
  Professions, ProfessionsPreload, Social, Spellbook, SpellbookBindings, SpellbookFirstOpen, Talents,
  TalentsTab, Tooltips, Windows
- known: no
- what: 29 calls in 28 files run the module's own method (`M:OnDisable()`, `assert(M.OnDisable)(M)`, `(M :: AnyModule):OnDisable()`) instead of going through the registry (`settings.set(id, "enabled", false)`, `/suu disable`). The registry's part (`releaseAll`, `src/Core/Modules.wowlua:616`: the module's events, commands, sections, movers, extensions) therefore never runs for those modules in a unit test, and the module's state stays Enabled with all its listeners live while its frames are torn down. `LootRolls.test.wowlua:676-688` shows the cost: to call `M:OnEnable()` again the test has to unregister the settings section, the mover and the commands by hand (`registry.unregister(M)`, `editMode.unregister(M)`, `unregisterCommands(M)`), which is the registry's job. What the "stopped" tests assert is narrow: `Nameplates` asserts Blizzard's plate alpha and an empty `byUnit` (949-951) but not the CVars it set (asserted as set at 814-819: `nameplateMinAlpha`, `nameplateShowEnemies`); `UnitFrames` asserts SuuUI's frame hidden and the anchor withdrawn (834-838) but not that `PlayerFrame` is back (asserted hidden at 104); `LootRolls` asserts the tray hidden (686) but not `GroupLootContainer`'s alpha, which another test asserts as 0 while on (693). 16 files do go through the registry (`Alerts`, `AuraFilters`, `BuffIndicators`, `Campsite`, `ChatCommands`, `Convergences`, `CooldownManager`, `Defensives`, `Durability`, `FlightMap`, `Marks`, `MicroMenu`, `Notifications`, `Readiness`, `Welcome`, `WorldMap`); `tests/unit/Units/AuraFilters.test.wowlua:310-315` is the model (off: nothing filtered; on: the lists again). 22 of the 66 module test files have no disable of any kind: `ActionBars`, `AutoQuests`, `CharacterWindow`, `Chat`, `DeathRecap`, `Guild`, `Legacy`, `MicroBags`, `Minimap`, `MouseBindings`, `Professions`, `QuestAnnounce`, `Social`, `Spellbook`, `Talents`, `Tooltips`, `Windows`, the second files `ProfessionsPreload`, `SpellbookBindings`, `SpellbookFirstOpen`, `TalentsTab`, and `RankUpgrade` (a class, not a module). `MouseBindings` is new and toggles live: it sets override bindings (`CLICK SuuUIMouseBindingsWorld:mb1`) and `shift-type1`-style attributes on every unit frame, and its `OnDisable` is `self:Apply()`; no test asserts that turning it off removes either.
- why it matters: Leaks on disable/enable cycles (listeners registered twice, a timer outliving the module, a Blizzard frame left hidden, a CVar left changed, a key still overridden) are the bugs the module reviewers were asked to find by reading; these tests cannot catch any of them, and a change to a module's teardown is unprotected.
- fix: Add to `tests/helpers.wowlua` a helper `cycle(id, check)`: record `events.bus:count(m)`, the module's commands, sections and movers; turn the module off through `settings.set(id, "enabled", false)` (for `reloadToToggle` modules through a test-only entry that runs the registry's disable path, or cover them by the reload test of TEST-2); assert state Disabled and all counts 0; run the module's own `check` (Blizzard frames back, CVars back, own frames hidden, bindings gone); turn it on and assert the counts equal the first ones; `expectNoErrors()`. Replace each `-- (last: the module off)` test with it and add it to the 21 module files without one. For `MouseBindings` the check is: after off, `GetBindingAction("SHIFT-F", true)` over a moused-over unit is not `CLICK SuuUIMouseBindings…` and `SuuUIPlayerFrame:GetAttribute("shift-type1")` is nil; after on, both are back (the helpers `ours()` and the cases at MouseBindings.test.wowlua:277-328 already exist).

  (`compare`), 434-449 (`run`: `-u`); wowlua.json:25-27; .github/workflows/ci.yml:25-30
- known: no
- what: The first pass's "no performance or allocation test exists" no longer holds. `tests/perf` has 23 scenarios that play gameplay in the emulated client frame by frame (60 frames a second, seeded choices): a 40-player raid with four aura changes a frame, damage, heals, a wipe and a mass resurrect (`raid`), pulls of 12 and 30 mobs with plates, threat and target switches (`pull`), a five-player boss (`party`), a launch crowd with 60 to 160 plates (`crowd`), 10,800 players seen with memory recorded at three points (`churn`), twelve chat lines a second (`chat`), `BAG_UPDATE` and `BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` storms (`loot`, `bagcooldown`), a fight's end with a roster change (`combatend`), windows opened, typing a command, themes, travel, a pet fight, guild and Battle.net churn, idle. `tools/perf.py` runs them with `wowlua test --features perf -u --profile-out …` and reads wowlua's per-frame profile: per phase the **Lua instructions SuuUI ran per frame** (mean, 95th percentile, worst frame, with the events and entry points behind the worst frame), the **bytes SuuUI allocated per frame**, all UI instructions per frame, and memory after a full collection. Instruction and byte counts are exact and the same on every machine (README.md:56-58); host milliseconds are recorded but never compared. `top` breaks a phase or one event down by function. That is the right instrument for "work per frame, per `UNIT_AURA`, per roster event, per chat line".
  What is missing is any enforcement:
  1. **No threshold anywhere.** The scenario files contain no `expect` except `util.record`'s `toMatchSnapshot` (util.wowlua:81), and the run always passes `-u` (perf.py:424), which rewrites the snapshot, so it cannot fail. `compare` prints `WORSE` past 2 % (perf.py:340-343) and returns; `run` exits non-zero only when `wowlua test` itself fails (427-428). Memory rows get no mark at all (344-348). A change that doubles the instructions per frame of `raid` exits 0.
  2. **Not in `wowlua test` and not in CI.** Every test is behind `@if(features.perf)`; the `perf` feature is off by default (wowlua.json:25-27); `ci.yml` runs `wowlua test --locked` without `--features perf` and never calls `tools/perf.py`. The scenarios run only when someone remembers.
  3. **The baseline is stale.** `baseline.json` was written 2026-11-13 with wowlua 0.13.12 at commit `1c6dd456`. Since then 29 commits (22 touching `src`, four releases, the modules LootRolls and QuestAnnounce among them) landed and the project moved to wowlua ^0.13.15, without a new baseline, although README.md:102-103 says to re-baseline "after a wowlua update, on its own commit". `compare` only prints a note when the versions differ (perf.py:323-324). The next comparison mixes SuuUI's changes with the emulator's.
  4. **No per-event budget.** The numbers are per frame of a mixed scenario. Nothing states "one `UNIT_AURA` on a raid member costs at most N instructions" or "a second identical `BAG_UPDATE` allocates nothing", so a regression in one handler can hide inside a scenario's mean.
  5. **Not covered by a scenario:** the combat log as such (damage and heals fire it only as a side effect of `damage`/`heal`/`swing`), action-bar cooldown and usability storms in a fight (`zone` fires `ACTIONBAR_UPDATE_USABLE` out of combat only), the damage meter and threat meter windows open during a fight, the auction house and mail lists, the settings window (opened but never scrolled or searched), edit mode, a profile switch, tooltips over bag items, a 25- or 40-player raid with roster changes during the fight (`combatend` has 20 players and two changes), and the first frames after login (every scenario starts after `perf.settle(perf.AFTER_LOGIN)`, so login cost itself is never a measured phase; `idle` records only memory before and after).
- why it matters: Performance was one of the four subjects of this review, and the project now has the data to guard it but no guard. The baseline already shows frames that a threshold would hold: `themes` "pinkcat: picked" 3,540,662 instructions and 3,957 KB of garbage in one frame; `combatend` 658,208 instructions in its worst frame (245,414 in one `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` handler); `windows` first open 404,067; `mapglance` 141,229; `typing` 104,771 worst and 35 KB a frame on average; `bagcooldown` 30,158 instructions per `BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN`. Without a gate these can only get worse unnoticed, and each later perf fix has no proof that it stays fixed.
- fix: (1) Give `tools/perf.py compare` a `--fail-over <percent>` option that exits 1 when any compared metric of any phase is worse by more than that (start with 10 % for `suu_instr_mean`, `suu_instr_max`, `suu_kb_mean`, and for the `addon memory` records), and a check that fails when the baseline's `wowlua` differs from the running one. (2) Add a CI job (pull requests and pushes to `main`, separate from the build job so it cannot block a release by flakiness; the counts are deterministic, so it should not flake): `python3 -I tools/perf.py run` then `compare --fail-over 10`, and upload `dist/perf/results.json` as an artifact. Keep "update the baseline in the same commit as an accepted change" (README.md:94-100) as the way to pass it. (3) Re-baseline now on wowlua 0.13.15, on its own commit. (4) Add absolute ceilings for the frames that matter most, in `tools/perf.py` as a small table (scenario, phase, metric, maximum): for example `raid / boss fight` p95 instructions, `pull / big pull` worst frame, `chat / chat spam` KB per frame, `churn` addon memory growth between 3,600 and 10,800 players (baseline: 225,441 to 226,202 KB, about 0.1 KB per player seen; fail above, say, 2 MB). (5) Add scenarios for the gaps listed under 5, first a `raidroster` scenario (40 players, a join or leave every two seconds in a fight, damage meter open) and a `login` scenario whose measured phase is the first 300 frames.

#### TEST-18: The perf scenarios play the heaviest and most lockdown-prone situations of the whole suite and never check for errors or refused protected calls
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed in d8fa5ced (every scenario file ends with `setup: no errors`, `perf.expectClean()` in tests/perf/util.wowlua: no error caught by Fault or the game and no refused protected call; left: nothing checks between the combat phases of `raid`, `combatend`, `pull`, `party` and `crowd`, and the scenarios still run only by hand, not in CI)
- where: tests/perf/raid.test.wowlua:48-168; tests/perf/combatend.test.wowlua:70-108;
  tests/perf/pull.test.wowlua:150-158; tests/perf/crowd.test.wowlua:100-115;
  tests/perf/pet.test.wowlua:22-119; tests/perf/themes.test.wowlua:19-25 (all 23 scenario files)
- known: no
- what: None of the 23 scenario files imports `tests/helpers.wowlua` or calls `expectNoErrors()`, `errorsSoFar()` or `mock.refusals()` (script count: 23 of 23). SuuUI catches its own handler errors (`fault.call`), so a handler that throws in a scenario does not fail the test; it just stops early. Yet these files are the only tests in the repository that: form a 40-player raid with roles, eight subgroups, auras, incoming heals, a wipe and resurrects (`raid`); add and remove a raid member during combat and then end the fight (`combatend`, lines 92-106: `mock.group:add(late, { raid = true })` at frame 40 and `mock.group:remove(mates[3])` at frame 80, both after `enterCombat`); show 30 nameplates in combat, more than the pool holds ready (`pull` "big pull: thirty", "plates are built in combat"); show 160 plates at once (`crowd`); log in as a hunter and fight with a pet (`pet`); switch themes four times with a target and the character window open (`themes`). In the regular suite the largest raid is you and 24, and no test changes the roster in a fight. An error in one of those paths makes the scenario's numbers look *better* (less work was done), and a refused protected call in combat is exactly what these situations exist to provoke.
- why it matters: The scenarios already build the hard worlds that the first pass found missing from the smoke tests (40 players, roster change in combat, plates beyond the pool). Using them only for instruction counts leaves the cheapest available combat-lockdown and scale test unasserted, and it lets a broken handler pass as a performance gain.
- fix: In each scenario file add a last test named `setup: no errors` (a name starting with `setup` is not measured, tools/perf.py:210): `import expectNoErrors from "../helpers"`, then `expectNoErrors()` and `expect(#mock.refusals()).toBe(0)`. Do the same once after each combat phase of `raid`, `combatend`, `pull`, `party`, `crowd` (as extra `setup: …` tests between phases, so the profile's measured frames are unchanged). Then run them in CI as tests even where the perf comparison is not wanted: `wowlua test --features perf --locked tests/perf` (without `-u`; `tests/perf/__snapshots__` is git-ignored, so a fresh checkout writes the snapshots and passes). If the measured numbers move because of the added tests, re-baseline in the same commit.

#### TEST-1: CI runs the tests now, but not the coverage minimums, the identity scan, a publish dry-run or the perf scenarios
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: .github/workflows/ci.yml:23-30; wowlua.json:85-91; Docs/Testing.md:129-135
- known: no
- what: On the old commit the workflow only built. NEW's `ci.yml` builds (`wowlua build --release --locked`, line 23), then on pull requests and pushes to `main` runs `wowlua test --locked --message-format github` (25-26), and on a tag runs `wowlua publish` (27-28), which runs the tests itself before packaging and stops when one fails (comment at line 24; wowlua's publish step 3, `crates/wowlua-driver/src/publish/mod.rs`: "the tests failed; nothing was published"). So a failing test now blocks a merge check and a release. Still not automated:
  1. **Coverage minimums.** `wowlua.json` keeps `lines 98, branches 76.5, functions 97, conditions 72.5`, and wowlua checks them only in a run with `--coverage` and no filter (`crates/wowlua-cli/src/commands.rs`: `if args.coverage { … if let Some(s) = settings.as_ref().filter(|_| filters.is_empty())`). CI's `wowlua test` has no `--coverage`, and the test run inside `wowlua publish` is built with `coverage: false`. `src` grew by about 63,000 lines since the minimums were last measured; whether 0.17.0 still meets them is unknown to CI and was not measurable in this review.
  2. **Identity scan.** `tools/idscan.py` "runs before every commit" (CLAUDE.md) only by hand: there is no hook directory in the export and no CI step.
  3. **No `wowlua publish --dry-run`** on pull requests, so a packaging or changelog-section problem shows first on the tag.
  4. **No `wowlua check` step** of its own. The release build compiles the sources and `wowlua test` compiles the tests, so this is covered in effect for pull requests; on a tag the order is build, then publish (which tests), which is fine.
  5. **Perf scenarios** (TEST-12, TEST-18).
- why it matters: The minimums are "kept just under the current figures so a drop shows" (Docs/Testing.md:131-133); with nobody running `--coverage` a drop shows nowhere, and a new module without tests merges green. A real character or account name in a test or fixture reaches a public repository if the scan is forgotten once.
- fix: Change the test step to `wowlua test --coverage --locked --message-format github` (add `--reporter coverage-json` and upload it if a per-file report is wanted; see TEST-9). If the coverage run is too slow for every push, run it on pull requests only and keep the plain run on `main`. Add `wowlua publish --dry-run` to the pull-request path. For the identity scan: its name list comes from local recordings, so in CI run the parts that need no local data (GUID and player-link (`Hplayer`) patterns over the diff), and commit a hook (`.githooks/pre-commit` running `python3 -I tools/idscan.py .`, with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` in the setup notes).

In the raid power test assert the priest's and the warrior's buttons for each `power` value. #### TEST-13: The release path: the compiler version is pinned now, but the setup action is still `@main`, any `v*` tag on any commit publishes, and the write token covers pull-request runs
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6, 10-11, 13, 17-19, 29-35
- known: no
- what: Fixed since the old commit: the compiler is pinned, `with: { version: v0.13.15 }` (line 18, with the reason in the comment: "latest broke 0.10.0's publish"), and a tag's publish runs the tests first. Still as before:
  1. `uses: DomenikIrrgang/wowlua/.github/actions/setup-wowlua@main` (line 17): the action and the `scripts/install.sh` it runs come from the moving `main` branch of another repository. The pinned `version` input only chooses which release that script downloads. A change to the action or script takes effect in the next SuuUI release build without a change in SuuUI, and the binary it installs runs in the step that holds `CF_API_TOKEN`, `WAGO_API_TOKEN`, `WOWI_API_TOKEN` and a write token.
  2. `on.push.tags: ["v*"]` (5) matches a tag on any commit of any branch; nothing checks that the tagged commit is on `main`. `wowlua publish` stops when tag and `package.version` differ (E4319), which catches typos, not a correctly named tag on a feature branch or an old commit.
  3. `permissions: contents: write` (10-11) is set for the one job, so pull-request runs of branches in the repository and every push to `main` also run with a write token, although only the tag path needs it.
  4. No `concurrency` group: a deleted and re-pushed tag can run two publishes at once.
  5. `actions/checkout@v5` and `actions/cache@v4` are pinned by major tag, not by commit (low).
  Good as it is: secrets are passed only to the publish and Discord steps; the Discord step is `continue-on-error`; `wowlua.json` requires `^0.13.15`, matching the pin.
- why it matters: A release reaches players through CurseForge and Wago and cannot be recalled quietly. An unpinned third-party-repository script in the path that holds the upload tokens, and a tag filter that accepts any commit, are the two ways a build nobody reviewed gets published.
- fix: Pin the action to a tag or commit of the wowlua repository: `uses: DomenikIrrgang/wowlua/.github/actions/setup-wowlua@v0.13.15` (or the commit sha), bumped together with `version:` and `package.wowlua`. Split the workflow into two jobs: `verify` (pull requests, `main`, tags; `permissions: contents: read`; build and tests) and `publish` (tags only; `needs: verify`; `permissions: contents: write`; the secrets; `concurrency: { group: publish, cancel-in-progress: false }`). In `publish`, first step: fail unless `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main`. Narrow the tag filter to `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*`. Optionally a GitHub environment with a required reviewer for the publish job.

#### TEST-19: The garbage collector is stopped in every test file, perf scenarios included, as a workaround for wowlua 0.9.1
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- status: open

- known: partly: Docs/wowlua-0.9.1-report.md C40 records why the collector is stopped
- what: `tests/mocks/gc.wowlua` is still one statement, `collectgarbage("stop")`, with the comment "wowlua 0.9.1 workaround … Remove once wowlua is fixed"; the project now requires wowlua ^0.13.15. Mocks load before SuuUI in every test file, so no automatic collection runs in any unit, smoke, compat or perf run. The only collections are the explicit `collectgarbage("collect")` calls in the perf helpers (`memoryKB`, `addonKB`). Consequences: weak tables and anything that relies on collection behave differently from the game in every test; a full run holds all garbage of each file in memory; and the perf scenarios' per-frame numbers never include a collector step, while their memory records depend on the explicit full collection only. It could not be checked here whether the 0.9.1 crash ("stale handle" when building the coverage report) still exists in 0.13.15; "probe" here means one run, not an in-game probe.
- why it matters: Low by itself, but it is a standing difference between the test client and the game in the area (garbage, weak caches, pooled frames) that the perf work is about, kept for a bug that may be long fixed.
- fix: On wowlua 0.13.15 run `wowlua test --coverage` once with `tests/mocks/gc.wowlua` emptied. If it passes, delete the file and the note in `Docs/HANDOFF-tests.md`; if the crash is still there, report it to wowlua with the version and restrict the stop to coverage runs. Re-baseline the perf scenarios in the same commit if their numbers move.

### Fixed since the first pass

- None of the 17 findings is fully fixed. Parts that are fixed, restated inside the changed findings above:
  - TEST-1 (part): CI runs `wowlua test --locked` on pull requests and pushes to `main` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:25-26`) and a tag's `wowlua publish` runs the tests before uploading (line 24 and 27-28); commit `3f6d8761` "CI pins wowlua and runs the tests (unblocks 0.10.0) (#187)".
  - TEST-13 (part): the compiler version is pinned, `with: { version: v0.13.15 }` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:18`); commits `3f6d8761`, `1c6dd456`.
  - TEST-12 (part): performance scenarios exist (`tests/perf/`, `tools/perf.py`); commits `9c9afa61` (#110), `17d80d4d` (#112), `9423841e` (#153).
  - TEST-4 (part): `tests/compat/lootRollsOff.test.wowlua` with `tests/profiles/lootrolls-off.json` tests one migration on stored pre-migration data.

### Withdrawn

- No finding is withdrawn as a whole. Two first-pass statements were wrong and are corrected above:
  - TEST-4: "no migration ever runs on real old data". `tests/profiles/cooldowns-migrations.json` with `tests/unit/Units/CooldownManager/Migrations.test.wowlua` already ran the cooldown migrations on an old profile at the old commit. The finding is narrowed to the 13 migrations without such data and downgraded from high to medium.
  - TEST-4: "`legacy.json` carries `__migrated` entries for 12 migrations". It carries 18 (the file is unchanged since the old commit).

### Cross-cutting observations

- **The perf baseline is a ready-made list of hot spots for the other reviewers** (`tests/perf/baseline.json`, wowlua 0.13.12, commit `1c6dd456`; instructions are SuuUI's Lua instructions in one frame):
  - Picking a theme: 1.4 to 3.5 million instructions and up to 3,957 KB of garbage in one frame, entry `Core/Themes.wowlua:557`; memory grows by about 7 MB over four theme switches and does not come back on "suuui again" (418,166 KB to 425,344 KB).
  - A fight's end in a 20-player raid with two mouse bindings: worst frame 658,208 instructions, 245,414 of them in one `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` handler; 421 KB of garbage in that frame.
  - First open of the windows: worst frame 404,067 instructions (entry `Core/API.wowlua:546`) and 1,196 KB; second open still 189,003 (`PaperDollFrame:OnShow` hook 51,980).
  - Map glance: worst frame 141,229. Opening the bags: 129,862 (`Units/Bags.wowlua:2901`).
  - Typing a command: 13,830 instructions and 35 KB per frame on average over three seconds, worst 104,771.
  - `BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` with the bags open: 30,158 instructions per event.
  - Crowds: 21 to 39 KB of garbage per frame on average, worst frames 60,000 to 82,000 instructions in `NAME_PLATE_UNIT_ADDED`.
  - `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED` is the top entry of the worst frame in six scenarios (8,890 to 24,603 instructions).
  - Raid of 40: one `UNIT_HEALTH` dispatch accounts for 30,688 instructions in the worst frame of the boss fight.
  - Idle: 434 instructions per frame on average, worst 3,196 (`Units/Chat.wowlua:3720` OnUpdate 1,571, `Units/MicroMenu.wowlua:756` OnUpdate 1,165, `Units/Threat.wowlua:608` OnUpdate 1,249 while a target exists): three always-on `OnUpdate` scripts worth a look.
  - Churn (the leak check): addon memory 216,823 KB before, 225,441 KB after 3,600 players, 226,202 KB after 10,800: flat after warm-up, about 0.1 KB per player seen.
  These are emulator numbers at an older commit; they say where to look, not what the game costs.
- **A broken handler looks like a speed-up in a perf scenario** (TEST-18). Any perf comparison should be read together with an error check until the scenarios assert one.
- **Line coverage was reached partly by "touching" code** (TEST-8): runs of `M:Set(...)` at the end of a test, a final theme-change or preview call with nothing after it. When a reviewer finds a bug in a setting watcher, a theme handler or a preview path, the existing test for it probably ran the line without checking it.
- **Every module test asserts through `import internal M`**, and new tests also import other modules' internals (`tests/unit/Units/AuraFilters.test.wowlua` imports the internals of PartyFrames, RaidFrames, Auras and Nameplates). Any fix that reshapes a module's state breaks tests for reasons unrelated to behaviour; plan for that when estimating fixes in `src/Units`.
- **The registry-level guarantees are tested only on the registry's own fake modules** (`tests/unit/Core/Modules.test.wowlua`). That real modules use only owned registrations and nothing a disable cannot undo (`hooksecurefunc`, `frame:HookScript`, raw timers, CVar writes, override bindings, attributes on other modules' frames) is assumed, not tested (TEST-2, TEST-3). `MouseBindings` and `LootRolls` are the newest modules where this matters.
- **Emulator gaps shape what is tested.** Where `wowlua:mock` has no state (group loot rolls R24, combo points V31, a unit turning hostile V30, tapped units V49, power spent by casts V44, a pet trainer V41, auction house filters and buyouts V42/V48, `mock.click` ignoring what lies over a frame V47), the tests stub globals or skip the path. Those are the places where in-game probes are needed, and V47 in particular means a click test cannot catch an overlay that swallows clicks.
- **CI's cost.** On the old commit a full run took 3 minutes on about 9 busy cores; NEW has 201 regular test files against 185 and the hosted runner has 4 cores. Adding `--coverage` and a perf job (TEST-1, TEST-12) roughly doubles CI time; splitting them into separate jobs keeps the merge check short.
