### Summary

- **The data is now lazy, which removes most of the first pass's largest finding.** The six big tables (QuestStarts, MapPlaces, CollectionSources, RecipeSources, FlightPaths, MapOverlays: 7.7 MB built) are generated as lists of step functions and built on first use by the new `Core/Data` (DATA-1). What remains: the step code itself is resident from login (3.6 MB measured in Lua 5.4) until each table is first used, QuestStarts is built for nearly everyone by the first NPC tooltip, and nothing is released when the owning module turns off.
- **Per-class data and the three wasteful table shapes are unchanged** (DATA-2 to DATA-5): all nine classes' preset and trainer functions stay loaded (675 KB), `CollectionSources.item` has grown to 8,982 rows of which 2,659 are distinct.
- **The public API is still complete on paper and bypassed in practice** (API-1): 474 internal imports in `src/Units`, 123 of them run-time values, now including `/Core/Data`, `/Core/Ahead` and `/UI/Dress`, which have no public counterpart at all.
- **The three module/service bugs are unchanged** (API-2, API-4, API-5). API-4 occurs only with the "assign `M:OnEnable` after `RegisterModule`" style, which is the style `Docs/PluginGuide.md` and the LevelBadge example teach.
- **Docs and versions:** every `SuuUI.*` and `SuuUI.UI.*` export through API 0.46 is documented and every documented name exists. `Docs/API.md:3` still says 0.19.0. 25 patch releases shipped new features and 11 of them a new API version, against the project's own version rules (API-16).
- **Generators:** `Tokens.wowlua` matches its generator again (DATA-6 fixed), the data builds are unified on 70888, QuestStarts no longer sits at a Lua limit (DATA-13 fixed). New: 2,487 generated theme textures (46.8 MB) are committed and shipped (DATA-16).
- **Identity data in `tools/data` headers is still there**, and the identity scan now reads its name lists from a game folder the other tools have moved away from (DATA-8).
- **Build config follows the "Builds per site" rules.** CI now runs the test suite on every push and PR; the `readable` profile is still first built at tag time (DATA-10).

### Findings

#### API-1: every feature module imports Core and UI internals; "only the public API" does not hold
- severity: high
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code; mechanical scan, Appendix A3)
- status: fixed in a5082e2d (src/Units imports nothing of SuuUI's but /Core/API, the classes, service keys, helpers, BuildAhead, Data and Dress are exported, and tools/check_imports.py enforces it in CI; it passes at d74864f8)
- where: all 61 module files in `src/Units/*.wowlua` and their submodules; 474 import statements that are not `/Core/API`, `wowlua:*`, `/Data/*`, a sibling submodule of the same feature or a package: 351 `import type`, 123 run-time values. The stated rule: `src/Core/API.wowlua:2-6`, `CLAUDE.md:19`.
- known: no (the project's documents state the opposite as the rule)
- what: the value imports, by what forces them (file:line for each in Appendix A3.1):
  1. **The module base class**, 61 files: `import Module from "/Core/Modules"`, then a class extending it and `SuuUI.AddModule(X.new())` (61 files call `SuuUI.AddModule`; none calls `SuuUI.RegisterModule`). `SuuUI.Module` is exported (`src/Core/API.wowlua:129`) and nothing in `src/`, `Examples/` or `tests/` uses it.
  2. **Service keys**, 16 imports from `/Core/ServiceKeys` (`Alerts:26`, `AuctionHouse:34`, `Bags:40`, `Campsite:23`, `Collections:26`, `Convergences:32`, `FlightMap:48`, `Marks:18`, `MouseBindings:46`, `Notifications:27`, `Professions:20`, `RaidPlanner:30`, `Social:22`, `Spellbook:54`, `Talents:26`, `WorldMap:41`). The keys are not on `SuuUI`.
  3. **UI classes to subclass**, 16 imports: `Panel` (`BuffIndicators:22`, `Chat:36`, `CooldownManager:33`, `FlightMap:50`, `Talents:28`), `ItemSlot` (`Bags:42`, `Inspect:25`, `Macros:19`, `Mail:14`, `Merchant:16`), `UnitFrame` (`PartyFrames:36`, `RaidFrames:32`), `MapPin` (`FlightMap:52`, `WorldMap:45`), `ActionButton` (`ObjectiveTracker:34`). `SuuUI.UI.Panel` and the others are factory functions; the classes are only in the unstable `SuuUI.Raw.Mixins`.
  4. **Helpers that are not exported**: from `/UI/Draw` `inlineMark` (`ChatCommands:47`, `Inspect:16`, `Mail:11`, `Merchant:11`), `isColor`, `rgba`, `hex` (`Chat:31`, `Chat/Lines:12`) and the whole module (`Nameplates:43`); `moneyText` from `/UI/Inventory` (`Windows:25`); `chromeOf` from `/UI/WindowSkin` (`FlightMap:49`, `Guild:16`, `Windows:21`, `WorldMap:44`); `leave`, `markOwn`, `isOwn`, `openRoot`, `reskinPart` from `/UI/Reskin` (`CharacterWindow:40`, `Guild:17`, `Tooltips:34`, `Windows:23`); `gameUnits`, `curveAmount` from `/UI/UnitFrame` (`Nameplates:38`); `filterList` from `/UI/FilterMenu` (`Trainer:38`); all of `/UI/HealthFill` (`Nameplates:53`).
  5. **Whole subsystems with no public counterpart (new since 0.6):** `/Core/Ahead` (work built ahead after login: `Bags:58`, `ChatCommands:52`, `DamageMeter:20`, `Notifications:36`, `Spellbook:62`, `Threat:28`), `/Core/Data` (the lazy data tables: `Collections:43`, `Professions:35`, `WorldMap:62`; see API-17), `/UI/Dress` (theme art on frames: `Chat:25`, `Minimap:20`).
  6. **One feature importing another:** `src/Units/ActionBars.wowlua:51` imports `RankUpgrader` from `/Units/RankUpgrade` (and its type at `:52`).
  The 351 type-only imports reach 62 internal modules (`/Core/Modules` 42, `/UI/Text` 36, `/UI/Panel` 28, `/EditMode/EditMode` 25, `/UI/Controls` 25, …; Appendix A3.2).
  Related, not imports: modules reach other modules' internals through `SuuUI.GetModule` (23 calls in `src/Units`): `src/Units/DamageMeter.wowlua:654` reads `threat.PreviewView`, `src/Units/Chat.wowlua:2091` calls `palette`'s `TakesArrows` through `errors.tryMethod`, and the rest ask whether another module is on or read its settings, in three different ways (`:Get("enabled")`, `:IsEnabled()`, `:Setting(key)`).
  Nothing in `src/UI`, `src/Core`, `src/SettingsUI` or `src/EditMode` imports `src/Units`. The other direction is not clean: `src/UI/Legacy.wowlua:23` and `src/SettingsUI/Sections.wowlua:17` import `/Core/API`; `src/Core/Init.wowlua:11`, `src/Core/Modules.wowlua:46-47` and `src/Core/Themes.wowlua:76-77` import SettingsUI, EditMode and UI as values.
- why it matters: the project's claim (README, `Docs/API.md:3`, `Docs/PluginGuide.md:3`) is that a plugin can do anything a built-in module does. It cannot: write a class-based module, subclass `Panel`/`ItemSlot`/`UnitFrame`, use a typed service, build work ahead, prepare data over frames, or dress a frame. Any internal rename in UI breaks modules with no API version change, and the "exported but nil in game" check (Appendix A2) passes only because the calls that would fail go around the API. The count grows with every feature (415 at 0.6.0-beta.1, 474 now).
- fix: decide per group and write the decision into `Docs/wowlua-port-conventions.md`:
  1. make `class X extends SuuUI.Module<…>` work and switch the 61 modules (if wowlua cannot extend a member expression, export `Module` from `/Core/API` as a named export next to `SuuUI`); document `SuuUI.Module` and `SuuUI.AddModule` in `Docs/API.md`; re-export the `SettingsSection` type from `/Core/API`.
  2. put the keys on the API (`SuuUI.Services = { ALERTS = …, … }`) and import from `/Core/API` only (see API-3).
  3. publish the subclassable classes as stable API (`SuuUI.Classes.Panel`, `.ItemSlot`, `.UnitFrame`, `.MapPin`, `.ActionButton`), documented under the API version they arrive in.
  4. export the helpers (`UI.InlineMark`, `UI.IsColor`, `UI.Hex`, `UI.MoneyText`, `UI.WindowChrome(frame)`, `UI.ReskinLeave`, `UI.MarkOwn`, `UI.IsOwn`, `UI.CurveAmount`, `UI.GameUnits`, `UI.FilterList`) or move the code that needs them into `src/UI`.
  5. `SuuUI.Ahead.Schedule(key, step)`, the data handles of API-17, and `SuuUI.UI.Dress…` for the art.
  6. move `RankUpgrade` to `src/UI` or reach it through a service.
  7. type-only imports: bless them explicitly (the guide already tells plugins to `import type … from "suuui/UI/…"`) or re-export the types from `/Core/API`.
  8. replace `threat.PreviewView` and `TakesArrows` with services, and add one `SuuUI.ModuleEnabled(id)` (the state, not the setting) for the "is module X on" readers: `:Get("enabled")` is true for a module that is replaced, errored or waiting for a reload.
  Then add a test or a `tools/` check that runs the Appendix A3 scan and fails on a new violation (`imports.py`, 73 lines, in `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/api/`).

#### DATA-1: the big data tables are lazy now, but their code stays resident until first use, QuestStarts is built by the first NPC tooltip, and nothing is released
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the mechanism; sizes measured in Lua 5.4.8 outside the game: needs in-game probe for the client's figures (`/suu perf` or `/suu probe memory`, at login and after opening the map)
- status: open
- where: src/Core/Data.wowlua:43-93, 214-219 (the step lists, resident until first use; nothing released);
  src/Units/AutoQuests.wowlua:58-64 (dataLevel calls SuuUI.QuestStarts(), building it in one frame);
  src/Units/WorldMap/GiverTips.wowlua:180-181 (the first NPC tooltip prepares QuestStarts);
  src/Core/API.wowlua:802 (the 'only your class's data loads' comment)
- known: no
- what: each of the six files now exports a list of step functions (`export const questStartsSteps: ((t: QuestStarts) -> ())[]`), and `LazyData` runs them on `Get()` (all at once), `Until(fn)` (the first steps only) or `Prepare(fn)` (a few a frame, 1.5 ms or four steps), dropping each step once it ran (`self.steps[i] = nil`, `Data.wowlua:78`). Measured:

  | Table | Steps | Loaded, not built (the step functions) | Built | Built, Lua 5.1 estimate |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `QuestStarts` | 28 | 1,839 KB | 3,192 KB | 3,460 KB |
  | `MapPlaces` | 10 | 516 KB | 978 KB | 1,021 KB |
  | `CollectionSources` | 19 | 778 KB | 2,174 KB | 2,827 KB |
  | `RecipeSources` | 9 | 332 KB | 930 KB | 1,237 KB |
  | `FlightPaths` | 3 | 66 KB | 215 KB | 224 KB |
  | `MapOverlays` | 2 | 75 KB | 177 KB | 188 KB |
  | **Sum** | | **3,606 KB** | **7,666 KB** | **8,957 KB** |

  Parsing all six took 21.5 ms, building all of them 4.3 ms, the slowest single step 0.34 ms (Lua 5.4 on this machine; the comments in `Data.wowlua:164-166` give 0.35 ms a step in game).
  What is left of the finding:
  1. **The step functions are resident from login until the table is first used:** 3.6 MB in Lua 5.4 (bytecode plus constants; QuestStarts' strings alone are 770 KB). Lua 5.1 stores four bytes of line information per instruction where 5.4 stores one, so the client's figure is probably higher. A player who never opens the map, the collections or the professions window keeps all of it for the session.
  2. **QuestStarts is built for nearly everyone anyway.** With the world map module on (the default), the first mouseover of any NPC calls `lazyData.questStarts:Prepare()` (`WorldMap.wowlua:1417-1419`, from the tooltip hook `QuestTip`), and `OnEnable` then indexes the givers (`:2780-2782`). The Collections module's `toyList()` at login runs only the first step (`Collections.wowlua:218-222`), which is as intended.
  3. **`AutoQuests` builds all of QuestStarts in one frame:** `dataLevel(id)` calls `SuuUI.QuestStarts()` (`AutoQuests.wowlua:54`, used at `:307` when a quest opens without a list to read its level from). That is `Get()`: every remaining step at once, the stutter `WorldMap.wowlua:2572-2574` says `Prepare` was written to avoid ("3 MB in one frame was a stutter"). The same holds for any plugin calling `SuuUI.QuestStarts()` or `SuuUI.CollectionSources()` (API-17).
  4. **Nothing is released.** Once built, a table is held by its `LazyData` for the session; turning off World map, Collections or Professions frees nothing.
  5. **Still built at login for everyone** (`API.wowlua:100-107`): `AuraCatalog` 123 KB, `Talents` (all nine classes) 92 KB, `FlightRoutes` 16 KB, `Defensives` 8 KB, `InstanceLevels` 8 KB, `RaidPlanner` (hand-written, about 40 KB), plus the per-class files (DATA-2). About 290 KB without DATA-2: acceptable, listed for completeness.
  6. `src/Core/API.wowlua:638` still says "only your class's data loads" (see DATA-2).
- why it matters: the fixed cost at login dropped from about 8 MB of tables to about 3.6 MB of code, and in ordinary play QuestStarts (3.2 MB) comes back within the first minutes. The remaining 3.6 MB and the one-frame build in AutoQuests are what a memory or frame-time investigation will meet next.
- fix:
  1. `AutoQuests.wowlua:53-57`: return nil while `lazyData.questStarts:Ready()` is false and call `Prepare()` (as `WorldMap.wowlua:506-508` does), or route it through the handle of API-17.
  2. Shrink what is built (DATA-3, DATA-4, DATA-5): the step code shrinks with it.
  3. For the unbuilt code, measure in game first. If it matters, the remaining lever is to keep the data out of the client until wanted: a load-on-demand companion addon (a workspace member with `LoadOnDemand: 1`) holding the six files, loaded by `LazyData` on first `Get`/`Prepare`. Two checks first: that `wowlua publish` can ship two addon folders in one package, and (in game) that `C_AddOns.LoadAddOn` is allowed in combat on Forever.
  4. Optional: `LazyData:Release()` for a table whose only user turned off (the generator would have to keep the steps, so this only pays together with 3).
  5. Correct the comment at `API.wowlua:638`.
  Tests: `tests/unit/Core/Data.test.wowlua`; `tests/unit/Units/AutoQuests.test.wowlua` for item 1.

#### API-2: a service has one slot; the provider that is replaced is not restored
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Core/Services.wowlua:33-38 (provide), 57-64 (unregister)
- known: no
- what: `provide` overwrites whoever held the name:
  ```
  self.providers[name] = { impl = impl, owner = owner }
  ```
  and `unregister(owner)` sets `self.providers[name] = nil` for entries whose owner matches. There is one slot per name and no memory of the previous provider.
- why it matters: a plugin that calls `M:Provide("bags", …)` (`Docs/PluginGuide.md:158` shows exactly this) without `replaces`, or whose `replaces` target could not be replaced, takes the slot from the Bags module. When the plugin turns off the slot is nil although Bags is still enabled: `SuuUI.ToggleBags()` falls through to Blizzard's `ToggleAllBags()` (`src/Core/API.wowlua:828-834`) until a reload. The same holds for `alerts` (alerts silently stop), `notifications` (`SuuUI.Notify` returns nil), `talents`, `worldmap`, `mousebindings`, `auctionhouse`. In the other order (plugin first, the built-in enabling after combat) the built-in silently wins.
- fix: keep a stack per name (`providers[name] = { {impl, owner}, … }`; `get`/`use` return the top; `unregister` removes the owner's entry wherever it is and emits `SUUUI_SERVICE_CHANGED` only when the top changed). Test in `tests/unit/Core/Services.test.wowlua`: provide A, provide B, unregister B → `get` returns A; unregister A while B is on top → `get` still returns B and no message.

#### API-4: a module registered after login is enabled before an `OnEnable` assigned afterwards exists
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); showing it in game needs a load-on-demand plugin
- status: fixed in 4950cdcd (a module added after the registry started starts on the next frame through the registry's NextFrame runner)
- where: `src/Core/Modules.wowlua:801-803` (`add`: `if self.started then self:start(m) end`), `:751-767` (`start` → `self.runner:run` → `enable`), `src/Core/Combat.wowlua:118-123` (`run` calls the function at once out of combat), `src/Core/Modules.wowlua:520-534` (`PluginModule` takes callbacks only from the definition table), `:306-308` (the class's empty callbacks); taught by `Docs/PluginGuide.md:39-54`, `:67`, `:98` and `Examples/SuuUI_LevelBadge/src/LevelBadge.wowlua:31,124`
- known: no
- what: exactly when it happens. All four must hold:
  1. the plugin calls `SuuUI.RegisterModule(def)` **without** `OnEnable` in `def` and assigns it afterwards (`function M:OnEnable() … end`). Callbacks inside `def` are safe (`rawset` in the constructor, `Modules.wowlua:527-529`), and so is a class module whose `OnEnable` is a class member before `SuuUI.AddModule(X.new())`: every built-in module and `Examples/SuuUI_HelloPlugin` are of these two kinds;
  2. the registry has started (`registry.started`, set at `PLAYER_LOGIN`, `:776`), which means the plugin's file runs after login: a `LoadOnDemand` addon, or one loaded by another addon. A plugin with `## Dependencies: SuuUI` that loads at startup registers before login and is fine;
  3. the module's `enabled` setting is on;
  4. the player is out of combat, or the module is `combatSafe` (`:755-758`). In combat the queue defers `enable` to the end of the fight, by which time the file has finished and the assignment has happened.
  Then `add` → `start` → `runner:run` → `enable` runs inside `RegisterModule`, `m:OnEnable()` is the class's empty method, and the state becomes `enabled`. The plugin's `OnEnable`, assigned on the following lines, never runs. `OnInitialize` assigned afterwards is lost the same way.
  The after-the-fact style is the one the documentation teaches: the guide's first module (`PluginGuide.md:39-54`), its settings and frames sections, and the LevelBadge example. Only `Docs/API.md:20-34` and HelloPlugin show the callbacks inside the table.
- why it matters: such a plugin shows as "on" in `/suu modules` and does nothing, with no error. An author who copies the guide and marks the addon load-on-demand meets it, and only out of combat, which makes it look intermittent.
- fix: in `add`, when `self.started`, defer `self:start(m)` to the end of the current frame (`wowlua:timer` `after(0, …)`), so the registering file finishes first; `get`/`all` already return the module in state `registered` meanwhile. Keep the immediate path for tests through the injected runner if needed. Add one sentence to `Docs/API.md` and the guide ("a module registered after login starts on the next frame"). Test in `tests/unit/Core/Modules.test.wowlua`: `startAll()`, then `register` without callbacks, assign `OnEnable`, advance a frame, expect it called once.

#### API-3: the typed service API (0.19) cannot be used by a plugin, and two built-ins skip it
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in a5082e2d (the keys are on SuuUI.Services, Durability, Welcome and the settings section use them, the three service types' functions are optional, the welcome service is documented, and ModuleOf is gone)
- where: `src/Core/API.wowlua:216` (`UseService`), `src/Core/Modules.wowlua:467-469` (`ProvideService`), `:540-593` (`ModuleOf` has `Provide` at `:585`, no `ProvideService`), `src/Core/ServiceKeys.wowlua:1-5,55,95,99`, `Docs/API.md:110`, `Docs/PluginGuide.md:11`
- known: no
- what: `M:ProvideService(key, impl)` and `SuuUI.UseService(key)` take a `ServiceKey` object that exists only as an export of `/Core/ServiceKeys`. The guide says a plugin can "import SuuUI's types, never its code", and the keys are not on the global, so both functions are unreachable for plugins (a hand-made `{ name = "bags" }` works at run time because only `key.name` is read, untyped and undocumented). `ModuleOf`, the type `RegisterModule` returns, has no `ProvideService`. Inside SuuUI, `src/Units/Durability.wowlua:878` and `src/Units/Welcome.wowlua:777` still provide by string and `src/SettingsUI/Sections.wowlua:292` reads `"welcome"` by string, although `DURABILITY` and `WELCOME` keys exist. The header of `ServiceKeys.wowlua` says "Every function is optional", but `BagsService` (`:55`), `WelcomeService` (`:95`) and `RaidPlannerService` (`:99`) declare required functions while their callers still test them (`API.wowlua:830,1164`). The `welcome` service is missing from the services table in `Docs/API.md` (from `:183`).
- why it matters: a replacement module, the documented use of services, gets no type checking exactly where the contract matters, and the docs point plugin authors at functions they cannot call.
- fix: export the keys as `SuuUI.Services` (API-1 item 2); use them in Durability, Welcome and Sections; make the three service types' functions optional (or drop the sentence); add `ProvideService` to `ModuleOf`; add `welcome` to the docs table.

#### API-5: a plugin's own fields can shadow the module's methods; fields in the definition table are dropped
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the `__newindex` behaviour is the wowlua runtime's and was read in the 0.13 runtime, not re-read for 0.13.15
- status: fixed in a5082e2d (a plugin's field or definition key that would hide a module method or SuuUI's own field is an error naming it, at registration and on later assignment, and the definition's other fields stay on the module)
- where: `src/Core/Modules.wowlua:158-187` (SuuUI's own fields kept apart), `:258-302` (getters), `:311-506` (the methods), `:520-534` (`PluginModule`)
- known: partly (`Docs/API.md:113` covers the read-only fields)
- what: `id`, `name`, `state` and the other twelve are getters, and assigning one errors. All the methods (`Get`, `Set`, `Reset`, `Watch`, `On`, `Off`, `Emit`, `Each`, `Hook`, `Override`, `Provide`, `Print`, `Guard`, `Setting`, `IsEnabled`, `CharData`, `Migrate`, …) are plain class members: `self.Hook = {}`, `self.On = true` or `function M:Reset()` on a plugin's module silently replaces SuuUI's method for that module. The core and other modules then call the shadowed names on it (`m:IsEnabled()`, `m:Setting(key)` through `SuuUI.GetModule`, 23 calls in `src/Units`). Second gap: `RegisterModule(def)` builds a new `PluginModule` and copies only `OnInitialize`, `OnEnable`, `OnDisable` from `def` (`:524-532`); any other function a plain-Lua plugin puts in the table (`Refresh = function(self) … end`) is not on the returned module, and the docs do not say so.
- why it matters: a plugin author gets "attempt to call a table value" far from the cause, or a module that other modules read wrongly. The names are common words.
- fix: for `PluginModule` instances, refuse assignment of any name that is a method of `Module` other than the three callbacks, with an error naming the field and the module id (built-in classes override methods at class level, which stays allowed). Either copy the remaining function fields of `def` onto the module or document that they are dropped. Tests in `tests/unit/Core/Modules.test.wowlua`.

#### API-6: below 1.0 the compatibility check cannot express a breaking change
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Core/Modules.wowlua:147-161 (apiAtLeast), Docs/API.md:9
- known: no
- what: `apiAtLeast` accepts a module when the major versions are equal and SuuUI's minor is at least the wanted one. Every API version so far has major 0, so a module declaring `api = "0.4"` is accepted by 0.46. The API has changed existing behaviour along the way (0.19: a multiple `Select` reports through `onChangeAll`, `AuraContainer:ShowPreview`'s `place` takes named fields, the marks module's `:Get(id)` became `:Mark(id)`, `Raw.ns` no longer holds the modules; 0.36: a theme's `chat-*` colours are refused with a warning; 0.46: positions are kept per screen size). `CLAUDE.md`'s rule for the package ("below 1.0, breaking changes bump MINOR") has no counterpart here, and `Docs/API.md:9` says breaking changes bump the major version, "which is `0` until …".
- why it matters: a plugin written for an older minor that used a changed behaviour loads as compatible and misbehaves; the "Can't load" protection the guide promises never triggers.
- fix: keep a floor next to `API_VERSION` (`export const API_BREAKS = { "0.19", … }`): a module whose `api` is below the newest break is loaded but listed with a warning naming the break, or refused. Record breaks in `Docs/API.md` under a "Breaking changes" heading per version. Test in `tests/unit/Core/Modules.test.wowlua`.

- severity: medium

Measured, files loaded and nothing called: Presets 316 KB, Trainer 359 KB for the nine classes. The player's own class is then held twice, as prototype and as built table (Presets 62-165 KB built, Trainer 35-59 KB).

Alternatively generate the literal at module top level behind the class test (`local _, classFile = UnitClass("player")`, `export local presets: CooldownPreset[]? = classFile == "MAGE" and { … } or nil`), so the constants live in the file's chunk, which is collected after load. When the template changes, update `tools/gen_trainer.lua:57`, whose `existing()` finds the old list with the pattern `"\nexport function spells%(%): TrainerSpell%[%] return (%{.-\n%}) end\n"` and silently returns nothing (no merge, levels of known spells lost) if the template no longer matches. Tests: `tests/unit/Data/Presets/init.test.wowlua`, `tests/unit/Data/Trainer/init.test.wowlua`.

#### DATA-4: `QuestStarts.quests` and `MapPlaces.npcs` rows are positional lists with `nil` holes, and the world map keeps a second decoded copy of each
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code and counts); sizes estimated
- status: open
- where: tools/gen_quest_starts.lua (row writers); src/Data/QuestStarts.wowlua, src/Data/MapPlaces.wowlua;
  src/Units/WorldMap/Rows.wowlua:62 (quests = tbl.weakKeys()), 105 (npcs = tbl.weakKeys())
- known: no
- what: a quest row is a list of up to sixteen positions. After trimming, the 5,242 rows still span 46,314 positions for 29,308 values (17,006 holes), plus 3,971 sub-tables: an estimated 1,766 KB. `Rows.quest(row)` then builds a record with sixteen named fields and copies of the sub-lists, and caches it in a weak-keyed table keyed by the row:
  ```
  local quests: { [unknown[]]: Quest } = tbl.weakKeys()
  ```
  The rows are referenced by the data table for the whole session, so a weak-keyed entry is never collected: every quest the map has shown is held twice, the copy (a 16-node hash plus sub-lists) larger than the row. `Rows.npc` does the same for the 2,208 NPC rows (642 KB estimated, 15,476 positions for 12,388 values).
- why it matters: 1.8 MB at rest once QuestStarts is built (which the first NPC tooltip does, DATA-1), growing by up to about 3 MB more as the player opens zone maps over a session.
- fix: write each quest and each NPC as one packed string and decode it in the function that already is the single decode point:
  - generator: `s[id] = "Name\t1\t5\t\t\t\t123\t…"` (lists comma-separated inside a field; the tools already strip tabs from names); the types become `quests: { [number]: string }`, `npcs: { [number]: string }`.
  - consumer: `Rows.quest` and `Rows.npc` take the string, split it and cache by the string in an ordinary table (or by ID if the callers pass it); the decoded record is then the only table form.
  - expected: quests about 0.75 MB instead of 1.77 MB at rest, NPCs about 0.3 MB instead of 0.64 MB, no duplicate, and smaller step code.
  The smaller fix, if strings are not wanted: read fields by position through small accessors (`questName(row)`, `questLevel(row)`) instead of materialising a record, and delete the two caches.
  Tests: `tests/unit/Units/WorldMap/Rows.test.wowlua`.

#### DATA-8: real character names in `tools/data` headers, and the identity scan cannot catch this kind of leak
- severity: medium
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed that the eighteen header lines are byte-identical to the ones the first pass matched against the local SavedVariables (`git diff 4c6ea485 36f5f407` shows no change to line 1 of any of them); the names are not repeated here
- status: open
- where: line 1 of the nine tools/data/class_*.tsv and nine tools/data/spellbook_*.tsv;
  tools/extract_classdata.lua:35-36, tools/extract_spellbooks.lua:16; tools/idscan.py:11,43,47,55,62,78
- known: no
- what: the extract scripts copy the probing character's name into the header comment of each data file (the class files: the name after the class token and again in the parentheses; the spellbook files: the character's key at the start of the line), and the files are committed. `CLAUDE.md` says "Placeholder names only" and the repository is public. `idscan.py` would not have stopped it and will not stop the next one:
  - it reads only the staged diff (`git diff --cached`, lines 43 and 78), so what is already committed is never checked;
  - it has no failing exit and there is no git hook in the repository (no `tools/hooks`, no `.githooks`): "runs before every commit" is a convention;
  - its name lists come from SavedVariables under `/Applications/World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/…` (lines 11, 47, 55, 62), while `tools/update_recipe_sources.sh:20` has moved to `_forever_`. - why it matters: the owner's character names are published, against the project's own rule; names already in git history stay there unless history is rewritten, which is the owner's call.
- fix: (1) write the header without the name in `extract_classdata.lua:35-36` and `extract_spellbooks.lua:16` (class, level, race, dates only) and rewrite line 1 of the eighteen files. (2) Give `idscan.py` a non-zero exit when any count is above zero, a `--tree` mode that checks every tracked file, both game folders (or a path argument) for its name lists, and install it as a `pre-commit` hook from a checked-in `tools/hooks/` (`git config core.hooksPath tools/hooks`). (3) Run the tree mode once.

#### DATA-16: 2,487 generated theme textures (46.8 MB) are committed and shipped to every player
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (file counts and sizes from the tree); the effect on the game's memory: none expected (a texture loads when drawn), not probed
- status: open
- where: Media/Textures/Themes/Raids/, Stranglethorn/, PinkCat/; tools/raid_art.py, tools/stv_art.py,
  tools/pinkcat_art.py; wowlua.json:32-34 (build.assets)
- known: no
- what: the three scripts draw the built-in themes' art procedurally (standard library only; shapes rasterised with supersampling; every random choice from a fixed `random.Random(n)` seed; no embedded image or table data: the largest tables are the theme concept lists, `CONCEPTS` at `raid_art.py:4146` and `GLYPH_STYLES` at `:799`). The output is committed: 2,487 uncompressed 32-bit TGA files (image type 2), 46.8 MB. Each raid theme folder has 16 art files and its own copy of all 95 glyphs (`Glyphs/*.tga`, 16,402 bytes each): 21 × 95 = 1,995 glyph files, 32.7 MB. At 0.6 the whole addon had 139 textures. `Media` is now 59 MB on disk in 2,669 files; zipped it is 2.9 MB, so the download is small and the installed addon is not.
  Nothing documents these generators (`CLAUDE.md` names only `src/Core/Tokens.wowlua` and `src/Data/*` as generated), nothing checks that the committed art matches the scripts, and `raid_art.py --check` (the colour contrast check that reads `src/Core/ThemesRaids.wowlua`, `:4373`) is not run by CI.
- why it matters: every player installs 59 MB for themes most never pick; every regeneration rewrites up to 2,487 binary files in git history (they do not delta well when a drawing routine changes); and a hand-edited or stale texture cannot be told from a generated one.
- fix, in order of effort:
  1. Say in `CLAUDE.md` that `Media/Textures/Themes/**` is generated by the three scripts and must not be edited, and run `python3 -I tools/raid_art.py --check` in CI.
  2. One glyph atlas per theme instead of 95 files (a 1024 × 640 sheet, the glyph token giving the file and its texture coordinates): 1,995 files become 21. This needs `draw.glyph` and a theme's `glyphs` to accept coordinates, so it is an API change (`Docs/API.md`, a new API version).
  3. If the size matters to the owner: ship the raid themes as a load-on-demand companion addon, or probe whether the Forever client loads RLE-compressed TGA or BLP (confidence: needs in-game probe) and write that instead; the art is mostly flat alpha masks and compresses about 16:1.
  4. Optional: stop committing the output and generate it in CI before `wowlua build`. Only worth it if wowlua gets a pre-build step; otherwise a CI job that regenerates and fails on `git diff --exit-code` gives the same guarantee.

#### API-9: several things a plugin can register have no owner and no way back
- severity: low
- category: gap
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed (PublishAnchor takes an owner and is undone with it, so Chat's anchor goes when Chat turns off, 4950cdcd; AddInstance still has no owner or removal, the non-module RegisterSettings and RegisterMover are permanent, and the M:* registrations have no per-item handle)
- where: src/Core/API.wowlua:296-297 (AddInstance), 675, 692 (RegisterSettings, RegisterMover);
  src/Core/Extend.wowlua:310 (add)
- known: no
- what:
  - `SuuUI.PublishAnchor(name, frame)` has no owner: a module must unpublish itself. `src/Units/Chat.wowlua:3603` publishes `chat` and never unpublishes it (the only `PublishAnchor` in the file; 21 calls in `src/Units` in all), so after the chat module is turned off `SuuUI.GetAnchor("chat")` still returns its hidden box.
  - `SuuUI.AddInstance(kind, object, info)` has no removal: a replacement module's frames stay in `SuuUI.Instances(kind)` and keep receiving other plugins' `Each` and hooks after it is turned off.
  - `SuuUI.RegisterSettings(def)` and `SuuUI.RegisterMover(frame, opts)` (the non-module forms) register with no owner and cannot be removed.
  - `SuuUI.RegisterTheme` and `SuuUI.RegisterAuraFilter` have no unregister (acceptable: file load); `SuuUI.AllowAlertOutOfCombat(key)` is permanent.
  - `M:Watch`, `M:Veto`, `M:Each`, `M:Hook`, `M:Override`, `M:RegisterCommand`, `M:Provide`, `M:ExtendMenu` and the `Add…` methods can only be removed by turning the whole module off; `M:Off(name)` removes all of the module's listeners for a name, not one.
- why it matters: a module that toggles a feature by a setting keeps its own "is it on" flags inside callbacks instead of unregistering; anchors and instances go stale.
- fix: add `M:PublishAnchor(name, frame)` and `M:AddInstance(kind, object, info)` that record the owner and are undone in `releaseAll` (`Modules.wowlua:616-624`), switch the modules to them; let the registering methods return a handle with `:Remove()`; unpublish `chat` in Chat's `OnDisable` (`tests/unit/Units/Chat.test.wowlua`).

#### API-10: `Hook`/`Override` on a method that does not exist does nothing, forever; hooked methods return at most four values
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Core/Extend.wowlua:222-236 (base), 238-281 (wrap; 274-279 four return values)
- known: no
- what: `base()` caches `{ fn = raw or obj[method], raw = raw ~= nil }` per object and method the first time. When that is not a function, `wrap` returns silently (`:241-243`) and the non-function stays cached, so a later hook on the same name never applies even if the method exists by then (a callback field set after the frame was registered). A misspelt method name in `M:Hook("unitframe", "UpdateHealht", fn)` gives no error. The after-hook wrapper returns four values only:
  ```
  local a, b2, c, d = inner(this, ...)
  …
  return a, b2, c, d
  ```
  And when the last hook goes, `rawset(obj, method, b.raw and made or nil)` (`:245`) restores the function cached at first wrap, dropping any instance-level reassignment SuuUI made in between.
- why it matters: plugin authors get silence instead of an error on a typo or on a method outside the documented list.
- fix: in the hook registration, when the kind has instances and none has a function under `method`, report once through the reporter; do not cache a non-function base; return all values (pack and unpack, or document the limit). Tests in `tests/unit/Core/Extend.test.wowlua`.

#### API-11: every module method call and `self.id` read goes through a function `__index`
- severity: low
- category: performance
- confidence: likely (the getters are in the code; that a class with getters gets a function `__index` was read in the wowlua 0.13 runtime at the first pass and not re-read for 0.13.15)
- status: partly fixed in d8fa5ced (`Get`, `Peek` and `IsEnabled` read the module's own record directly, and hooks and timers read a plain gate instead of calling `IsEnabled`; `Set`, `Reset`, `Setting` and outside readers still go through the getters, and the method lookup itself is unchanged)
- where: src/Core/Modules.wowlua:318-362 (getters), 373-394 (Get, Peek, Set, Reset read self.id)
- known: no
- what: `M:Get(key)` costs: the `__index` function to find `Get` (then up the class chain), inside it `self.id` → `__index` again → the getter → `ownOf(self)` → `assert(owns[m])`, then `settings.get`. Reading a field the module has not set yet (`if not self.frame`) takes the same path and walks the class chain to nil.
- why it matters: modules call `self:Get`/`self:Peek` in event handlers; each call is several extra Lua function calls. Not a frame drop by itself, but it is on every setting read of every module.
- fix: inside `Module`'s own methods use `owns[self].id` (one table read) instead of `self.id`; keep the getters for outside readers. Hot paths in modules should keep settings in locals refreshed by `M:Watch`.

#### DATA-18: `Core/Data`'s failure paths leave a table half built or its waiters unanswered
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); a step failing needs a broken data file, so it has not happened
- status: open
- where: src/Core/Data.wowlua:70-81 (Step), 84-93 (Get), 97-104 (Until), 185-212 (the driver)
- known: no
- what: `Step` advances `nextStep` and drops the step before running it:
  ```
  self.nextStep = i + 1
  self.steps[i] = nil
  step(self.value)
  ```
  A step that errors is therefore never retried and the rest of what it would have written is missing, while `Ready()` later reports true. Through `Get()` and `Until()` the error is not caught at all: it surfaces in whichever module called `SuuUI.QuestStarts()`. In the driver, a failed step removes the table from `preparing` without calling `Done()` (`:194-206`), so the callbacks given to `Prepare` wait until someone else finishes the table. Separately, `Get()` and `Until()` call `Done()` synchronously (`:88-90`, `:100-102`): the waiters (a window's `Refresh`) run inside the caller's frame, on top of the build.
- why it matters: a generator bug in one step (a typo in a refreshed data file) would show as an error in an unrelated module and as silently missing map pins afterwards.
- fix: run each step under `fault.call` in `Step` itself and record a `failed` flag that `Ready()` and the header of `/suu errors` can show; in the driver call `Done()` (or drop the waiters with a report) when a table cannot be finished; let `Get()` schedule `Done()` with `after(0, …)` as the driver does. Tests in `tests/unit/Core/Data.test.wowlua` with a step that errors.

### Fixed since the first pass

- **DATA-6** (`src/Core/Tokens.wowlua` hand-edited; regenerating breaks three files): `tools/gen_tokens.py:299` now writes `export type ColorToken = keyof Colors`, and the later token additions went into the generator's own tables (`EXTRA_COLORS`, `TEXTURES`, the glyph directory; commits 6d082261, 7f5a1ccc, bce023d5, 7bd2b9bc, ef2e00fa changed generator and output together). Every key in `Tokens.wowlua` is found in `Design/tokens.json`, the generator or `Media/Textures/Glyphs`. Not verified by a run.
- **DATA-13** (`QuestStarts` at a Lua 5.1 per-function limit): the file is no longer one table literal; `tools/lazy_data.py:388-416` cuts it into 28 functions of about 5,000 values each (`src/Data/QuestStarts.wowlua:38`).

### Withdrawn

- None as whole findings. One sub-item of DATA-12 (that `tools/make_textures.py` rasterises every texture before filtering by name) is dropped: the jobs list at `:668-698` holds pixel functions and the filter at `:699-702` runs before `write_tga`, so whether work is done eagerly depends on helpers that were not re-read.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **Direct imports hide API gaps, and the gap widens with each subsystem.** Since 0.6 three new Core/UI subsystems (`Core/Ahead`, `Core/Data`, `UI/Dress`) were added with no public form at all; modules import them. Without a mechanical gate (the Appendix A3 scan as a test) the count keeps growing (415 → 474).
- **"Is module X on" is asked three ways** (`:Get("enabled")`, `:IsEnabled()`, a service being present). `:Get("enabled")` is the setting: true also for a module that errored, is replaced or waits for a reload. Worth a sweep in every module that adapts to another one.
- **Unowned registrations:** anything registered through `SuuUI.*` rather than `M:*` (anchors, instances, notes, LFG listeners, alert keys) survives the module. Reviewers of `src/Units` should check each `OnDisable` against the module's `SuuUI.PublishAnchor` calls (21 in `src/Units`; Chat's `chat` anchor is one miss).
- **Silent no-ops in the plugin surface:** hooks on unknown methods, late registration, shadowed methods, a replaced service. Each fails without a message; the fault reporter exists and should be used for them.
- **Lazy data is only lazy if every reader plays along.** One synchronous `SuuUI.QuestStarts()` in an event handler (AutoQuests) builds the whole table in a frame; a tooltip hook builds it for everyone. Reviewers of `src/Units` should treat every `SuuUI.QuestStarts()`, `MapPlaces()`, `CollectionSources()`, `MapOverlays()`, `FlightPaths()` call that is not behind `Ready()` as suspect (list: `AutoQuests:54`, `WorldMap:509,1268,1320,2515`, `WorldMap/Tips:83`, `FlightMap:219`).
- **A function that holds a table literal keeps the literal's constants alive.** That is what makes the step form work (drop the function, the code goes) and what makes the per-class files cost 675 KB (the functions are never dropped). The same holds for any module-level `function() return { big literal } end` elsewhere in `src/`.
- **Read-once decode caches keyed by a permanent table** (`tbl.weakKeys()` with data rows as keys, `WorldMap/Rows.wowlua`) never release anything, because the key is always referenced by the data.
- **Generators that patch their input in code** (`gen_trainer.lua`'s `CHANGED`, `gen_tokens.py`'s `EXTRA_COLORS`) are reproducible but hide data in scripts; the first has an expiry condition that nothing enforces.
- **Docs carry old file names and numbers** (`.lua`, the version in `Docs/API.md:3`, the README badge, `CLAUDE.md`'s wowlua version, module function and game folder). Anything that states a version or a path by hand goes stale within days at this release pace: generate or drop.
- **Third-party data and licences.** The addon is MIT; it embeds values derived from cMaNGOS classic-db (GPL-3.0: trainer skill values in `RecipeSources`, quest group types in `QuestStarts.group`; both file headers say so) and from QuestieDB and Questie (no licence stated). Whether derived game facts carry the GPL is a question for the owner, not a code finding; it is noted because every refresh re-imports them.

## Area: Cross-cutting sweep


All file:line references are for the 0.17.0 sources (`36f5f407`), repo-relative. Scope: `src/Core`, `src/EditMode`, `src/SettingsUI`, `src/UI`, `src/Units` (182 files, about 160,000 lines; 167 files and 134,000 lines at the old commit). `src/Diagnostics` and `src/Data` are out of scope, except for the scan of pattern 16, which ran over all of `src/`. Where a section says NEW it means these 0.17.0 sources; "the first pass" is the earlier review of commit `4c6ea485` (0.6.0-beta.1). Scan scripts and their outputs named `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/…` are in `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/`.

### Coverage

- **First-pass findings re-checked: all 35** (X-2.1 to 2.6, X-3.1 to 3.4, X-4.1 to 4.7, X-5.1, X-6.1, X-6.2, X-10.1 to 10.3, X-11.a1 to a6, X-11.b1 to b4, X-13.1, X-13.2), each against the 0.17.0 code that proves or disproves it.
- **Method:** the first pass's scan scripts were copied and pointed at 0.17.0 (`Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/p1.py`, `combat.py`, `hooks.py`), their output compared with the old output to find the sites that are new, and three scans added (`Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/fwdlocal.py` for pattern 16, `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/globwrite.py` for bare-name global writes, and per-pattern greps). Every reported finding was confirmed by reading the 0.17.0 code. The work was split in four: patterns 2 and 3; pattern 11 for modules A to G; pattern 11 for modules H to Z; and the rest (patterns 1, 4 to 10, 12 to 16) by the lead reviewer.
- **Read in full (new files):** `Core/Ahead`, `UI/PowerCost`, `Units/AuraFilters`, `Units/AutoQuests`, `Units/LootRolls`, `Units/MouseBindings`, `Units/QuestAnnounce`; `Units/RankUpgrade` for its timers and owner. `Core/AuraFilters`, `Core/Data`, `UI/CombatBadge`, `UI/Dress`, `UI/HealthFill`, `UI/LootRollTray` were read for the parts each pattern touches (events, timers, scripts, caches, unit reads), not start to end.
- **Closed from the first pass's open list:** pattern 11 for the long `OnEnable` bodies of AuctionHouse (`:4097-4297`), Bags (`:2919-3208`), Chat (`:3589-3731`) and Collections (`:3905-4105`), each read start to end; pattern 7 for MouseBindings and for the secure buttons of Bags and of the Spellbook (UI and module).
- **Still not covered** (plainly):
  - Pattern 4: the 127 `after(0, …)` deferrals were not read one by one.
  - Pattern 5: once-guards of hooks in `reloadToToggle` modules by sample only.
  - Pattern 7: plain `Show`/`Hide`/`SetPoint`/`SetParent` on secure frames outside MouseBindings, Bags and the Spellbook (unit frames, action and class bars, objective tracker, notification and guild overlays).
  - Pattern 11: the `OnEnable` bodies of 17 reload modules in H to Z (Loot, Macros, Mail, Merchant, MicroMenu, NpcDialogue, ObjectiveTracker, PartyFrames, Professions, RaidFrames, Social, Spellbook, Support, Tooltips, Trainer, UnitFrames, Windows) and most of Nameplates' were tabulated from greps, with flags and `OnDisable` read.
  - Patterns 2 and 3: the deeper callees of some unchanged `OnUpdate` drivers and the 20 `CHAT_MSG_*` chat-tab listeners were not re-read line by line; the 63,000-line diff as a whole was not read line by line.
  - Pattern 6: field writes on Blizzard frames cannot be found by grep.
  - Nothing was run in game; findings marked "needs in-game probe" stay open until probed.

#### Detail: patterns 2 and 3

- Re-checked on NEW: X-2.1 to X-2.6, X-3.1 to X-3.4, and items 7 to 10 of the first pass's "ten worst" (Threat, CooldownTracker, Visibility, Panel).
- **OnUpdate:** grep for `"OnUpdate"` in `src/Core`, `src/EditMode`, `src/SettingsUI`, `src/UI`, `src/Units`: 65 lines, 51 handlers (the rest are `SetScript("OnUpdate", nil)`). Every handler read, and for the ones that call a method (`Tick`, `Layout`, `Update`, `Drag`, `WatchPresent`, `PlaceMinimapPins`, `MinimapMoved`, `rowsLook`) the method too. Not read to the bottom: the callees of `Notifications:Tick`, `DamageMeter:Refresh`, `FlightMap:TickTimer/MoveTimer/DrawInk`, `NpcDialogue:Type`, `ObjectiveTracker:TickItems`, `Bags:SortTick`, `Chat:DragStep` (rows carried from the first pass with new line numbers; the handler itself was read).

- **Events:** 518 registration lines in scope (`OnGameEvent(`, `OnUnitEvent(`, `events.on*`, `onUnit(`, `onGame(`, `RegisterEvent(`, `RegisterUnitEvent(`; there is no `@event(` in scope). 213 lines name one of the listed high-frequency events; each of those was looked at, and the handler bodies read for all the roster, aura, threat, cooldown, addon-message, loot and bag rows. `Core/Events.wowlua` read in full.
- **New files read in full:** `Core/Ahead`, `UI/PowerCost`. Read for their events, timers and scripts plus the handlers behind them: `Core/Data` (driver), `Units/LootRolls` (events, `Tick`, `Refresh`, `Data`, `Row`, `OnLootLine`, `RollFor`, `roster`, `waitingOn`), `UI/LootRollTray` (`SetData`, `SetRemaining`), `Units/QuestAnnounce` (module part in full), `Units/MouseBindings` (`bookWatch`, `ApplySoon`, `OnEnable`), `Units/RankUpgrade` (lines 120-245), `Units/AutoQuests` (registrations only: gossip and quest dialogue events, none frequent). `Core/AuraFilters`, `UI/CombatBadge`, `UI/Dress`, `UI/HealthFill`, `Units/AuraFilters` have no OnUpdate, ticker or game-event registration (grep), so they were not read further for this part.

### Summary

- 0.17.0 fixed little of what the first pass found: of 35 findings 29 are still present, 5 changed form, 1 is fixed (the chat tick, X-2.4), none is withdrawn in full. 8 are new. 42 remain: 3 high, 13 medium, 26 low.
- The new high one is a lifecycle bug with one root: `self:IsEnabled()` is false for the whole of `OnEnable` and true for the whole of `OnDisable` (`src/Core/Modules.wowlua:668-673`, `:685-689`). Mouseover bindings therefore cannot be turned off (X-11.b5), loot rolls running at a reload are never shown (X-11.b6), Convergences' pins stay away after a re-enable (X-11.a8), and Timeline hands a boss mod's option back at each login (X-11.b7).
- The group frames are still the biggest cost, and wider: every unit frame now carries four all-units listeners, raid pet buttons are unit frames too, and a roster change refreshes a button up to three times, uncoalesced (X-3.1); party and raid still both take every unit's `UNIT_AURA` (X-3.3).
- Per-frame allocation is unchanged in the encounter timeline (X-2.1) and the swing timer (X-2.2). New: the loot roll tray is rebuilt for every vote line (X-3.5).
- `Module` still owns no timers (X-4.1) and no CVars; CVars changed by modules are still not given back (X-11.a2, a4, b1, b2), and Readiness still sends on every roster and cooldown event (X-3.2).
- Secure-frame work in the new code is careful: MouseBindings, the bag overlays and the Spellbook's secure cells are all behind combat guards; no lockdown problem was found. The secret-value handling of the new files is right as well.
- Three writes to Blizzard globals or tables need `/suu probe taint`: `ChatEdit_CustomTabPressed` (X-6.1), `CURRENT_CHAT_FRAME_ID` (X-6.3, missed before), `UISpecialFrames` (X-6.2, where the code now records that the tainted closing was blocked for a protected window).
- Duplication grew with the new modules (`spellLookup` is now four identical copies, `ago` seven, `playerClass` four); the media path cluster is the one that shrank (60 files to 14).
- No file-level local is used above its declaration anywhere in 0.17.0 (pattern 16); the old `GLYPHS` case is gone.

### Findings

#### X-11.b5: Turning Mouseover bindings off changes nothing: OnDisable re-applies every binding, and moved Target/Menu clicks are never given back
- severity: high
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in 4950cdcd (IsEnabled is false inside OnDisable, so Apply clears every binding; db302207 closes the boxes and gives the game's clicks back at login when the module is off)
- where: src/Units/MouseBindings.wowlua:2494-2496 (`OnDisable`), :2288-2421 (`Apply`, the test at :2315-2316), :2231-2285 (`SyncClickBindings`, the test at :2238-2240); src/Core/Modules.wowlua:678-691 (`disable`), :500-502 (`IsEnabled`)
- known: no
- what: `OnDisable` is one line:
  ```
  override function OnDisable()
      self:Apply()
  end
  ```
  and `Apply` decides what to set from `IsEnabled()`:
  ```
  local on = self:IsEnabled()
  for _, b in ipairs(on and self:Binds() or {}) do
  ```
  as does `SyncClickBindings` (`if not self:IsEnabled() then clicks, mods = DEFAULT_CLICKS, { target = 0, menu = 0 } end`). But the registry calls `OnDisable` while the module's state is still `Enabled` (`disable()`: `m:OnDisable()` at :685-687, `state = Disabled` at :689), so `IsEnabled()` is true there. `Apply` therefore clears the old attributes and sets all of them again: the virtual-button attributes on the two secure buttons, the click attributes on every SuuUI unit frame, the `_refresh` snippet with its `SetBindingClick` lines; the state driver and the wrapped `OnEnter`/`OnLeave`/`OnClick` stay as well. After that the module's events are released, so nothing calls `Apply` again (only an `ApplySoon` timer that happened to be pending, :2429-2432, would clear things by accident). The unit test never turns the module off, and the smoke test only checks that `/suu disable` raises no error.
- why it matters: (1) A player turns "Mouseover bindings" off in the settings: every bound key, click and wheel direction keeps casting on the unit under the mouse until `/reload`. (2) The game's click-bindings profile is kept by the game, not by SuuUI: a player who moved Target to, say, Shift-Left and then turns the module off keeps that profile after the reload (the module is off, so `Apply` never runs again and `store.clickSynced` stays set). By the file's own notes (:27-35) a unit frame targets only on the click the game's click bindings have for it, so plain Left click no longer targets on any unit frame, with no SuuUI setting left to fix it. The same state is reached without ever disabling on that character: "enabled" is per profile and the clicks are per character (`CharData`), so a character that logs in on a profile where the module is off, after having moved its clicks, is stuck the same way.
- fix: do not ask `IsEnabled()` during the callbacks. Give `Apply` (and `SyncClickBindings`) an explicit argument, e.g. `Apply(on: boolean)`; `OnEnable` calls `self:Apply(true)`, `OnDisable` calls `self:Apply(false)`, and the other callers pass `self:IsEnabled()`. In `OnDisable` also close `self.box` and `self.clickBox` (after a disable there is no `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` listener to close them, and an open box that last ran `SetPropagateKeyboardInput(false)` swallows the keyboard in the next fight, :927-949). For the click-bindings profile add a login check that does not depend on the module being on (a file-level `@onLogin`, or in `Core/Modules.start` for modules that are off): if `store.clickSynced` is set and the module is not enabled, run `SyncClickBindings` with the default clicks out of combat. Optionally unwrap the unit frames (`SecureHandlerUnwrapScript`) and `UnregisterStateDriver(owner, "mo")` on disable. Test in tests/unit/Units/MouseBindings.test.wowlua: bind a key and a frame click, `/suu disable mousebindings`, then expect the attributes gone from the frame and from `SuuUIMouseBindingsWorld`, `_refresh` equal to the empty snippet, and the click-bindings stub called with the default Target and Menu clicks.

#### X-3.1: A roster change refreshes every group frame in full, twice, with no coalescing
- severity: high
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed on 2026-11-16 (branch `high-perf`; one shared listener each in UI/UnitFrame for the roster, raid marks, roles, the world and the theme, walking the active frames, the roster one coalesced to the next frame; the raid and party modules' passes are the only redraw of their frames, once per burst and only of the frames showing someone new (UF-1); the header hook no longer refreshes; party frames do nothing while hidden)
- where: src/UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:2217-2300 (`Activate`, the per-frame RAID_TARGET_UPDATE,
  PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD, GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE, PLAYER_ROLES_ASSIGNED listeners at :2262-2300), :2202-2214
  (`Refresh`); src/Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1952-2000 (roster handler), :1213-1235 (the header's
  `OnAttributeChanged` hook); src/Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:1456 (roster handler); src/UI/Auras.wowlua:887-900
- known: no
- what: `UnitFrame:Activate` registers four all-units game listeners per frame. For a party or raid frame:
  ```
  events.onGame("GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE", function()
      if grouped then
          self:Refresh()
  ```
  and `Refresh` is `FitRow`, `UpdateIdentity`, `UpdateHealth(true)`, `UpdatePower`, `UpdateRaidMarker`. The raid module's own listener then walks all buttons again: `f:UpdateIsMe()`, `f:ApplyWho()`, `auras:Refresh()`, every dispel container and every indicator container `Refresh()` (each an `UpdateAllAuras` on an engine container), then `UpdateStates()`, `UpdateSelected()`, `UpdateRange()`, and a second loop with `f:UpdateIndicatorPresence()` for every button. When the header moves a token, the button's `OnAttributeChanged` hook also does `SetUnit`, `UpdateIsMe`, `ApplyWho`, `auras:SetUnit` and `btn:Refresh()`: a third refresh of the same frame. The raid's pet buttons are unit frames too (`StylePetButton`, `:1259-1302`) and carry the same four listeners. Aura containers built with a `party`/`raid` unit register their own roster listener as well (`UI/Auras.wowlua:889`). Nothing is deferred to the next frame, so each of the several `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` events the game sends per change repeats all of it.
- why it matters: in a 40-player raid one roster event is 40 (plus pets) full refreshes through as many protected calls, then the module's pass with several aura container rescans per button and an indicator presence scan per button. Roster events come in bursts while a raid forms, and during fights when people die, disconnect or are moved. `RAID_TARGET_UPDATE` and `PLAYER_ROLES_ASSIGNED` likewise dispatch to every frame.
- fix: (1) in `UnitFrame`, drop the per-frame `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`, `RAID_TARGET_UPDATE`, `PLAYER_ROLES_ASSIGNED` and `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` registrations; keep one file-level listener per event in `UI/UnitFrame.wowlua` that walks the active frames (a weak set filled in `Activate`, emptied in `Deactivate`). (2) Coalesce the roster one to once per frame (a dirty flag and the next-frame runner in `Core/Extend`, or the flusher pattern of `UI/ActionBar.wowlua:433-460`). (3) In the raid module, remove from the roster handler what the frame's own refresh and the `OnAttributeChanged` hook already did (`UpdateIsMe`, `ApplyWho`, the aura refreshes), or make the module the only one that does it. (4) Skip frames whose unit's GUID did not change (`UnitGUID` may be secret: compare only when `secret.readable`, refresh when it is not). Tests: tests/unit/UI/UnitFrame.test.wowlua (the bus's listener count stays constant with 40 frames active), tests/unit/Units/RaidFrames.test.wowlua (three roster events in one frame give one refresh per button).

#### X-11.a2: The CVar a module turned off is remembered in a profile setting, so a profile switch loses the restore
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (both CVars go through M:SetCVar, kept per character outside profiles; the old profile notes move to CharData by migrations)
- where: src/Units/DamageMeter.wowlua:41, :452-471, :783; src/Units/CooldownManager.wowlua:78, :3401-3405, :3501-3508; src/Core/Settings.wowlua:705-726
- known: no
- what: both modules switch a Blizzard CVar off in `OnEnable` and note that in one of their own settings, which live in the profile. DamageMeter: `if self:Get("blizzardWas") == "" then self:Set("blizzardWas", was) end … pcall(C_CVar.SetCVar, "damageMeterEnabled", "0")`, and on disable `local was = self:Get("blizzardWas"); if was ~= "" then pcall(C_CVar.SetCVar, "damageMeterEnabled", was); self:Set("blizzardWas", "") end`. CooldownManager: `if pcall(C_CVar.SetCVar, "cooldownViewerEnabled", "0") then self:Set("viewerOff", true) end`, and on disable `if self:Get("viewerOff") then self:Set("viewerOff", false) … SetCVar("cooldownViewerEnabled", "1")`. `useProfile` makes the target profile current (`self.profile = target`) before it notifies the changed keys, so an `OnDisable` caused by the switch reads the new profile.
- why it matters: the CVar belongs to the account or character, the note to one profile. Profile A has the module on (CVar off, A remembers). The player switches to profile B where the module is off (or switches to B and turns it off there): `OnDisable` reads B's default (`""` / `false`) and restores nothing. Blizzard's damage meter or cooldown viewer stays off although SuuUI's is off too, until the player finds the game's own option. The note also travels in exported profiles and role profiles to characters whose CVar was never touched, where a later disable writes a value that character never had.
- fix: keep the note outside the profile: `self:CharData()` (the CVars are per character on this client; use `SuuUI.AccountData` if a probe shows them account wide). In `OnEnable` write `CharData().blizzardWas` / `.viewerOff`, in `OnDisable` read and clear it there. Move the old values with `M:Migrate` (the migration gets the profile's values: copy a non-default value into the character data once, then drop the keys from `DEFAULTS`). Tests: tests/unit/Units/DamageMeter.test.wowlua and tests/unit/Units/CooldownManager.test.wowlua: enable, switch to a profile with the module off, expect the CVar back.

#### X-11.b6: Loot rolls running at a /reload are never shown, while Blizzard's roll frames are already off screen
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code) for the missing refresh; the in-game effect needs `GetActiveLootRollIDs` to exist on Forever (the code tests for it)
- status: fixed in 4950cdcd (IsEnabled is true inside OnEnable, so Refresh shows the tray for rolls already running)
- where: src/Units/LootRolls.wowlua:822-826 (`Refresh`), :1692-1708 (`OnEnable`), :1711-1764 (`Wire`, the running rolls at :1754-1763), :1248-1263 (`Add`), :1436-1459 (`HideBlizzardRolls`); src/Core/Modules.wowlua:668-673
- known: no
- what: `Refresh` starts with
  ```
  if not tray or not self:IsEnabled() then
      return
  end
  ```
  `OnEnable` calls `self:Wire()` and then `self:Refresh()`. `Wire` first moves `GroupLootContainer` off screen (`HideBlizzardRolls`) and then adds the rolls that are already running ("rolls already running (a /reload mid-roll)": `StartRoll` → `Add` → `Refresh`). All of this runs inside `OnEnable`, where the module's state is not yet `Enabled` (`Modules.wowlua:673` sets it after `OnEnable` returns), so every one of these `Refresh` calls returns at once: the tray and its driver stay hidden. Nothing refreshes afterwards until another roll event arrives (someone else's vote line for an open roll, a new roll, the item-data callback when the item was not cached). The unit test for this case passes because it calls `M:OnEnable()` by hand on a module that is already enabled (tests/unit/Units/LootRolls.test.wowlua:676-684).
- why it matters: `/reload` (or a disconnect and login) while a roll is open, which is common after a boss kill: Blizzard's roll frames are off screen and SuuUI's tray is hidden. If everyone else has already chosen, no further event comes, the roll runs out and the player passes by timeout on an item they wanted.
- fix: `Refresh` should not gate on `IsEnabled()` while enabling. Either drop the test from `Refresh` (a reload module's tray is hidden in `OnDisable` anyway, and the events are gone then) or keep a field of its own (`self.on = true` at the top of `OnEnable`, `false` in `OnDisable`) and test that. Change the test's `again()` to go through a real disable/enable (or set the state to disabled first) so it would have caught this. Test file: tests/unit/Units/LootRolls.test.wowlua.

#### X-3.2: Readiness sends an addon message on every roster event and shares on every cooldown event
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code); the game's throttle behaviour needs an in-game probe
- status: fixed in db302207 (shares go out only when changed or asked, questions only for newcomers not heard from and at most once per 10 s, through Core/Comm with per-sender rates)
- where: src/Units/Readiness.wowlua:442-448 (roster), :452-456 (cooldowns), :266-278 (`Send`), :280-300 (`Share`, `ShareSoon`), :314-317 (answering `RDYQ`), :484-490 (heartbeat, 30 s)
- known: no
- what:
  ```
  self:OnGameEvent("GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE", function()
      self:Update()
      if channel() then
          self:Send("RDYQ")
          self:ShareSoon()
  ```
  sends at once, unthrottled, on every roster event. Every client that hears `RDYQ` answers with its own share after 2 s (`:314-317`). `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` (every global cooldown) out of combat in a group → `ShareSoon()`: one share every 2 s for as long as the player casts anything. `Share` does not compare with what was sent last. - fix: (1) send `RDYQ` only when the member count grew (someone new who has no data), at most once per 10 s; (2) share only when the encoded text differs from the last one sent, or a cooldown's ready time moved by more than a few seconds, with a floor of 10 s between shares; (3) let the heartbeat be the only periodic sender; (4) route sends through one throttled sender shared by the modules that use the addon channel (see shared pieces). #### X-10.1: The auction house keeps every scanned item's price per character for ever
- severity: medium
- category: performance
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: open
- where: src/Units/AuctionHouse/Prices.wowlua:37-66 (`recordSeen`, `lowestSeen`);
  src/Units/AuctionHouse.wowlua:195-203 (`CharStore`), :292-301 (`Saved`, `AllSaved`);
  src/Units/AuctionHouse/Auctions.wowlua:560-566 (`rememberBid`); src/Units/AuctionHouse/Sell.wowlua:621
  (`posted`)
- known: no
- what: `seen[itemID] = { price = low, at = time(), qty = total, n = n, most = most }` is written into the scanning character's `CharData` for every item of a full scan and every search result; nothing removes an entry. `bids[auctionID] = amount` is written on every bid and never removed (auction ids are not reused). `posted[itemID]` likewise. `LowestSeen` walks every character's store (`for _, d in ipairs(self:AllSaved())`) for each lookup, and the item tooltips call it.
- why it matters: one full scan is tens of thousands of five-field tables in `SuuUIDB` for that character; each character that scans keeps its own copy, old prices never age out, and the whole file is parsed at every login and written at every logout and reload.
- fix: (1) keep prices per realm and faction in account data, not per character (one copy; `LowestSeen` becomes one lookup); migrate by taking the newest `at` per item; (2) drop entries older than 30 days when a scan finishes and at login, and store them as arrays (`{ price, at, qty, n, most }`); (3) remove `bids[id]` when the auction is no longer in the bids list the page already reads (`:3699-3709`). Tests: tests/unit/Units/AuctionHouse.test.wowlua, and a `tests/compat` profile with the old shape.

Its neighbours have one (`HookQuestProviders`: `if not f or self.questHooked then return end`, `:2426-2429`; FlightMap's `TakeTaxiNode` hook: `self.takeHooked`, `src/Units/FlightMap.wowlua:2555-2557`). `wowlua:hooks` neither dedupes nor returns a handle, so the hook is permanent.

#### X-4.1: A module has no way to own a timer, so every module guards (or forgets to guard) by hand
- severity: medium
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: partly fixed in 4950cdcd (M:After and M:Every are owned and cancelled when the module turns off, and db302207 moved most modules onto them; 36 plain `after` calls from wowlua:timer remain in 18 files under src/Units, several with delays of seconds)
- where: plain `after` from wowlua:timer, with delays of a second or more: src/Units/RaidPlanner.wowlua:511,
  544; src/Units/RaidPlanner/Specs.wowlua:230, 252, 270, 301, 335; src/Units/RaidPlanner/Arrange.wowlua:153,
  165; src/Units/RaidPlanner/Fill.wowlua:290; src/Units/WorldMap/Collect.wowlua:155, 158;
  src/Units/Bags/Saved.wowlua:68; src/Units/Alerts.wowlua:245; src/Units/Spellbook.wowlua:1760;
  src/Units/Welcome.wowlua:819; src/Units/ActionBars/RankUpgrade.wowlua:61; next-frame `after(0, …)` in
  MicroBags, NpcDialogue, Legacy, CharacterWindow, Chat/Panel, MouseBindings/Boxes, Windows/QuestLog,
  WorldMap/GiverTips
- known: no
- what: timers are the one thing a module schedules that the registry does not take away on disable. `Module` has no `After`/`Every`; modules import `after`/`every` from `wowlua:timer` and each callback has to start with `if not self:IsEnabled() then return end`. The ones without it are the bugs: Campsite `src/Units/Campsite.wowlua:604-609` (X-11.a1), Convergences `:490-492`, `:579-581`, `:795-798` (X-4.4), CooldownManager `:3463-3470` (X-4.3), MouseBindings `:2429-2432`, and the tickers whose handle is never kept (X-4.6).
- why it matters: each new timer is a chance to act after disable, and a test cannot catch a missing guard without one case per timer.
- fix: add `M:After(seconds, fn)` and `M:Every(seconds, fn)` to `Module` (next API version, `API_VERSION` in `src/Core/Modules.wowlua`, documented in `Docs/API.md`): they wrap `wowlua:timer`, keep the handles in the module's `Own`, run the callback through the module's fault source, and `releaseAll` cancels them. Then replace `after`/`every` in the module classes of `src/Units` (not in widget classes of `src/UI`). Test: tests/unit/Core/Modules.test.wowlua: a timer set in `OnEnable` does not fire after disable; a ticker stops.

#### X-6.1: ChatEdit_CustomTabPressed is replaced, not hooked
- severity: medium
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- status: open (unverified: needs /suu probe taint after Tab in a chat edit box in combat and a protected chat action)
- see also: Part 1, "Found after the review", the chat send path: a taint scan right after a typed slash command already lists `ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX`, `LAST_ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX` and `ChatFrame1EditBox` fields as addon-written, and a `SendChatMessage` was blocked in combat after a whisper started from SuuUI's chat. The owner decided not to fix the chat send path now: the chat will be redone as a reskin of the game's own chat frames, which also settles this finding.
- where: src/Units/ChatCommands.wowlua:1716-1733 (`WrapTab`), called from `OnEnable` (:1823)
- known: Docs/wowlua-port-notes.md:1430, Docs/port-notes/units-chat.md:54 (recorded as kept on purpose; no probe result recorded)
- what: `local original = field(_G, "ChatEdit_CustomTabPressed"); _G.ChatEdit_CustomTabPressed = function(box, ...) if self:IsEnabled() then local ok, took = pcall(self.OnTab, self, box); if ok and took then return true end end; return try(original, box, ...) end`. Once-guarded (`self.tabWrapped`). It is the only Blizzard function SuuUI replaces; the comment says the game calls it through `securecall`. `Core/TaintScan.wowlua:117` lists the name among the globals to check.
- why it matters: an addon-written global is tainted for every reader. If the Forever client reads it anywhere outside `securecall`, chat input in combat can be blocked for everyone with the module on. The replacement also stays after the module is turned off, and an addon that replaces the global later hides SuuUI's.
- fix: probe first: `/suu probe taint` after pressing Tab in a chat edit box in combat and then using a protected chat action. If clean, record the result in the comment and in `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` and keep it. If it taints: take Tab with an override binding on TAB while the palette shows (cleared when it hides), or from the edit box's `OnTabPressed` post-hook and undo the game's completion.

#### X-11.a1: Campsite's after-combat timer runs after the module was turned off and restarts its ticker
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)

- known: no
- what: `self:OnGameEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED", function() after(0.2, function() self.phase = "unknown"; self:Update() end) end)` has no `IsEnabled` check; the `sayNow` timer right below has one (`:619`). A toggle made in a fight is carried out by the combat queue at the same `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`, so "listener schedules the timer, `OnDisable` cancels ticker and timers, 0.2 s later `Update()`" can happen (it also happens when the module is turned off within 0.2 s after a fight). `Update()` at a fire calls `Alert("resting")`, which does `show(); self.ticker = every(0.5, show)`; `Alert("nearby")`/`("rested")` start a new `briefTimer`.
- why it matters: Campfire turned off during a fight while resting at a fire: a 0.5 s ticker keeps calling `SuuUI.ShowAlert` with the module shown as off. Nothing cancels it (the `UNIT_AURA` listener is gone), so it runs until reload or until the module is turned on and off again.
- fix: first line of the timer body `if not self:IsEnabled() then return end`; set `self.phase = nil` and `self.near = nil` in `OnDisable`. Test in tests/unit/Units/Campsite.test.wowlua: fire `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`, disable, advance 0.2 s, expect no ticker and no alert.

#### X-11.a5: FlightMap's OnEnable re-enters itself from an ADDON_LOADED listener it never removes
- severity: low
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code); whether the world map can be missing at login on Forever needs an in-game probe
- status: partly fixed (db302207: the late half is Start() and the ADDON_LOADED listener is removed once the map is there; an error in Start still bypasses the registry's fail, leaving the module on with half its wiring)
- where: src/Units/FlightMap.wowlua:703-726 (`OnEnable`, the listener at :717-725), :729 (`Start`)
- known: no
- what: `self:ProvideService(FLIGHT_MAP, …); self:Attach(); local world = self.world; if not world then self:OnGameEvent("ADDON_LOADED", function() if not self.world and frames.find("WorldMapFrame") then self:Attach(); if self.world then self:OnEnable() end end end); return end`. The second run provides the service again and registers everything else. It runs inside the event bus's error guard, not the registry's: an error in it is reported, but the registry's `fail` (state Errored, `OnDisable`, release) does not happen, so the module stays Enabled with part of its listeners. The first listener stays for the session.
- why it matters: only where the world map loads on demand. There a failure in the late half leaves a module that reports as on with half its wiring, and every later `ADDON_LOADED` still calls the listener.
- fix: split into `OnEnable` (provide the service, `Attach`, else wait) and `Start()` (everything from `:2537` on). The listener calls `self:Start()` and then `self:Off("ADDON_LOADED")` (the module has no other `ADDON_LOADED` listener). Test: tests/unit/Units/FlightMap.test.wowlua with the world map frame absent at enable.

For AuraFilters the effect is smaller: the Auras module is `combatSafe` and builds your buff container in the fight (`Auras.wowlua:773-787`, `filtered(…)`) before the player's lists are published, so your own lists are missing on your buffs for the rest of that fight (they are applied at its end through `ApplyFilters`).

- what: `Shown()` is `return self:IsEnabled() and self:IsSkyborne()`. `OnEnable` ends with `changed(self)`, which emits `SUUUI_CONVERGENCES_CHANGED` and calls `UpdateMinimap()`. At that moment the state is not yet Enabled (the registry sets it after `OnEnable` returned), so the world map's refresh on that message asks the service `shown()` and gets false. The only later call is `after(1, function() … readBlessing(self); self:UpdateMinimap() end)`: `readBlessing` emits again only `if now ~= self.blessed`, and `OnDisable` does not reset `self.blessed`, so on a second enable in a session nothing is emitted once the module counts as on.
- why it matters: turn Convergences off and on again (or on for the first time while the blessing cannot be read, in combat) with the world map open: the pins and the "Skyborne" filter group stay away until the map is redrawn for another reason. The minimap is fine because `:808` calls `UpdateMinimap` directly.
- fix: `Shown()` does not need `IsEnabled`: the service exists only while the module is on (the registry removes it), and `OnDisable` hides the minimap layer; make it `return self:IsSkyborne()` and let `UpdateMinimap` keep its own check. Or emit once the module is on: replace `changed(self)` at `:810` by `after(0, function() if self:IsEnabled() then changed(self) end end)` and set `self.blessed = nil` in `OnDisable`. Test: tests/unit/Units/Convergences.test.wowlua: disable, enable, expect `SUUUI_CONVERGENCES_CHANGED` after the state is Enabled.

#### X-11.b7: Timeline hands the boss mod's warnings option back at every login
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: likely (from code; needs the boss mod's options table to exist when SuuUI's modules start, which is at `PLAYER_LOGIN`)
- status: fixed in 4950cdcd (IsEnabled is true inside OnEnable, so ApplySuppression keeps the boss mod's warnings hidden; db302207 keeps the player's value per character)
- where: src/Units/Timeline.wowlua:441-443 (`Suppressing`), :445-460 (`ApplySuppression`), :961 (called from `OnEnable`), :1048 (the comment in `OnDisable`); src/Core/Modules.wowlua:668-673
- known: no
- what: `Suppressing` is `self:IsEnabled() and self:Get("hideTheirs") and self:Get("source") == source`. `OnEnable` calls `self:ApplySuppression()`, but inside `OnEnable` `IsEnabled()` is still false, so `want` is false, and with the saved `dbmWarningsWas` not empty (it was set in the last session) the branch
  ```
  elseif not want and was ~= "" then
      options.HideDBMWarnings = was == "true"
      self:Set("dbmWarningsWas", "")
  ```
  runs: the boss mod's own setting is restored and SuuUI forgets it had taken it. Nothing applies it again until the player changes `source` or `hideTheirs`. The comment in `OnDisable` ("Suppressing is false once disabled") shows the opposite assumption; that block is written out by hand and works.
- why it matters: "Hide their own display" holds only for the session in which it was switched on: after each `/reload` or login the boss mod's warnings are back while SuuUI's setting still says hidden (its bars stay hidden, they are tested later).
- fix: let `ApplySuppression` take the wanted state from its caller instead of `IsEnabled()` (`OnEnable`: `self:Get("hideTheirs") and self:Get("source") == "dbm"`; `OnDisable`: false), or keep a field set at the top of `OnEnable`. Test: tests/unit/Units/Timeline.test.wowlua, enable with `hideTheirs` on, a boss-mod source and `dbmWarningsWas = "false"`, expect the option still true after `OnEnable`.

#### X-11.b1: Marks leaves the navigation CVar, the game's waypoint and "following" behind when it is turned off
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)

- known: no
- what: while a mark shows the way, `navigation(self, true)` keeps the player's `showInGameNavigation` in `data.navWas` and sets the CVar to "1", and `Follow` sets the game's waypoint and super-tracks it. `OnDisable` is
  ```

  if hint then hint:Hide() end
  self:CloseCard()
  changed(self)
  local layer = self.mmLayer
  if layer then layer:Hide() end
  ```
  It neither clears `self.following` and `store(self).following`, nor calls `navigation(self, false)`, nor clears the waypoint. The CVar goes back only at the next `OnEnable` (`:1184-1187`). The game's own waypoint pin, hidden by `HideGamePin` (`pin:SetAlpha(hide and 0 or 1)`), stays at alpha 0 until its provider refreshes.
