Test: tests/unit/Units/Marks.test.wowlua.

#### X-11.b4: WorldMap re-enters OnEnable from an event handler
- severity: low
- category: architecture
- confidence: confirmed (from code); whether the path is ever taken needs an in-game check (it runs only if `WorldMapFrame` does not exist when modules start)
- status: partly fixed (db302207: OnEnable no longer runs again, the map half is OnMap; it still runs from an ADDON_LOADED listener outside the registry's fail path, and the listener stays for the session)
- where: src/Units/WorldMap.wowlua:701-736 (`OnEnable`, the listener at :730-735), :740 (`OnMap`)
- known: no
- what:
  ```
  if not (f and layer and reveal and menu and provider) then
      self:OnGameEvent("ADDON_LOADED", function()
          if not self.map and frames.find("WorldMapFrame") then
              self:Attach()
              if self.map then
                  self:OnEnable()
              end
          end
      end)
      return
  end
  ```
  The second run of `OnEnable` is outside the registry's `reporter:call` for enabling: an error in it is reported as an event error and the module stays "enabled" half built (no `fail()`, no `OnDisable`). It also repeats `ProvideService` and `QuestObjectivesOnce`, and the `ADDON_LOADED` listener stays for the session.
- why it matters: structural: a module's enable has two entry points with different error handling. The same wait exists in Marks (`:1193-1201`, which only calls `HookMap`) and, per part a, in FlightMap.
- fix: split the part after the wait into a method (`Start()`), call it from `OnEnable` and from the listener inside `self:Guard(...)`, and drop the listener once attached (`self:Off`-style removal for game events, or a flag). A shared helper on `Module` (`M:WhenFrame("WorldMapFrame", fn)`) would serve WorldMap, Marks and FlightMap. Test: tests/unit/Units/WorldMap.test.wowlua.

#### X-6.3: Chat writes the Blizzard global CURRENT_CHAT_FRAME_ID
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (in game: the write); nothing blocked in one fight
- status: open (the write is confirmed in game, with no harm seen in the next fight; a protected chat action in that fight, such as moving or docking a chat window, was not seen. The in-fight opening is CHAT-12's open half)
- probe (2026-11-15, `/suu probe all`; read 2026-11-19): after the chat settings were opened from a SuuUI tab out of combat, `CURRENT_CHAT_FRAME_ID` read as written by SuuUI; in the next fight nothing was blocked and nothing new became addon-written.
- see also: Part 1, "Found after the review", the chat send path: a taint scan right after a typed slash command already lists `ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX`, `LAST_ACTIVE_CHAT_EDIT_BOX` and `ChatFrame1EditBox` fields as addon-written, and a `SendChatMessage` was blocked in combat after a whisper started from SuuUI's chat. The owner decided not to fix the chat send path now: the chat will be redone as a reskin of the game's own chat frames, which also settles this finding.
- where: src/Units/Chat/Windows.wowlua:224-235 (`openChatSettings`, the write at :230)
- known: Docs/port-notes/units-chat.md:54-58 ("written the same way")
- what: `CURRENT_CHAT_FRAME_ID = idOf(cf); if config:IsShown() then HideUIPanel(config) end; ShowUIPanel(config)`: a bare assignment to a global Blizzard's chat code reads (the chat settings window and the tab menu's functions use it to know which window they act on). It is the second Blizzard global SuuUI writes; the scan `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/globwrite.py` (below) finds bare-name global writes.
- why it matters: the value stays addon-written (tainted) until Blizzard's own code writes it again; every Blizzard function that reads it meanwhile runs tainted. Opening the chat settings from SuuUI's tab menu and then using a protected chat function (for example moving or docking a chat window in combat, or anything the settings window does through protected calls) may be blocked.
- fix: probe with `/suu probe taint` after opening the chat settings from a SuuUI chat tab. If it taints, open the settings the way Blizzard's tab menu does without writing the global: click Blizzard's hidden tab menu entry through a secure overlay as the game menu entries do (`src/Units/GameMenu.wowlua:474`).

#### X-6.2: Three windows still close on Escape through UISpecialFrames
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: needs in-game probe
- status: open (unverified: needs Escape in combat with a SuuUI window and a protected Blizzard window open, then /suu probe taint)
- where: src/UI/Panel.wowlua:705-707 (`opts.secure` -> `SecureEscape`, else `tinsert(UISpecialFrames, …)`),
  :714-718 (`SecureEscape`); src/SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:671, :1088; src/Units/Talents/Window.wowlua:110
- known: no
- what: `UI/Panel.wowlua:999-1003` records what was found in game: "the game's closing of UISpecialFrames, run tainted by an addon's entry there, was blocked for [a protected window] in a fight (found in game with the Collections window)". Only Collections passes `secure = true` (`src/Units/Collections.wowlua:2423`). Every other named window, the settings window, the profile dialog and Talents still insert into `UISpecialFrames`. Talents' window is the game's own frame with a secure placer (`UI.SecurePlacement(f)`, `src/Units/Talents.wowlua:2776`).
- why it matters: the same tainted walk of `UISpecialFrames` runs on every Escape. For a plain window `Hide` is allowed, so it works; but anything protected the game's Escape path does after the walk in the same execution (closing a protected window, and on Forever possibly more) runs tainted. Windows that later gain a secure child (an overlay parented into them) fall into the case already seen.

#### X-4.3: The cooldown manager's "seen recently" timers run after the module was turned off
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (both scans go through one pending flag on the module's M:After timers, and the list is in the character's data, not a copied profile setting)
- where: src/Units/CooldownManager.wowlua:3457-3470 (timers), :460-492 (`rememberAuras`: `M:Set("recent", all)`)
- known: no
- what: `after(1, function() pending = false; rememberAuras() end)` (on the player's or target's `UNIT_AURA`) and `after(0.5, rememberAuras)` (on `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED`) have no `IsEnabled` check. `rememberAuras` scans up to 80 auras and, when it finds a new name, copies the whole `recent` setting and writes it (`local all = copy(M:Get("recent")) … M:Set("recent", all)`). The target-change timer is not deduped: tabbing through five targets queues five scans; each reads `M:Get("recent")` (a copy) even when nothing is new.
- why it matters: a profile write from a module that is off (within a second of turning it off), and repeated scans and copies out of combat on every target change.
- fix: start both callbacks with `if not M:IsEnabled() then return end`, share the `pending` flag between the two paths, and read the list with `Peek` in `recent()` (`:453-456`).

#### X-4.4: Convergences sends and resolves from unguarded timers
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (Share all is one owned ticker that re-reads the channels per send and stops when the module turns off; the Resolve timers are M:After)
- where: src/Units/Convergences.wowlua:573-583 (`ShareAll`), :490-492, :795-798
- known: no
- what: `for i, spot in ipairs(self:Spots()) do after((i - 1) * 0.25, function() send(message(spot), channels) end) end`: one message per known spot, 0.25 s apart (up to 200 spots: 50 s of sends), with no check that the module is still on or the group still the same, and no way to cancel. `after(0.5, function() self:Resolve() end)` and `after(0.5, function() readBlessing(self); self:Resolve() end)` can add a spot to the account data after disable.
- why it matters: up to 200 queued addon messages go to the channel list read at the start, also after the module was turned off or the group left; they use the addon channel's budget other SuuUI features share.
- fix: one self-rescheduling sender with a token (`self.shareToken`, bumped by a new share and in `OnDisable`), which re-reads `self:Channels()` per send; guard the two `Resolve` timers with `IsEnabled`. With X-4.1: `M:After`.

#### X-4.5: The auction scan's per-frame reader has no stop but its own end
- severity: low
- category: bug
- confidence: confirmed (from code)
- status: fixed in db302207 (the reader is kept as readTicker, owned, cancelled by EndScan and stops when the scan is no longer current; 68ae02ee ends the scan when the house closes)
- where: src/Units/AuctionHouse.wowlua:3122-3174 (`ReadScan`), :3106-3118 (`EndScan`), :4299 (`OnDisable`)
- known: no
- what: `local ticker: TickerHandle; ticker = every(0, function() … for k = i, stop - 1 do local ok, … = pcall(AH.GetReplicateItemInfo, k) … end … if i >= n then ticker:Cancel() … self:EndScan() … end end)` reads 2,500 replicate items per frame; the handle is a local. `EndScan` (called by the 60 s timeout and when the window closes) cancels `self.scanTicker` only and sets `self.scanning = nil`; the reader does not test `self.scanning == sc`.
- why it matters: closing the auction house mid-read keeps a per-frame job of 2,500 `pcall`s alive for the rest of the list, after which it writes all prices, calls `EndScan` again and prints "Scan done" out of context.
- fix: keep the handle in `self.readTicker`, cancel it in `EndScan` and `OnDisable`, and return at the top of each tick when `self.scanning ~= sc`.

- severity: low

- known: no

### Pattern tables for 0.17.0

#### Pattern 1: multi-returns truncated by and/or

Re-run on NEW with the first pass's script (copy pointed at NEW: `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/p1.py`): 8,109 function headers walked; 155 multi-variable assignments with `and`/`or` on the right, 291 tuple-typed functions, 548 single-expression `return … and/or …`. **0 hits**: no assignment has fewer expressions than variables with a top-level `and`/`or` in the last one, and no tuple-typed function returns a single `and`/`or` expression.

#### Pattern 2: OnUpdate scripts and tickers

Hits examined: **51 `OnUpdate` handlers** (65 grep lines), **20 `every(`**, **3 `C_Timer`** (1 ticker). **Real problems: 6** (X-2.1, X-2.2, X-2.3, X-2.5, X-2.6, X-2.7). A frame's `OnUpdate` does not run while the frame is hidden; a ticker does.

##### Table: OnUpdate

| Where | Drives | Throttled | Stops | Allocates per run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Core/Extend.wowlua:154` | next-frame queue | one shot | hides itself | one table per flush |
| `Core/Motion.wowlua:130` | all alpha fades (one shared driver); sets alpha only for a step of 3% or more | no (needed) | hides when no fade is left | no |
| `Core/Ahead.wowlua:61` (new) | work built ahead after login, one step of one job a frame | one step a frame | hides in combat and when no job is left; shown again 1 s after `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED` | `"Ahead: " .. job.key` per step |
| `Core/Data.wowlua:183` (new) | lazy data built in steps (1.5 ms or 4 steps a frame) | by time | hides when nothing is preparing | no (source names cached); one closure when a data set finishes |
| `EditMode/EditMode.wowlua:467` | dragging a mover: lead frame follows, other outlines sync | no | cleared in `StopDrag` (`:485`, `:518`) | no |
| `UI/Inputs.wowlua:180` | toggle knob slide | no | clears itself when done | closure per toggle click |
| `UI/RaidPlanner.wowlua:798` | drag ghost follows the cursor, drop target | no | ghost hidden outside a drag | no |
| `UI/TalentTree.wowlua:608` | order list drag (`Drag`, `:642`) | no; returns at once without a press | runs every frame while the order list shows | no |
| `UI/Visibility.wowlua:107` | mouseover fade poll | 0.1 s | **never**: the frame is always shown; returns early when no frame uses mouseover | `also[frame] or {}` (`:95`) per hover frame without extra frames |

##### The ten worst (0.17.0)

1. `UI/Timeline.wowlua:413` (X-2.1): full layout with allocations every frame during an encounter.
2. `UI/SwingTimer.wowlua:239` (X-2.2): a formatted string per live row per frame, all fight long.
3. `Units/Convergences.wowlua:724` and `Units/Marks.wowlua:850` (X-2.3): two separate 10 Hz placers with the same position code; Convergences allocates standing still, Marks reads the game six times a tick with no marks.
4. `Units/Threat.wowlua:608`: 5 Hz in combat with a settings copy (`self:Get("position")`, `:516`) and fresh row tables; use `Peek`.
5. `UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:1531`: walks every cell every frame to find a dirty flag; one "any cell dirty" flag on the tracker would do.
6. `Units/Windows.wowlua:2048` (X-2.6): 20 Hz format + measure + resize while the map is open.
7. `Units/Bags.wowlua:2859` (X-2.5): two closures per frame while a sort runs.
8. `UI/Panel.wowlua:480`: an `OnUpdate` on every scroll grip; set it on mouse down and clear it on mouse up instead.
9. `UI/Visibility.wowlua:107`: never hidden; hide the poll frame while `hover` is empty.
10. `Units/LootRolls.wowlua:1679`: 10 Hz with one or two new tables a tick while the tray shows (only results left: still the `kept` list); small, and the natural place to flush a coalesced refresh (X-3.5).

Gone from the list: the chat tick (X-2.4, now the idle fade only).

##### First pass's un-numbered items 7 to 10

- **Threat** (`Units/Threat.wowlua:506-538`, driver `:608`): still holds. `local placedOff = self:Get("position").hidden` copies the position table five times a second (`Core/Settings.wowlua:339-341`: `get` returns `copy(...)`), `readRows()` and `entries(rows)` build new tables per tick. The driver now also runs out of combat for "group" and "instance" (`ShowsOutside`, `:543`).
- **CooldownTracker** (`UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:1531-1552`): still holds. `for _, cell in ipairs(self.cells) do if cell.dirty then …` runs every frame while the tracker runs.
- **Visibility** (`UI/Visibility.wowlua:105-125`): still holds. The poll frame is never hidden; it returns after the 0.1 s gate when `hover` is empty.
- **Panel** (`UI/Panel.wowlua:480-488`): still holds. Every scroll grip has an `OnUpdate` that tests `scroll.dragging` each frame.

#### Pattern 3: handlers of high-frequency events

Hits examined: 518 registration lines in scope, 213 of them for the listed events. **Real problems: 5** (X-3.1, X-3.2, X-3.3, X-3.4, X-3.5). There is still no `COMBAT_LOG_EVENT_UNFILTERED`, `UPDATE_MOUSEOVER_UNIT` or all-units `UNIT_SPELLCAST_*` listener in scope, and no listener on mouse motion.

How the bus costs (`Core/Events.wowlua:86-94`): every listener is a closure that checks its subscription and goes through `reporter:call` (a protected call, and timing when `/suu perf` runs). So N listeners on one event are N protected calls. **The bus gained no coalescing and no shared roster or addon-message dispatcher** since the first pass; what changed in it is bookkeeping by owner (`byOwner`, `:75-79`), which makes `off`/`offAll` cheap. There is no `SUUUI_ROSTER_*` message and no use of `wowlua:comm`.

##### Shared pieces worth having (0.17.0)

- **One roster dispatcher.** `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` has 17 registration sites; in a raid that is 40 raid frames, their pet buttons, the single frames and the modules: about 60 to 100 live listeners. A `SUUUI_ROSTER_CHANGED` message from one listener in `src/Core` (or `src/UI/GroupUnits`), emitted once per frame at most, would replace all of them, and could carry what changed (size tier, who is where). `PLAYER_ROLES_ASSIGNED` (7 sites, one per frame too) belongs to it.
- **One unit→frame map for group frames** (`src/UI`, owned by the group frames): serves `UNIT_AURA`, `UNIT_THREAT_SITUATION_UPDATE`, `UNIT_CONNECTION` and range for party and raid without the linear walks.
- **One addon-message router** (`src/Core`, on `wowlua:comm` if its behaviour fits): modules register a prefix and get only their messages; it is also the place for a shared send throttle (X-3.2). Six modules each listen to every `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` now, and each carries its own "sender is me" test (`Readiness:OnMessage` `:310`, `Marks:OnMessage` `:786-789`, `Timeline:OnMessage` `:897`, `fromMe` in Campsite and Convergences).
- **One minimap placer** (`src/UI`, next to `UI/MapPin`): "player position, view radius, rotation, yards to pixels, has it moved" read once per tick and handed to Marks and Convergences. Marks has the moved test (`Units/Marks.wowlua:869-896`), Convergences does not (X-2.3).
- **One "player aura by spell" reader**: Campsite and Convergences each wrap `C_UnitAuras.GetPlayerAuraBySpellID` and each listen to the player's `UNIT_AURA`.
- **One cast cost per session**: `UI/PowerCost.wowlua:156-174` registers seven player cast listeners per caller; the resource bar (`UI/ResourceBar.wowlua:483`) and the player frame (`UI/UnitFrame.wowlua:2243-2248`) each make their own `CastCost`, so every cast reads `GetSpellPowerCost` twice and runs 14 listeners. A shared instance with a list of `changed` callbacks halves it.
- **One next-frame flusher for bar passes**: `UI/ActionBar.wowlua:433-460` (`later(kind)`) and the stance bar's own copy (`UI/ClassBars.wowlua:264-283`) do the same thing; the totem bar has none (X-3.4).

#### Pattern 7: combat lockdown

281 secure-API lines on NEW (188 before), from the first pass's script (`Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/combat.py`, output `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/combat.txt`); 126 have a combat guard in the enclosing function. The 97 lines that are new were compared against the old list and the unguarded ones read. **Real problems: 0.**

Closed this pass (the first pass had not covered `Show`/`Hide`/`SetPoint`/`SetParent` on secure frames here):

- **`Units/MouseBindings.wowlua`** (read in full by the pattern-11 pass): every secure operation is behind `InCombatLockdown()` (`Apply` `:2289-2295` defers itself with `RunOutOfCombat`; `SyncClickBindings` `:2233`; `SetClick` `:1905`; the CVar write `:809`), `Build` (`:2186-2206`: two named `SecureActionButtonTemplate` buttons and a `SecureHandlerStateTemplate` owner) is reached only from `Apply`, and what it writes on unit frames is recorded in `frameAttrs` and cleared at the start of each `Apply`. The module is not `combatSafe`, which is right. Its fault is the disable path (X-11.b5), not lockdown.
- **`Units/Bags.wowlua`**: the bank's buy overlay (`PlaceBuy`, `:1510-1535`) returns in combat; the use overlay (`UseButton` `:1560-1611`, `UseOn` `:1614-1632`, `DrawUseTarget` `:1639-1657`, `HideUse` `:1659-1664`) is made, moved, shown and re-parented only out of combat (`UseOn` and `DrawUseTarget` return on `InCombatLockdown()`; the stdlib overlay's `set`/`show`/`hide` return false in combat, `wowlua-stdlib/std/secure.wowlua:122-147`), its holder has a `[combat] hide; show` state driver, and `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED` hides both overlays before the lockdown starts (`:3044-3050`), which also takes their anchors off the bag slots.
- **`UI/Spellbook.wowlua` and `Units/Spellbook.wowlua`**: the spell cells are `SecureActionButtonTemplate,SecureHandlerDragTemplate` buttons made in `cell()`; `SetSpells` lays the grid and cells out only when `not InCombatLockdown()` (`:782-800`), `SetCasts`, `SetCastPage` and `FitRows` return in combat (`:829`, `:868`, `:879`), `SetSchools` moves, shows and hides tabs and their secure covers only out of combat (`:953-973`). The one path that would create a secure cover in combat (a new school tab) cannot be reached: `Render` in combat requires `self.prepared` (`Units/Spellbook.wowlua:1022-1026`), the pet's school is frozen in combat (`PetSchool`, `:634-641`), and the book itself is only built out of combat (`:1147`). `ShowView` uses alpha, not `Hide`, on frames that hold secure buttons.
- Also read among the new lines: `UI/Panel.wowlua:1004-1012` (`SecureEscape`, from a window's constructor), `Units/Collections.wowlua:3789-3830` (`SecureTabs`, from `OnEnable` of a module that is not `combatSafe`), `Units/RaidFrames.wowlua:1306-1355` (`LayoutPets`, only from `Layout`, whose callers are all inside `RunOutOfCombat`: `:1835`, `:1880`, `:1888`, `:1986`), and the stdlib overlays in AuctionHouse `:2419`, ObjectiveTracker `:858-880`, Trainer `:1007`, Windows `:1839-1841`.

**Still not covered:** plain `Show`/`Hide`/`SetPoint`/`SetParent`/`SetSize` on secure frames outside those three areas (unit frames, action bars, class bars, objective tracker, notifications' macro buttons, guild overlays) were not swept call by call. The three `combatSafe` + `reloadToToggle` modules (Auras, CastBars, Notifications) are still worth one `/reload` in combat with `/suu probe taint`.

#### Pattern 11: module hygiene

61 module classes in `src/Units` (57 before; new: AuraFilters, AutoQuests, LootRolls, MouseBindings, QuestAnnounce; `Units/RankUpgrade.wowlua` is a helper class owned by ActionBars, not a module). 39 are `reloadToToggle`, 22 toggle live. **Real problems: 15** (X-11.a1 to a8, X-11.b1 to b7).

##### What the registry does (`src/Core/Modules.wowlua` on 0.17.0)

- **Released on disable** (`releaseAll`, `:616-624`): `events.offAll` (bus messages, game and unit events), `settings.unwatch` (watchers and vetoes), `unregisterCommands`, `settingsRegistry.unregister` (sections), `editMode.unregister` (movers), `extend.unregister` (`Each`/`Hook`/`Override`, menu extensions, micro menu, game menu, notification kinds, role presets), `services.unregister`. Nothing else. Timers and tickers, `wowlua:hooks` hooks, `HookScript`, CVars, shown frames, suppressed Blizzard frames, `EventRegistry` callbacks, jobs queued with `M:RunOutOfCombat` (`:409-411`, they go to `combat.run` and are not owned) and `Core/Ahead` jobs all stay the module's business.
- **Disable** (`disable`, `:678-691`): only for a module in state Enabled; `OnDisable` inside `reporter:call` (an error in it is reported and the release still happens), then `release`, state Disabled, `SUUUI_MODULE_DISABLED`.
- **reloadToToggle** (`sync`, `:694-716`): for such a module `sync` only sets `pendingReload` (`:699-704`) and returns; a toggle never calls `OnDisable`. `OnDisable` runs for it only from `fail` (`:641-654`) when `OnEnable` threw (`:647-651`), followed by `release`. An errored reload module retries only at the next load (`:701`, `toggle` `:909-914`). So this still holds in NEW.
- **Other modules**: `sync` puts the enable or disable on the combat queue (`self.runner:run("module:" .. m.id, …)`, `:705-715`), so a toggle in combat happens when combat ends, also for a `combatSafe` module.
- **combatSafe** (`start`, `:751-767`): matters only at start (login, reload, or a module added later). `if m.combatSafe and self.lockdown:inCombat() then` the module is enabled at once inside `reporter:call`; otherwise the first enable goes through the combat queue. Nothing checks that a `combatSafe` module really makes no secure frames.
- **IsEnabled is false inside OnEnable**: the state becomes Enabled only after `OnEnable` returned (`:668-673`). Code called synchronously from `OnEnable` that gates on `self:IsEnabled()` does nothing (see X-11.a8; FlightMap works around it with `after(0, …)` at `:2628-2631`).
- **A profile switch** (`Core/Settings.wowlua:705-726`) makes the new profile current first and then notifies every changed key, `enabled` included, so `OnDisable` of a module that is off in the new profile reads the new profile's settings.
- **Gained since the first pass**: only `layout` in `ModuleDef` (`:97-100`, 0.46: settings kept per screen size). `Module` still has no owned timers (`After`/`Every`), no CVar helper and no "wait for a frame or addon" helper. `Core/Blizzard.restore` (`:144-146`) still never restores (`-- Kept for the public API: always false for a suppressed frame`).
- The event bus keeps several listeners per owner and event (`listen`, `:95-100`), so registering the same event twice in one `OnEnable` (AuctionHouse, Bags, ActionBars do) is fine.

Flags: no wrong `reloadToToggle` or `combatSafe` flag found in these 26. No `combatSafe` module creates or touches a secure or protected frame of its own in `OnEnable`; the two that suppress Blizzard frames in combat (Auras, CastBars) go through `Core/Blizzard`, which defers for protected frames. No listener, hook or ticker is registered twice on a disable/enable cycle in the nine modules that toggle without a reload plus Alerts/AuraFilters/AutoQuests (all once-guarded or owned by the registry).

`src/Units/RankUpgrade.wowlua` is not a module: it exports the class `RankUpgrader` (`:56`), a helper that keeps the best known rank of each spell (`Read`, `:74-96`), swaps a newly learned rank onto the action slots that held the best one before (`Learned`/`Apply`, `:182-244`) and lists and replaces stale ranks after a spec switch (`Stale`/`Place`, `:103-166`). It registers no events and builds no frames. **ActionBars owns its lifecycle**: `ActionBarsModule:OnEnable` makes one (`src/Units/ActionBars.wowlua:1421-1426`, `self.ranks`) and feeds it from its own module events (`LEARNED_SPELL_IN_SKILL_LINE`, `SPELLS_CHANGED`, `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`, `:1430-1447`), which the registry drops with ActionBars (itself `reloadToToggle`, `:741`, part a). Its only loose ends are two 1 s `after` timers (`:171`, `:214`) that may fire once after the owner is gone; both only read the spellbook or re-try `Apply`, which is guarded by `InCombatLockdown()` and the cursor check (`:204-221`). Nothing to undo.

#### Pattern 16 (added this pass): a file-level local used above its declaration

The old code had `local GLYPHS = TEX .. "Glyphs\\"` at `src/UI/GroupFinder.wowlua:173` and `GLYPHS .. glyph .. ".tga"` inside a class body at `:108` and `:146`. wowlua hoists a module's top-level `function`, `class` and `enum` declarations (`wowlua/crates/wowlua-lower/src/class.rs:47-100`), but not `local NAME`, `local function NAME`, `const NAME` or `local { a, b } = …`; a use on an earlier line, inside a function, method or class body, therefore compiles to a read of the global of that name (nil), and the strict check does not flag it.

Scan: `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/fwdlocal.py <src dir>`. For every file it takes each file-level (column 0) `local`, `local function`, `const`, `export local/const` and destructuring declaration that is not also imported or hoisted, and reports every earlier line where the name appears as an identifier (not after `.` or `:`, not a table key, field declaration or type position). A hit is marked `SHADOW?` when the enclosing top-level statement declares the same name as a local, parameter, loop variable or class field before the use.

Result over all of NEW `src/` (Core, Data, Diagnostics, EditMode, SettingsUI, UI, Units; 294 files):

- **0 real cases.** 0 lines reported as `HIT`.
- 37 lines reported as `SHADOW?`, all read and all false: the earlier use is a local, parameter or type parameter of the same name inside another function (`Diagnostics/MouseoverProbe.wowlua:96-106` `keys`, `Diagnostics/Probe.wowlua:511` `state`, `Diagnostics/SocialProbe.wowlua:558-591` `tree`, `Diagnostics/SpellData.wowlua:120-159` `count`, `Diagnostics/TaxiProbe.wowlua:132-144` `out`/`T`, `SettingsUI/Window.wowlua:268-447` `build`, `UI/ActionBar.wowlua:396-398` `on`, `UI/Layout.wowlua:64-105` `number` in type positions, `Units/LootRolls.wowlua:201-238` `me`, `Units/Nameplates.wowlua:186-213` `home`/`fill`, `Units/WorldMap/Tips.wowlua:101-114` `shown`).
- Control: run on the old tree, the scan reports exactly the known case (`src/UI/GroupFinder.wowlua:108` and `:146`, `GLYPHS` declared at `:173`). On NEW that file no longer has the constant: the glyphs go through `draw.glyph(self.glyph, glyph)` (`src/UI/GroupFinder.wowlua:108`, `:146`).

Limits: the shadow test is by enclosing top-level statement, so a real forward use inside a function that also has an unrelated local of the same name in another nested function would be listed as `SHADOW?` (still listed, to be read), not dropped. Names used only through `_G` or `rawget` are not seen.

### Cross-cutting observations

- **`IsEnabled()` inside `OnEnable` and `OnDisable` is the wrong way round for what module code expects** (false while enabling, true while disabling: `src/Core/Modules.wowlua:668-673`, `:685-689`). Four findings rest on it (X-11.b5, b6, b7, a8) and several modules already work around it (Marks `:1217-1238`, FlightMap `:2628-2631`). Either set the state before `OnEnable` and before `OnDisable` in the registry (and set it back when `OnEnable` fails), or give modules `self:IsStarting()`/`IsStopping()`; then grep every `IsEnabled()` reachable from an `OnEnable` or `OnDisable`. The unit tests miss this class because they call `M:OnEnable()` by hand on a module that is already enabled: tests should toggle through the registry.
- **`reloadToToggle` still hides lifecycle bugs.** 39 of 61 modules never run `OnDisable` on a toggle; what they change outside themselves (CVars, another addon's options, globals, the game's click bindings) is never undone. The undo has to run at the next login for modules that are off (X-11.b2).
- **CVars are the common leftover**: DamageMeter, CooldownManager, Guild, Marks, Nameplates, Windows, with four ways of remembering the old value (a profile setting, character data, a session field, nothing). One helper that the registry restores from.
- **Timers are unowned** (X-4.1); `RunOutOfCombat` jobs and `Core/Ahead` jobs are unowned too.
- **Event bursts have a working answer in this code base that four places do not use yet**: the hidden flusher frame shown by the event (`Core/Extend.wowlua:154`, `UI/Layout.wowlua`, `UI/ActionBar.wowlua`, `UI/ClassBars.wowlua:268`). X-3.1, X-3.3, X-3.4 and X-3.5 are the ones without it; `Core/Events` itself still has no coalescing and no shared roster or addon-message dispatcher (17 `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` sites, 6 `CHAT_MSG_ADDON` listeners).
- **Party and raid frames are two copies** of the same event wiring and helpers, and both grew; fixes found in one apply to both.
- **Probe leftovers in feature modules** (X-13.2) and **bare-name global writes** (X-6.3) are invisible to a search for `_G.`; `Docs/review-2026-11-15-scripts/sweep/globwrite.py` finds both and is worth running before a release.
- **Probe before changing**: X-6.1, X-6.2, X-6.3, the three `combatSafe` + `reloadToToggle` modules after a `/reload` in combat (Auras, CastBars, Notifications), whether `WorldMapFrame` can be missing when modules start (X-11.a5, X-11.b4), and whether `GetActiveLootRollIDs` exists on Forever (X-11.b6).

#### From patterns 2 and 3

- The pattern "one hidden flusher frame, shown by the event, hides itself in its `OnUpdate`" now exists five times (`Core/Extend.wowlua:154`, `UI/Layout.wowlua:384`, `UI/ActionBar.wowlua:440`, `UI/ClassBars.wowlua:268`, plus dirty flags in `UI/CooldownTracker.wowlua:1531`). It is the working answer to event bursts in this code base; X-3.1, X-3.3, X-3.4 and X-3.5 are the places that do not use it yet. `Core/Extend`'s `GameNextFrame` could be the one implementation.
- Fixes since the first pass that came from in-game measurement (comments cite `/suu perf` and probes): the action bars do one kind of pass a frame, the range pass moved out of `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED`, the nameplates stopped listening to `QUEST_LOG_UPDATE` (`Units/Nameplates.wowlua:2014-2019`), `Core/Motion` skips alpha steps under 3%, `Core/Ahead` and `Core/Data` spread login work over frames. The unit frames' roster path (X-3.1) and the group frames' `UNIT_AURA` (X-3.3) were not touched by that work.
- `Units/WorldMap.wowlua:2852-2863`: `QUEST_LOG_UPDATE` is in the list that calls `forgetQuests()` (`judged = {}`), the cache whose comment (`:461-466`) says a map refresh without it cost "320k instructions and 357 KB". `QUEST_LOG_UPDATE` fires very often (the nameplates' comment at `Units/Nameplates.wowlua:2014` says so), so the cache is dropped far more often than "a quest turned in, accepted or abandoned, your level, skills or reputation". It only costs when the map refreshes afterwards; worth checking in game whether opening the map itself fires `QUEST_LOG_UPDATE` (then the cache never survives an open). The other part's reviewer of `Units/WorldMap` should judge it.
- Event frames outside the bus: `Units/Nameplates.wowlua:870-900` (per plate), `Core/Ahead.wowlua:62`, `UI/WindowSkin.wowlua:961`, `UI/Panel.wowlua:183`, `Units/MouseBindings.wowlua:511`. Their handlers are not fault-isolated and not seen by `/suu perf`. The plates' is deliberate (unit tokens change as plates are reused); `MouseBindings`' `bookWatch` is file-level and stays registered when the module is off (it only clears a cache).
- `Units/Bags.wowlua:3034` registers `UNIT_INVENTORY_CHANGED` for all units and tests `unit == "player"`; `OnUnitEvent(…, "player", …)` would keep other players' equipment changes away from it. Same shape: `Units/PartyFrames.wowlua:1401` (`UNIT_PET` for all units, refreshes the party's pets on any pet change nearby) and `Units/Nameplates.wowlua:2020` (`UNIT_QUEST_LOG_CHANGED`, tests `unit == "player"`).
- `C_Timer` is still used directly only in `Units/GameMenu.wowlua` (`:480`, `:568`, `:582`), against the conventions (stdlib timer everywhere else).

#### From pattern 11, modules A to G

- `self:IsEnabled()` is false for the whole of `OnEnable`. In this part it bites only Convergences (X-11.a8). Benign cases: Bags `HideBlizzardBank()` at `:2934` takes its "off" branch at enable (`local on = self:IsEnabled() and self:Get("bank")`, `:2184`) and the bank is put away by the `OnShow` hook later; GameMenu `self:Away(g)` at `:545` likewise. FlightMap already defers (`:2628-2631`, "once the module counts as on"). Worth a sweep in H to Z for emits and service answers made inside `OnEnable`.
- `Module` has no owned timers. Every non-reload module in this part hand-writes `if not self:IsEnabled() then return end` in its timer bodies, and the misses are exactly the unguarded ones (Campsite `:605`, Convergences `:795`, CooldownManager `:3463-3478`, FlightMap `:2573`, `:2579`). `M:After(seconds, fn)` / `M:Every(seconds, fn)` that the registry cancels in `releaseAll` would remove the class of bug (X-11.a1) and the unkept `every(15)` handles.
- Remembering a game setting the module changed (CVar) has three hand-written forms: a profile string (DamageMeter), a profile boolean (CooldownManager), nothing (Guild). One helper (`M:SetCVarWhileOn(name, value)`, value kept in character data, restored by the registry on disable and at login for a reload module that is now off) would cover X-11.a2 and X-11.a4.
- `M:RunOutOfCombat` jobs are not owned: a job queued in combat by a module that is then turned off still runs at the end of combat. In this part the queued bodies are harmless after a disable (CooldownManager's CVar restore is meant to run then).
- ActionBars `:1353-1357`: the `InCombatLockdown()` branch in `OnEnable` is dead for a module that is not `combatSafe`.
- ActionBars `TakeOverQuickKeybind` (`:1219-1246`) hooks `QuickKeybindFrame` only if it exists at `OnEnable` and is never tried again; if that frame loads on demand on Forever the takeover silently never happens. Needs an in-game probe (`/dump QuickKeybindFrame ~= nil` right after login).
- AuraFilters `mutate` (`:156-161`) writes `lists` and then `attached` as two settings; `DeleteList` changes both, so every frame kind re-applies its filters twice for one click, the first time with attachments that still name the deleted list. Harmless, but one `Publish` after both writes would do.
- CooldownManager `:3401-3405`: after a reload in combat the `SetCVar` runs in combat; if the client refuses it there, `viewerOff` is not set and it is not tried again at the end of the fight (only matters the first time the module is ever on). Not probed.

#### From pattern 11, modules H to Z

- **`IsEnabled()` inside the lifecycle callbacks is the common root of X-11.b5, X-11.b6 and X-11.b7** (false in `OnEnable`, true in `OnDisable`; `src/Core/Modules.wowlua:668-673`, `:685-689`). Marks already carries two comments and extra code for it (`src/Units/Marks.wowlua:1217-1223`, `:1233-1238`), WorldMap loses its first draw on a live re-enable (`:2555`, `:2259`). The per-module fixes above are local; the alternative is to change the registry so the state is `Enabled` before `OnEnable` runs (`fail()` already sets `Errored` on a throw) and `Disabled` before `OnDisable` runs. That needs a sweep of every module's `OnDisable` for helpers that rely on `IsEnabled()` being true there, and of part a's modules for the same three bug shapes: a `Refresh`/`Apply`/`Update` that starts with `if not self:IsEnabled()` and is called from `OnEnable`, or that branches on `IsEnabled()` and is called from `OnDisable`. Grep: `IsEnabled()` in functions reached from `OnEnable`/`OnDisable`. The unit tests cannot see it where they call `M:OnEnable()` / `M:OnDisable()` by hand on a module the registry already enabled (tests/unit/Units/LootRolls.test.wowlua:676-685).
- MouseBindings' secure work is otherwise clean: every `SetAttribute`, `SecureHandlerWrapScript`, `SecureHandlerExecute`, `RegisterStateDriver`, the click-bindings write and the CVar write sit behind `InCombatLockdown()` (`:2289`, `:2233`, `:1905`, `:809`), `Build` is reached only from `Apply`, the module is not `combatSafe`, and what `Apply` writes on other modules' unit buttons is recorded per frame (`frameAttrs`, `:2364-2374`) and cleared at the start of the next `Apply` (`:2306-2311`). Frames that appear during a fight get their click attributes when it ends (`GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` → `ApplySoon` → `Apply` → `RunOutOfCombat`), as the header says. The file-level frame on `SPELLS_CHANGED` (`:510-514`) runs whether or not the module is on (it only drops a cache).
- "Could be `combatSafe`" (no secure or protected frames, so nothing forces the wait for the fight's end after a `/reload` in combat): Marks, QuestAnnounce, Welcome, WorldMap, LootRolls. Only LootRolls and QuestAnnounce lose something by waiting (rolls and finished objectives during that fight).
- Published anchors are not released by the registry (`releaseAll`), so each module must withdraw its own: Threat does (`:694`), Timeline does not (X-11.b3). Worth a sweep in part a (`PublishAnchor` without a matching `nil` in `OnDisable` of a live-toggle module), or make `PublishAnchor` take an owner and release it in `releaseAll`.
- Timeline writes into the diagnostics' saved table from module code (`rawset(_G, "SuuUIProbe", probe)` and `saved.countdown`, `src/Units/Timeline.wowlua:824-843`, capped at 12 entries) on every countdown: a probe left in a shipping path.
- LootRolls' error path: when `OnEnable` throws after `Wire`, Blizzard's roll frames stay off screen (`:1450-1458`, hooks not gated on the module being on) and the tray is hidden, so there is no roll UI until `/reload`. Gating `away()` on the module being on would cover it.
